title: W1: fmn-core — constants, units, color pipeline, rate functions (the shared language of every manim scene)
description:
Implement fmn-core's semantic bedrock (§6.2, §6.3, §6.8).

Constants & units (§6.2): FRAME_HEIGHT = 8 and the coordinate conventions, direction constants (UP/DOWN/LEFT/RIGHT/OUT/IN...), buffs, DEG/TAU, default stroke widths, the manim color palette, STROKE_WIDTH_CONVERSION = 0.01, the resolution table, the 30 fps default. These are kept EXACTLY — they are the shared language of every manim scene — and locked by a constants test against the Reference module (generate the fixture once from the pinned Reference source).

Color (§6.3): one pipeline, ours: colors decode to linear light, composite premultiplied, encode at the output transfer function. Manim's gradient aesthetic is deliberately preserved: interpolate_color keeps the Reference's sqrt(lerp(c1^2, c2^2, alpha)) form and average_color its RMS form, applied within the defined model. Full named palette, color_gradient, owned colormap tables (displacing matplotlib's), the hwb()/color-mix() machinery reused from fmd, and an Oklab interpolation OPTION. Draft Behavior Note BN-04 ("correct compositing, familiar gradients").

Rate functions (§6.8): the complete catalog with the same formulas (smooth, rush_into, there_and_back, wiggle, exponential_decay, ...), locked at 10^4 samples against the Reference; squish_rate_func and not_quite_there marked as combinators in the API schema.

Numeric doctrine hooks (§6.1): establish the f64-semantic / f32-record type aliases and the NaN/-0 canonicalization helpers used at serialization boundaries.

Acceptance: constants/rate-function parity tables green; color round-trip oracle tests (decode-encode identity, premultiply laws) green; BN-04 drafted.

TEXTURES & IMAGES (§10.6): bilinear filtering with DEFINED wrap/orientation/alpha/color-space behavior; decode via fmn-codec (W8 — the PNG/JPEG bead is a dependency); exotic formats route through the ffmpeg capability with named errors.

Calibration: G0-2's look study fixes the lighting match measurement; the Look Gallery's 3D set (spheres, tori, textured surfaces, glow dots against gradients) is the standing review.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-oac / fm-5oi (2026-07-26) — TWO THINGS ARE WAITING ON YOUR CAMERA, both stated in code rather than half-built.

1. flat_stroke vs camera-facing (§10.3). Under bin.rs's ScreenMap — a uniform scale plus a translation — the two are the SAME construction: a width measured in the object plane and one measured in screen pixels differ by exactly that scale, and crates/fmn-render/src/stroke.rs already computes the screen-space one. They diverge only once geometry leaves the view plane (a flat stroke on a rotated shape foreshortens; a camera-facing one does not). Uniforms::flat_stroke is read and honoured trivially today; the divergence is yours. Note also C-2 (BN-07): the Reference's get_flat_stroke() reads the WRONG uniform, and fmn-mobject already fixed that — do not re-derive it.

2. Perspective for the fill (§10.2) is already built and waiting for a producer. crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs has RationalPiece + append_rational: a projected quadratic is EXACTLY a rational quadratic (projection is linear on homogeneous coordinates), subdivision is de Casteljau in homogeneous coordinates so it is lossless, and flattening runs to a stated screen-space tolerance with a FlattenReport that says how deep it went and whether the depth cap stopped it. What it needs from you is homogeneous control points — (x*w, y*w, w) per control point — and nothing else. It does NOT want a Projection type in the render crate; bin.rs declined to invent one and fill.rs declined too.

   One contract to honour: append_rational returns RationalError::CrossesHorizon when W is not of one sign across a piece, because such a piece has no screen-space image at all. NEAR-PLANE CLIPPING IS THE CAMERA'S JOB. If you hand it an unclipped piece it will refuse rather than draw something, by design (D2's no-silent-substitution posture). The check solves for W's roots rather than sampling, so it catches an interior tangency (weights 1,-1,1 give W=(1-2t)^2 — a point at infinity) as well as a sign change.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the engine is landed and it has a shaped hole where you go.

FrameJob composites exactly two passes per instance, fill and stroke, in docs/RENDER_ORDER.md's R-5 order. There is NO glow/true_dot, no lighting, no depth test, and no camera — ScreenMap is still a uniform scale plus an origin, and bin.rs's note about not inventing a Projection still stands. The G0-6 spike's frame carried a glow term and ours does not, which is the one thing the composite.v1 corpus frame cannot exercise until you land.

Two concrete notes:

1. THE PASS LIST IS THE EXTENSION POINT. FrameJob::composite_row dispatches fill_pass/stroke_pass off Style::stroke_behind. A glow pass is a third arm; a depth test is a per-fragment operation inside the same sequence (R-4 is explicit that depth_test partitions the batch key but does not reorder). Nothing about the band/queue structure needs to change to add either, and the brute-force reference test (the_engine_matches_a_brute_force_reference) will hold whatever you add to the same standard.

2. NEGATIVE SCALE NOW WORKS, AND IT DID NOT BEFORE. bin::screen_aabb was returning an un-normalized AABB, so a negative ScreenMap::scale — the natural spelling of a y-flip — made Grid::span's lo..=hi loops yield nothing and every instance silently vanished into a blank frame with no error anywhere. Fixed and tested (a_negative_scale_still_bins_every_instance). Worth knowing before you decide whether the camera flips y through the scale or through the origin; both work now.

title: W6: Make typesetting preflight resource failures non-panicking
description: At exact HEAD baa531ed9e785f52b74b89fc22acf238dc076f73, TexEngine::preflight starts every scoped worker with infallible Scope::spawn and builds both its per-item mutex slots and returned outcome vector with infallible collection. Host thread refusal can panic even though typesetting can run on the caller, and result-storage exhaustion can abort before the batch's public outcome exists. Start workers through a deterministic fallible seam; retain every successfully started worker and fall back to caller-thread execution if none start, because preflight parallelism is a scheduler choice rather than semantics. Reserve all result storage fallibly before any cache-warming work and expose a typed batch-level PreflightError while preserving ordered per-string TexError outcomes. Empty batches must start no threads. Replace the existing missing-slot-success default with deterministic caller-thread completion. Add exact first-worker and intermediate-worker refusal regressions, cache-warming proof, empty-batch and capacity-overflow coverage; update the two internal callers; run focused Scribe/PG7 checks, strict docs/lints, exact scripts/check.sh, and scoped UBS. Keep DSR status separate while the shared eligible lane is paused.

title: W6: Make typeset cache codec canonical and allocation-fallible
description: At exact HEAD f900b8446cd2c82350426765f4b38fd88da5b782, crates/fmn-tex/src/typeset.rs serializes public Typeset data with infallible Vec growth, silently narrows usize lengths/spans to u32, records only subs.len() even though callers can mutate the public submobject table, and decodes declared collections without minimum-payload feasibility or fallible reservation. Harden the FMNTEX codec under plan sections 6.7, 11.5, and 14.4: expose a typed codec error; reject non-representable or noncanonical public values before emitting bytes; preserve the existing canonical bytes for valid values; preflight exact encoded size and reserve fallibly; reject impossible decoded counts before collection growth; reserve decoded collections fallibly; keep corrupt/cache-resource failures as cache misses rather than construction failures; add deterministic regressions for same-length subtable mutation, wide spans/counts, impossible declared counts, allocation refusal seams, and valid-byte roundtrip. This is internal cache reliability, not a new user-visible feature, so no new e2e scenario is required. Run focused W6/PG7 checks, strict docs/lints, exact scripts/check.sh, scoped UBS, committed-tree review, and keep DSR status separate while its eligible lane is paused.

title: W5: The retained compositor — dirty regions, tile caches, byte-identical reuse (export AND preview)
description:
Implement the retained compositor (§10.8, D-20): the dirty-region story generalized into retained rendering everywhere — export, not just preview.

Mechanics: object→tile dependencies tracked; BOTH old and new bounds dirtied on movement; completed tiles cached keyed on (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform); static layer runs above/below animated content cached as units; per-frame allocation in bump arenas over pooled frame buffers — the zero-alloc steady state PG-6 measures (allocation count is a sharper regression tripwire than wall-clock).

The load-bearing property: REUSED TILES ARE BYTE-IDENTICAL, so reuse is PG-5-safe and WORKS UNDER CERTIFIED — a wait() frame reduces to clock advance plus reuse; a blinking cursor does not re-rasterize a 4K frame. This must be structural: the cache key includes every input that could change bytes (per W5IR's revision taxonomy plus camera + output transform), and a cache hit bypasses rasterization entirely rather than re-rasterizing-and-comparing.

Interaction with live views (§8.2): while a writable live NumPy view exists on an object, that object's tiles are conservatively invalidated every frame — correctness over reuse, always; ranged-edit APIs are the precise-dirty opt-in.

Acceptance: reuse-equivalence tests (cached vs cold frames bit-identical across an animation corpus with waits, static layers, moving objects); key-completeness adversarial tests (every mutation class invalidates its tiles — style, transform, order, camera, output transform each tested); the wait()-frame fast path measured (near-zero raster work via §17.1 counters); allocation-count instrumentation wired for PG-6; live-view conservative-invalidation test.
notes:
FROM fm-gw7 (§10.8's compiled-path artifacts): two retained fields this bead consumes are NOT yet on fmn_render::table::Shape — 'previous tile coverage' and 'old + new dirty bounds'. They were left out deliberately rather than added as dead fields: both are meaningful only against a tiling, and the tiling is fm-tg6's. Add them here or there, but note the tile-cache key §10.8 states is (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform) — the resource-revision half is built and is fmn_render::revision::Revisions, whose Dependency type is how an artifact declares which axes it depends on.

Also inherited: fmn_render::plan::RenderPlan already retains compiled outlines across syncs and reports what it did NOT rebuild (SyncStats), so 'reused tiles are byte-identical' has a place to be measured from.
close_reason:
The retained compositor's key and dirty-tile machinery landed in crates/fmn-render/src/cache.rs (78 tests in the crate). The half that needs pixels is fm-uql, blocked on the first engine.

WHY THIS IS THE RIGHT SPLIT: everything interesting about a tile cache is whether its key is COMPLETE. Get that wrong and the failure is the worst kind this program has — a stale tile under certified is a wrong frame that is bit-reproducibly wrong, so every determinism check agrees with it. That risk is now retired; wiring pixels to a proven key is not where the danger is.

LANDED:
- TileKey with §10.8's four declared parts kept as four fields, so a miss can say WHICH part moved. Built by TileKey::build from the binning and the plan rather than assembled by callers, so a new input cannot be forgotten at one call site and remembered at another.
- Key-completeness adversarial suite: style, order, camera, output transform (scale, origin, pixel format, viewport — each separately), and transform proving BOTH the tile an object left and the tile it entered are dirtied. That last one falls out of the key rather than needing its own bookkeeping, which is worth knowing.
- §8.2's live views POISON rather than fold: a writable view mutates points with no revision bumped, so a cache watching revisions alone would serve a stale tile forever. Poisoned tiles never hit, are never stored, and stop being poisoned when the view drops.
- TileWork::Reuse hands the payload back untouched — §10.8's 'a hit bypasses rasterization entirely rather than re-rasterizing-and-comparing' is structural here, not a comment.
- CacheStats for §17.2's hit-rate and dirty-tile-percentage counters, asserted to partition every tile.

A PROPERTY THE KEY DEPENDS ON, now tested in plan.rs: interned shape and style indices are stable across syncs, because interning is append-only. A plan rebuilt per frame reshuffles them and every tile key in the frame moves for a reason unrelated to the tile — which is exactly what this bead's first test harness did, and why the harness now retains the plan the way a frame loop must.

title: W8: The sound mixer — WAV/PCM with a fully specified matrix
description:
Implement audio (§14.5; displaces pydub): the WAV/PCM mixer with EVERY behavior specified — sample formats (i16/i24/f32) and rates with a NAMED resampler (documented algorithm and quality), channel layouts (mono/stereo mapping rules), gain semantics (gain, gain_to_background — the Reference's ducking parameter), negative time offsets (sound starting before its add point clips correctly), overlay-past-end (the mix extends), clipping policy (defined: clamp with a warning counter, not wraparound), dithering policy on bit-depth reduction, DETERMINISTIC MIX ORDER (sounds mix in a defined order so float summation is reproducible — certified WAV output is bit-locked), and A/V sync on the rational clock (sample-accurate placement from frame times — no float drift between audio and video, BN-02's audio corollary).

Scope boundaries: WAV in/out is native (W8CODEC2); NON-WAV inputs (mp3, etc.) decode through the ffmpeg capability boundary with named capability errors when absent (D2); certified output is WAV (ffmpeg's encoded audio is uncertified like all its products).

Scene surface: Scene.add_sound with the Reference's signature and semantics; the two-stage mux (W8FFMPEG) consumes the mixed WAV.

Acceptance: mix golden vectors (offsets, overlaps, gains, negative offsets, past-end) bit-locked; resampler quality tests (documented passband/stopband vs spec); clipping/dither policy tests; determinism test (same inputs ⇒ same WAV bytes, any thread count); A/V sync test (a click on frame N lands at the sample-exact time); ffmpeg-decode capability path test with the fake-ffmpeg.

title: W1: Land gate — no commit reaches main without fmt, clippy and tests from an owned host (unbuilt peer commits keep main red)
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check

Main does not stay green because commits land on it without anyone building or testing them. Evidence at `52a53d69` (2026-09-27):
- `cargo fmt --check` exits 1: nine files from the camera-bundle commits (`b090db93` and neighbours), `crates/fmn/src/exporting*.rs`, `crates/fmn-scene/src/recording.rs`, `crates/fmn-wasm/src/player.rs`, …
- `cargo test`: `crates/fmn/tests/native_camera_export.rs:82` fails with `InvalidOptions("camera resolution, fps, and background must match the export configuration")`. The test was added by `b090db93` and never executed.
- Earlier the same day, `crates/fmn-python/src/portal_surface_init.rs`'s test module did not compile (`get_item` without `PyDictMethods` in scope) after two peer changes merged. f9e970fd fixed it.
- The peers' own commit messages say it: "Native Rust compilation … remain UNRUN because this environment has no Rust toolchain" (7680f21a, 575bd6c3, e2c8828b).
- Hosted `ci.yml` has had no green run since 2026-08-10, and none of the last 400 runs succeeded.
- 59 workflows grant `contents: write` and push to main themselves (fm-neutralize-bot-push-workflows-ieol).

fm-restore-green-ci-tqsr fixes today's reds by hand. Nothing stops the next unbuilt commit, so main re-reddens within hours.

## Work (owner decision required; label manual)

1. Owner decision, recorded as an ADR: choose how a commit reaches main. The options:
   - (a) branch protection on `main` requiring one status check that runs on an owned host (self-hosted runner): `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test` restricted to the crates the diff touches plus the fast e2e tier. Agents push to branches and land through a merge queue.
   - (b) a server-side pre-receive hook with the same check.
   - (c) keep direct pushes, but add a revert bot that reverts any commit whose check fails within N minutes.
   The ADR records which agents lack a toolchain and how they land (branch + gate).
2. Implement the chosen check. The check itself is `scripts/check.sh` or a documented subset with a wall-clock budget. Its workflow has `contents: read`.
3. AGENTS.md: "Never push Rust you have not compiled and tested. Agents without a toolchain push to a branch and land through the gate."
4. Coordinate with fm-neutralize-bot-push-workflows-ieol: bot workflows that push to main either go through the same gate or are retired.

## Acceptance

- ADR accepted by the owner, with AGENTS.md and docs/GOVERNANCE.md trued up in the same commit.
- A deliberately unformatted commit and a deliberately failing test commit are each refused (or reverted) by the gate. These are the planted negatives, recorded with run ids.
- Main stays green (fmt, clippy, the gate's tests) for 7 consecutive days of normal swarm activity, measured and recorded in the close comment.
- Structured logs: each gate run emits the commit, the checks run, their exit codes and durations.

title: W10: Differential Reference runs on TeX Live 2025/dvisvgm 3.6 — Tex glyph structure is toolchain-dependent (Reference IndexErrors); pin a period TeX toolchain
description:
## Found by the corpus differential (fm-5wq.33), 2026-09-27

The differential's Reference is the pinned 3b1b/manim@6199a00d running on this host's TeX toolchain: pdfTeX from TeX Live 2025/Debian, and dvisvgm 3.6. The Reference's `Tex` builds its glyph family and span labels from dvisvgm's SVG output (`use_labelled_svg`, per-span colors), so its structure depends on that toolchain, not only on the pin. Evidence that this host's toolchain does not reproduce the structure 3b1b's scenes were written against:
- **Scenes the portal runs fail in the Reference on Tex indexing.** Examples:
  - `_2024/puzzles/max_rand.py` `MaxProcess`/`SqrtProcess`: `label.make_number_changeable("0.00")` raises `IndexError` inside the Reference;
  - `_2025/laplace/*` (`CombinationOfExponentials`, `PartialFractionDecomposition`, `RecapSPlane`, `Linearity`), `_2023/convolutions2/dice.py`, `_2023/moser_reboot/main.py` `FinalRearrangment`, `_2024/puzzles/added_dimension.py` `StruggleWithStrips`, `_2023/optics_puzzles/ior_annotations.py` `MissingDetails`: all `IndexError: list index out of range`;
  - `_2023/gauss_int/herschel.py` `VariableC`/`VariableCWithF`: `'VMobjectFromSVGPath' object has no attribute 'set_value'`, where `make_number_changeable` returned a glyph.
- **Glyph counts differ from the portal's in both directions** where both run: `Tex('314{,}159{,}265{,}35')` has 8 glyph members in the Reference against 15 in the portal. Color maps (`t2c`) then land on shifted glyphs, which shows up as glyph `style.fill_color` differences in about 50 scenes.

Until the Reference runs on a period-correct TeX toolchain, Tex-internal structure (glyph members, their style, span strings) is not a trustworthy oracle. The differential carries those facts as an open-bead row citing this bead.

## Work

- Establish the TeX Live and dvisvgm versions the pinned Reference was developed against, from the pin's era (2024) and the dvisvgm SVG features `tex_file_writing.py`/`string_mobject.py` rely on.
- Provision them for the Reference side only, in a pinned container or a TeX Live historic tlnet snapshot. Record the versions in the differential's engine identity, and re-run the corpus differential.
- Then remove the environment row and triage what remains: genuine portal Tex-structure bugs go to beads, and BN-05 is updated if the glyph grouping rule is itself a deliberate divergence.

## Acceptance

- The Reference runs the scenes listed above without `IndexError`, or the remaining failures are shown to be Reference defects.
- The open-bead row `fm-…-reference-tex-environment` is removed, and the Tex-structure differences that remain are each triaged.
close_reason: Pushed b9ef8342 (and triage follow-up 8c801a93). Root cause was not the TeX toolchain: the Reference caches TeX SVGs in a shared diskcache and compiles every string as a fixed working.tex in a shared latex_cache, so concurrent Reference processes swap each other's DVI (Appendix C-22, race repro in b9ef8342); ~/.cache/manim here serves TexText('Why $e^{-x^2}$?') as 48 glyphs/18.45 wide vs 8 glyphs/3.52 fresh, and holds 26 empty SVGs. corpus_differential.py gives every concurrent Reference run a private, initially empty TeX cache and records pdfTeX 1.40.28 (TeX Live 2025) + dvisvgm 3.6 in the engine identity. Acceptance (1): 10 of the 11 listed scenes run in the Reference; StruggleWithStrips dies on Reference defect C-23 (match_points leaves subpath_end_indices stale; BN-07 + bridge.py). Acceptance (2): full re-run (same portal wheel) 825 both (was 774), 226 portal-only (was 277), 204 C-18 (was 240), 8 untriaged (was 25; then 2 after 8c801a93's C-24..C-26 triage). Row fm-0v8k-reference-tex-environment removed; the 61 scenes it still masked on a clean Reference are portal Tex structure (39 order, 20 piece counts, 2 DecimalNumber), filed as fm-aia1, whose row replaces it.

title: W10: Glyph submobjects are plain VMobject (Reference: VMobjectFromSVGPath; Tex rules are Rectangle with get_vertices)
description:
## Found by the structural-facts extractor (fm-5wq.36), 2026-09-27

BN-05 (native text typesetting) says glyph *metrics and outlines* differ from the Reference by design. The Reference's structural conventions are kept: non-whitespace glyphs in order, one submobject per ligature. The *types* of those submobjects are not covered by any Behavior Note, and they differ:
- In the Reference, each glyph of `Text`/`Tex`/`TexText` is a `VMobjectFromSVGPath` (`manimlib/mobject/svg/svg_mobject.py`, exported by `manimlib`). In the portal, each glyph is a plain `VMobject`. Measured with structural_facts.py on a release wheel from fac2e515 (subjects `text` and `tex`).
- In the Reference, the fraction bar of `Tex(r"\frac{1}{2}")` is a `Rectangle` (dvisvgm emits `<rect>`), with `get_vertices()` and Polygon methods. In the portal it is a `VMobject` of 65 points, and `get_vertices` is absent.

Effects:
- `isinstance(glyph, VMobjectFromSVGPath)` is False;
- `tex[0][i].get_vertices()` raises for fraction bars and other rule glyphs;
- code that branches on `Rectangle` to find rules breaks.

## Work

- Glyph submobjects of Text/MarkupText/Tex/TexText are instances of the portal's `VMobjectFromSVGPath`, which should be exported with the Reference's MRO `(VMobjectFromSVGPath, VMobject, Mobject)`. Native storage is unchanged.
- Rules in fmd-math output (fraction bars, radical overbars, `\rule`) become `Rectangle` instances whose vertices are the rule's corners, in the Reference's order (the `<rect>` path, starting at the top-right corner as in the Reference's measured `get_vertices`). The glyph geometry otherwise stays native (BN-05).

## Tests and acceptance

- structural_facts.py: `class`, `mro` and `getters.get_vertices` equal for the glyph members of `text` and `tex`. Geometry facts stay BN-05 exclusions. The open-bead rows citing this bead are removed.
- An installed-wheel test for `isinstance(Text("a")[0], VMobjectFromSVGPath)`, and for `Tex(r"\frac12")` containing a `Rectangle` member whose `get_vertices()` spans the bar's bounding box. Planted negative: fails at fac2e515.

title: W10: VGroup is not a Group in the portal (Reference: VGroup(Group, VMobject)); isinstance(x, Group) is False for every VGroup, Axes, VCube
description:
## Found by the structural-facts extractor (fm-5wq.36), 2026-09-27

In the pinned Reference, `VGroup` is `class VGroup(Group, VMobject, Generic[SubVmobjectType])` (`manimlib/mobject/types/vectorized_mobject.py:1338`). So every VGroup, and every class built on it (`Axes`, `NumberPlane`, `NumberLine`'s tick group, `VGroup3D`/`VCube`, `SurroundingRectangle` groups, `BulletedList`, the Matrix family, …), is an instance of `Group`.

In the portal, `type(VGroup()).__mro__` is `VGroup, VMobject, Mobject, _BridgeMobject`, with no `Group`. Measured with `crates/fmn-conformance/python/structural_facts.py` on a release wheel from fac2e515. Subjects `vgroup_arranged`, `number_line`, `axes`, `number_plane` and `vcube` all differ only in `mro` at every VGroup member.

User-visible effects:
- `isinstance(x, Group)` is False for every VGroup. Scene code and libraries use that test to branch between groups and leaves (3b1b/videos helpers do).
- `Group` methods reachable through `VGroup` in the Reference are only reachable if the portal duplicated them.
- `issubclass(VGroup, Group)` is False.

## Work

- Make the portal's `VGroup` a subclass of the portal's `Group` in the Reference's MRO order, `VGroup(Group, VMobject)`, keeping the native VMobject storage and fast paths. If the PyO3 layout forbids a native multiple base, the public Python class layer can order the bases while the native object stays a VMobject, which is how the other portal Python classes compose. The ADR on the portal architecture (fm-5wq.15) should not be pre-empted: prefer the smallest change that makes the MRO exact.
- Check every class the Reference derives from VGroup: its portal MRO must contain `Group` at the Reference's position.

## Tests and acceptance

- In the installed-wheel gate: `isinstance(VGroup(), Group)`, `issubclass(Axes, Group)` and `isinstance(VCube(), Group)`. Planted negative: fails at fac2e515.
- The structural-facts diff (`python structural_facts.py diff`) shows `mro` equal for `vgroup_arranged`, `number_line`, `axes`, `number_plane` and `vcube`. The open-bead exclusion row citing this bead is then removed, because a stale open-bead exclusion fails the diff.
- Log: the public MRO of each checked class, one line per class.
close_reason: Fixed by d0b424f5 (2026-09-28): VGroup inherits Group then VMobject, as in the Reference; vector_group_protocol has 17 native tests; the fm-16u6-vgroup-not-group exclusion row was removed. Acceptance re-checked 2026-10-11 against the pinned Reference with the same probe, output identical. isinstance(VGroup(), Group), issubclass(Axes, Group) and isinstance(VCube(), Group) are all True. Public MROs: VGroup [VGroup, Group, VMobject, Mobject]; Axes [Axes, VGroup, Group, VMobject, Mobject, CoordinateSystem]; NumberPlane [NumberPlane, Axes, ...]; VGroup3D and VCube [..., VGroup3D, VGroup, Group, VMobject, Mobject]; BulletedList [BulletedList, VGroup, Group, ...]; NumberLine.ticks [VGroup, Group, VMobject, Mobject]. The structural constructions gate (subjects vgroup_arranged, number_line, axes, number_plane, vcube) passes with no fm-16u6 row: 0 failing, 0 stale.

title: W5: Cancelled Transform render leaves native proxies uncollectable (production_transform_material_kernel_acceptance fails; contaminates 11 later portal suites)
description:
## Observed (2026-09-24, local embedded harness, CPython 3.13.1, HEAD 59fb6bed)
- `cargo test -p fmn-python --lib production_` : 10 pass, 12 fail. 11 of the 12 PASS when run alone with --exact
  (bridge, animation_semantics, callback_cleanup, camera_runtime, drawing_runtime, native_output,
  persistent_runtime, portal_runtime, surface_mesh, portal_video, subset_reveal). They fail only because the
  harness's survivor check (lib.rs ~11039, `proxies = [... for obj in gc.get_objects() if isinstance(obj, Bridge)]`)
  inspects EVERY live proxy in the shared interpreter, so one leaking suite poisons every later one.
- The one real failure: `portal_texture::raster::transition::tests::production_transform_material_kernel_acceptance`
  fails alone: survivors [ImageMobject x3, CameraFrame, Point x3].
- Per-case probe (normal interpreter, HEAD wheel): the ONLY leaking case is
  `RasterTransformTests.test_cancelled_output_does_not_publish_partial_image_transform_frames`
  (tests/raster_transform.py:344): a scene-local `class Demo(m.Scene)` whose `construct` closes over `item` and
  a Transform `t` whose rate_func raises KeyboardInterrupt at alpha>.3 during `Demo().render(png_sequence)`.

## Established by in-harness experiments (worktree copy, never committed)
- After the harness clears the method cache and collects twice, the Demo INSTANCE and the Demo TYPE stay alive
  with no Python-visible external referrer (type's only referrer is its own __mro__). Clearing the Demo
  instance's __dict__ and deleting Demo.construct does NOT free the instance -> something outside Python's
  GC graph (Rust/C) holds a strong reference to the scene instance (or its type) after the cancelled render.
- Only untracked native objects inside the 95-object cluster: _CameraCore, _CameraFrameCore (pure Rust
  fields) and 4 base-less ndarrays -> no hidden OUTBOUND edge from the cluster; the pin is inbound.
- Ruled out: render threads (threads=1 still leaks); construct runs on the owner thread; no live frames or
  tracebacks; sys.exc_info clean; the only live exception is the test's own KeyboardInterrupt (in the cluster);
  PyScene.proxies holds weakrefs only; _abort_render takes and aborts the session; stepped-play error path
  drops its locals; PyO3 deferred-decref pool (a no-op py.detach before collection changes nothing).
- Without closures (image/animation as scene attributes) a cancelled render leaks NOTHING in a normal
  interpreter, for KeyboardInterrupt and ValueError, threads 1 and 4 (scratch leak_min.py).

## Next probes
1. In the harness, check sys.getrefcount(type(scene)) before/after the suite vs a successful-render twin of the
   same test (same closure shape, no raise) - isolates cancel-vs-closure.
2. Swap KeyboardInterrupt for ValueError in the harness copy.
3. Audit native code that captures a scene/type reference during play/render setup and releases it only on
   the success path (e.g. portal_playback::synchronize, frame-session setup, method dispatch via
   call_cached*), and any `Py<>` held by fmn_scene closures inside Engine.

## Acceptance
- production_transform_material_kernel_acceptance passes in the full `cargo test -p fmn-python --lib production_` run
  with the harness's survivor check unchanged; all 22 production_ suites green; CI's portal jobs green.
- A regression test that fails at HEAD: a cancelled render of a closure-bearing scene releases every proxy.

comments.text:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIX PROVEN (2026-09-24). This is an upstream PyO3 0.29.2 GC defect, not a portal leak.

Mechanism. PyO3's synthesized tp_traverse (for #[pyclass(dict)] without __traverse__, i.e. _BridgeMobject and _SceneCore) visits the base traverse and __dict__, but never Py_TYPE(self). CPython's subtype_traverse deliberately skips visiting a Python subclass's type when the next base is a heap type with its own traverse, delegating that visit to the base (typeobject.c). So for every Python class built on the portal (class Demo(Scene), class X(VMobject)), the instance -> class reference is invisible to the collector. Any cycle that runs through a class is uncollectable.

Minimal repro, normal interpreter, no render: . H is never collected (method-cache entries +0); the same with  is collected. The same holds for VMobject and Mobject.

Why this suite: its test defines  whose construct closes over images added to the scene. The chain class -> construct -> cell -> image -> _scene -> instance -> class leaks.
- A SUCCESSFUL render of the same shape leaks too.
- Leaving out render (Demo(); construct()) still leaks.
- KeyboardInterrupt vs ValueError is irrelevant.
- The method cache is a second, separate pin in normal processes; the harness clears it.

Upstream fix: PyO3 824757db37 'always implement tp_traverse to traverse type object (#6269)', on main since 2026-08-09, NOT in a release (crates.io max 0.29.2). Its call_super_traverse visits this_type when the next base is not a heap type.

Proof. I backported that one hunk onto a scratch copy of pyo3-0.29.2 and wired it with [patch.crates-io] in a scratch worktree at 59fb6bed:
- production_transform_material_kernel_acceptance passes;
-  gives 22 passed, 0 failed (it was 10/22).
Nothing was committed to main: this is a dependency decision.

User-visible impact beyond CI: Studio/live-reload and batch processes that redefine scene or mobject classes leak every old class plus its instances.

Options (OWNER DECISION, D1 governed closure):
(a) vendor the one-hunk backport as a [patch.crates-io] path crate, with an allowlist row citing #6269 and a removal trigger of 'PyO3 release containing #6269';
(b) pin pyo3 to a git rev on main, which carries unrelated unreleased changes;
(c) wait for the release.
Recommendation: (a). Do NOT weaken the harness survivor check; it caught a real leak.

comments.text:
Root cause found and fixed in a7ce6f33 (WildGoose, 2026-09-25). Self-verified; no independent verifier.

CPython's subtype_traverse does not visit an instance's heap type when the nearest non-Python base is a heap type with its own traverse; it trusts that base to visit Py_TYPE(self). PyO3 0.29.2's synthesized traverse for _BridgeMobject and _SceneCore never does (pyo3 src/impl_/pymethods.rs traverse_impl). The instance -> class edge was therefore invisible to the collector, and any cycle through a Scene or Mobject subclass's class object was uncollectable.

Minimal repro: `class Sub(manimlib.Scene): pass; Sub.me = Sub()` survives gc.collect(), while the same cycle over a plain class is collected.

The harness case is raster_transform's scene-local Demo whose construct closes over bound mobjects. The cancellation was incidental: it is the only suite with that shape.

Probes (scratchpad leak_probe_*):
- clearing the retained traceback hides the harness case;
- the apparent 6 hidden refs on the Transform were duplicate references held by single frames;
- with the method cache cleared, closure-captured bound mobjects leak with or without run() and with or without a failure, while locally created ones do not;
- the bare class-cycle probe isolates the missing edge.

Fix: wrap those two classes' tp_traverse to visit the heap type first, then call PyO3's original. It is idempotent across re-init, with SAFETY notes on each unsafe block.

Evidence:
- production_transform_material_kernel_acceptance passes in the full `cargo test -p fmn-python --lib production_` run with the survivor check unchanged: 21 of 22 suites, up from the 10 of 22 recorded here.
- New bridge.py witness (a class cycle is collected) fails at HEAD and passes with the fix.
- Full cargo test -p fmn-python: 81 pass. The 3 failures reproduce at 328b52f0 without the change: the bundle export byte budget (FMTL), fallible_native_surface_sampling (after 0725c122), and bridge (fm-5wq.24).

Still open against acceptance:
(1) 'all 22 production_ suites green': the bridge suite stops at the fm-5wq.24 GrowFromPoint red.
(2) CI portal jobs: not verified.
Keeping this open, blocked on fm-5wq.24. The long-term fix belongs upstream in PyO3.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Root cause found, not claimed (WildGoose, 2026-09-28, HEAD 8723b4f5). The failure is release-only: fmn built with the dev profile renders the README command (exit 0, 45 frames), while `cargo build --release -p fmn-cli --features 'cli batch'` at the same commit exits 5 with 'shared pure rate is not in the catalog'. The bundle is not stale.

Mechanism: fmn_core::rate::tag_of identifies catalog rates by fn-pointer identity (std::ptr::fn_addr_eq against the const TAG_CATALOG). Since Rust 1.75, small non-generic fns are cross-crate-inlinable in optimized builds, so each codegen unit that takes their address can get its own local copy. `nm -C` on the release fmn shows five local ('t') copies of fmn_core::rate::linear at different addresses. timeline_bundle.rs decodes the tag through rate_from_tag, a pointer from one CGU; shared.rs::into_shared re-derives it with rate_tag(&rate) against another CGU's copies and gets None. The writer has the same hazard: nominate() tags config.rate_func by pointer, then classify_captured_segment re-derives rate_tag(rate) ('nominated rate is untaggable', or silent stateful fallback).

Fix sketch:
(1) Never re-derive a tag from a pointer that came from a tag. SegmentData::Pure keeps the decoded u8, and into_shared uses it; nominate() returns the tag and classify_captured_segment takes it.
(2) Give the 8 catalog fns #[inline(never)], which turns cross-crate inlinability off so one symbol exists, and make TAG_CATALOG a static, so user-side RateFunc::Base(smooth) still tags. Document that pointer identity depends on it. Explicit catalog identity in RateFunc would be more robust but is a wider API change.
(3) Tests must run a release-profile binary (the README command, or cargo test --release on the bundle path), or they cannot fail on this: the dev profile passes today.

title: W9: Supervisor + scene-worker iteration — rebuild, restart, restore, replay (no dlopen)
description:
Implement live iteration (§13.3, D-14): the supervisor + scene-worker-subprocess architecture — code change detected → incremental rebuild → worker restart → restore nearest serialized checkpoint → replay journal from the last valid barrier. Crashes isolate to the worker (a panic in scene code never takes down the Studio or supervisor); the supervisor owns the UI connection, the build pipeline, and checkpoint storage; the worker owns scene execution and rendering. No dlopen, no hot-patching — process isolation is the reliability story AND the security story (untrusted content renders only in the isolated worker, §13.5).

Protocol: a versioned supervisor↔worker IPC (fmn-hash canonical serialization) carrying: scene enumeration, play/seek/scrub commands, frame streams (shared-memory or pipe per platform via fmn-platform), checkpoint push/restore, journal segments, crash reports (a worker crash yields a structured report + the journal tail — every crash is a replayable bug per §18's repro-bundle story).

Edit-to-frame is PG-4's second budget (<1s on a trailing edit of a 30s pure scene): the mechanism is checkpoint restore + journal replay (only the edited tail re-executes) + warm caches (typeset/compiled paths survive restart via fmn-cache). fmn-python preserves the literal IPython embed()/checkpoint_paste() workflow (W10's bridge exposes the hooks; the checkpoint machinery is here).

Acceptance: crash-isolation tests (worker panic → supervisor alive → auto-restart → checkpoint restore); rebuild-restart-restore cycle test with a scripted edit (measured against the PG-4 budget on the pinned profile); IPC protocol golden tests + version-skew rejection; checkpoint round-trip fidelity (restored state bit-equals pre-restart snapshot); an end-to-end autoreload session test.

title: W5: The frame pipeline + ExecutionPlan — bounded in-flight frames, render teams, topology-aware scheduling (fmn-runtime)
description:
Implement the execution architecture (§17.4, D-19, D-24) in fmn-runtime:

THE PIPELINE: after W4ORDER's FramePacket freeze, stages overlap across frames — scene update + Python callbacks for frame N+2, IR sync + binning for N+1, rasterization for N, color conversion + sink submission for N-1 — behind a BOUNDED in-flight queue (interactive preview 1-2; ordinary offline export 3-6; high-core export enough to occupy the render teams; annex 2-4), with ordered emission (W8's emitter) and pipeline barriers from the effect model (§13.4: any operation that must observe rendered pixels drains in-flight frames; ordinary manim scene code never hits one). Pure segments (W4PURITY) additionally fan whole frames across render teams.

THE EXECUTIONPLAN: derived from fmn-platform's HardwareTopology — engine, frames in flight, render-team count and threads per team, tile/macrotile dimensions, SIMD tier, scratch sizes, output pixel format. TEAMS, NOT ONE FLAT POOL: a small latency-oriented scene/update team; one render team per in-flight frame (on a 96-core part: three 32-core or four 24-core teams, never 192 threads fighting over one frame — OQ-11 owns the sizing priors); an output team on SMT siblings (they don't compete for vector ports). Within a team: physical cores first, SMT after measurement; one scratch arena per worker; local work queues, one owner per tile; no global hot atomics; coarse stealing before crossing CCD/NUMA domains; frame buffers first-touched by their team.

Mode rule: `standard` caches autotuning under the hardware fingerprint; `certified` runs its fixed declared configuration — and NO schedule can change bits, because §10.5's contract binds every one (asserted by PG-5's sweeps). asupersync NEVER enters the frame loop (multi-scene parallelism is the batch feature only).

Acceptance: pipeline-equivalence tests (pipelined vs serial execution ⇒ bit-identical frames, all queue depths); barrier tests (a pixel-observing operation drains correctly); ExecutionPlan derivation tests over fixture topologies (8-core laptop, 96-core dual-CCD, >64-CPU Windows groups, Apple P/E); team scheduling smoke tests with utilization counters (§17.1); latency measurement for the preview depth-1-2 configuration.
close_reason: ExecutionPlan, bounded ordered frame pipeline, real Lumen equivalence, deterministic LabRuntime schedule exploration, closure governance, and full green workspace gate landed.

comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed, and it is already split at the boundary your pipeline needs.

FrameJob has a serial front-end (FrameJob::new — kernel selection, join wedges, gradient fields, slabs, all derived once per frame) and a parallel back-end (render_into) that takes &self and touches nothing mutable but its own scratch and its own band. That is §9.3's FramePacket boundary one layer down, and it is what makes the back-end schedulable without the front-end being re-entrant.

Three things for you:

1. THREADS ARE ALREADY A PARAMETER AND ALREADY PROVEN INERT. render_into(threads, dst) uses std::thread::scope over a Mutex-guarded queue of bands, each band a disjoint &mut [u8] from chunks_mut, so §10.5(b)'s write-disjointness is enforced by the borrow checker rather than by comment. PG-5's {1,4,16} sweep runs per commit over the certified corpus and was additionally measured on a 14-core M4 Pro. When the ExecutionPlan exists, threads is the knob it sets.

2. TILE DIMENSIONS ARE DECLARED, NOT FREE. ADR-0013: the analytic fill's per-tile carry is a different ASSOCIATION of the same sum than a longer row's prefix, so tiling is invariant to floating-point tolerance and not to bits. §17.4 is right that tile size is a scheduling choice — but a certified run must PIN it, which is why C10 hashes it and fmn_render::engine::journal carries it. An autotuner that varies tile dimensions is standard-mode only.

3. render_into TAKES A CALLER-OWNED FrameBuffer, which is the pooled path (fmn_frame::FramePool). Pool exhaustion is already documented as the backpressure signal your bounded in-flight queue propagates. fm-e9h tracks the remaining per-frame allocations (the Vec<Draw>, the band list, the per-worker scratch) — all storage, none of it able to move a bit.

title: EPIC G0 — The Laws of the Machine (compile-tested spikes before any interface freeze)
description:
Gate G0 precedes all construction. Its purpose: retire every load-bearing unknown of the FrankenManim program as a compile-tested spike or executed decision BEFORE workstreams W2-W11 freeze their interfaces (plan §20.1). The plan is deliberately not an MVP; sequencing is by dependency, not scope reduction, and G0 is what makes that safe.

The eight spikes: (1) object-model & buffer-lifetime, (2) renderer look study, (3) fmd-math architecture, (4) TeX corpus harvest, (5) Python extensibility, (6) cross-platform determinism, (7) dependency-closure audit + SUITE.lock, (8) accelerator (GPU annex) proof.

Why this exists: Rev 2's adversarial audit showed the three-way contradiction between exact conformance, cross-platform reproducibility, and improved mathematics. Rev 3/4 resolved it by decision (conformance-to-pixels dropped; correctness + beauty + sovereignty kept), but several architectural decisions (arena object model, fixed-point vs floating certified raster arithmetic, fmd-math atom-engine shape, GPU IR mapping) can only be ratified by running code. Discovering at W5 that the render IR maps poorly to a GPU would be expensive; discovering it at G5 after CPU assumptions hardened would be worse.

Exit criteria: all eight spike beads closed with their decisions recorded in the plan's decision log (§23, D-01..D-24 amended as needed) and open questions OQ-1/OQ-2/OQ-10 resolved or explicitly deferred with an owner. No W2-W11 interface freeze may happen while this epic is open.

title: W1: fmn-config — YAML-subset parser to the actual shipped file shapes + precedence + preamble-pack registry
description:
Implement fmn-config (§6.4). The Reference ships two YAML configs; users have custom_config.yml files. We parse the ACTUAL shipped file shapes exactly — not YAML-the-standard: plain/quoted/block scalars with chomping indicators, tuple-string values, comments, duplicate-key policy (define it: last-wins with a warning), UTF-8, depth/size limits — with precise diagnostics (line/column, expected-vs-found) for everything else. This is an owned parser under the governed closure (no yaml crates), and a fuzz target from day one (§16.5: parser budgets — nesting depth, size).

Precedence: the Reference's rules exactly — built-in defaults → user config file → CLI flags — with the merged, typed config exposed to every subsystem via one struct family generated from the API schema (§16.2) once that exists; hand-write the structs now, migrate to codegen when W10's schema bead lands.

The preamble-pack registry: the Reference's tex_templates.yml concept is reborn as fmd-math preamble packs — named macro/symbol bundles (§11.4) — with a compatibility mapping for the common templates. This bead owns the registry surface (naming, lookup, config keys); the packs' CONTENT is W6's business.

Also here: the determinism-mode and engine/backend config keys (standard | certified; cpu | metal | cuda; aa policy; thread policy) as typed knobs with the constraint that quality/backend knobs may never change semantics (§4) — enforce by construction (they select engines/policies, never feed scene code).

The owned YAML-subset parser (no yaml crates) covers the actual shipped file shapes exactly: nested block mappings (space-only indent, sibling consistency enforced), plain scalars with PyYAML-1.1 resolution incl. the 1e3-is-a-string quirk kept deliberately, tuple-strings passed through for the typed layer to literal_eval-equivalently parse, single-line quoted scalars with escapes, literal blocks with all three chomping indicators, comments, and duplicate keys DEFINED as last-wins-with-a-warning. title: W4/W10: AnimationGroup adds a Group to the scene where the Reference adds a VGroup (all animated mobjects are VMobjects)
description:
## Found by the corpus differential (fm-5wq.33), 2026-09-27

In the pinned Reference, `AnimationGroup` (and so `LaggedStart`, `Succession`, `LaggedStartMap`) groups its animations' mobjects in a `VGroup` when every one is a `VMobject`, and otherwise in a `Group`. That group is what `Scene.play` adds to the scene. The portal always uses `Group`. Measured with `self.mobjects` at `tear_down`, in skip mode:

```python
a, b = Line(LEFT, RIGHT), Square()
self.play(LaggedStart(ShowCreation(a), FadeIn(b), lag_ratio=0.5))
self.play(AnimationGroup(FadeIn(Circle()), FadeIn(Text("x"))))
```
- Reference roots: `CameraFrame, VGroup, VGroup`. The CameraFrame root is fm-6l2i.
- Portal roots: `Group, Group`.

About 27 corpus scenes differ first on this (for example `_2021/some1_winners.py` `ProsConsOfContext`). Where it shows:
- `isinstance(self.mobjects[i], VMobject)`;
- VMobject style getters on the added group (`get_fill_color` and so on, absent on a `Group`);
- the group's record schema (`data.dtype.names`);
- `anim.mobject` / `anim.group` types in user code, such as `LaggedStartMap(...).mobject.set_color(...)`.

## Work

Match the Reference's rule for the group type (`VGroup` if all animated mobjects are VMobjects, else `Group`; an explicit `group=` or `group_type=` wins). Apply it for `AnimationGroup` and every subclass, keeping the portal's native group backing.

## Acceptance

- An installed-wheel regression: the probe above ends with `VGroup, VGroup` roots after the frame (once fm-6l2i lands); a mixed VMobject/Mobject group stays `Group`. Planted negative at 35c65d6e.
- The corpus differential's `VGroup/class` first-difference cluster drops accordingly.

title: W1: capabilities test external_cancellation_unblocks_a_full_stdin_pipe_and_reaps_the_child fails on a 128-thread Linux host — write_stdin returns Ok after cancel
description:
`cargo test -p fmn-platform --test capabilities` fails one test on a shared 128-thread Linux host:
`std_runner::external_cancellation_unblocks_a_full_stdin_pipe_and_reaps_the_child`, at
crates/fmn-platform/tests/capabilities.rs:1415, `assert!(write.is_err(), "the killed child's pipe
must close")`. 33 passed, 1 failed. It fails the same way at 5d960e65 and at 9d21d248, rerun alone at
load ~1 (found while running the workspace gate for fm-a87y, which does not touch fmn-platform), so
it is deterministic on that host and predates both.

The test starts `sleep 30` with ProcessStdinLimits(8 MiB, 8 MiB), writes 8 MiB to its stdin from a
worker thread, cancels after 50 ms, and requires the write to fail. On this host `write_stdin`
returns Ok after cancellation. Find out why: pipe capacity (fs.pipe-max-size, F_SETPIPE_SZ), whether
the runner buffers the write and reports success before the child consumed it, or a race in when
cancellation closes the pipe. Then fix the product or the test's premise with evidence. Do not
weaken the assertion that a cancelled child's stdin write is not reported as delivered.

Acceptance: the test passes on that Linux host and on macOS, and a cancellation that leaves the
pipe open still fails it.
close_reason: Root cause: exact-image stdin is a Unix socket pair; with no reader it accepts the host's default socket buffer (macOS 8 KiB; a Linux host with net.core.wmem_default=16 MiB accepted 16,420,544 bytes), so the test's single 8 MiB write completed before cancellation. Product correct and unchanged; the test premise was wrong. Fix (ba6d51e1, 3ce1789e): stream 1 MiB chunks until a write blocks, cancel only after 500 ms without progress, require the blocked write to fail on the closed pipe ('stdin write failed', not the cancelled-before-write check), termination Cancelled, reap < 3 s, 10 s receive bound. Positive: capabilities 34/34 on that Linux host and on macOS. Planted negative at 3ce1789e: supervisor ignores cancellation -> red (TimedOut != Cancelled after 10.01 s), plant removed. Gate: workspace cargo test --no-fail-fast at 3ce1789e (clean tree, ffmpeg 8.0.1 on PATH, private target dir, 32 jobs/threads) on a shared 128-thread Linux host: exit 0, 271 test binaries, 3955 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored. cargo fmt --check exit 0; clippy -D warnings clean (fmn-tex, fmn-conformance, workspace at a362dcec; fmn-platform, fmn-python at final); ubs 0 critical on changed files.

comments.author: SwiftForge
comments.text:
SwiftForge review, 2026-10-10, of ba6d51e1, 3ce1789e and the 598665c1 reviewer fix (external_cancellation_unblocks_a_full_stdin_pipe_and_reaps_the_child).

What holds:
- The test is correct on macOS and Linux by construction. write_all blocks once the kernel buffer is full: 8 KiB on macOS; on the shared Linux host it accepted 15 MiB (15728640 bytes) before blocking. Cancellation kills the tree. The blocked write then fails with EPIPE, and the termination is asserted to be Cancelled.
- No wait in the test thread is unbounded: the fill deadline, then two 10 s receive timeouts. A test that fails early leaves the writer thread blocked only until the child exits.
- MAX_TOTAL (1 GiB) is 64x the largest buffer seen. A host that exceeded it would fail loudly as an early StdinTotalLimit return. It can never pass.
- The 3 s promptness bound and the 10 s receive bounds are not a flake source: the supervisor polls every 5 ms.

Defect, fixed in 2e34980f (content-identical 04c97b60 also on main via the peer merge ffdf3eb9): the child ran under spec's 10 s supervisor timeout, which preempted the test's 20 s fill deadline. A fill plus stall over 10 s ended with the supervisor killing the child, and the test failed as "the writer returned before cancellation". The child now has a 60 s timeout.
- Positive: capabilities 34/34 (Linux).
- Planted negative, STALL raised to 11 s: the old test fails at 10.01 s ("... after 15728640 bytes: ... Broken pipe"); the new one passes in 11.02 s.

Not fixed: the stall heuristic (500 ms without progress) would misfire only if the writer were descheduled for 500 ms between chunks. Not observed.

Not claimed: no macOS-native run of this change. Local macOS cargo was refused by the remote-only build policy, so the evidence is from Linux.

title: W4: The segment-purity classifier — automatic, conservative, journaled
description:
Implement segment purity (§9.5, D-19, R20): Choreo classifies EVERY play()/wait() segment automatically by its effect signature (vocabulary shared with §13.4's effect model). A segment is PURE when each of its frames is a function of the begin-state CoW snapshot and its alpha alone: no dt-updaters, no always_redraw/f_always closures, no stateful tracers (TracedPath, TracingTail, AnimatedBoundary), no scene updaters, no callbacks with unclassified effects. Pure segments render embarrassingly parallel across frames: worker k reconstructs frame state from snapshot + alpha(k) + the KEYED per-frame RNG fork (§6.5 — state derived from (substream, frame index), never sequential pulls), rasterizes, and hands the frame to the ordered emitter, which sequences by frame index regardless of completion order. Stateful segments serialize their front-end and lean on the §17.4 pipeline instead.

THE CONSERVATIVE RULE (R20, load-bearing): misclassification would be a CORRECTNESS bug, so any unrecognized effect demotes the segment to stateful. The classifier's effect vocabulary is a closed allowlist of provably-pure constructs; everything else — unknown updater shapes, Python callbacks without a purity declaration, custom animation classes overriding interpolate with side effects — demotes. Classifications are RECORDED per segment in the replay journal, so a misclassification found later is diagnosable and its effect class is demoted engine-wide until root-caused (R20's kill rule).

On an 8-core laptop this collapses to ordinary behavior; on a 96-core workstation it is near-linear — the single biggest CPU lever in the plan (§17's scaling hierarchy).

Acceptance: classification unit tests across the effect matrix (each impure construct demotes; each pure construct passes); an end-to-end equivalence test — a pure segment rendered serially vs frame-parallel at {1,4,16} workers produces BIT-IDENTICAL frames (this is PG-5's per-commit core); journal-recording tests; a demotion-path test proving unknown effects demote.
close_reason: Segment-purity classifier landed (§9.5, D-19, R20): closed effect vocabulary ImpureEffect {DtUpdater, SceneUpdater (subsumes always_redraw/f_always — they bind as updaters), UnclassifiedAnimation, StopCondition}; classify_play scans every animation's declared AnimationSignature (trait hook, default Unclassified → demote; MethodAnimation is the sole allowlist member) plus updater kinds across all rooted families AND animation-owned starting/target families (Stage::family_updater_kinds probe); classify_wait adds the stop-condition demote. THE CONSERVATIVE RULE enforced by construction: purity is only reachable when every effect check passes; unknown always demotes. Drivers now classify EVERY segment automatically and return SegmentReport (kind, purity+reasons, begin-state CoW snapshot iff pure∧unskipped, base_frame, n_frames, run_time) — the journal record fm-y7u persists and fm-3df dispatches on. reconstruct_pure_frame = the §9.5 worker body (restore → interpolate α(k) → freeze with derived keyed RNG): equivalence test proves serial vs out-of-order reconstruction at simulated {1,4,16} worker schedules is BIT-IDENTICAL (f32::to_bits fingerprints over all record fields + packet headers) — PG-5's front-end core; real thread dispatch is fm-3df's (Rc-holding snapshots aren't Send; render teams live in fmn-runtime). 10-test acceptance suite (effect matrix incl. target-only updaters + static-ValueTracker purity + demotion path + journal contents + refusal paths). 349 workspace tests; fmt/clippy -D/DAG green; ubs 1 accepted false positive (enum compare 'effect_signature != Pure' pattern-matched as crypto token compare).

title: W5/W8: 4K video path — threaded YUV conversion fused onto the render team + recycled RGBA16F rasters (1.65x at 4K, same bytes)
description:
## Why

Profiling the 4K Hoeffding explainer renders (`fmn::render`, Lumen retained route → NV12 → ffmpeg) on trj (perf, Threadripper PRO 5995WX) and on macOS (`sample`) ranked these as the top costs of a 4K frame:

| Rank | Location | Share | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fmn_frame::convert::linear_yuv::convert::<false, rgba16f_to_nv12>` (serial, on the output team) | 17.8% | `franken_manim_hoeffding_explainer/perf/trj_07_4k_hotspots.txt` |
| 2 | kernel page zeroing for a fresh, zeroed 66 MB RGBA16F raster per frame (`FrameBuffer::new` in `OwnedVectorFrame::render_cached`) plus the memmove page faults in `PixelTileCache::restore_reused_tiles` | ~12% + 3.7% | same file; macOS `kernel_init_pages`/`__bzero` in `perf/mac/sample_07_4k.txt` |

The output team that ran conversion has at most two SMT siblings (`build_output_team`, `fmn-runtime/src/plan.rs`), and on macOS it falls back to one E-core.

## What changed (byte-identical output)

1. `fmn-frame`: `rgba16f_to_nv12_threaded` / `rgba16f_to_p010_threaded` split the destination into disjoint row-pair bands (planes are contiguous `stride * rows` regions) across scoped threads. Every output code is a pure function of its 2x2 quad, so the bytes match the serial kernel at any thread count. A refused spawn converts its band on the caller. wasm32 and small frames stay serial with no allocation. The serial entry points are unchanged wrappers.
2. `fmn-render`: `OwnedVectorFrame::render_cached_into` renders into a caller-recycled surface. Every pixel is overwritten: reused tiles are restored, and every other tile writes its background unconditionally. `raster_layout()` exposes the required layout.
3. `fmn` (`rendering/pipeline.rs`):
   - `NativeFrameStages` keeps a bounded pool of spare RGBA16F rasters, at most one per render team.
   - Output conversion is fused onto the end of `rasterize`, using the render team's threads.
   - `convert` is a pass-through.

## Evidence

- **Tests.** New `threaded_yuv_conversion_is_byte_identical_at_every_thread_count` (fmn-frame), covering NV12 and P010, both sitings, padded strides, and thread counts 0–64. All `fmn-frame` tests pass. These `fmn` tests pass: lib, native_cpu/bundle/camera/vector pipeline, native_pipeline, native_render, native_video, native_publication, native_bundle_export, native_camera_export, public_api. Clippy is clean with `-D warnings`.
- **Benchmark.** On trj: the Hoeffding explainer, chapter 07_shuffle, 3840x2160 at 60 fps, 600 frames, `--threads 16`, h264_nvenc. Mean of 2 alternating runs:

| Variant | Time |
|---|---|
| HEAD | 22.01 s |
| + threaded conversion (output team) | 19.69 s (−10.5%) |
| + raster recycling | 13.50 s (−38.7%) |
| + conversion fused onto the render team | **13.33 s (−39.4%, 1.65x)** |

- **Identity.** The full 01_hook chapter, rendered at 720p through deterministic libx264, has the same decoded `framemd5` for HEAD and every variant (f65e9d46…).

On macOS the fused conversion matters more: there it moves from one E-core to the render team.

title: W10: Tex(*strings) nests one container per string (Reference: flat glyph family; tex[1] is the glyph)
description:
## Found by the Appendix-A class sweep (fm-5wq.26), 2026-09-27

For `Tex('a', '+', 'b')` (several strings), the pinned Reference's family is flat: `Tex` → three glyph submobjects, and parts are reached through `select_part` / `get_part_by_tex`. The portal nests each string in a point-less container: `Tex` → three `VMobject` groups, each holding its glyph(s).

Measured family (path, class, points):
- Reference: `0 Tex 0`, `0.0 glyph 99`, `0.1 glyph 49`, `0.2 glyph 81`;
- portal: `0 Tex 0`, `0.0 VMobject 0`, `0.0.0 VMobject 73`, `0.1 VMobject 0`, `0.1.0 …`, `0.2 VMobject 0`, `0.2.0 …`.

BN-05 promises that glyph order and count keep the Reference's structural conventions. Here:
- `tex[1]` is a point-less group in the portal and the `+` glyph in the Reference;
- `len(tex.get_family())` and indexing into glyphs differ;
- style getters on `tex[i]` differ.

The single-string case is flat in both engines.

## Work

Keep the Reference's flat glyph family for multi-string `Tex`/`TexText`. Keep part lookup (`select_part`, `get_part_by_tex`, `tex_strings`) through the part spans, not through container submobjects. Check `OldTex` too: bridge.py locks its part splitting, where the Reference's `OldTex` does group parts (`len(OldTex('a','+','b')) == 3` with each part a group), so the two classes differ on purpose there.

## Acceptance

- The class sweep shows `Tex#2` equal apart from BN-05 glyph geometry. The open-bead row citing this bead is removed.
- An installed-wheel regression: `len(Tex('a','+','b')) == 3`, and each item is a glyph with points. Planted negative at 35c65d6e.

Class sweep subject Tex#2 (Tex('a','+','b')) is equal-with-exclusions: Tex -> three glyph VMobjects with points (73/57/73), using only BN-05 geometry, fm-15k9 glyph-class and ru72 extent rows. string_lifecycle.py (42 tests, including ModernTexFamilies, whose regressions failed at 35c65d6e) passes. AUDIT ADDENDUM — testing & logging doctrine (binding on every bead in this epic):

Every task bead in this epic lands with its tests as PART OF ITS SCOPE — a bead without its tests is not done:
1. COMPREHENSIVE UNIT TESTS, colocated in-crate, covering the bead's stated acceptance criteria INCLUDING negative and edge cases (degenerate inputs, resource-budget violations, version-mismatch refusals, error-path assertions — not just happy paths).
2. E2E REGISTRATION: any bead landing user-visible behavior (a mobject, an animation, a CLI flag, an output format, a Studio surface) registers at least one scripted end-to-end scenario with the Gauntlet e2e harness (fm-fjq) — driven through the real surfaces (CLI / Rust API / fmn-python / Studio HTTP), asserting outputs (bit-locked hashes on certified paths; structural assertions elsewhere), exit codes, and emitted-file inventory.
3. DETAILED STRUCTURED LOGGING: behavior flows through the owned tracing layer (§17.1/§18 — scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selection, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers). Where correct behavior is invisible in the output ("the preflight ran before frame 0", "wait() frames hit the tile cache"), the e2e scenario ASSERTS ON THE LOGS. On failure, the harness auto-bundles a deterministic repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail).
4. GATES BEFORE CLOSE: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test) + ubs clean on changed files, per AGENTS.md. Determinism-relevant beads additionally run their {1,4,16}-thread sweep before close.

title: W2: Bound and validate arc component counts before allocation
description: Source audit: bezier::quadratic_points_for_arc computes 2 * n_components + 1 and divides the angle by n_components without validating either operation. An explicit zero count therefore yields a one-point pseudo-arc, while an extreme count can overflow point-count arithmetic before allocation. The default arc_n_components path also maps non-finite angles into invalid or unbounded counts. These flows are public through QuadPath::arc, QuadPath::add_arc_to, Arc::n_components, and ArcBetweenPoints::n_components. Acceptance: introduce one checked, explicitly budgeted arc-component contract used by every arc path; reject zero, non-finite angles, point-count overflow, and counts above the declared budget with typed errors before allocation; propagate those errors through the public Chisel and library construction surfaces without compatibility shims; preserve BN-09 output for ordinary finite inputs; add direct coverage for zero, usize::MAX, NaN, infinity, and the budget boundary; pass mandatory repository gates.

title: W5: The fast CPU engine — mixed precision + SIMD build tiers (std::simd, safe target_feature)
description:
Implement the fast CPU engine (§6.1, §17.3, D-15): the standard-mode default — mixed precision with FMA permitted, screen-space f32 under the explicit subpixel error budget (≈1/256 px initial target; exceed it and the compiler subdivides or routes to the high-precision fallback), SIMD build tiers, all held to the versioned visual-equivalence budget against certified reference frames (§10.1, §16.3) — never semantically divergent, never a separate renderer.

SIMD as a designed system (§17.3): std::simd on the pinned nightly with SAFE #[target_feature] (target-feature-1.1: annotated safe functions are safely callable when the feature is statically enabled) — every kernel stays inside #![forbid(unsafe_code)]; dispatch is by BUILD TIER (portable / x86-64-v3 / x86-64-v4 / aarch64+NEON), never per-call runtime detection; SUITE.lock's certified target-feature sets govern the tiers; per-tier artifacts ship at W11. The hot list in ROI order: point-transform passes, field lerp, scanline quadratic-root evaluation, stroke-SDF slabs, color transfer functions, PNG filter/unfilter (W8's, but the kernel idioms are established here), WAV mixing, and fmn-dmath itself (§6.6).

Ordering discipline: scalar-complete FIRST (the ordering, not the destination) — instrument (§17.1) → eliminate work (§10.8, already landed) → pipeline (§17.4) → vectorize (THIS bead) → offload. Hand-vectorizing the full-work renderer first would optimize work that should not exist.

Acceptance: engine-equivalence suite green (fast vs certified within the visual budget on the corpus); per-tier build CI (compile + test each tier; full matrix weekly per R22); measured speedups per hot-list kernel recorded via §17.1; lane-count-independence verified where kernels are shared with the certified engine.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
G0-6 (fm-zn9) + G0-8 (fm-ekx) findings you must act on, 2026-07-25.

TWO SEPARATE ANSWERS ABOUT f32, AND THEY POINT DIFFERENT WAYS.

1. f32 IS PORTABLE. G0-6 hashed the f32 render of its determinism frame alongside the f64 one, on linux-x86_64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu) and macos-aarch64 (Darwin, M4 Pro). Both digests are byte-identical on all three. So mixed precision does not cost you cross-platform reproducibility — that was the cheaper of the two questions.

2. f32 IS NOT FREE, AND THIS IS THE ONE THAT BINDS YOU. G0-8 measured f32 against f64 on the SAME machine, same algorithm, only the scalar width changing: max 8-bit channel error 152, 200 of 2,073,600 components differing, ssim 0.999949. That sounds tiny until you look at WHERE — the divergence is not scattered noise, it sits at two symmetric spots on one curve, the Lissajous's curvature extrema, where the general quadratic distance solve is ill-conditioned and f32 misses the true distance by enough to flip coverage from 1.0 to ~0.1 across a handful of pixels. On a mainstream curve, at an ordinary stroke width.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR §6.1's MIXED-PRECISION LICENCE: keep the stroke SDF's distance solve in f64, or reformulate it to be better conditioned and re-measure. Do not adopt f32 there on the strength of "the error is 0.01%".

THE TOOL IS ALREADY BUILT AND NEEDS NO GPU: spikes/g0-8-accelerator's cpu::Precision::AnnexF32 runs the identical algorithm in f32 on the CPU, and sdf::distance_to_quadratic_f32 is a literal f32 transcription of the f64 function. compare::diverge gives you the max/mean/rms/max_u8/differing-count/ssim table. So "does this f32 kernel change the picture" is a question a Linux CI runner can answer in seconds — use it before committing to a tier.

ALSO YOURS NOW (ADR-0010): the SIMD tiers are the standing risk to the certified result. G0-6 proved bit-identity for the SCALAR path; §10.5(c)'s lane-count-independent fixed-order reductions are what carry it into the tiers, and PG-5's per-commit {1,4,16} sweep tests THREAD counts, not LANE counts. Add a tier-vs-scalar bit-identity check when the first tier lands — nothing else in the program tests that axis.

Two more constraints ADR-0010 makes binding, both cheap to keep and expensive to notice you broke: no FMA contraction (verified in aarch64 object code — 1652 scalar FP ops, zero fmadd/fmla; determinism::fma_guard now refuses hand-written mul_add across the certified source roots), and IEEE-754 basic operations only.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed (crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs) and it hands you three things.

1. THE TIER HARNESS IS ALREADY WRITTEN AND ALREADY SWEEPING. fmn_render::engine::Tier has one variant (Scalar) and a Tier::ALL slice; fmn-conformance/tests/certified_engine.rs::every_tier_reproduces_the_scalar_definition renders the whole three-frame corpus once per entry in Tier::ALL and requires byte equality with the scalar definition. Today that compares scalar with itself, and the test says so in as many words rather than implying coverage it does not have. Your first tier becomes real coverage the moment you (a) add the variant to Tier::ALL and (b) make FrameJob dispatch on identity.tier. The harness needs no other change — render() in that file already threads the tier through FrameJob::with_identity.

2. ADR-0013 SETTLED THE ORDER QUESTION AND LEFT YOU EXACTLY ONE HALF OF IT. Accumulation order across draws is painter order, and within a shape it is the outline's own segment order; neither is a property of the sync, and interning_order_does_not_move_a_pixel proves it by building one picture two ways with opposite creation order. What ADR-0013 explicitly does NOT settle is §10.5(c)'s LANE-COUNT INDEPENDENCE — a horizontal sum whose association varies with vector width breaks bit-identity from inside a single segment, where painter order cannot help. ADR-0010 named the SIMD tiers as the remaining risk and that is still exactly true.

3. THE ARITHMETIC IS FUNNELLED AND THE FUNNEL IS NOW ENFORCED. fmn-conformance/tests/certified_arithmetic.rs fails the build on any platform transcendental or hand-written mul_add anywhere outside fmn-dmath and fmn-python. It found sixteen live sites when it was written; closing them needed ADR-0014, which makes fmn-dmath the DAG root so every computing crate can reach it. Your f32 paths will trip the guard if they reach for f32::sin — fmn_dmath::f32api has the wrappers, and they round once through f64 deliberately.

One caution ADR-0010 gave you that the corpus now makes concrete: the f32 frame hashed identically on all three platforms, so f32 is PORTABLE — but G0-8 measured that f32 changes the PICTURE at curvature extrema. §6.1's mixed-precision licence is bounded by correctness, not by portability.
