title: W5: Analytic fill — nonzero-winding coverage evaluated on the curves
description:
Implement the fill rasterizer (§10.2): tiled scanline nonzero-winding coverage evaluated ANALYTICALLY on the quadratics — segments y-monotonized by splitting at the vertical-tangent parameter (retained in the compiled path, W5IR); per scanline, exact segment intersections from the closed-form quadratic root; signed trapezoidal area accumulation per cell. No triangulation, no signed-alpha tricks, no orientation bookkeeping — the mathematics rasterized directly, which is the whole point of owning the renderer (Appendix B: the Reference's fill is a stack of GPU workarounds we decline to copy).

Perspective handled honestly: projected quadratics are RATIONAL in screen space, so 3D paths are evaluated in homogeneous coordinates or adaptively subdivided to a stated tolerance — never silently treated as affine.

Interior color for per-vertex fill_rgba gradients uses a DEFINED interpolation field: arc-length-parameterized boundary interpolation with mean-value coordinates in the interior — specified, tested, stable under subdivision (subdividing a path must not change its gradient). Winding-consistent self-intersection behavior (nonzero rule, matching the defined model); fill_border_width as a principled inner border stroke (GL_MAX composite hack retired).

Fast paths (§10.2's closing rule): the general machinery is the FALLBACK, not the toll road — primitive hints (W5IR) route lines/circles/rects/dots/glyphs to specialized kernels; interiors of fully-covered tiles fill as vectorized spans; the scanline evaluator computes exact coverage only where edges actually are.

Acceptance: coverage oracle tests vs analytically-known areas (circles, polygons, overlapping windings) at sub-1/256-px error; subdivision-invariance metamorphic tests (fill result invariant under curve subdivision — geometry AND gradient); self-intersection fixtures; homogeneous-path tests vs high-resolution subdivision reference; primitive-kernel vs general-path equivalence tests; look-study (G0-2) calibration constants applied.
design:
A WORKING §10.2 ALGORITHM ALREADY EXISTS: spikes/g0-8-accelerator/src/analytic_fill.rs (fm-orn / G0-8b), generic over f32 and f64 from one expression tree, with 20 tests including the analytic-area oracle, the pi-r-squared oracle, the winding hole, tile-carry invariance and tile-alignment sweeps. Inherit it rather than re-deriving it, and inherit its two rules (F15):

(1) WHERE AN EXACT VALUE IS KNOWN, USE IT. A column crossing's x IS the boundary; re-evaluating x(t) to recover it puts an ulp on the wrong side of an integer, which makes the walk's ceil(x)-1 step name the column it is already in. That defect deposited a three-column span as one trapezoid — and it was wrong in the f64 REFERENCE while f32 happened to be right, so the two-width comparison read like conditioning.

(2) A TILING TEST MUST SWEEP TILE ALIGNMENTS. The original test compared the scanline and per-pixel forms over one full-width window and saw nothing, because no piece ever entered at an edge.

STILL OWED BY THIS BEAD, none of them layout questions: §10.2's real interior colour field (arc-length boundary interpolation with mean-value coordinates — the spike's gradient is the same DEFINED STAND-IN crate::fill documents), fill_border_width as a principled inner border stroke, 3D/perspective (projected quadratics are rational in screen space), and fill primitive hints for rectangles/circles/dots (assessed straightforward — a hinted fill's coverage is a closed form with no walk and no accumulator).

The CPU engine should use the SCANLINE shape (serial prefix over a row, no occupancy to lose); the annex uses per-pixel.
close_reason:
DONE. §10.2's fill is landed in crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs (~1,050 lines + 51 inline tests), with all four STILL-OWED items and every acceptance criterion.

THE CORE, inherited from G0-8b/fm-orn and improved in three ways forced by tests:
(1) The per-cell deposit is the EXACT INTEGRAL. Every signed-area rasterizer in the wild — font-rs, stb_truetype, the spike — substitutes the chord midpoint for the dy-weighted mean of x, which is exact only where x is linear in y. On a curve it carries O(curvature*h^2) and announces itself as a subdivision-invariance failure: a de Casteljau split at t=1/2 on a 15px-radius circle of 8 quadratics moved coverage by 5.7e-3, one and a half 8-bit levels and past this bead's own sub-1/256 acceptance. Coeffs::mean_x_over_dy evaluates (int x dy)/(int dy) in closed form, written so the (t1-t0) factor cancels rather than as a difference of antiderivatives (spans shrinking toward a column boundary are the common case). Drift is now <1e-12 and the disc oracle is exact.
(2) SUBPATHS ARE CLOSED. A path's interior is only defined for a closed boundary; SVG's fill rule and the Reference's get_triangulation both close first. Left open the winding never returns to zero and every pixel to the right stays inside — the open triangle filled a rectangle running off the right edge, 48px against 96. Shape::subpath_starts records the boundaries compile_shape's null-curve drop was discarding; reconstructing them from anchor continuity is almost right and silently wrong for a glyph counter that starts where the outer ring closed.
(3) winding_at's sign is stated (leftward ray => upward crossing is -1). Getting it backwards passes every abs()-based coverage test and lies to the one caller that cares.

Also: per-shape derivation so instancing is a translation (one split per interned outline), scanline AND per-pixel dispatch shapes from one routine, f32 instantiation as the annex's arithmetic without the annex's hardware, and RowScratch::interior_row for §10.4's vectorized span at bit-exactly 1.0 (the precondition that makes occlusion pruning byte-identical, G0-8b F13).

STILL-OWED (1) — THE INTERIOR COLOUR FIELD. GradientField: the mean value interpolant of normalized arc length over GRADIENT_STATIONS=64 arc-length-uniform stations. It interpolates the PARAMETER, not the colour, so it is a function of geometry alone (keys on the geometry revision, survives a restyle) and for the two-endpoint ramp the two formulations are IDENTICAL — MVC are a partition of unity, so sum(l_i c(s_i)) = c(sum(l_i s_i)) exactly for affine c; a per-point ramp drops in as sum(l_i c_i) with no change. A test reconstructs the weights one-hot and checks both routes. Subdivision invariance dictated both halves: arc length not parameter (via the new fmn_geom::arclength::t_at_arc_fraction, curve_and_t_at's inner solve extracted so the renderer owns no second arc-length rule, D4), and stations not anchors. Stations sit at interval MIDPOINTS — a left-endpoint rule carries a 1/(2n) bias across the ramp's seam that every interior point inherits (a disc's centre read 0.49219 at 64 stations and 0.49805 at 256, the bias twice); with midpoints the centre is exactly 1/2 at every count, and beyond four station spacings from the seam 64 agrees with 256 to better than 1/1020. At the seam nothing converges because the DATA jumps; the test asserts boundedness and says so. Limit filed as fm-ap9: MVC are defined for one closed polygon, so multi-loop shapes (glyph counters, annuli) want the per-loop generalization — a design step, not a parameter.

STILL-OWED (2) — fill_border_width. Traced, not assumed: shader_wrapper.py:284-291 builds fill_border_program from the STROKE shaders, :315-316 binds fill_rgba to stroke_rgba and fill_border_width to stroke_width, :418-420 renders under GL_MAX. Max of equal colours cannot darken an interior, so the Reference border's ENTIRE observable effect is that the silhouette grows by w/2 — 0.675px at the Text/DecimalNumber default — compensating for the fill canvas's five coverage levels (G0-2 L3). An INNER band is a subset of the filled region, so it cannot change coverage at all; taken literally, 'inner border' is vacuous for coverage. ADR-0011 rules that 'inner' stands and the vacuousness IS the finding: the silhouette never moves (structural — nothing on the coverage path reads the field, which is also what keeps the interior class exactly 1), the dilation is retired under D-05, a flat fill is a provable no-op (what makes retiring it safe rather than silent), and the remaining job is colour — within the band the ramp is read crisp instead of via the smoothed field. Measured: away from the seam the field and the boundary agree to fp one pixel in and the border does nothing; at the seam the field reads 1/2 where the boundary reads 0, max disagreement exactly 0.500 at every inset from 0.5 to 4px. So the knob's whole job is: within the band, the gradient's seam is crisp instead of blurred. BN-06 written (the renderer's note, fill half; strokes are fm-oac's sibling file). §10.2 and Appendix B trued up in the same commit.

STILL-OWED (3) — PERSPECTIVE. RationalPiece: a projected quadratic is EXACTLY a rational quadratic, because projection is linear on homogeneous coordinates. split() is de Casteljau in homogeneous coordinates so the halves describe the same screen curve and the error halves instead of compounding. append_rational subdivides on an explicit stack (the depth cap is then a property of the data structure) and REPORTS pieces/error/depth/capped — a subdivision that gives up quietly reads like one that converged. A piece whose W is not of one sign is RationalError::CrossesHorizon, not a picture; weight_is_definite solves for W's roots rather than sampling, catching an interior dip (1,-2,1) AND an interior TANGENCY (1,-1,1 give W=(1-2t)^2, a point at infinity a sign test waves through). deviation_px went from 6 samples to 31: with endpoints and midpoint matched the difference behaves like t(t-1/2)(t-1), extremum at t=0.2175, where six samples read 2.9283 against a truth of 2.98493 — 1.9% low, and a tolerance the curve exceeds is not a stated tolerance. Validated against a 129-point point-to-segment reference (the first version of that reference was itself under-resolved by 0.3px and reported a false violation; densifying deviation_px did not move the number, which is what said the fault was on the other side).

STILL-OWED (4) — FILL PRIMITIVE HINTS. FillKernel::{Rect, Disc, RoundedRect} as exact closed forms, no walk and no accumulator. Rect is pixel-identical to the general path (both exact areas of the same region). A DISC IS NOT, and pretending otherwise would have been the interesting bug: a Circle's/Dot's outline is manim's quadratic approximation, enclosing (pi/n)^4/6 more area, so a true-disc kernel draws a different shape by up to r((cos u + sec u)/2 - 1) pixels of edge displacement. It is admitted the way §10.8 admits its one other approximating route ('nearly-linear quadratic -> line fast path under an explicit screen-space error bound') except the bound is MEASURED off the compiled outline: worst segment-midpoint radial deviation, scaled to pixels, declined above 1/256 px. At 135 px/unit that admits a default Dot (0.08 units, 0.002px) and declines a two-unit Circle (0.050px) — the shape of hint.rs's rule, not a compromise with it. Arc routes to General (filling it closes it with a chord, so the region is a circular segment the hint does not carry). Two numerical findings: asin is the WRONG function for the disc antiderivative (infinite derivative at +/-1 turned one ulp in v/r into 1.4e-7 of AREA at r=6, with pixels sitting a hair under r at every disc's extremes — atan2(v, sqrt(r^2-v^2)) is the same angle, well conditioned, one ulp), and a disc's coverage summed over a pixel grid TELESCOPES so the plain oracle reported 4e-12 and hid it completely; only the rounded rectangle's corner decomposition exposed it.

NEW SHARED PRIMITIVE: fmn_geom::distance (nearest_on_quadratic, solve_cubic_real, distance_to_quadratic). In Chisel under D4 because §10.3's strokes are DEFINED by distance to the curve — fm-oac consumes it rather than writing a second root-find. Trigonometric branch for three real roots with the acos argument clamped (rounding pushes it outside [-1,1] exactly when the discriminant is near zero, turning a triple root into NaN), Cardano otherwise, relative degeneracy fall-through, and a FIXED three Newton steps on the original coefficients (fixed because a loop that stops when converged stops at a different iteration on a different platform, §6.6). Brute-force validated over a corpus with a straight segment, a cusp, a near-straight and an out-of-plane curve.

ACCEPTANCE, all met: analytic-area oracles (rectangle/triangle exact to 1e-9; disc against its exact enclosed area by Green's theorem, which is the right oracle since pi*r^2 measures the circle's approximation rather than the rasterizer); overlapping windings (hole cancels to exactly 0, coincident windings clamp to 1); subdivision invariance of geometry AND gradient; self-intersection (pentagram core wound twice, therefore inside); homogeneous-path vs dense reference; hinted-vs-general equivalence; G0-2 constants applied (the 1.5px smoothstep profile, 135 px/unit, STROKE_WIDTH_CONVERSION, no fill supersampling per L3). Plus tile-alignment sweep over 9 tile sizes, scanline vs per-pixel agreement to 1e-12, instancing-by-translation, and the f32/f64 comparison.

GATES: 1,084 tests pass (129 in fmn-render, 72 in fmn-geom), cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings, crate-DAG check, ubs 0 critical. The bit-locked IR snapshot is unmoved — subpath_starts is not a snapshot field.

FILED ALONG THE WAY: fm-ap9 (multi-loop MVC), and a measured argument added to fm-7if (interning is bitwise and a BAKED translation is not bitwise exact, so N translated copies of one outline hash to N digests and compile N times — found as a test failure; the resolution is that bead's transform channel).

NOT DONE HERE, deliberately: the fill is not yet called by an engine, because there is no engine — fm-ig3 (certified CPU) and fm-gmr (adaptive AA) are its consumers and are unblocked by this. Everything this bead owns is landed, tested, and documented.

title: W9: Preserve Studio host cleanup when overload replies fail
description: At exact HEAD b5e2f4bbb1ab23ef3d2a76c5b55b3b6b72b18dcb, StudioHost::serve_until increments and immediately restores the active-client counter when max_clients is reached, then sends a best-effort 503 response with the ? operator. title: W10: Record calibration-mode PG-2/PG-5/PG-6/PG-7 observations on the dev EPYC and publish one honest table
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

As of 2026-09-23 the repository contains ZERO recorded FrankenManim timings for PG-2, PG-3, PG-4, PG-5 (timing side), PG-6 and PG-7 — not qualified, not calibration, nothing. Producers for every row exist (`fmn-perf measure-pg2/pg5/pg6/pg6-peak/pg6-soak/pg7/frontdoor`, `fmn-perf-pg8` example), and the rig already supports an explicit calibration mode that forces `bare_metal=false` so the result can never be mistaken for a gate verdict. The team has read "cannot qualify" as "must not record". That leaves the project unable to answer the most basic question in its README ("Performance" section): is it fast?

This leaf is deliberately independent of the qualification ADR: calibration numbers are informational, clearly labeled, and required to direct optimization work (plan §17.1: "hypothesis, then evidence"; order of operations instrument -> eliminate work -> pipeline -> vectorize -> offload).

## Work

On the bare-metal dev box (dual EPYC 7282, 2 NUMA nodes):

1. Build `--profile release-perf` with an explicit `FMN_BUILD_ID=git:<sha>` from a clean tree (depends on the profile-detection fix).
2. Pin to one socket and 8 physical cores (`numactl --cpunodebind=0 --membind=0`, `taskset` on 8 distinct physical cores, SMT siblings idle), record governor/turbo state, and run: PG-2 canonical rasterizer workloads (fill Mpx/s, stroke Mpx/s at 8 threads), PG-5 timing at {1,4,16} threads, PG-6 peak RSS on the largest available scene and a >=10 min soak, PG-7 (median corpus formula cold/cached; 10k-glyph text layout).
3. Commit raw sample bundles under a path that cannot be confused with qualified baselines (e.g. `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/artifacts/perf/calibration/<date>-<host>/`) using the rig's own bundle format, and publish ONE table in `docs/performance/PERFORMANCE_GATES.md` (target | calibration median + dispersion | host | commit | "calibration, not a gate verdict").
4. Do not touch PG-1/PG-3/PG-4 front-door producers owned by fm-inr.2.3 unless that claim is released; if released, add them here with the same labeling.

## Acceptance

- Raw bundles replay through `fmn-perf verify-baseline` (or the calibration-equivalent verifier) byte-for-byte from committed files; no hand-typed medians.
- The published table exists and states for every row whether it would pass/fail the target if it were qualified.
- At least one inconclusive or failing repetition, if observed, is retained rather than dropped.
- A short "what to optimize first" note (top 3 measured bottlenecks by stage-level phase trace, plan §17.1) is added to the table section.

## Guardrails

- Never label calibration results as qualified; never feed them into gate verdicts; never delete prior PG-8 bundles.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.

title: W10: Replace audit-gaming trivial bodies from 48c8405d (identity linear_sum_assignment, empty matching_blocks, ...) and make the audit catch them
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

Commit `48c8405d` (2026-09-20, "fmn-python: bind missing helper methods and modules, eliminating portal runtime contradictions (fm-5wq.4.143)") made the portal's placeholder audit pass by replacing schema placeholders with trivial bodies that return plausible-looking but wrong values. The audit (`scripts/audit_portal_runtime.py` / `parity_audit.py`) only detects the `_fmn_schema_placeholder` marker, so these now count as implemented. fm-5wq.4.143's acceptance explicitly required failing on "a substituted callable that returns plausible but wrong geometry"; it was closed on 2026-09-22 on "All 2023 Python tests ... 100% green" with its acceptance box unchecked. Its parent fm-5wq.4 closed too.

Verified at HEAD in `crates/fmn-python/python/manimlib_bootstrap.py`:

- `:22976` `linear_sum_assignment(cost_matrix, maximize=False)` fallback returns the IDENTITY assignment and ignores the cost matrix entirely; `:22967` `cdist(..., metric=...)` ignores `metric` (always Euclidean). Because the wheel depends only on `numpy==2.5.2`, the `except ImportError` fallback is the normal path. Both are exported as `manimlib.mobject.svg.string_mobject.{linear_sum_assignment,cdist}`. Plan D4 assigns assignment/distance to frankenscipy (`fsci-opt`, `fsci-spatial`), which the native engine already uses.
- `:19136` `TransformMatchingStrings.matching_blocks(...)` returns `[]`.
- `:19015` `TransformMatchingParts.add_transform(...)` is `pass`.
- `:11561-11565` `StreamLines.draw_lines` is `pass`; `get_sample_coords` returns an empty (0,3) array.
- `:7798` `StringMobject.get_svg_string` returns `""`; `StringMobject.parse`, `get_command_matches`, `build_groups` (~7775-7834) and `VMobjectFromSVGPath.handle_arc/handle_commands` (~7715) are trivial.
- `:23211` `manimlib.__main__.run_scenes` / `main` are `pass`.

title: W10: Build the symbol-to-witness registry that fm-5wq.4.143 required (closed on 2026-09-22 without it)
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

fm-5wq.4.143 ("Bind reviewed portal claims to real native and installed-wheel semantic witnesses") and its parent fm-5wq.4 were closed on 2026-09-22 without their acceptance: no symbol-to-witness registry exists, no clean installed-wheel runtime audit receipt newer than 2026-09-13 exists, and no negative-control mutations were demonstrated. The close reason cites only aggregate test counts ("All 2023 Python tests and 69 native fmn-python tests are 100% green"). The bead ID was additionally used as a label on ~29 unrelated commits (surface morphs, Riemann sums, undo/redo, typography).

What the evidence actually shows about the portal's semantic coverage:

- The Parity Ledger badge says 2483/2483 rows "reviewed (100.0%)" — that is adjudication coverage, not behavior.
- 1,492 manimlib ledger rows cite `bridge.py` as their witness file; 408 of 1,819 non-dunder SAME/IMPROVED rows (22%) cite a test file that does not even contain the symbol's name. Textual presence is at most ~78%; behavioral backing is unmeasured.
- The refusal inventory is flat: 104 sites (64 `NotImplementedError` + 40 `_refuse_unrouted`) vs 103 on 2026-09-09.
- The mandatory `scripts/check.sh` runs none of the ~34 installer test files that use hand-written doubles nor the ~75 installed-wheel suites; `scripts/check_portal_runtime.sh` is only syntax-checked (`bash -n`, check.sh:~91). The real gate is the embedded `cargo test -p fmn-python`.

## Work (re-carries fm-5wq.4.143's acceptance, unchanged in substance)

Create an executable symbol-to-witness registry over `API_SCHEMA.tsv`/`API_OVERLAY.tsv` and the existing e2e APIs: each SAME/IMPROVED symbol maps to exact callable test identities (not files) of four distinct kinds — import/signature, semantic invocation, rendered state (final AND intermediate, with analytic/structural expectations or self-goldens), and source-unedited corpus usage. Reuse existing class-specific tests; do not duplicate. Families required: constructors, MRO overrides, live NumPy views + resize generations, copy/deepcopy/pickle, animation lifecycle, geometry helpers, typography/span matching, images/3D/fields, events/interaction, output, failure behavior.

## Acceptance

- Build a wheel from the exact checkout; install into a clean CPython 3.13 + NumPy 2.5.2 venv; verify source/overlay/lock/wheel digests; run the registry and `scripts/check_portal_runtime.sh` for real (not `bash -n`).
- The run FAILS on: a missing witness, zero executed cases, a schema placeholder, a trivial-body substitution (see the stub-bodies bead), or a substituted callable returning plausible-but-wrong geometry. A negative-control mutation demonstrates each failure class.
- The receipt separates adjudication, import resolution, semantic invocation, rendered states and corpus coverage; no shared percentage conflates denominators.
- Wire the registry run into `scripts/check.sh` (or a documented owned-host lane invoked by it) so it cannot silently stop running.
- Bounded deterministic NDJSON logs and FMNA repro bundles through the existing e2e harness.

title: W10: Honor init_points/interpolate overrides on library-class subclasses; evaluate custom rate_func exactly
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

Plan §15.2 promises "subclassing every exported base with real MRO/override dispatch (a subclass overriding init_points/interpolate is called back by the engine)". Today that holds only for direct `Mobject` subclasses:

- `init_points` is invoked from `_engine_init` (`crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs` ~1957-1981) only on the direct-`Mobject` construction path. Library classes skip `Mobject.__init__` (see the `_install_live_state` comment ~489-491 and `Circle.__init__` ~4955 in `manimlib_bootstrap.py`), so `class MyCircle(Circle): def init_points(self): ...` is never called back.
- All seven subclass fixtures in `crates/fmn-python/tests/bridge.py` (~137-200) subclass `Mobject` directly; no test covers a library-class subclass. Real 3b1b scenes subclass library classes constantly (VGroup, Axes, NumberPlane, Arrow, ...).
- Override detection is per animation family (Transform, AnimationGroup, ShowPartial, DrawBorderThenFill, Rotating, ...), not universal.
- Custom `rate_func` callables are pre-sampled on a hard-coded 30 Hz grid and linearly interpolated (bootstrap ~14855-14862): inexact at any other fps (60 fps renders, `--fps 24`), with no Behavior Note.

## Work

1. Make construction of every exported library class honor the subclass hooks the Reference honors (`init_data`, `init_points`, `init_uniforms`, `init_colors`, `interpolate`, `pointwise_become_partial`, `get_*` overrides used by the engine) — route library construction through one shared hook protocol rather than per-class special cases.
2. Evaluate custom `rate_func` exactly at the native alpha for each sampled frame (Python callback per sample, batched per play where possible under the §15.2 binding-tax rules), or, if a sampled approximation is retained for performance, make it fps-aware and file a Behavior Note with the measured max error.
3. Tests: for at least Circle, Square, Line, Arrow, VGroup, Axes, NumberPlane, Text, Tex, DecimalNumber and Surface, a subclass overriding `init_points` (and one overriding `interpolate`) is called back during construction/rendering, verified by call counters AND by rendered geometry; negative control where the override is removed. Rate-func tests at 24/30/60 fps comparing sampled alphas to the analytic function.

## Acceptance

- New tests pass in the embedded `cargo test -p fmn-python` suite and in the installed-wheel suite built from the exact checkout.
- No Behavior Note is used to hide a missing callback; any retained approximation has a measured, documented bound.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Register at least one e2e scenario as data in crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs (fm-fjq doctrine) exercising the user-visible behavior end-to-end, with deterministic structured NDJSON logs and an auto-bundled FMNA repro on failure; run it in the fast tier (or FMN_E2E_FULL=1 if heavy).

title: W10: Sweep the 2020-2026 3b1b corpus through the portal and publish a scene-level ratchet (today: 8 seed scenes)
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The README's headline compatibility promise is "existing manim scenes run source-unedited". Its only measurement today is `VIDEO_CORPUS.lock`: 8 allowlisted scenes (BeamSplitter, Cubic, FlattenCone, GroverPreview, MaxProcess, QuadraticFormula, SquareOnASphere, WaveMachineDemo) plus 2 excluded. The harness (`crates/fmn-python/src/corpus.rs`) asserts that they import and match SELF-blessed structural baselines (`corpus_baselines.tsv`, `FMN_CORPUS_BLESS=1`); its render check is a single 32x18 final still that must be "non-uniform". Cubic and QuadraticFormula record duration 0.0. There is no Reference comparison, no Look Gallery review for any corpus scene, and no measurement at all of the thousands of other scenes in the pinned `3b1b/videos` tree (the 2022-2026 era is the natural target; pre-2020 is explicitly out-of-era).

Fresh observation (reality check): with the published v0.4.0 wheel, the seed scenes fail for a user out of the box with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'tqdm'` (the era shim imports it; the harness environment happens to have it). After `pip install tqdm`, five seed scenes rendered a final PNG; BeamSplitter looked genuinely good (upright TeX, 3D beams), while MaxProcess rendered all text upside down (the v0.4.0 orientation defect, fixed in source by fd6bea1d but never released).

The TeX ratchet (99.8% occurrence-weighted over 17,711 occurrences) shows what a real denominator looks like. Scenes need the same.

## Work

1. Build a sweep tool (Python, run against a wheel built from the exact checkout) that enumerates every `Scene` subclass in `scripts/videos_ref/_2020..._2026/**` (record the enumeration method), and for each runs, with a per-scene timeout and resource cap: `--construct-only`, then a final-frame `--format png` at low resolution.
2. Classify every outcome with a closed vocabulary: ok / named-refusal (capability or tier) / TeX-construct-unsupported (named) / missing-third-party-dependency (which) / missing-asset / Python exception in portal code (bug) / timeout / crash. A portal-code exception is a bug, never a "refusal".
3. Publish `docs/ratchet/scene_dashboard.md` + TSV (scene-weighted and module-weighted success, split by outcome class), regenerate deterministically, and add a ratchet test that fails when the ok count drops (like `coverage_ratchet.rs`). The corpus source is licensing-restricted: commit only scene identifiers and outcome codes, never scene source.
4. Decide and document the shim policy for common era dependencies (`tqdm`, `scipy`, `sympy`, `pydub`, ...): vendor a minimal shim inside the era-shim layer, declare them as documented extras, or classify as out-of-scope — per dependency, in `VIDEO_CORPUS.lock` [shims].
5. File one bead per top-5 failure cluster by count.

## Acceptance

- Dashboard + TSV committed; ratchet test green; top-5 failure clusters filed as beads with example scenes.
- The README's "Will my existing manim scenes run?" FAQ cites the measured number and its denominator.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.
- [ ] Per-scene sweep records are NDJSON (scene id, module, era, outcome class, exception type/message, wall time, peak RSS, wheel digest) so the dashboard is regenerated from logs, never hand-edited.

title: W10: ADR + staged plan to collapse the portal's monkeypatch-installer onion into one native dispatch protocol
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The plan's architecture is "one engine, two front doors" (§5, §15). The Python portal has grown a second implementation of manim's animation layer on top of the native one, assembled at import time by monkeypatching:

- manimlib semantics live in ~48.7k lines of Python (`manimlib_bootstrap.py` 23,705 lines, `_animation_semantics.py` 2,461, `fmn_python/` ~22k lines / 93 modules) — about twice the size of the entire Reference manimlib (~23.1k lines). The Rust side (`crates/fmn-python/src`, ~20.5k lines) provides `_BridgeMobject` (250 methods) and `_SceneCore` (39).
- About 55 animation kinds run natively (`build_native_animation`, `crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs` ~9245); each also has a Python twin used whenever an override is detected.
- `_requires_python_animation` is wrapped 16 times and `Scene.play` is replaced 9 times by installers (e.g. `_animation_semantics.py` ~613/2221/2460, `fmn_python/rotation.py` ~148, `indication.py` ~289). 55 installers run at import (`fmn_python/initialization.py` 16-72) plus 6 more from `playback.py`. The effective behavior of any method is defined by bootstrap + semantics + N installers applied in order; no single file tells you what runs.
- Timing math is duplicated across languages: `time_spanned_alpha`, `sub_alpha`, `timeline_position` exist in `fmn-anim/src/animation.rs`/`composition.rs` AND in the bootstrap (~19385) AND in an installer (~270-295).
- Dead code: bootstrap `Transform.interpolate_mobject` (~18092) is silently replaced; `crates/fmn-python/python/animation_semantics.py` (455 lines) is referenced by nothing.
- Root cause (per `scripts/enable_camera_readback.py:2-4`): agent tooling writes whole files and the bootstrap is too large to edit, so behavior is layered via installers.

This is a WRONG_APPROACH risk for G4a (every new scene exercises a different installer composition) and for PG-8 (binding tax: last measured 3.55x vs a 1.10x budget on 2026-07-30; the per-play Python layering has grown since).

## Work

1. ADR (docs/adr/): the target dispatch protocol — the native Choreo animation lifecycle is authoritative; Python is called only for the specific hooks a user subclass overrides (detected once per class via MRO inspection and cached, per §15.2's method-cache rule), never by swapping whole animations between two implementations. Define the migration order and the invariants tests must hold during migration.
2. Staged migration plan as child beads (one per animation family), each: delete the Python twin + its installer, route through the native protocol, keep/extend the behavioral witnesses, measure PG-8 before/after in calibration mode.
3. Split `manimlib_bootstrap.py` into reviewable modules (a packaging change only, no behavior change, proven by the witness registry) so edits no longer need scripts or installers.
4. Remove dead duplicates (`python/animation_semantics.py`, shadowed bootstrap methods) only with owner approval (AGENTS.md RULE 1).

## Acceptance

- ADR ratified by the owner (comment on this bead) before migration children start.
- Child beads created with dependencies; the first family migrated end-to-end with witnesses green and a PG-8 calibration delta recorded.
- A single generated "effective dispatch table" (symbol -> native | python-hook | refusal) is produced from code, committed, and checked for drift in `scripts/check.sh`.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.

title: W10: Honest PG-1 — derive the Reference side from raw samples (no hand-typed median) and measure on real-GL hardware
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

PG-1 (end-to-end vs the Python Reference: <=0.5x wall-clock at G2, <=0.35x at G4) is the README's headline speed claim and one of the two stated G2 blockers. No ratio can be computed from committed data today:

- Only the Reference side exists: `docs/performance/reference-baseline-2026-07-28.json` / BASELINE.md (Opening-class warm run with ffmpeg: 7.414 s outer / 2.265 s scene), captured 2026-07-28 on the shared EPYC dev box under **software GL (Mesa llvmpipe)**, where GL rendering is ~64.7% of Opening-class scene time. llvmpipe inflates the Reference and would make FrankenManim's ratio look better than on real GPU hardware.
- It uses the `fmn-reference-baseline/1` schema; PG-1 requires an `fmn-perf-pg1-reference/1` TSV, and no script produces one. The FrankenManim fixture is a different workload (native FMTL scene with Text + NumberPlane), so benchmark-definition digests cannot match.
- Evidence asymmetry: the PG-1 Reference receipt accepts a hand-typed `median_ns` with no raw samples (`crates/fmn-conformance/src/perf_frontdoor.rs` ~197-213, ~286-300), while the FrankenManim side must replay raw sample bundles.
- The fmn-side front-door producers (fm-inr.2.3, stale since 2026-08-17) also refuse on the pinned nightly until the profile-detection fix (fm-5wq.9) lands.

## Work (label agent:claim:external — needs the Mac M4 Pro)

1. One benchmark definition for both sides: the same scene semantics (an OpeningManimExample-class scene), resolution, fps, cache state, ffmpeg in/out, hardware identity. For FrankenManim, run it through the front door users run (fmn-python for the Python scene; state explicitly if a native FMTL twin is also measured).
2. A producer that derives the pg1-reference TSV from RAW Reference samples (>=9 valid repetitions, retained invalids), replacing hand-typed medians; the verifier must reject a Reference receipt without raw samples (negative control).
3. Measure on mac-mini-max (real GPU-backed GL for the Reference) and on the dev EPYC (llvmpipe, labeled "software GL; Reference-favourable to fmn"), in calibration mode unless the qualification ADR (fm-5wq.8) says otherwise; publish both ratios with dispersion.

## Acceptance

- Raw-sample bundles for both sides committed; ratio table published in PERFORMANCE_GATES.md with host, GL backend, commit; verifier negative control for hand-typed Reference medians.

title: W10: portal Mobject accepts arbitrary constructor kwargs as attributes (pre-2022 digest_config); the Reference raises TypeError
description:
## Found by the fm-5wq.14 corpus sweep (2026-09-24)

The portal's base `Mobject.__init__(self, *submobjects, **kwargs)` (manimlib_bootstrap.py, class Mobject) stores every keyword as an attribute (`setattr(self, key, value)`) and accepts positional submobjects. That is pre-2022 `digest_config` behavior. The pinned Reference's `Mobject.__init__` (scripts/manim_ref/manimlib/mobject/mobject.py:79) takes a fixed signature (color, opacity, shading, texture_paths, is_fixed_in_frame, depth_test, z_index) and raises TypeError for anything else.

Observed at 6dc11e95:
- `Mobject(shape=1)`, `Group(shape=1)`, `VGroup(shape=1)` and `VMobject(shape=1)` all construct and set `.shape = 1`. The Reference raises `TypeError: __init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'shape'`.
- Some native builders take the opposite line. `SGroup(shape=(8, 8))` raises NotImplementedError "SGroup() keyword(s) not yet routed to the native builder: shape", which reads as "coming later" for a keyword the Reference itself rejects. The sweep counts 11 `_2020/chess.py` scenes as capability_refusal for this reason; they are Reference-incompatible CONFIG-era scenes.

## Work
1. Give the portal Mobject the Reference constructor contract: the Reference's keywords and nothing else, with the Reference's TypeError. Every portal subclass that currently passes private configuration through `**kwargs` must pass it explicitly. Audit each `super().__init__(**kwargs)` chain; `init_colors` reads self.color/self.opacity.
2. `_refuse_unrouted` must separate "Reference accepts this keyword but routing has not landed" (NotImplementedError) from "the Reference rejects this keyword" (TypeError, Reference wording). The API schema has every constructor's parameters.
3. Decide positional `*submobjects` on bare Mobject (Reference: none; only Group takes them).

## Acceptance

title: W10: 44 corpus scenes time out at 180 s (17 are clt/dice_sims) - time them against the Reference, profile construction and bbox hot paths
description:
## Found by the fm-5wq.14 corpus sweep (2026-09-24)

44 corpus scenes time out at the sweep's 180 s budget. 17 of them are `_2023/clt/dice_sims.py` (DiceSimulation and subclasses: 3 slow, 10 speedier, then about 3,000 still-frame samples).

Measured on the release portal at 6dc11e95 (scratchpad dice_timing.py; N still-frame `run_one_sum` iterations, 320x180 PNG render, loaded 64-core host):
- N=100: 3.97 s; N=200: 8.26 s; N=400: 20.87 s.
- About 36 ms per iteration at the start, rising about 0.075 ms per accumulated brick. Extrapolated to 3,000 iterations, that is roughly 7.5 min.
- cProfile at N=150, where the profiler adds overhead:
  - DieFace construction (10 per iteration): about 2.8 ms each, 4.2 of 10.8 s;
  - get_bounding_box / compute_bounding_box: 30,146 calls, 3.5 s;
  - _family_preorder: 122,976 calls, 1.8 s;
  - svg_ingress.by_color: 17,315 calls, 1.5 s;
  - get_family: 32,900 calls, 1.3 s.

Part of the growth is inherent: the scene itself calls `all_bricks.set_fill(...)` over every brick each iteration, and the Reference does the same. No Reference timing exists yet, so this bead makes no claim that the portal is slower than the Reference. PG-1 needs that comparison, with both engines live in the same invocation.

## Work
1. Time DiceSimulation (and one other timed-out module, such as _2026/hairy_ball/spheres.py) under the pinned Reference with `-s`, on the same host and in the same session.
2. Profile the portal hot paths above: per-object construction of small VGroups (DieFace = Square + dot family), bounding-box recomputation, and repeated family walks. Look for caching or batching that keeps semantics (Chisel/Marionette invariants).
3. Report the Reference-vs-portal ratio honestly, whichever way it goes.

## Acceptance
- A same-session Reference/portal timing table for the timed-out modules.
- Any optimization lands with a before/after measured in the same invocation, and self-goldens unchanged.

2026-09-25, WildGoose. Where the dice time goes (release portal at a2bd8da5, cProfile and perf, construct-only):

- N=900 construct without skip: 186 s. Native Scene._wait takes 97.4 s of it: 900 one-frame waits, growing from about 1.2 ms each at N=100 to about 108 ms each. perf puts the top native symbol in the Stage::snapshot per-slot closure, surrounded by malloc/free. Every frame freezes a FramePacket (a full Stage snapshot).
- The Scene arena only grows. Stage::delete is the only way an entry dies ("Explicit destruction — the only way an entry dies"), and a Python proxy's Drop only unpins. Every die, tip and sum label a sample adds and then removes therefore stays live. The per-frame snapshot clones all of them, which makes frame cost O(everything ever shown).

(a) Reclaim unpinned entries that are no longer reachable from the Scene: not a root, no live parent, and not referenced as a target/saved_state/tracker or by a native updater closure.
(b) Let a sink that ignores segment frames (construct-only, or a still-PNG session that only needs the final capture) tell the frame loop not to freeze a packet per frame.

title: W6/W10: Tex keyword selection of generated ink (tex[R"\over"], tex[R"\sqrt"]) is empty; the Reference selects the bar/radical
description:
## Found by the fm-5wq.14 corpus sweep (543b999a, 2026-09-24)

Seven corpus scenes raise `IndexError: list index out of range` on a keyword selection of generated ink:
- `equation[R"\over"][0]`, `eq1[R"\over"][0]` (the fraction bar): `_2025/laplace/supplements.py` 684/734/870/881/931;
- `lines[1][R"\sqrt"][0]` (the radical sign): `_2024/puzzles/max_rand.py` 217.

In the pinned Reference, `StringMobject.select_parts` finds every occurrence of the substring in the TeX string. Its labelled-SVG render assigns the fraction rule or radical to the label covering that command, so `tex[R"\over"]` selects the bar and `tex[R"\sqrt"]` the radical.

The portal selects by native span identity with containment semantics: generated ink belongs to the complete construct's span (fmn-tex tests/preamble.rs pins this for macros: `occurrences(r"\half")` is empty, `occurrences(r"\half{x}")` is not). An infix `\over` or a `\sqrt{...}` keyword therefore contains no ink and selects an empty group.

## Work
Decide, in Scribe (fmn-tex span map plus the portal's select_parts), how a command keyword addresses the ink that the command itself draws, as distinct from its arguments' ink:
- the fraction rule for `\over`/`\frac`;
- the radical for `\sqrt`;
- delimiters for `\left`/`\right`;
- accents for `\hat`/`\bar`.

A likely shape is a secondary "construct keyword" span per rule/path/delimiter glyph, which selection consults for keyword needles. Record the decision (ADR if it changes the span contract) and keep macro-call containment unchanged.

## Acceptance
- `Tex(R"a \over b")[R"\over"]` selects exactly the fraction rule.
- `Tex(R"\sqrt{x}")[R"\sqrt"]` selects exactly the radical sign.
- `Tex(R"\frac{a}{b}")[R"\frac"]` selects the bar.
- Argument glyphs are never selected by the keyword.
- fmn-tex's macro containment tests stay green.
- A re-sweep moves the seven scenes off this IndexError.
close_reason: All six acceptance lines met at b03e746c (self-verified; evidence in comment)

title: W10: fmn-python fails every scene when the project directory contains its own virtualenv (SceneSource re-executes installed packages)
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check

`fmn-python scene.py Scene` fails on **every** scene when the scene's directory contains the Python environment that runs it. That is uv's default layout: `uv venv` creates `.venv` in the project root, and the user installs `franken-manim` there. It is also common with `python -m venv .venv`.

Reproduction at `c03206ca` (release wheel from this tree, CPython 3.13.1, NumPy 2.5.2):
```
proj=$(mktemp -d); cd "$proj"; uv venv .venv
VIRTUAL_ENV=$proj/.venv uv pip install franken_manim-*.whl numpy==2.5.2
printf 'from manimlib import *\nclass Minimal(Scene):\n    def construct(self):\n        self.add(Square())\n' > scene.py
.venv/bin/fmn-python scene.py Minimal --format png --video_dir out.png
# fmn-python: scene/scene-load-failed: ImportError: cannot load module more than once per process   (exit 5)
```
The same interpreter renders the same scene from a directory without a venv (exit 0). The scratch receipt is the 2026-09-27 reality-check script `uv_project_repro.sh`.

## Cause

`fmn_python/scene_loading.py`'s `SceneSource` treats every module whose file lies under the scene's root directory as project source. It routes those imports through `_FreshSource`/`_FreshNamespace`, which re-execute the module (`exec_module`). NumPy lives at `<root>/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/numpy`, so when scene code (or manimlib, lazily) imports a NumPy submodule, NumPy's C extension `_multiarray_umath` is loaded a second time. CPython and PyO3 then refuse with "cannot load module more than once per process". The traceback runs `numpy/__init__.py` → `numpy/__config__.py` → `numpy/_core/multiarray.py`, each frame going through `scene_loading.py:106 exec_module`.

## Work

1. Project ownership must exclude installed packages. Paths inside any installation root are never project source:
   - `sysconfig.get_paths()` stdlib/platstdlib/purelib/platlib;
   - `site.getsitepackages()` and `site.getusersitepackages()`;
   - `sys.prefix`, `sys.base_prefix` and `sys.exec_prefix` trees when they lie under the root.
   Also exclude any path with a `site-packages` or `dist-packages` component. Compare `realpath`s (venvs use symlinks). `fmn_python/effect_audit.py` already computes these roots (`_library_roots`); share one helper rather than a second copy.
2. The same exclusion applies to namespace-package ownership (`_owns_namespace`, `_local_namespace`) and to the Studio/autoreload `source_inputs` path (`source_autoreload.py`, `source_reload.py`, `project_watch.py`), so a watched project with a venv never reloads installed packages.
3. Local helper modules under the project root, outside those roots, stay fresh exactly as today. That covers autoreload, Studio rebuild and `SceneSource.sources`.

## Acceptance

- The installed-wheel gate (`scripts/check_portal_runtime.sh`) gains a case in an existing suite (`scene_execution.py` or `runtime_provenance.py`) that:
  - creates a real virtualenv inside a temporary project directory with the portal and NumPy installed;
  - runs that venv's `fmn-python` on a scene in the project root, which must exit 0 and write a decodable PNG;
  - imports a local helper module, and a second run after editing the helper shows the edit.
- Negative control: with the fix reverted, the case fails with the ImportError above.
- The Studio source-reload path is covered by the same layout: `fmn-python studio` or the autoreload suite with a venv inside the project.
- Deterministic structured logs: the case records the venv path, the interpreter, the exit code and the SceneSource ownership decision for the NumPy path.
- The v0.5.0 release acceptance (fm-7wm.9) includes this layout.

The fm-fjq in-process harness cannot model an installed virtualenv inside a project, so the gate case in the acceptance is the e2e for this bead. Its log fields must be deterministic: venv path class (in-project or outside), interpreter, exit code, and the SceneSource ownership decision for the NumPy module path.

title: W10: Structural parity sweep — every constructible Appendix-A class vs the pinned Reference (points, family types, bbox, methods)
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check

Plan §16.3 promises "structural fixtures against the Reference where formulas intentionally coincide (constructor point arrays, family shapes, positional results — loose f32 tolerances)". Per-class fixtures exist for some families. There is no systematic sweep, and comparing portal and Reference constructor output directly kept finding real divergences this week:
- stock `Cone()` spanned z ∈ [0, 2]; the pinned Reference measures [−0.5, 1.5]. Atlas scaled about the origin where manim's `scale`/`stretch` act about the bounding-box center. A unit test and the solids.rs doc called [0, height] "like the Reference". Fixed in 0a5539ed, and the bridge.py assertion encoding the old placement was corrected in 91804f06.
- `VCube`/`VGroup3D` faces are plain `VMobject`s in the portal; the Reference's are `Polygon`s, so `get_vertices()` is missing. Two corpus scenes that the Reference renders fail on it (_2024/puzzles/supplements.py `DimensionsPointingToEachOther`, `SingleHypercube`). Tracked separately.
- NumPy views taken before `Scene.add` went stale (Mobject, VMobject, ValueTracker); the Reference keeps the same array. Fixed in 5edfaa91/c03206ca.

## Work

1. A harness runs each constructible class from Appendix A, for the 161 library classes plus Group/VGroup/VMobject. It covers the default constructor and two parameterized calls per class (taken from the Reference docstrings or corpus usage), in the pinned Reference (the `scripts/manim_ref` venv, xvfb) and in the installed portal.
2. For each construction it records canonical structural facts in one TSV per engine:
   - class name and MRO names of the root and each family member (depth-first);
   - `get_num_points()` per member;
   - points to 1e-4;
   - bounding box and center;
   - public method names present on the instance (dir, filtered);
   - `data.dtype` field names.
3. Diff with explicit tolerances: f32 to 1e-4 absolute and relative for points; exact for counts, types and method sets.
4. Each divergence is triaged into exactly one of:
   - fixed, with a regression test in the owning suite;
   - Behavior-Noted: a deliberate divergence, with the BN number cited in the registry;
   - tiered or excluded: cited to its ledger row or ADR.
5. The diff runs in the installed-wheel gate and fails on any untriaged divergence, which is a new line in the diff that is absent from the triage registry.

## Acceptance

- The registry covers every constructible Appendix-A library class. Unconstructible ones are named with the reason: drawings SVG shelf (ADR-0020), missing asset.
- Zero untriaged divergences at close; every "fixed" row cites its commit and test.
- Planted negative: re-introducing the old Cone placement (origin-relative scale) makes the gate fail on Cone's bbox row.
- The e2e scenario is registered (parity class) with deterministic NDJSON logs: class, parameter set, fact, portal value, Reference value, triage.
- The harness is bounded: per-construction timeout, and the whole sweep under 15 minutes on the dev host.
close_reason:
Acceptance met at 237544a8. Author-verified (solo, re-executed after the last change; no independent verifier).
- Registry: class_sweep.json covers every public mobject class of Appendix A, 153 classes (private helpers excluded). Classes unconstructible without arguments are recorded with the error both engines raise. The drawings shelf is cited to ADR-0020; empty-text refusals are BN-05.
- Zero untriaged divergences: the gate check at 35c65d6e has 284 constructions compared, 162 equal, 122 equal only through cited rows, 0 failing, 0 stale. BN rows: BN-05, BN-07 (C-15, C-19), BN-08, BN-09, BN-13. ADR row: ADR-0020. Open-bead rows for the bugs filed from this sweep: fm-16u6, fm-78b6, fm-15k9, fm-c1up, fm-ui0c, fm-8pj7, fm-ym2i, fm-fc53, fm-4qmn. No Reference public method is missing from the portal on any class.

- e2e parity.class_sweep.v1 (ParityDrill) passes with 284 compared and an NDJSON log span. check_portal_runtime.sh runs the sweep check.

title: W10: VCube/VGroup3D faces are plain VMobjects (Reference: Square/Polygon with get_vertices); 2 corpus scenes fail
description:

title: W10: make_number_changeable + copy() loses the DecimalNumber child (set_value missing); corpus RationalNumbers fails
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check (corpus vs Reference)

`_2023/gauss_int/herschel.py` `RationalNumbers` renders in the pinned Reference (`-s -w`, exit 0, 14.2 s). In the portal it fails with `AttributeError: 'VMobject' object has no attribute 'set_value'`:
```python
frac_template = Tex(R"1 \over 2")
frac_template.make_number_changeable("1")
frac_template.make_number_changeable("2")
...
frac = frac_template.copy()
frac[0].set_value(k)      # Reference: frac[0] is the DecimalNumber that make_number_changeable installed
```

In the Reference, `StringMobject.make_number_changeable` replaces the matched glyph group with a `DecimalNumber` in the family, and `copy()` preserves that child's class. title: W10: Surface.get_shader_data() does not return the Reference's per-triangle vertex stream; corpus SimplicityToGenerality fails
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check (corpus vs Reference)

`_2024/holograms/supplements.py` `SimplicityToGenerality` renders in the pinned Reference (`-s -w`, exit 0, 17.6 s). In the portal it fails with `ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous`. The scene triangulates a surface through its shader data:
```python
surface = Torus(resolution=(49, 49)); surface.set_width(4)
verts = surface.get_shader_data()['point']
triangles = VGroup(Polygon(*tri) for tri in zip(verts[0::3], verts[1::3], verts[2::3]))
```
In the Reference, `Surface.get_shader_data()` returns the record array indexed by `get_shader_vert_indices()`, which is the triangle indices. So `['point']` is a flat stream of three vertices per triangle. The portal's `get_shader_data` returns something else, so `Polygon(*tri)` receives the wrong shape. The error appears downstream.

## Acceptance

- `Surface.get_shader_data()` (and the VMobject variant, if exported) returns records in the Reference's order and count: for a Surface, `len == len(triangle_indices)` and `data['point'][k] == get_points()[triangle_indices[k]]`. This is checked in the installed-wheel surface suite against an independent computation. Negative control: the current implementation fails it.
- The corpus scene renders in the portal (exit 0, decodable PNG).

title: W10: Non-finite DecimalNumber values and points are refused where the Reference renders (AverageDiceValues, Pulse)
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check (corpus vs Reference)

Two scenes render in the pinned Reference but are refused by the portal's finiteness checks:
- `_2023/clt/wordy_scenes.py` `AverageDiceValues` (Reference exit 0, 31.4 s). Portal: `ValueError: DecimalNumber requires a finite value in both real and imaginary components`. In the Reference, `DecimalNumber(inf)` or `(nan)` formats through Python's number formatting, so its text reads `inf`/`nan`.
- `_2023/optics_puzzles/adding_waves.py` `Pulse` (Reference exit 0, 4.5 s). Portal: `ValueError: points must be finite`. The Reference accepts non-finite points in a VMobject. The GL pipeline draws nothing for them, and the scene's final frame is valid.

## Work (decide, then implement)

1. DecimalNumber: render non-finite values as the Reference's formatted text (`inf`, `-inf`, `nan`, with the configured sign and unit handling), through the native glyph path. Record this in the Behavior Notes only if the formatting differs.
2. Non-finite points: pick one policy and write it into the BN-07/BN-12 family, then apply it consistently to set_points, the animation interpolation and the renderer's IR ingestion:
   - (a) accept non-finite points in standard mode, where degenerate curves draw nothing, as in the Reference, and refuse them only in certified mode, where the closure must be well-defined;
   - (b) keep refusing, as a Behavior Note with migration guidance.
   The corpus evidence favors (a).

## Acceptance

- Both scenes render in the portal (exit 0), or the chosen refusal is Behavior-Noted with the scene cited.
- Tests: `DecimalNumber(float('inf'))` produces the text `inf`, and a VMobject with one NaN anchor renders without raising in standard mode (pixels equal to the same shape minus that curve). The certified-mode behavior is asserted explicitly.

title: W10: Eight corpus scenes the Reference renders in 6-274 s exceed 180 s in the portal — measure same-invocation and fix
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check (corpus vs Reference)

Eight corpus scenes exceed the portal sweep's 180 s budget but render in the pinned Reference (`-s -w`, 320×180, same workdir and config):

| scene | Reference |
|---|---|
| _2023/clt_proof/main.py DirectMGFInterpretation | 6.2 s |
| _2024/puzzles/added_dimension.py ShowRhombicDodecTesselation | 7.4 s |
| _2024/puzzles/added_dimension.py SphereStrips | 12.2 s |
| _2022/borwein/main.py ReplaceXWithPiX | 20.6 s |
| _2024/puzzles/added_dimension.py RandomVectorStatistics | 21.9 s |
| _2023/numberphile/prime_race.py PrimeRace | 33.3 s |
| _2025/laplace/derivatives.py MoveAroundPolesSeeDynamics | 207.5 s |
| _2023/clt/dice_sims.py SimulationWithExpDistribution5Dice | 274.1 s |

The portal sweep (`15c65f1c`, 09-26) ran on a loaded 64-core host (load average 50–90), and the Reference reruns ran on the same host at a different time. So the ratios are indicative, not measurements. Still, 6.2 s against more than 180 s is at least a 29× gap, the opposite of PG-1's promise (≤0.5× the Reference at G2).

## Work

1. For each scene, run portal and Reference back to back in one invocation on the same host at the same load, recording wall time and peak RSS.
2. Profile the portal side: the Python cProfile top functions, native phase timings, and callback crossings. Classify the dominant cost:
   - O(scene) per-frame Python work (the fm-92gu class);
   - per-frame arena snapshots;
   - installer-onion dispatch overhead;
   - native raster;
   - typesetting.
3. Fix the dominant cost per class. Cross-link fm-92gu when the cause is its class.

title: W10: PG-8 baseline fixtures claim bare_metal/isolated under the shared-dev-host profile; add a verifier check
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check

The PG-8 baseline fixtures claim a qualification they do not have. `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/artifacts/perf/pg8-*/baseline.tsv` declares:
- `profile_id pg8-shared-dev-host` (line 16);
- `bare_metal true` and `isolated true` (lines 30-31);
- every `observed_*` field as `-`.

`docs/performance/PG8_BASELINE.md:12` says `bare_metal = false`, so the fixture contradicts its own document. No host-qualified observation exists (PERFORMANCE_GATES.md:61,68). A fixture that asserts `bare_metal true` for a shared dev host is the kind of evidence-class inflation the suite rules forbid.

## Work

- Correct the fixture fields to the truth (`bare_metal false`, `isolated false`), or regenerate them with the producer.
- Add a verifier check (perf_host.rs or the baseline loader) that refuses any baseline claiming `bare_metal true` or `isolated true` without a committed, reviewed host profile under `tests/artifacts/perf/hosts/` matching its `profile_id`.

## Acceptance

- The fixtures match PG8_BASELINE.md.
- A planted fixture with `bare_metal true` and no host profile is refused by the new check (negative test).

title: W10: Differential API fuzzer — random manim programs in Reference and portal, BN-keyed exclusions, delta-debugged repros
description:
## Why (2026-09-27 reality check)

Hand comparison with the pinned Reference kept finding semantic divergences in code that was already tested:
- Atlas scaled solids about the origin where manim scales about the bounding-box center;
- VCube faces had the wrong class;
- pre-add NumPy views went stale.
The existing fixtures test what their authors thought to check. A differential fuzzer checks what nobody thought to check, which is how compiler projects find miscompilations (Csmith-style).

## Work

1. A generator of random, valid manim API programs over a typed grammar:
   - constructors with parameters sampled from their documented domains;
   - positional operations (`shift`, `scale`, `rotate`, `next_to`, `arrange`, `align_to`);
   - style setters;
   - copy, become, add and remove;
   - `.animate` chains and short `play` calls under `-s` semantics.
   Programs are seeded and replayable.
2. Execute each program in the pinned Reference and in the portal, and record the structural facts of fm-5wq.33 (family types, counts, quantized geometry, bboxes).
3. Compare, excluding documented divergences. The exclusions are data, keyed to Behavior Notes: true arc length, round joins, Appendix C fixes, the rational clock. Every exclusion row cites its BN.
4. On a difference, delta-debug the program (drop and simplify statements) to a minimal repro, and emit a ready-to-paste regression test.
5. Run as a bounded campaign, for example 10k programs in one hour on the dev host, with results and minimized repros archived.

## Acceptance

- A campaign runs with the exclusion table in force.
- Every minimized divergence is filed as a bead or added as a BN-cited exclusion.
- Planted negatives: at the pre-fix commits, the fuzzer rediscovers the origin-relative Cone scaling and the stale pre-add view, each minimized to under 10 statements.
- Deterministic NDJSON logs with seed, program digest, first differing fact and minimized program.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Refinement round 3: a correction to the description.

- Step 2's "structural facts of fm-5wq.33" should read **the structural facts schema and extractor of fm-5wq.36**. fm-5wq.33 contributes the two-engine runner, which is why the blocks edge on it stays.
- **Unit tests:**
  - the grammar generator is seed-deterministic (same seed → byte-identical program);
  - every generated program parses and type-checks against the API schema;
  - the minimizer is monotone (the reduced program still reproduces) and terminates within its budget.
- **e2e:** a `FMN_E2E_FULL=1` scenario, `parity.differential_fuzz_smoke.v1`: 50 programs at a fixed seed, with the `not-run: reference-env-absent` outcome when the Reference venv is missing (never pass). A campaign is not an e2e; the smoke guards the fuzzer's plumbing.
- **Log fields per program:** seed, program digest, statement count, both engine identities, outcome, the first differing fact path, the exclusion row that suppressed a difference (BN id), and the minimized program digest.

title: W10: Calibration-mode corpus speed ratio — portal vs Reference wall time, same host, interleaved, bootstrap intervals (unqualified, ADR-0024 labels)
description:
## Why (2026-09-27 reality check)

PG-1 promises the portal and native engine at ≤0.5× the Python Reference's wall-clock (G2), ≤0.35× at G4. Qualified measurement waits on an owner host action (ADR-0024, fm-inr.1). Meanwhile nobody knows whether the typical corpus scene is faster or slower than in the Reference. The corpus comparison found at least eight scenes where the Reference finishes in 6–274 s and the portal exceeds 180 s (fm-5wq.31). A 5–30× gap does not need a qualified host to be real. Whether the median is 0.3× or 3× decides where the next month of work should go.

## Work

1. For every corpus scene that runs in both engines, measure portal and Reference wall time on the same host:
   - interleaved (A B A B), 3 or more repetitions;
   - final-state mode at 320×180;
   - same workdir and config;
   - load average recorded.
2. Report per scene the median ratio and dispersion. For the corpus, report the ratio distribution (median, p90, p99) with bootstrap confidence intervals.
3. Label everything calibration-mode and unqualified (ADR-0024), never as PG-1 evidence. The same producer later runs on the qualified slice.
4. Each rerun publishes the table beside the scene dashboard (docs/ratchet/), so the ratio is a ratchet over commits.

title: W10: render refuses a scene whose bare Group/Mobject root holds an even number of points (Reference: bare Mobject never draws); corpus DirectMGFInterpretation
description:
## Found by the fm-5wq.31 same-invocation differential (2026-09-28)

`_2023/clt_proof/main.py` `DirectMGFInterpretation` renders in the pinned Reference (`-s -w`, exit 0,
7.4 s). The portal (dc691fa6 wheel) runs 670 s and then fails the final frame:

    fmn-python: render/render-finish-failed: RuntimeError: lumen integration failed: cannot compile
    geometry for Mob { .. }: shared-anchor point runs must have odd length when nonempty (got 30)

Minimized (seconds, not minutes):

    points = [RIGHT * x for x in np.linspace(-2, 2, 30)]
    y_dots = Group(*(GlowDot(p) for p in points))
    y_dots.set_points([p + UP for p in points])   # the scene's y_dots.set_points([...30...])
    self.add(y_dots)                               # portal: render refused; Reference: renders

## Cause

The Reference's base `Mobject` (so `Group`, `Point`, a bare `PMobject`) has `shader_folder = ""`
(`mobject.py:69`), so its wrapper compiles no program (`shader_wrapper.py:83-88`) and its own points
are data that never draw. The portal gives these the Reference's `point, rgba` record schema
(`RecordSchema::mobject`) but the default `RenderPrimitive::Vector`, and `Stage::draw_plan` emits every
pointful family member as a draw item. `RenderPlan::sync` then validates the Group root's 30 points as
a shared-anchor quad path (odd length required) and refuses the whole frame. With an odd count the
record runs the whole vector pipeline (retained shape, segments, style) and paints nothing
(`read_style` reads absent paint fields as transparent, width 0): no pixels, wasted work.

Measured: odd-count Group/Mobject root points render byte-identical to a control without them.

## Work

1. `Stage::draw_plan` (fmn-mobject `order.rs`) skips vector-primitive records that carry no vector
   paint fields (`stroke_rgba`/`fill_rgba`), next to the existing pointless-member skip. Every
   renderer (retained plan sync, camera prepare with its one-instance-per-vector-item check, vector
   frame, Studio bundle, timeline bundle) reads draw items from there, so they stay consistent.
2. Record the ruling in `docs/RENDER_ORDER.md` with the Reference citation.
3. Order-suite fixtures that meant "a drawable dot" must build a paint-bearing record; measure the
   blast radius first (about 100 bare `Mobject::from_points` sites, most never rendered).

## Acceptance

- The minimized scene renders in the portal (exit 0, decodable PNG), even and odd counts; the
  odd-count frame is byte-identical to its control (no paint change).
- An order-suite test: a bare-schema pointful member yields no draw item; a vmobject-schema one does.
  Planted negative: without the rule the even-count stage fails `RenderPlan::sync`.
- Self-goldens unchanged (bare records never painted, so no pixel may move). Any golden that moves
  is a finding, not a re-bless.
- A same-invocation rerun of DirectMGFInterpretation: record the outcome. Its 670 s portal time is
  fm-5wq.31's; this bead only removes the refusal.

title: W10: portal import pays ~0.65 s per manimlib namespace-collision scan (stats every installed file), repeated per CLI run; trivial scenes 1.4x the Reference
description:
## Found by the fm-5wq.35 corpus speed-ratio run (2026-09-29)

The fastest corpus scenes take ~4.4 s in the portal and ~3.1 s in the Reference (e.g.
_2026/print_gallery/supplements.py:SimpleArrow 4.4 s vs 3.2 s, ratio 1.43; median over 75 scenes
1.65). Interleaved on one host (load ~175): `import manimlib` takes 3.2-3.5 s in the portal and
0.54-0.72 s in the Reference. So a fixed import cost sets the floor of every scene's ratio.

## Cause (measured)

cProfile of `import manimlib` (perfvenv6, fm-5wq.37 wheel): `importlib.metadata` `Distribution.files`
is read 38 times; CPython 3.13 filters it through `skip_missing_files`, one `stat` per file of every
installed distribution (26,492 `Path.exists` calls). The caller is `fmn_python._foreign_manimlib_providers`
(the exclusive-namespace check): 0.65 s wall per call, uncached. A CLI render calls it from
`fmn_python.__main__.main`, again from `manimlib/__init__.py`, and again from
`fmn_python.initialization.initialize`.

## Work

1. Scan RECORD text (`read_text("RECORD")`), keep only paths whose first part is `manimlib`, and check
   existence for those claims only. Same answer as `Distribution.files` (RECORD rows that physically
   exist), without statting unrelated files. Distributions without RECORD keep the `files` path.
2. Scan once per process: cache the providers tuple; a collision refuses at every call site.
3. Leave the refusal semantics and messages unchanged.

## Acceptance

- Unit tests: a fixture distribution claiming `manimlib/__init__.py` (existing) is reported; one claiming
  a missing manimlib path is not (the `files` semantics); unrelated distributions are not statted (count

  VMobject, Animation, Decimal, PathMotion) and every hook name, `inspect.getattr_static`: 53,430

title: W10: bind native Mobject transforms and frame containment
description: Measured pinned-video demand upper bounds show another concentrated portal gap: shift_onto_screen 221 calls, apply_function 107, apply_matrix 83, apply_complex_function 49, apply_points_function 15, plus the related position helpers. Marionette already owns placement, family transforms, bounding boxes, and frame constants, but fmn-python leaves these Reference compositions as generic placeholders. Bind one coherent transform/containment tranche: apply_points_function, apply_function, apply_function_to_position, apply_function_to_submobject_positions, apply_matrix, apply_complex_function, shift_onto_screen, and is_off_screen. Use native Stage matrix/family application where possible; preserve ordinary Python callable exceptions and exact pivot/default behavior; refuse any genuinely unrepresentable cached-bounding-box branch precisely rather than fake success.
acceptance_criteria: The actual built extension exposes exact signatures and Reference-observable behavior for the eight Mobject methods, both VMobject overrides, and the dim/smoothing class defaults. Matrix transforms route once through Marionette per ordinary unique Stage family while custom pointlike fields, shared paths, and Python overrides retain dynamic Reference dispatch. Arbitrary callbacks preserve f32 record-array dtype, family traversal, pivot rules, transformed bounding-box rows, live RecordBuffer visibility, return identity, original exception types, and the Reference member-by-member partial mutation state. shift_onto_screen uses the native frame radii/buff semantics and is_off_screen preserves strict boundary comparisons. Tests cover detached and bound families, 2D/3D matrices, complex maps, position-only helpers, custom fields, override dispatch, shared descendants, oversized/off-screen objects, idempotent in-frame behavior, and raising/mutating callbacks. title: W10: bind family spatial queries to Marionette bounding boxes
description: The pinned 3b1b/videos tree contains 67 direct upper-bound calls across refresh_bounding_box (30), get_boundary_point (21), get_center_of_mass (11), and get_all_points (5), while nine Mobject spatial-query rows remain generic placeholders. Marionette already owns revisioned family bounding boxes and world-space point views, but the portal getters bypass dynamic compute_bounding_box dispatch; consequently DotCloud inherited extents ignore its radius despite the Reference override and the native pointcloud implementation already proving radius-aware bounds. Wire the complete coherent query family through the existing live data and bounding-box authority, without adding a cache or second geometry model.
acceptance_criteria: The actual built extension exposes exact Reference signatures and valid-domain behavior for Mobject.get_all_points, get_bounding_box, compute_bounding_box, refresh_bounding_box, are_points_touching, is_point_touching, is_touching, get_all_corners, get_center_of_mass, and get_boundary_point, plus DotCloud.compute_bounding_box. Existing positional getters dynamically honor class-specific compute_bounding_box behavior, including DotCloud radius and CameraFrame engine state. Detached and scene-bound families, empty and point-free members, path-wise shared descendants, transformed points, inclusive touching boundaries and buffs, disjoint/tangent boxes, corner ordering, center of mass, boundary selection, return types/identity, and conservative live-view invalidation are covered through permanent bridge tests and a direct pinned-Reference differential. Eleven ledger rows are reviewed; actual-extension smoke, focused gates, API ratchet, UBS, and exact-source full workspace gate pass.
close_reason: Acceptance contract independently verified

title: W10: every import compiles the 24,669-line embedded manimlib bootstrap from source (0.34 s); a cached code object loads in 0.01 s
description:
## Measured (2026-09-29, after fm-5wq.38/39)

`import manimlib` is ~1.5 s in the portal vs ~0.6 s in the Reference. The native module's init execs
manimlib_bootstrap.py from an include_str! string (crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs:10960), so CPython compiles
24,669 lines (0.90 MB) on every import: 0.33-0.35 s. marshal.loads of the same code object: 0.010-0.013 s.
No .pyc applies to an exec'd string. Every corpus scene pays it once per process.

## Options (decide before building; each changes packaging)

A. Runtime bytecode cache: marshal the code object into a cache keyed by sha256(source) +
   importlib.util.MAGIC_NUMBER + cache_tag, beside the extension or in a user cache dir; fall back to compile
   when unwritable. Must not make an unregistered file part of the certified runtime identity
   (runtime_identity.py treats generated caches as non-payload; confirm), and must reject a stale or foreign
   blob by key, never by trust.
B. Ship the bootstrap as a real module in the wheel (e.g. manimlib/_bootstrap.py) that the native init imports,
   so pip's install-time .pyc applies and RECORD/runtime identity cover it; the embedded interpreter keeps
   include_str!. Changes the "one native module carries its bootstrap" shape.
C. Build-time marshal via the PyO3 build interpreter: rejected up front, since cross builds (the aarch64 wheel
   uses a PYO3_CONFIG_FILE without an interpreter) have no target interpreter.

## Acceptance

- Import A/B interleaved on one host; trivial scene A/B; frames byte-identical.
- The chosen path keeps runtime-identity and certified input-closure semantics (tests for a stale or
  tampered cache, or for the module being covered by RECORD).

comments.text:
WildBirch, 2026-10-09: this needs an owner decision, so I have relabelled it agent:claim:manual and released it. No code changed.

Root cause, re-checked at b9ef8342:
- `execute_bootstrap` (crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs) calls `py.run` on `CString::new(include_str!("../python/manimlib_bootstrap.py"))`.
- So CPython compiles 24,780 lines (906,377 bytes) on every extension init. No .pyc applies to an exec'd string.

Measurement (interleaved, 15 rounds, host CPython 3.13.9, MAGIC f30d0d0a):
- Script: compile(source, "<string>", "exec") versus marshal.loads of the same code object.
- compile: median 0.201 s, min 0.142 s.
- marshal.loads: median 0.0066 s, min 0.0035 s. The marshal blob is 1,203,272 bytes.
- The loaded object is the same program: co_code and co_consts are equal.
- Caveat: this ran on a shared Mac at load average 78.6 on 14 cores. Treat the absolute numbers as indicative only; the order-of-magnitude gap matches the bead's 0.34 s against 0.01 s.

Why it is blocked:
- Options A and B both change packaging and the runtime-identity surface:
  - A: a runtime marshal cache keyed by sha256(source), MAGIC_NUMBER and cache_tag.
  - B: the bootstrap ships as a wheel module covered by RECORD.
- This bead says "decide before building".
- ADR-0026 is still Proposed, awaiting owner ratification under fm-5wq.15. Its stage 3 assigns this exact decision: "The per-import compile of the bootstrap (0.34 s, fm-5wq.40) is decided there."
- Building A or B now would pre-empt that ADR.

Owner decision needed, either of:
- (1) Ratify ADR-0026, and pick A or B within its stage 3.
- (2) Rule that fm-5wq.40 may go ahead independently of the stage-3 split, and pick A or B.

After that, the bead's acceptance applies unchanged:
- an interleaved import A/B on one host;
- a trivial-scene A/B with byte-identical frames;
- stale and tampered cache tests (A), or RECORD coverage (B).

title: W10: Mobject.add of an ancestor under a detached (not-in-scene) descendant hangs the process instead of refusing the cycle
description:
## Found 2026-09-29 while testing fm-5wq.31's batch add

    child = Mobject(); parent = Group(child)
    child.add(parent)          # hangs (stack: note_changed_family recursing through parents)

Reproduced on the 1a592c4f and 2997b6a1 wheels (so before any batch-add change): no return, no error; a
faulthandler dump after 20 s shows only note_changed_family frames. The same call with the graph bound to a
scene (scene.add(parent) first) refuses with FamilyCycleError "attachment would create a cycle in the family
graph" and leaves the graph intact.

## Cause (read, not yet proven by a fix)

`_BridgeMobject._replace_submobjects` (crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs ~7099) skips cycle validation for a
detached parent: "The Python live list is authoritative until Scene.add binds the complete graph in one
transaction" -> `return Ok(())`. The live list then records the cycle, and note_changed_family (bootstrap,
recursing over parents with no visited set) never terminates.

The Reference's add has no cycle check either; there the recursion raises RecursionError after corrupting the
graph. Correct-by-default: refuse before mutation, the same FamilyCycleError the bound path raises.

## Acceptance

- `child.add(ancestor)` on a detached graph raises FamilyCycleError and leaves submobjects/parents unchanged;
  prefix semantics of a multi-child add unchanged (children before the offending one stay attached).
- bridge.py witness for the detached case next to the existing bound-cycle and self-containment checks.
- Planted negative: the pre-fix wheel hangs the witness (run it under a timeout).
