title: W11: README truth-up — unreleased portal features labeled as shipped in v0.4.0, self-contradictions, front-door --video_dir drift
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The README tells users that specific commands "work today (v0.4.0)". Executed against the published v0.4.0 artifacts (checksums verified, clean CPython 3.13.1 + NumPy 2.5.2 venv), several are false, and some statements contradict each other:

- `fmn-python scene.py SquareToCircle --format gif` and `--format y4m` are listed under "Works today (v0.4.0 portal)" (README ~73-75, ~259-262). The v0.4.0 wheel returns exit 4: "portal output format 'gif' is not connected; use --format png or --format png_sequence". These lines were moved into the v0.4.0 block by later commits (`8e1a8a40` 09-08, `b286a86a` 09-19) although no release has shipped since 08-18.
- `fmn-python studio scene.py SquareToCircle` (CLI block ~265 and Quick Start step 4 ~405) returns exit 4 `studio-unavailable` on v0.4.0, while the status paragraph (~361-379) says the Python Studio route fails closed — the README contradicts itself.
- The v0.4.0 portal renders every Text/Tex glyph upside down (README's own SquareToCircle and Hello scenes: flipped text, label below the square, title off-center). Fixed in source by `fd6bea1d` (fm-5wq.4.20), never released.
- `fmn --format png_sequence demo/wasm/bundle.fmtl DemoTimeline` is in the shipped block; v0.4.0 fails with exit 5 and the error is now an engine-identity mismatch (`certified-cpu:scalar:6:fmtl-law:2` vs `certified-cpu:scalar:6`), not the "minor 7 vs 6" reason the README note gives.
- `pip install franken-manim` (~356): PyPI returns 404. npm `fmn-wasm`: 404, while the README speaks of a "shipped npm artifact".
- Performance section (~456): "enforced on pinned bare-metal profiles" — no such profiles exist and no FrankenManim timing has been recorded for any gate.
- "Font bundle manifest shipped with releases" (~520): the native archive contains only the `fmn` binary (the installer's `validate_archive` rejects extra files); the wheel carries three license texts but no FONT_BUNDLE.json.
- At HEAD the portal wires `--reproducible` for png/png_sequence/wav (`portal_provenance.rs` ~220, `console_rendering.py` ~239), yet the README lists it as failing closed.
- Help text of the CPython-free `fmn` binary copies Reference strings that do not apply: `--autoreload` "reload Python modules", `-e` "iPython session", `-v` "version of manimgl".
- Front-door flag drift (plan §16.2: "drift between front doors is a build error"): `fmn --format png --video_dir X` writes `X/<scene>.png` (directory semantics, like the Reference), while `fmn-python scene.py S --format png --video_dir X` writes the PNG AS the file `X` (`crates/fmn-python/python/fmn_python/console_rendering.py:47-48`: "With one scene, --video_dir retains its existing single-output destination meaning"). title: W11: install.sh version fallback is corrupted by warn() on stdout — the README one-liner breaks when GitHub rate-limits
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The README's primary install path (`curl -fsSL .../scripts/install.sh | bash`) breaks whenever version discovery falls back:

- `resolve_version` (`scripts/install.sh:440-465`) is invoked as `version=$(resolve_version)` (`:646`). On the fallback path it calls `warn "could not resolve the newest published release; using installer fallback ..."`.
- `warn()` (`:73-82`) prints to STDOUT (`printf '%s\n' "WARNING: $*"` / gum / ANSI branches), so the warning text is captured into `version`, then `normalize_version` or the download URL receives garbage and curl fails with `curl: (3) URL rejected` (reproduced during the audit).
- Discovery itself is fragile: it extracts `tag_name` by line-matching GitHub's JSON (`sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*"tag_name":...'`), which only works when GitHub pretty-prints the response. Unauthenticated GitHub API calls are rate-limited (60/hour/IP), so the fallback path is hit in practice (CI runners, NAT'd offices, repeated installs).
- The fallback version is hard-coded (`FALLBACK_VERSION="0.4.0"`, `:15`).
- Tier selection always falls back to portable (no tier artifacts are published), and the wrong-tier launch check in the binary may run after the compiler has already emitted AVX-512 under crate-wide target features.

## Work

1. Send all diagnostics (`info`/`warn`/`ok`) to stderr; keep stdout for values only. Audit every `$(...)` capture in the script.
2. Parse `tag_name` robustly for compact or pretty JSON (e.g. `grep -o '"tag_name":[[:space:]]*"[^"]*"' | head -1`), and prefer `https://github.com/<repo>/releases/latest` redirect resolution which is not API-rate-limited — or document why not.
3. Extend `scripts/test_install.sh` with regression cases: API 403/rate-limit, compact JSON, pretty JSON, empty response, network failure, each asserting the resolved version and that no warning text leaks into URLs.

## Acceptance

- New test cases fail on the current script (demonstrate) and pass on the fix; `bash -n` + shellcheck clean; the README one-liner succeeds when the API is rate-limited (simulated).
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.
close_reason: install.sh diagnostics now on stderr (version=$(resolve_version) can no longer capture warnings); tag discovery parses compact and pretty JSON. scripts/test_install.sh adds hermetic online-path cases via a stand-in curl (compact JSON, pretty JSON, API refusal, empty answer), asserting published version, well-formed URLs, no stdout diagnostics. Negative control: the new cases fail against the previous install.sh ('expected WARNING: could not resolve ... 0.4.0'). shellcheck -S warning clean; bash -n clean. Commits 2e3075b4, and the empty-case follow-up. Verified by re-running scripts/test_install.sh at the committed tree (exit 0).

title: W1: fmn-dmath — owned deterministic elementary functions (the certified transcendental layer)
description:
Implement fmn-dmath (§6.6, D-17): an owned, fixed-implementation elementary-function layer, because std's transcendentals defer to platform libm and differ across glibc/macOS/WASM — and this engine is transcendental-dense (arc construction, per-vertex atan2 joints, rate functions, glow falloffs, tanh normalization, Euler conversions).

Scope: sin, cos, tan, atan, atan2, asin, acos, exp, ln, log2, pow, sqrt, cbrt, tanh, sinh, cosh at minimum — f64 and f32 entry points; fixed polynomial/range-reduction implementations with DOCUMENTED accuracy bounds (state max ULP error per function per domain); bit-identical on every certified target (linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64, windows-x86-64 functional) — locked by cross-platform vector files in CI: a committed table of (input, expected-bits) pairs covering normals, denormals, near-branch-cut and near-singularity inputs.

Mode policy: standard mode MAY use fast paths (std/libm); certified uses fmn-dmath EXCLUSIVELY. The seam is a trait or function-table chosen at engine construction, never a scattered cfg.

SIMD posture (§6.6, §17.3): design the kernels as fixed-coefficient, fixed-order polynomials so they vectorize bit-reproducibly later — same operation order in scalar and every lane width. Do NOT vectorize in this bead; just don't preclude it (no table-lookup designs that defeat lanes).

Interlock: G0-6 (determinism spike) consumes a prototype of this crate; its cross-platform findings may force implementation adjustments — budget for one revision pass after the spike lands.

Acceptance: accuracy docs per function; cross-platform vector CI green; property tests (range reduction identities, symmetry laws); the standard/certified seam demonstrated in a test.
notes: In progress 2026-07-22: crate scaffolding + mode seam (Transcendentals table, CERTIFIED/FAST) + bits helpers landed; sqrt delegated (IEEE correctly rounded, documented). Ground-truth vectors committed: 16 files, ~9.6k (input-bits, correctly-rounded-expected-bits) pairs from mpmath prec=150 via scripts/gen_dmath_vectors.py, incl. denormals, near-branch-cuts, Payne-Hanek stress inputs. tests/vectors.rs asserts per-fn ULP bounds (sin/cos/atan/asin/acos/exp/expm1/ln/cbrt ≤1; tan/atan2/log2/pow/sinh/cosh/tanh ≤2). f32 API = f64 layer + single rounding (documented double-rounding caveat). FDLIBM-structure f64 implementations being written by three parallel subagents (trig+rem_pio2 / inverse-trig+cbrt / exp,log,pow,hyper).
close_reason: fmn-dmath landed: owned FDLIBM-structure f64 implementations of sin/cos/tan (+Payne-Hanek rem_pio2), atan/atan2/asin/acos, exp/expm1/ln/log2, full e_pow, cbrt, sinh/cosh/tanh; sqrt delegated (IEEE correctly rounded). f32 API = f64 + single rounding (documented). Mode seam = Transcendentals fn table (CERTIFIED/FAST) chosen at construction, demonstrated in test. Accuracy documented per module and enforced by tests/vectors.rs against 16 committed mpmath ground-truth vector files (~9.6k vectors incl. denormals, branch cuts, reduction stress): measured max 1 ulp everywhere within bounds (sin/cos/atan/asin/acos/exp/expm1/ln/cbrt ≤1; tan/atan2/log2/pow/sinh/cosh/tanh ≤2). Known inherited FDLIBM pow limitation for |y|>2^31 with |x-1|<2^-20 documented in module doc + dedicated test. All constants pinned via from_bits hex. Gates green; ubs critical = test-harness panic only. Built by 3 parallel subagents + integration; generator fix: mpf() collapses -0.0 (atan2 specials now via IEEE-exact libm).

title: W2: Scalar-field isolines + ear-clip triangulation utilities
description:
Two owned geometry utilities (§7.7–7.8):

(1) ISOLINES: an adaptive quadtree isoline extractor for ImplicitFunction (displaces the isosurfaces package), honoring the Reference's min_depth / max_quads API knobs as BUDGET semantics (the knobs bound work; they do not promise a particular mesh). Everything underdefined in the original is DEFINED here: traversal order (deterministic), truncation behavior when max_quads is hit (which regions coarsen, in what order), segment orientation convention, domain-boundary handling, and NaN/undefined-region behavior (functions may divide by zero — cells containing non-finite samples are handled by a stated rule, not UB). Quality target: "ours, and good" — adaptive refinement should visibly beat uniform sampling on curvature-varying implicit curves.

(2) EAR-CLIP: a polygon triangulator with hole support (displaces mapbox-earcut) — deterministic tie-breaks, honest acceptance criteria (valid triangulation of valid input; no Delaunay quality pretensions). It is a UTILITY for booleans' flatten fallback, mesh export, and future mesh work; the live fill path needs no triangulation at all (§10.2 rasterizes winding coverage analytically — that independence is a design feature, keep it).

Acceptance: isoline determinism tests (same field + budget ⇒ identical segments); budget-semantics tests (max_quads respected exactly); NaN-region tests; known-curve accuracy tests (circle/lemniscate implicit forms vs analytic); triangulator validity property tests (area preservation, no flipped/degenerate triangles, hole containment) over fuzzed polygons.

title: W2: Refuse unbounded or non-terminating isoline configurations
description: The current fm-81u isoline implementation accepts zero, negative, NaN, or infinite tolerance components. edge_crossing terminates only when both edge spans are smaller than tolerance, so midpoint rounding can stop making progress while the predicate remains false, causing a permanent loop. The min_depth <= 30 check is also false on 32-bit targets because 1_usize << (2 * min_depth) can shift past usize width, and accepted min_depth/max_quads values permit impractical allocation and CPU work. Add typed finite-positive tolerance and finite-domain/level validation, checked architecture-independent budget arithmetic, a declared hard leaf/evaluation cap consistent with the public budget semantics, and adversarial tests proving invalid or oversized configurations return named errors without field evaluation, panic, hang, or allocation blowup. Preserve deterministic valid-input output.

title: W2: Normalize ear-clip predicate space and cap adversarial vertex work

title: GATE G1: Reject mismatched shape identities during interning
description: At exact HEAD 7aba1db083e8016a10eab0bb3f79192074825a4f, public ShapeTable::intern_shape(digest, build) indexes the new row under the caller-supplied digest but stores build().digest without checking equality. A mismatched builder therefore leaves by_digest key A pointing at a Shape that reports digest B; lookup by B misses, later interning can duplicate the row, and canonical snapshots publish an identity different from the reuse authority. Existing fm-o3j.13 made table admission atomic/fallible but did not bind these two identities; br and CASS searches found no owner. Acceptance: add a typed pre-mutation mismatch refusal carrying both digests; preserve the capacity/index preflight before build; leave rows, lookup index, and instance state semantically unchanged on refusal; prove a correct retry occupies row zero and duplicate reuse still works; run focused/full renderer checks, strict rustdoc, scoped UBS, and exact scripts/check.sh; land only reserved table.rs; keep DSR paused pending committed W11 inputs. This is an internal retained-IR invariant correction with unit coverage, not a new user-facing e2e surface.

title: W3: Arena snapshots & serialization — SceneState, undo, replay barriers, fixtures
description:

title: W2: Planar path booleans — flatten-and-clip certified first, curve-aware pipeline behind topology-aware acceptance

Implement path booleans (§7.4; displaces skia-pathops) in the plan's two-stage posture:

Acceptance: stage 1 green under the full acceptance battery + fuzzing; stage-2 classes each land with their topology spec + differential tests vs stage 1.

title: W10/W7: ParametricSurface refuses non-finite samples at poles; 4 laplace scenes (|f| = inf on the grid) stop there
description:
Found by the fm-1rb8 rerun (ec63a187, 2026-09-26). After the 262144 surface budget landed, four _2025/laplace scenes moved off the budget error to: ValueError: surface uv_func must return finite f32-representable coordinates. The scenes are ShowSolutionPoles and SimplePole (derivatives.py/integration.py), TranslateToNewLanguage (main_equations.py) and PreviewAnalyticContinuation (main_supplements.py).

## Cause
integration.py get_complex_graph samples z = unit_size * abs(func(complex(u, v))) on a 301x301 grid. With u, v = linspace(-3, 3, 301) (step 0.02), grid points land exactly on poles such as s = +-2i. np.divide(s, 0) gives inf+nanj, so abs() is inf. sampling_callbacks.point_sample and Atlas's SurfaceSpec::try_sample refuse every non-finite sample by design, preserving the finite-record invariant.

## Reference behavior
The pinned Reference stores inf in the point records. OpenGL discards the triangles that touch that vertex (clip coordinates become NaN). The spike around the pole leaves the frustum anyway, so the visible result is the surface with a tiny hole at the top of an off-screen spike.

## Design question (decide before code)
Records are finite everywhere today (bboxes, alignment, transforms, the CPU rasterizer). Candidates:
(a) Admit non-finite samples as explicit holes. Triangles touching one are skipped in Lumen, and bbox/alignment/normals ignore them. This needs a Behavior Note and an audit of every point consumer.
(b) Keep the refusal, but name the pole and suggest an offset grid. The scenes would still not render.
Do not clamp: that fabricates geometry.

## Acceptance
- A decision recorded as an ADR or a Behavior Note.
- If (a): the four scenes render ok, a witness surface with one inf sample renders a hole whose triangles are absent, and finite surfaces are bit-identical (self-goldens unchanged).

title: W10: Scene arena never reclaims removed mobjects; every frame snapshots all of them (dice_sims per-sample cost grows with samples shown)
description:
## Found by fm-5wq.21 (2026-09-25, WildGoose)

`Stage::delete` is the only way an entry dies ("Explicit destruction — the only way an entry dies", crates/fmn-mobject/src/stage.rs). A Python proxy's Drop only unpins (crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs, `impl Drop for BridgeMobject` -> `release_pin`). A mobject the scene adds and then removes therefore stays live in the Scene arena after Python drops it.

Every non-skip frame freezes a FramePacket, which is a full `Stage::snapshot` (fmn-anim frame.rs `FramePacket::freeze`). That snapshot clones every live entry: buffer handle, child and parent vectors, updaters. Frame cost is therefore O(every mobject ever shown).

Evidence (release portal at a2bd8da5, construct-only, cProfile and perf):
- clt/dice_sims, 900 still-frame samples: 186 s. Native Scene._wait took 97.4 s of it; each one-frame wait grows from about 1.2 ms at N=100 to about 108 ms.
- perf's top native symbol is the `Stage::snapshot` per-slot closure, surrounded by malloc/free.
- With skip_animations the per-frame freeze is skipped: 500 samples take 37.6 s, against 66.6 s without skip.
- Same-session under -s: the portal is 0.64x the Reference at 400 samples but 1.11x at 1200 (fm-5wq.21 table).

## Work (both touch handle lifetimes; design before code)
(a) Reclaim entries that are unpinned and unreachable from the Scene: not a root, no live parent, and not referenced as a target, saved_state or tracker, nor captured by a native updater closure. Journals and checkpoints hold snapshots, not handles, but verify that.
(b) Alternatively, or additionally, let a sink that ignores segment frames tell the frame loop not to freeze a packet per frame: construct-only, and a still-PNG session that needs only the final capture.

## Acceptance
- dice_sims per-sample cost no longer grows with samples already shown. Measure N=100/400/900 in the same invocation before and after.
- Self-goldens, the engine-equivalence suite, PG-5 determinism and bridge.py are unchanged. A negative test proves a removed-then-dropped mobject is reclaimed, while one still referenced (target/saved_state/updater) is not.

title: W1: Pin frankenscipy >= 5a7aafa2 (deterministic RK step control) — closure review for the 2,433-commit jump (thiserror ^2.0.20, fsci-sparse)
description:
## Why (from fm-certified-libm-leak-3aja, 2026-09-27)

`fsci-integrate` at the SUITE.lock pin `5b1441b` computes RK step control and the initial step through `f64::powf`:
- four sites in `rk.rs` step control;
- one in `step_size.rs` `select_initial_step`.

That is the platform libm, whose last bits differ across glibc, macOS and wasm. FrankenManim's StreamLines/AnimatedStreamLines (`fmn-library/src/fields.rs`) run `solve_ivp(Rk45)`, so certified output with stream lines is not bit-reproducible across the certified matrix (ADR-0010 property 1).

The upstream fix has landed: frankenscipy `5a7aafa27951bd3eeb2a678763df05faaa68b679` on main (and master). A deterministic `kth_root` (IEEE `+ - * /` only, exact decomposition, monotone Newton) replaces those five `powf` calls. fsci-integrate: 316 tests pass.

The pin cannot simply move. frankenscipy main is 2,433 commits past `5b1441b`:
- `fsci-integrate` now depends on `fsci-sparse`, which requires `thiserror ^2.0.20`;
- our lockfile holds `thiserror 2.0.19` through asupersync, so resolution fails as it stands;
- the new transitive packages must pass the governed closure (D1: per-package allowlist, licence, build script, unsafe audit).

## Work

1. Bump `fsci-integrate`, `fsci-linalg` and `fsci-opt` to one frankenscipy commit at or after `5a7aafa2` (SUITE.lock row and `Cargo.toml` revs). Update `Cargo.lock` (`cargo update -p thiserror` and the new suite crates).
2. Governed closure: list every new package, allowlist or refuse each per D1, and keep `governed_closure` green. Record the diff in the Gauntlet repin ritual (UPSTREAM_LEDGER row).
3. API drift: fix every fmn call site broken by the 2,433-commit jump (StreamLines `solve_ivp` options, `fsci-linalg` solves in smoothing.rs, `fsci-opt` assignment).
4. Remove the two `SUITE_KNOWN_LEAKS` entries in `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/certified_arithmetic.rs`; they fail as stale once the calls are gone.
5. A certified StreamLines self-golden: one scene, `--reproducible`, hashed on linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64 and macos-aarch64 (the certified matrix), which must be bit-identical.

## Acceptance

- The certified-arithmetic guard passes with no fsci known leaks.
- The StreamLines certified golden is bit-identical on the three platforms. This closes the second half of fm-certified-libm-leak-3aja.
- Existing StreamLines tests and goldens: any change is explained by the step-control change (ulp-level step sizes) and shown frame by frame, not re-blessed blindly.

title: W8: fmn-frame — frame buffers, pixel formats, transfer functions
description:
Implement the frame substrate (§14.1): buffer types over pooled allocations (the preallocated ring the emitter and pipeline ride — no frame-sized allocation on the hot path, PG-6's zero-steady-state-alloc rule); pixel formats — RGBA8/BGRA8, RGBA16F intermediates where quality demands, NV12/P010 video planes (with correct chroma siting and range semantics), canonical RGBA for certified output; transfer functions applied ONCE, natively, at the defined point (the ffmpeg boundary's "no obligatory eq" rule depends on us owning transfer correctly); row-stride discipline (sinks negotiate stride; internal buffers may pad).

Format conversion kernels: linear-light RGBA16F → sRGB RGBA8; RGBA → NV12/P010 (BT.709 matrix, defined rounding — these are §17.3 hot-list adjacent: color transfer functions are named); orientation is ALWAYS output orientation — fmn-frame renders the right way up and no vflip exists anywhere in the system (D-23).

Certified interaction: canonical RGBA output bytes are part of the certified artifact set — conversion kernels on the certified path use fixed-order, defined-rounding arithmetic (W5CERT's rules extend here); NV12/P010 conversions are standard-mode (they feed ffmpeg, whose products are uncertified by construction).

Acceptance: format round-trip tests (within documented precision per conversion); NV12/P010 golden vectors vs reference matrices; pool reuse tests (steady-state render loop performs zero frame allocations — instrumented via §17.1); stride/negotiation unit tests; certified-conversion determinism tests.
close_reason: fmn-frame landed: formats+layouts, pooled buffers, certified transfer tables over fmn-dmath, NV12/P010 fixed-point kernels with range/siting semantics, 26 acceptance tests. All gates green (478 tests).

title: W1: Enforce canonical writer limits before payload growth
description: Read-only audit at exact HEAD 20f67d27c32d390170897f39bc9a4bd7a011d8fb found that fmn_hash::serial::Writer enforces max_field before appending a field, but enforces max_total only in finish after its payload Vec has already grown. Scalar put methods append without consulting the total budget, and scalar writes after a sticky oversized-field error continue growing the buffer. Large aggregate encoders can therefore allocate far beyond their declared canonical document ceiling before returning SizeLimit. Fix in the W1 serializer: apply a checked remaining-payload budget before every append, make a sticky error stop subsequent growth, keep length-prefixed fields atomic, use checked width conversions, and add tight-limit boundary tests proving refusal occurs before payload growth. Audit all Writer consumers after the root fix. FILED, NOT FIXED because W1 is not active under the current four-workstream governance cap.
close_reason: Consolidated fix landed in 283b035 and gate-verified (gate19 'OK: all gates green'): every Writer append routes through one admit(n) gate — sticky short-circuit stops all growth after the first error (fm-a4qr), the total budget is enforced against the projected FRAME_LEN+payload+n BEFORE any growth (fm-6h6.1), and reservation is fallible via try_reserve with a new typed Error::AllocationFailed; finish assembles the sealed document through try_reserve_exact (fm-6h6.2). put_bytes admits prefix+bytes atomically so no partial length ever lands. Regressions: budget-fires-before-growth with the needed value frozen at the offending put; refused field appends neither prefix nor bytes (clean sibling document byte-verified); scalar writes after an oversized field neither grow nor mask the first error. fmn-hash 23/23; full workspace sweep zero failures; clippy/fmt/UBS clean.

title: W6: Tex submobjects are not in TeX's emission order (glyphs, then rules, then paths), and multi-piece constructions are one submobject: index compatibility with the Reference
description:
## Found by the corpus differential on a clean Reference (fm-0v8k), 2026-10-09

With the Reference's TeX cache race fixed (Appendix C-22), 61 two-engine scenes differ only inside
Tex/TexText. Both kinds below break manim's index contract. BN-05 promises that scene code indexes
identically, and 3b1b scenes slice formulas by index (`eq[0][4:7]`).

### 1. Order (39 scenes)

The portal's Tex submobjects are every glyph, then every rule, then every drawn path
(crates/fmn-tex/src/typeset.rs `Typeset::new`). fmd-math's `Layout` keeps three separate vectors, so
the emission order is lost. The Reference's order is TeX's emission (DVI) order.

Measured in both engines:
- `d = \frac{s}{\sqrt{\sigma_1^2 + \sigma_2^2}}`:
  - Reference: d, =, s, fraction bar, surd, overbar, then the radicand glyphs;
  - portal: all glyphs, then overbar, fraction bar, surd.
- `\frac{1}{2}\Big( ... \Big)`: the Reference's bar is index 1 and its delimiters sit in place. The
  portal appends the bar and both delimiters.

In all 39 scenes the glyph counts are equal. A t2c color then sits on a different index.

TeX's DVI order differs from naive box order in a few constructs, which need checking:
- \underbrace and \underline put the content before the brace or rule;
- limits put the upper limit before the operator.

### 2. Piece counts (20 scenes)

TeX builds some constructions from several characters where the portal emits one submobject:

| construct | Reference | portal |
|---|---|---|
| `\longrightarrow`, `\Longrightarrow`, `\mapsto` | 2 | 1 |
| ``` `` ``` and `''` in TexText | 2 each | 1 each |
| a 3-row `\left[...\right]` bracket | 2 pieces a side | 1 |
| a 4-row `\left[...\right]` bracket | 4 pieces a side | 1 |
| `\overbrace` / `\underbrace` | 6 pieces (4 cmex tips + 2 rules) | 1 |

Every index after such a construct shifts.

## Work

- fmd-math: give `Layout` its emission order, a traversal of the box tree in TeX's DVI order. Fix
  the child order of the constructs where TeX's order differs.
- fmn-tex: build `subs` in emission order. Version the typeset-cache payload if the layout encoding
  changes.
- Piece counts: decide per construct. Either the portal emits TeX's pieces as separate submobjects,
  matching the index contract, or BN-05 documents a divergence with migration guidance. Drawn
  delimiters and braces relate to ADR-0005 and ADR-0028.

## Acceptance

- The structural differential (scenes scope) shows no Tex-internal member or style difference from
  ordering.
- The open-bead exclusion row citing this bead narrows to the piece-count constructs, or is removed.
- A regression test in fmn-tex asserts the emission order for a fraction, a radical, `\Big`
  delimiters and limits.
- Scene goldens are re-blessed under GOVERNANCE §4 if draw order changes pixels.

comments.text:
2026-10-10: the long-arrow piece split is built and tested in fmd-math, but deferred until CM math faces land (ADR-0028, fm-cm-math-faces-impl-n12u).

The design: a NodeKind::JoinedRel, one Rel atom of two glyphs.
- The pieces overlap by -3 mu (\joinrel).
- The box height and depth come from the unsmashed pieces; \relbar is a smashed minus.
- Both glyphs carry the command span and are emitted left to right.
- MathML still uses the single Unicode arrow.
- amsmath's \implies, \impliedby and \iff add \; on each side.
- The compositions follow fontmath.ltx, as listed in the 2026-10-09 comment.

Why it is deferred: the bundled CM Unicode face has no U+2212 or U+2192, so both pieces come from Noto Sans Math (advances measured with fontTools).
- Noto's minus is 0.572 em and its arrow 1.012 em, so the joined \longrightarrow is 1.417 em.
- TeX's is 1.611 em (cmsy minus 0.778 + arrow 1.0 - 3 mu, measured under the Reference's preamble), and `a\longrightarrow b` is 3.124 em.
- Today's single Noto glyph is 1.558 em, so the split would move the width from -3% to -12%.
- \Longrightarrow would join a CM Unicode `=` to a Noto `⇒`, two designs whose bars need not line up.

So piece-count parity would cost width and look. Once cmsy's minus, arrows and equals sign are bundled, the split is a small change. It is kept as a patch, and the description above is enough to rebuild it.

title: W5: Mean-value colour field over multiple boundary loops (glyph counters, annuli)
description:
fm-5oi landed §10.2's interior colour field as the mean-value interpolant of normalized arc length over GRADIENT_STATIONS=64 arc-length-uniform boundary stations (crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs, GradientField).

Mean value coordinates are defined for ONE closed polygon. For a shape whose path has several subpaths the stations currently run over the whole path in path order, so the station polygon connects one subpath's end to the next one's start. That field is defined, deterministic, and subdivision-invariant — the three properties §10.2 requires — and it coincides exactly with the region boundary whenever there is a single subpath, which is every gradient fill in the corpus so far.

It is NOT the region boundary for a shape with holes: a letter 'o' with a counter, an Annulus, a Sector with an inner arc. The per-loop generalization (Hormann-Floater's MVC for polygons with holes: sum the weights over every loop, with the outer loop and the hole loops carrying opposite traversal) is a DESIGN step, not a parameter — it has to decide what the boundary colour is on a hole's loop when the ramp is defined on the path's arc length as a whole, and whether a hole's stations get the same station count as the outer loop or a share proportional to its arc length.

Do not guess it. Trigger: a corpus case (or a Look Gallery panel) where a gradient-filled shape has a hole. Acceptance: subdivision invariance must survive the generalization (it is the property the whole construction exists for), and the single-loop case must be bit-identical to today's field.

Recorded in GradientField's doc comment as the module's stated limit.

title: W10: Arc.add_tip(at_start=True) leaves a zero-length first shaft component, so get_arc_center and the angle getters read a degenerate point
description:
## Found while closing fm-8pj7 (2026-10-09)

Probe: an installed portal wheel built at fb1c1b9e (the same behaviour appears on an earlier djox-tip wheel).

`Arc(angle=2.0).add_tip(at_start=True)` leaves the shaft's first quadratic component zero-length: its first three points are all (0.9394, 0.3429, 0).

- `get_arc_center()` reads `points[:3]`, as the Reference does, so it returns that degenerate point instead of the arc's center.
- Every getter built on the center is then wrong: `get_start_angle` gives 4.887 for a tip at (1, 0), and `move_arc_center_to` is affected too.

Cause: generic `Line`/`Arc`/`ArcBetweenPoints` deliberately keep the native true-arclength trimming policy (a2c9c31c). The Reference instead refits the whole shaft with `put_start_and_end_on(tip.get_base(), end)`. The start-side trim appears to collapse the first component rather than re-split it.

Work:
- Decide the generic-arc tip rule. Either:
  - follow the Reference's whole-shaft refit, as `CurvedArrow` now does; or
  - keep trimming but re-split, so no component is degenerate.
- Add a Behavior Note if trimming stays.
- Test: `Arc.add_tip(at_start=True)` and `Arc.add_tip()` keep `get_arc_center` within 1e-6 of the true center. Planted negative: the current wheel.

title: W10: portal certified manifest: C4 is the defaults document, so two fps values publish different frames under one closure digest
description:
## Found by the fresh-eyes review R3b (typeset cache / certified closure)

Two certified (`reproducible=True`) portal renders that differ only in `fps` publish
different frames under ONE closure digest. The certified closure therefore does not
determine the output, which §16.7 requires.

### Reproduction (fresh wheel built from b27526fb, CPython 3.13, Linux)

`render_scene(Dot1, out, format="png_sequence", resolution=(64, 36), fps=F, threads=1,
reproducible=True, sources={...})` for a one-`play` scene (run_time 0.5):

- fps 10: closure a81cf0db…, artifact 8ddd8924…, 5 frames
- fps 20: closure a81cf0db…, artifact cba1638b…, 10 frames

### Cause

`crates/fmn-python/src/portal_provenance.rs` (~L402-415) resolves the defaults and then
assigns typed fields (`config.camera.resolution`, `config.camera.fps`,
`config.determinism.seed`, `config.determinism.mode`), but
`fmn_config::Config::canonical_bytes` serializes `config.raw`, which those assignments
never touch. So the portal's C4 ("fully resolved configuration after defaults, files, and
CLI overlay") is the defaults document whatever the render's settings. Resolution still
reaches C7 (the renderer journal's viewport) and the seed C5; fps reaches no item. For
`wav` the C7 document is empty, so resolution is unbound there too (harmless for audio).

### Suggested fix

Build the portal's config through `Config::resolve(&[], Some(overlay([...])))` with the
render's camera.resolution / camera.fps / determinism.seed / determinism.mode, exactly as
the CLI's overlay does, so `raw` and the typed fields agree; add a test that fps 10 vs 20
give different closure digests (and threads 1 vs 4 the same). Owner of the portal manifest
path should confirm whether the user's custom_config.yml layers belong in the portal's C4.

Workspace cargo test exit 0 (271 binaries, 4087 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored) and clean-wheel gate exit 0 at a797c89c; planted negative on the 18c9a802 wheel. Owner question filed as fm-portal-c4-config-layers-zwzp.

title: Fix the non-fatal asupersync malformed Cargo.toml diagnostic in every workspace build/test
description:
P3 bug — developer-experience / CI hygiene.

Background: Every `cargo build`, `cargo check`, and `cargo test` invocation in the `franken_manim` workspace prints the following non-fatal diagnostic at the top of the output:

```
error: unclosed table, expected `]`
 --> ../../../home/ubuntu/.cargo/git/checkouts/asupersync-b12181f74b36652e/c48399f/tests/fixtures/migration_readiness_planner/malformed/Cargo.toml:1:9
  |
1 | [package
  |         ^
```

The build/test continues and succeeds, so the error is non-fatal. It appears to come from Cargo parsing a deliberately malformed `Cargo.toml` fixture inside the `asupersync` git dependency. Previous bead comments in the history call it "expected and nonfatal."

Why this still matters:
- It trains developers to ignore error output at the top of every CI log, making real errors harder to spot.
- It is noise in every agent session transcript.
- It is confusing for new contributors and for automated log parsers.

Acceptance:
- Identify exactly why Cargo parses this fixture (workspace discovery, test target discovery, or another mechanism).
- Fix it at the source by either:
  (a) renaming the fixture so Cargo does not attempt to parse it as a manifest, or
  (b) making the fixture valid TOML if it is meant to be parsed, or
  (c) excluding it from the asupersync crate manifest / include list, or
  (d) updating the `franken_manim` workspace/SUITE.lock to a fixed asupersync revision once upstream resolves it.
- Verify that `cargo test --workspace` and `cargo build --workspace` no longer emit the diagnostic.
- Do NOT suppress the diagnostic with wrapper scripts; fix the root cause.

It is non-fatal; every workspace build/test succeeds after the message. A source-level fix requires either an upstream asupersync change (rename the fixture so Cargo does not attempt to parse it, or make it valid TOML and use a different malformed fixture for the test) or a workspace [patch] to a fixed asupersync revision. Modifying the local cargo cache is a hygiene-only win and would be overwritten on fresh checkouts. title: W1: Baseline profiling report + permanent stage-level phase instrumentation
description:
Publish the checked-in baseline report BEFORE performance gates are finalized (§17.1): corpus, profiler, hardware, resolution, cache state, ffmpeg in/out, phase breakdown, raw data. The premise "Python churn dominates manim render time" is MEASURED here, not assumed — gate thresholds (PG-1's 0.5x/0.35x ratios) are calibrated against these numbers.

Two deliverables: (1) THE BASELINE — profile the Python Reference on the pinned benchmark definition (hardware including its GPU, environment, 30fps config stated, cache state, ffmpeg in/out) across representative scene classes (OpeningManimExample-class, text-heavy, 3D, dense-stroke); commit the report + raw data. (2) THE PERMANENT INSTRUMENTATION — stage-level phase timing built into the engine from the start, a fixture of every profiled run forever: scene/update, Python callback, geometry compilation, render-IR synchronization, binning, raster, color conversion, annex upload/readback, ffmpeg feed, encode — timed separately, exported in the owned structured-tracing format (§18: scene → play → frame → phase → tile, JSON + flame summaries). title: W6: tall binomial delimiters render broken (\binom, \choose, matrix parens); \tbinom unsupported; ✗ has no glyph; Text θ draws as ϑ
description:
## Found by the explainer-skill glyph probe (2026-10-07)

While building the scaffold template for the math-explainer skill, its glyph probe (a native `fmn::render` PNG still of every Text/Tex string a video uses) showed four typesetting defects. All four are reproducible with `Tex::new(..).font_size(36.0).build(stage.tex_engine()?)` or `Text::new(..).build(&FontBook::bundled()?)` through the facade. The build was franken_manim 7ef2eac2 plus the working tree, rendered on Linux x86_64 (trj).

### 1. Tall binomial parentheses render broken
- **Affected:** `\binom{N}{4}`, `{N \choose 4}` and `\left(\begin{matrix} N \\ 4 \end{matrix}\right)`. All three draw their parentheses as thin, disjoint stroke pieces with visible gaps. They look like a mis-assembled extensible delimiter: top and bottom pieces without the joining extender, or the wrong pieces chosen.
- **Unaffected:** ordinary `( )` around `C(N, 4)` and `\frac` bars render fine.
- **Expected:** solid, continuous parentheses sized to the stacked content, as in LaTeX.
- **Repro:** `r"\binom{N}{4} \quad {N \choose 4} \quad \left(\begin{matrix} N \\ 4 \end{matrix}\right) \quad C(N, 4)"`.

### 2. `\tbinom` is unsupported
- **Error:** "`\tbinom` is not supported; untiered (not observed in the G0-4 corpus)".
- **Expected:** amsmath `\tbinom`, along with `\dbinom`, which is probably also missing.

### 3. ✗ (U+2717) has no glyph in the bundled faces
- **Error:** `Text::new("✓ ✗")` fails with "character '✗' (U+2717) has no glyph in the selected faces".
- **Notes:** ✓ was not reported, because the first failure aborts the string. 3Blue1Brown-style comparison tables use ✓/✗.

### 4. Text θ draws as ϑ
- **Repro:** `Text::new("ρ τ α θ")` draws θ (U+03B8) in the script form ϑ.
- **Relation to existing bead:** the math-mode `\theta → ϑ` regression is fm-5wq.60. This is the same shape in plain Text, so it may share a cause (font mapping) or need its own fix.

### Workarounds the explainer template uses
- `C(N, 4)` notation instead of `\binom`.
- No ✗.
- No θ in Text.

### Acceptance
- A probe still of the repro strings shows continuous binomial parentheses.
- `\tbinom` and `\dbinom` typeset.
- ✗ renders, or the bundled-coverage docs list it as missing.
- Text θ draws the closed form.
- A golden or box test pins the binomial delimiter shape.

title: W2: fsci-linalg 0.2.0: 12 Simd::mul_add (FMA) sites in the SPD blocked-Cholesky kernels on solve()'s n>=128 path — make fmn's non-reachability structural or get an FMA-free certified mode upstream
description:
Found by the certified-arithmetic guard at the frankenscipy 5a7aafa2 pin (fm-9esi). fsci-linalg lib.rs now carries 12 explicit Simd::mul_add calls in cholesky_panel_trsm_blocked_fma_rows, cholesky_syrk_flat_rows_mr4_nr8_fma and cholesky_syrk_flat_rows_mr4_nr8_fma_nc. They run only on solve()'s Strict n>=solve_flat_min()=128 branch taken for assume_a=PositiveDefinite, assume_a=Symmetric/Hermitian, or a detected Symmetric structure. The old pin 5b1441b1 had no FMA there.

fmn's only dense solve is fmn-geom smoothing.rs solve_dense for closed smooth_cubic_handles, called with SolveOptions::default() (assume_a=None), dimension n=2(a-1) capped at 256. The closed-smoothing matrix depends only on n and is never symmetric (A[1][2]=1, A[2][1]=-2 for n>=4); fmn-geom's test closed_smoothing_matrix_is_never_symmetric pins that for every admissible n. So today the kernels cannot run for fmn, but only by a value-level argument. The guard is function-granular and records them as known leak SUITE_KNOWN_LEAKS fsci-linalg lib.rs mul_add=12.

D18 forbids FMA on certified paths. Explicit fma is IEEE-exact (deterministic across platforms), but the scalar path is the definition every tier must match.

Done when either: (a) fmn's closed smoothing passes an explicit assume_a (General), which skips the symmetric branches structurally, AND the self-goldens and smoothing tests are shown bit-unchanged for n<128 (the portfolio path for General vs None must be compared), then the entry's reason is updated; or (b) frankenscipy gains an FMA-free mode fmn can select, and the entry is removed. Owner W2/Chisel.

Also examine: the n>=128 LU fast path (f32 mixed-precision factor plus f64 refinement, rayon trailing update) is what fmn's closed smoothing takes today. Prove its bits are thread-count independent (PG-5 style, RAYON_NUM_THREADS 1 vs N in separate processes) for a 65+-anchor closed path.

How to land them when you get here: add authored sections to API_OVERLAY.tsv ([exit_codes] and [flag_interaction] alongside the existing [canonical]/[config_binding]/[status] sections), teach fmn_conformance::schema to read them (the sectioned-TSV reader is generic — a new section is a `typed(name, arity)` call plus a model struct), and extend generate_cli_table_md to emit them. The drift gate then covers them automatically. Keep the rule the other sections follow: a row naming something the extracted layer does not have is a hard error (SchemaError::DanglingOverlay), so the overlay cannot rot against a Reference pin bump.

One decision already visible in the inventory and worth making explicitly: the Reference's flags include several that no longer mean anything here (LaTeX/Pango-era knobs). §13.6's phrasing is "the Reference's flag surface where it still means something" — so each row wants a kept/re-specified/dropped verdict, which is exactly what the [status] vocabulary (same|improved|tiered|excluded) already expresses for symbols. Reusing it for flags rather than inventing a second vocabulary would be the cheaper design.

title: W10: the GroverPreview corpus baseline drifted (family 1110 -> 1162) between 6a7de9f2 and 6d4a4463, so the seed-module corpus test is red where the private corpus exists
description:
## Found by `cargo test -p fmn-python` on hz3, 2026-10-10

`corpus::tests::seed_modules_reach_precise_verdicts_under_the_import_shim` fails on a host that has the private corpus:

      expected: 18 1110 -6.291682 -21.500000 ... (crates/fmn-python/tests/corpus_baselines.tsv)

The two leading facts are the Stage draw-list roots and their family members (`scene._engine_facts()`). The roots, the bounding box, the time and the camera are unchanged. The family has 52 more members.

- The installed wheel 6d4a4463 (2026-10-09 10:19) already measures 18/1162 through the same `_engine_facts`, so the drift predates the 3ed1d332 repin, fm-kpvx and fm-skpp.
- WildBirch's green workspace run at fb1c1b9e (a descendant of 6d4a4463) probably did not have the private corpus, so the seed scenes did not run there.

The scene (`_2025/colliding_blocks_v2/grover.py` GroverPreview) is:

- nine kets `Tex(Rf"|{sym}\rangle")`;
- amplitude bars;
- plays that combine FadeOutToPoint/FadeInFromPoint with `frame.animate`.

Find which change between 6a7de9f2 and 6d4a4463 added 52 family members. Compare per-root family sizes between wheels from both revisions. Then either fix a regression, or re-bless with `FMN_CORPUS_BLESS=1` and cite the cause, as the harness asks.

`cargo test -p fmn-python` passes the seed-module corpus test on a host with the private corpus. A re-bless commit names the change that moved the row.

title: W10: the certified closure (C4 resolved config) includes directories.cache, so --cache-dir changes the closure digest of byte-identical certified renders
description:
## Found by the fresh-eyes review of the typeset cache wiring (fm-typeset-cache-preflight-wiring-1sn0)

The certified closure item C4 ("resolved-config.fmnf", `crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs`
`publish_manifest` path, bytes from `fmn_config::Config::canonical_bytes`) includes
`directories.cache`. Two certified renders that differ only in `--cache-dir` (or the
config's `directories.cache`) publish byte-identical frames but different closure digests.

### Reproduction (macOS arm64, local debug `fmn` 0.5.0)

`fmn --robot --reproducible --format png_sequence --resolution 160x90 --fps 8 --threads 2
--cache-dir <A> --video_dir <dir> @builtin formula_sheet.v1`, then the same with `<B>`:

- cacheA: closure_digest 50398948…, artifact_digest 6b9f7308…
- cacheB: closure_digest 12b7262f…, artifact_digest 6b9f7308…
- cacheA again (warm): closure_digest 50398948… (same as the cold run)

The typeset cache's own contract is that a hit is bit-identical to a miss, so the cache
location is as inert as `render.threads`, which `Config::canonical_bytes` already
normalizes to a structural marker because §16.7 proves it inert. `--video_dir` does not
change the digest; `--cache-dir` does.

### Why it matters

A certified closure should name semantic inputs. With the cache location in it, two hosts
(or two users) that render the same scene with different cache roots cannot compare
manifests by closure digest, although every certified byte matches.

### Suggested fix (owner decision: it changes closure digests)

Normalize `directories.cache` in `Config::canonical_bytes` the way `render.threads` is
normalized, with a test that two cache roots give one closure digest and identical frames.
If manifest self-goldens pin a digest that includes a cache path, they re-derive in the
same commit, with the reason. This touches fmn-config and the manifest contract, so it
probably wants an ADR line.
close_reason: Fixed at 98d3e923 (auto-commit of R3b-FM's edit; merged in ffdf3eb9): Config::canonical_bytes writes directories.cache as the inert marker cache-location-proven-inert/v1, the way render.threads is. Positive at b27526fb (Linux, 16-thread unit on a 128-thread host): fmn-cli typeset_cache 8/8, a_warm_second_process renders a second --cache-dir root cold with identical frames and the same closure digest; fmn-config the_cache_location_is_normalized_but_every_output_input_still_binds passes (tex.template, text.font, directories.base, directories.subdirs.* and render.cache still separate configs). Planted negative (normalization removed): typeset_cache.rs:278 fails, closure 8103507… != 8af04bb…; config.rs:926 fails. Workspace cargo test at b27526fb green (3854 + the 4 libpython binaries rerun: e2e_scenarios 43, engine_equivalence 5, perf_pg8 14, fmn-python lib 108); clean-wheel gate exit 0. No manifest golden pinned a C4 digest, so none re-derived. No ADR authored (owner decision recorded on this bead).

title: W3: The Stage arena — generational handles, rooted lifetimes, CoW snapshots (G0-1 ratified)
description:
Implement Marionette's ownership core exactly as ratified by G0-1 (§8.1, D-11). The design under ratification: a Stage arena owning all mobject storage; generational Mob handles (index + generation, invalidating on free); rooted lifetime semantics (what keeps an object alive: scene membership, parent links, explicit roots held by user code); copy-on-write snapshots backing SceneState, animation begin-states (§9.5's frame-parallel purity depends on cheap begin-state snapshots), Studio undo, and replay barriers.

Required behaviors (the ten G0-1 scenarios become this bead's permanent regression suite): detached construction; cross-group composition; multiple parents with cached family flattening (submobjects / parents / family with dirty invalidation — §1.1 API surface); removal with live handles outstanding (handles observe a defined state, never UB); the two-scene policy (defined: an object's relationship to multiple scenes is whatever G0-1 ratified); copy; Python proxy identity across collection; updater closures holding handles; snapshot/restore.

The public fluent Rust API is what the G0-1 prototype PROVED — implement that shape, not a new invention (current lean: scoped stage context + deferred-command .animate recording, §15.1).

Interlocks: the RecordBuffer bead layers per-object data storage into this arena; the family/positional bead consumes the family cache; fmn-python's proxy layer (W10) maps PyObjects onto handles.

Acceptance: the ten-scenario suite green as permanent tests; CoW snapshot cost measured (O(touched), not O(scene)); generational-safety tests (stale handle access is a defined error); miri-clean under the workspace's no-unsafe posture (trivially, but assert it).
notes: In progress 2026-07-22: production arena landed in crates/fmn-mobject (stage.rs arena + family cache w/ dirty invalidation, record.rs = ratified V1-V6 view-protocol core seeding fm-cus, mobject.rs detached values). 14 tests green: ten G0-1 scenarios (permanent suite) + generational safety + O(touched) snapshot cost + family-cache invalidation + cycle refusal (typed error; Reference recurses forever on cyclic families — Behavior Note to finalize with fm-jru). Updater slot minimal by design (insertion order + call_now-once); full semantics are fm-yra. Miri run pending.

title: W1: Certified manifest integrity — dirty BUILD_ID, font/asset digests in C6, platform-neutral closure digest, unique item ids
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

`--reproducible` works end-to-end on one host: the published v0.4.0 binary produced byte-identical PNGs for `@builtin circle_shift.v1` at 1 and 16 threads, with an FMNP manifest (items C1-C10). But the manifest does not yet capture the complete input closure that plan §16.7 and docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md promise, and the cross-platform claim cannot be checked mechanically:

- Build identity: `BUILD_ID` is the git HEAD hash with no dirty-tree flag (`crates/fmn-cli/build.rs` ~38-79). With many agents editing a shared working tree, a certified manifest can name a clean commit the binary was not built from.
- Fonts/assets (C6): the native CLI hard-codes `Absent("font reads")` (`crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs` ~4976) even for Text/Tex scenes, although INPUT_CLOSURE.md says bundling is not an exemption. The Python portal's certified route (added in `223780ea`, 2026-09-19; `crates/fmn-python/src/portal_provenance.rs` ~359-377) also unconditionally claims no asset or font reads, while Python scenes can read SVGs/images/CSV freely.
- C3 includes `TARGET_TRIPLE` and target features (`lib.rs` ~4943-4950), so closure digests always differ across platforms: the manifest cannot mechanically prove "same closure, same bits" across linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64.
- C3 records `CARGO_PROFILE="build"` (profile-detection bug; fixed by the separate perf-profile bead).
- v0.4.0 manifests contain duplicate item ids (two items with `id = 2`: SUITE.lock and franken_manim.build) — check whether HEAD still does.

## Work

1. BUILD_ID: include a dirty flag and a content digest of tracked sources when dirty; `--reproducible` refuses (named capability error) to publish certified artifacts from a dirty or unidentifiable build.
2. C6: hash every font face, preamble pack and asset actually read (bundled or user-supplied) for native Text/Tex/SVG/Image scenes; portal route: record every file the Python scene reads through the portal's asset APIs, and refuse certification when a scene performs uncontrolled I/O the closure cannot capture (plan §15.5).
3. Split the manifest into a platform-neutral "semantic closure digest" (sources, config, seeds, fonts/assets, engine semantics version) and a platform-specific build record; the cross-platform promise is "equal semantic digest => equal bits", which a verifier can check.
4. Unique, stable item ids; a manifest schema test.

## Acceptance

- Manifest schema tests cover all four points with negative controls (dirty build refused; a Text scene lists its font digests; a Python scene reading an undeclared file is refused under --reproducible).
- A verifier command compares two manifests from different platforms and reports equal semantic digests + equal frame hashes (exercised by the certified-matrix re-run bead).
- docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md and docs/RUNTIME_PROVENANCE.md trued up in the same commit.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Register at least one e2e scenario as data in crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs (fm-fjq doctrine) exercising the user-visible behavior end-to-end, with deterministic structured NDJSON logs and an auto-bundled FMNA repro on failure; run it in the fast tier (or FMN_E2E_FULL=1 if heavy).
close_reason: All four items landed with evidence (4d7ce83f ADR-0025, 8ac7571b+6c933cc2, 55b04723, dca0d479/7da4bef7); installed-wheel gate exit 0; see comment

title: W1: Close the certified libm leak via fsci-integrate powf (StreamLines) and extend the arithmetic guard to suite crates
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

ADR-0010 rests certified determinism on four binding properties, the first being "fmn-dmath owns every certified transcendental". `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/certified_arithmetic.rs` enforces this by scanning non-test source in `crates/*/src` (excluding fmn-dmath and fmn-python) for ~30 transcendental and `mul_add` patterns. It does not scan FrankenSuite crates that run on certified paths:

- The pinned `fsci-integrate@5b1441b` RK45 step control (`rk.rs`) calls std `powf` four times.
- `crates/fmn-library/src/fields.rs` (~1072-1083) drives StreamLines/AnimatedStreamLines through that integrator, so platform libm re-enters the certified path for any scene with stream lines.
- `fmd-math` and `fmd-font` are clean by the same scan.

This is exactly the class of cross-platform divergence (glibc vs macOS libm vs wasm) that fmn-dmath exists to eliminate; it is invisible to every current test because the certified matrix has not run green since 2026-08-10 and no certified corpus scene uses StreamLines.

## Work

1. Extend the certified-arithmetic guard to the governed closure: scan the source of every suite crate reachable from a certified path (at the SUITE.lock pins), with an explicit allowlist of audited call sites and reasons.
2. For fsci-integrate: either (a) upstream a dmath-backed (or integer-exponent) step-size computation via UPSTREAM_LEDGER.md and bump the pin, or (b) refuse StreamLines under `--reproducible` with a named capability error until (a) lands. Decide in the bead; (b) must not be permanent without an ADR.
3. Add a certified self-golden scene with StreamLines once (a) lands, hashed on the certified matrix.

## Acceptance

- Guard fails on a negative control (a fixture suite source calling `f64::powf` on a certified path) and passes on the fixed tree.
- Either the upstream fix is pinned and a StreamLines certified golden is bit-identical on linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64, or StreamLines is refused under certified mode with a test.

title: W8: Harden cache clear ownership and dangerous-root refusal
description: The CLI cannot safely implement --clear-cache against the current Store API. Store::open can stamp an arbitrary configured path and Store::clear recursively removes its root. Add a fail-closed owned-root contract: canonicalize safely, reject filesystem roots, cwd, home, ancestors, symlinked roots, and foreign or unstamped roots; prove race and lifecycle behavior; expose a narrowly authorized clear capability for fmn-cli. Blocks fm-c53 clear-cache acceptance.

title: W10: Circle.get_radius ignores get_start/get_center (family centre) under an overlay row that says same
description:
## Found in the fresh-eyes review of fm-8pj7 (2026-10-09)

The pinned Reference (geometry.py) is:

    def get_radius(self) -> float:
        return get_norm(self.get_start() - self.get_center())

`get_start` is TipableVMobject's tip-aware, overridable accessor. `get_center` is the centre of the
family bounding box, so it includes submobjects.

The portal's `Circle.get_radius` calls the native `_circle_radius`. That measures the first anchor of
the circle's own points from the centre of those own points, and dispatches through neither method.

Probe, an installed wheel at c580fd60: `c = Circle(radius=1); c.add(Dot(3 * RIGHT))`.
- Portal: `c.get_radius()` is 1.0.
- Reference formula, evaluated on the same portal object: 0.04. The family centre is x = 1.04.

API_OVERLAY.tsv marks Circle.get_radius `same` ("measures the live transformed first anchor from the
current bounding-box center"). The portal value is the geometrically meaningful one, but the
divergence is not labeled. Circles that carry children (labels, dots, tips) are where it shows.

## Work

Rule on this method. Either:
- follow the Reference through the public `get_start()` and `get_center()`, as fm-8pj7 did for the
  angle getters and fm-circle-point-at-angle-dispatch-7dbb did for `point_at_angle`; or
- keep own-points measurement as a Behavior Note, with the overlay row moved to `improved`.

Test: a Circle with a child Dot and a subclass that overrides `get_start`. Planted negative: the
current wheel.

title: W10: Circle.point_at_angle bypasses the overridable get_start_angle and point_from_proportion
description:
## Found in the fresh-eyes review of fm-8pj7 (2026-10-09)

The pinned Reference (geometry.py, `Circle.point_at_angle`) is:

    start_angle = self.get_start_angle()
    return self.point_from_proportion(((angle - start_angle) % TAU) / TAU)

It is the only Reference caller of `get_start_angle`, and both calls dispatch through overridable
methods. The portal's `Circle.point_at_angle` called the native `_circle_point_at_angle`, which
measured the raw first anchor and walked the native path. A subclass that overrides either method
was ignored:

- `class Q(Circle): get_start_angle -> TAU/4`; `Q(radius=2).point_at_angle(PI/2)`: portal (0, 2, 0),
  Reference formula (2, 0, 0).
- `class P(Circle): point_from_proportion -> (9, 9, 0)`; `P().point_at_angle(0)`: portal (1, 0, 0),
  Reference formula (9, 9, 0).

The overlay row says `same`, so the gap was unlabeled.

## Fix

The bootstrap computes the Reference formula through `self.get_start_angle()` and
`self.point_from_proportion()` (BN-03's true arclength, as before). The now-unused native
`_circle_point_at_angle` is removed. `fmn_library::arc::point_at_angle` stays as Rust library API.

## Acceptance

- bridge.py's Circle block checks both overrides. Planted negative: the pre-fix wheel fails it.
- For untipped and tipped circles, Dot and Ellipse, the outputs are bit-identical to the pre-fix
  wheel at 47 angles each.
close_reason: Fixed in 09fdd4c2 (content-identical dc0b232f is also on main via peer merge ffdf3eb9). Circle.point_at_angle computes the Reference formula through self.get_start_angle() and self.point_from_proportion(); the unused native _circle_point_at_angle is removed. Re-executed on a shared Linux host with ffmpeg 8.0.1. (1) Workspace cargo test --no-fail-fast at local main ffdf3eb9: exit 0, 271 binaries, 4000 passed, 0 failed, 11 ignored; this includes production_bridge_acceptance_suite, which runs bridge.py with the new override checks. (2) Clean-wheel gate (scripts/check_portal_runtime.sh) on a release wheel at 3267b308 (origin 8eb1c20e plus the four review commits): exit 0; bridge.py passed, the class sweep had 288 compared and 0 failing with no stale exclusions, and the runtime audit passed with 2007 rows. (3) Planted negative: the pre-fix wheel fails the new check with (0, 2, 0) where (2, 0, 0) is expected. (4) Untipped and tipped Circle, Dot and Ellipse outputs are bit-identical to the pre-fix wheel (329 points). Follow-up: fm-circle-get-radius-family-center-tkiz.

title: W9: Route 3D/camera content (Surface, DotCloud, Image, CameraFrame) through the fmn CLI — CameraRequired today
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

G3 ("Depth & Motion") promises 3D surfaces with the kept lighting, CameraFrame, depth/transparency/clip planes, dot clouds, images and textures. Lumen implements them (`three_d.rs`, `camera.rs`; `finalize_color` at three_d.rs ~166), and Studio and the Python portal reach them through `render_with_camera`. The standalone `fmn` CLI cannot:

- Every CLI frame goes through `RetainedFrameRenderer::render(stage, 0)` (`crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs` ~3978-3979) with camera revision hard-coded to 0 (~3971-3973).
- `render` rejects Surface, DotCloud and Image content with `CameraRequired` (`crates/fmn-render/src/retained.rs` ~210-224). `rg 'render_with_camera|ThreeDJob|CameraRequired' crates/fmn-cli crates/fmn/src` returns nothing.
- All 25 builtins are 2D, so no test notices; no test renders an FMTL bundle containing 3D content through the CLI.
- `CameraRequired` would surface to a CLI user as a "lumen" integration error, not a capability exit naming the cause.

## Work

1. Route CLI (and the facade render API, if landed) through the camera-aware path when the scene contains camera-requiring content or a non-default CameraFrame; carry the real camera revision into the retained plan.
2. Add builtins exercising a Surface with lighting, a DotCloud/GlowDot, an ImageMobject, a moving CameraFrame, and depth-tested overlap; add them to the self-golden corpus with certified hashes at {1,4,16} threads.
3. Map any remaining camera-path refusal to a named capability exit (never an integration error).
4. FMTL: ensure bundles carry camera state and 3D resources, with a round-trip test through `fmn` and the WASM player (player may refuse 3D with a named capability error if not supported).

## Acceptance

- New 3D builtins render through `fmn --format png_sequence` and `--reproducible`, thread-invariant, self-golden locked, Look-Gallery panel added for the lit surface.
- e2e scenarios registered (render-matrix + determinism classes).
- G3 (fm-o4q) evidence packet can cite the CLI, not only Studio/Python, for 3D.

title: W9: fmn CLI UI flags change exported timing (-f/--autoreload write 30-fps frames into a 60-fps file, -p drops frames) and -e/--show_animation_progress/--leave_progress_bars are silent no-ops
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check

Some Reference flags that the standalone `fmn` CLI accepts are **silently ignored**, and three of them **change the exported video's timing**. Both break the CLI contract (§13.6, BN-15). An accepted flag must either do what it says or fail closed with a capability error naming the alternative (D2's rule, applied to flags).

### Measured (shipped v0.5.0 `fmn`, 2026-10-04)

Each run used `fmn <flag> --fps 60 --format y4m --resolution 320x180 @builtin circle_shift.v1`.

| Flag | Frames written | y4m header | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| (none) | 23 | `F60:1` | correct |
| `-f` | **12** | `F60:1` | 30 fps clock in a 60 fps container: plays at 2× speed |
| `--autoreload` | **12** | `F60:1` | same as `-f` |
| `-p` | **8** | `F60:1` | wrong frame count; presenter mode changes exported content |
| `-e 3` | 23 | `F60:1` | silently ignored |

### Cause (read from source)
- `crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs:355-356`: `runtime.windowed = !self.write_file || self.presenter_mode || self.full_screen || self.autoreload;`
- `crates/fmn-scene/src/runtime.rs:113-116`: `effective_fps()` returns 30 whenever `windowed` is set. That is the Reference's preview-window override. The output sinks, however, keep the configured fps, so the clock and the container disagree.
- `crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs:1395-1409`: `-f`, `--show_animation_progress`, `--leave_progress_bars` and `--autoreload` only write config keys (`window.full_screen`, `scene.show_animation_progress`, `scene.leave_progress_bars`, `embed.autoreload`) that nothing in the standalone binary reads. `-e`/`--embed` is accepted and has no effect.
- `-p`: the default `HoldController` is `ImmediateRelease` (`fmn-scene/src/runtime.rs:514-526`), so presenter mode has no interactive meaning in a file render, yet it still alters the frame schedule.

### What to do
1. **Timing coherence first.** A windowed or UI flag must never change the frame schedule of a written file. When `write_file` is true, the clock and the sinks use one fps. Decide whether the Reference's windowed 30 fps override applies only to preview/Studio, and record the ruling in BN-15.
2. **No silent acceptance.** For each of `-e`, `-f`, `-p`, `--autoreload`, `--show_animation_progress`, `--leave_progress_bars`, either:
   - implement its meaning in the standalone binary (progress bars are easy; `--autoreload` could hand off to `fmn studio`); or
   - refuse it with exit 4 and a message naming the alternative (for example "use `fmn studio` for live reload").
   Update `docs/api/cli_flags.md` and `API_OVERLAY.tsv` statuses through the schema generator.
3. Audit every remaining CLI flag for "writes a config key nobody reads". A small generated test over the schema's flag→config-key table can assert that every key is consumed, or that the flag is marked refused.

### Acceptance
- **CLI contract tests** (`crates/fmn-cli/tests/`):
  - for each flag above, either the meaningful effect is observed, or exit 4 with the named alternative;
  - with `--fps 60`, every accepted flag combination writes `ceil(duration × 60)` frames with a matching header.
- **Schema test:** every flag-produced config key has a reader or the flag is marked refused (no orphan keys).
- **e2e scenario** (failure-path class) for one refused flag and one timing-coherence case.
- **Logging:** each test prints the argv, the resolved runtime config (fps, windowed, write_file) and the observed frame count and header.
- **Gates:** cargo fmt/clippy/test green; BN-15 updated.
close_reason: Acceptance met. Refusals 461d760c/e43a0135/282f483f. Since then: dd60ca4e adds cli_smoke every_flag_written_config_key_has_a_reader_or_a_refused_flag (every key resolve_render_config writes has a reader outside fmn-config, or its flag is refused and exercised by the refusal test; planted negatives for an unread key and an unexercised refused flag) and e2e failure_path.cli_window_flag_refused_timing_kept.v1 (-p exits 4, nothing published; plain --fps 60 render F60:1, 23 frames). d4b85dfd adds logging: each refusal-test run prints argv, the resolved fps/windowed/write_file, and the exit code or header rate and frames. The log shows -p/-f/--autoreload resolving windowed=true on a file render, the original mistiming, and all three now exit 4. BN-15 amended earlier. Gates: cargo test -p fmn-cli --features batch --all-targets green at d4b85dfd; workspace check.sh green apart from the fixed dispatch drift. Self-verified only.

comments.text: Fix landed (461d760c, e43a0135, 282f483f): file renders refuse -p/-f/--autoreload/-e and the two progress flags with exit 4 before any output; OOT-CLI-WINDOW and OOT-CLI-PROGRESS rows; BN-15 amendment; schema artifacts regenerated (api_schema 22/22). cli_smoke window_and_progress_flags_are_refused_and_never_mistime_a_file_render passes against the built binary (plain --fps 60 y4m: F60:1, 23 frames; each refused flag: exit 4, nothing published); v0.5.0 exits 0 on the same inputs. Still open from the acceptance: the schema-level orphan-config-key check (every flag-produced config key has a reader or the flag is refused) and a registered e2e failure-path scenario.

title: G0-8 route decision: the W5 chain is gated on hardware this program does not have
description:
STRUCTURAL BLOCKER, filed 2026-07-24 from a triage observation, not from a code defect.

bv ranks fm-5xm (W9 Scene runtime) the highest-value open bead in the graph — betweenness 100%, unblocks fm-39s/fm-c53/fm-eiw. Its dependency chain is fm-5xm <- fm-hv4 <- fm-3df <- fm-tg6 <- {fm-gw7, fm-jsc} <- fm-ekx. fm-jsc is now closed; every other link is open, and the ROOT of the chain, fm-ekx (G0-8, the accelerator proof spike), requires Apple silicon with Metal via frankentorch. The development machine is linux-x86-64 with no NVIDIA GPU either (nvidia-smi absent), so fm-ekx as written cannot be executed here at all. The entire W5 render-IR lineage and the W9 scene runtime therefore sit behind a spike that no available machine can run.

This needs a decision, not more waiting. The options, for the record:
(a) Execute fm-ekx on an Apple-silicon machine (the plan's intent: §20.1 spike 8, §10.7, §17.5). Needs hardware access.
(b) Execute the CUDA-via-ft half instead, on a Linux box with an NVIDIA GPU, and record the Metal half on the upstream ledger. §2.9/§10.7 already frame CUDA as a ledger spike, so this is a re-ordering of the annex's two backends, not a new claim. Needs a CUDA machine.
(c) Split fm-ekx: land the parts that need no GPU — the written IR-to-GPU mapping report (which IR tables/stages translate cleanly, which need layout changes, fed back into §10.8's design NOW, which is the spike's actual purpose) and the CUDA ledger item with its feasibility notes — and record a dated, public deferral of the executed-frame half under OQ-12's declared CPU fallback (GOVERNANCE §5's leapfrog-postponement policy, whose clause 1 says postponement never weakens core work). Then fm-gw7 unblocks on the mapping report rather than on a Metal frame.

(c) is the only option executable today and is the one the postponement policy is written for; it must be a recorded ruling (ADR or a dated note in the G0 epic), never a silent re-wiring of the dependency graph. The acceptance criteria of the executed half travel unmodified to whichever gate takes it.

Acceptance: the route is chosen and recorded (ADR if it amends a decision or resolves OQ-10/OQ-12's opening, otherwise a dated note in fm-3g6); if (c), fm-ekx is split with the deferred half re-pointed at its gate and fm-gw7's dependency updated to the artifact that actually gates it.
close_reason: Route (a) chosen and recorded: execute fm-ekx unmodified on Apple silicon. The bead's premise — 'hardware this program does not have' — was half right. This dev box (sensedemobox, x86-64, 64c, Matrox G200eH3 server VGA) indeed has neither Metal nor CUDA. But the program owner confirmed the fleet and mac-mini-max is reachable from here over SSH right now: Apple M4 Pro, Darwin 25.2.0 arm64, 14c/64GiB, with the SUITE.lock nightly-2026-07-05 pin installed and a live Metal compiler (Apple metal 32023.830). That is §17.6's Apple-silicon exemplar and the machine §20.1 spike 8 was written for, so no split, no deferral, no re-wiring: fm-ekx executes as written and is now unblocked. Per GOVERNANCE §3 this is a dated note on fm-3g6, not an ADR — nothing in the decision log is amended and no OQ is resolved. Options (b) and (c) declined with reasons on the record. Two operational findings carried onto fm-ekx: (1) mac-mini-max has no FrankenSuite checkout at all, so provisioning from SUITE.lock is the spike's step zero, and ft's Metal backend must be proven to build on pin e4c6bdd before kernels are written; (2) the 'trj' alias in this box's ssh config is STALE (HostName localhost -> resolves back to sensedemobox), so the owner's dual-4090 machine is NOT reachable here — the only reachable NVIDIA part is ts2's GTX 1070, fine for a CUDA feasibility probe but not PG-A's RTX-4090-class profile. Also recorded for §17.2: PG-A's Apple-silicon annex profile is now identified as an M4 Pro (Pro-class, not Max-class — pin it honestly), and both core PG profiles are satisfiable today.

title: W3: The RecordBuffer — interleaved f32 records, the live-view protocol, and lazy revisioned render mirrors
description:
Implement Marionette's data plane (§8.2, §1.1, D-20). Three layers, one bead, because their contracts interlock:

(1) THE AUTHORITATIVE BUFFER: interleaved f32 records with typed field views, matching the Reference dtypes exactly — [(point f32x3), (rgba f32x4)] for Mobject; the VMobject layout with stroke_rgba/stroke_width/joint_angle/fill_rgba/base_normal/fill_border_width; Surface/DotCloud/Image declaring their own; USER-DECLARED custom dtypes through the schema machinery. This layout is API surface: mobject.data is a zero-copy NumPy structured export (fnp-dtype is a structured-record engine — this is its native representation). Port field-for-field: aligned_data_keys / pointlike_data_keys, data locking as copy-elision, resize-with-interpolation, null-padding family alignment.

(2) THE VIEW PROTOCOL (G0-1-ratified): exported views pin their buffer; resize is copy-on-resize (old views detach with NumPy-natural semantics); mutation through a view marks render state dirty; reallocation under a live view is impossible by construction. While a WRITABLE live view exists, the affected object (or field, where the view is field-scoped) is conservatively invalidated each frame — a live view never silently receives weaker semantics to buy speed. Ranged editing APIs (edit_points(range, ...)-class) exist as the precise-dirty opt-in.

Acceptance: zero-copy NumPy round-trip tests (via fnp); view-protocol scenario tests (resize under live view, field-scoped dirty, ranged edits); mirror coherence property tests (mirror ≡ buffer at every observation point); mirror laziness tests (untouched fields never materialize); custom-dtype end-to-end test.

title: W8: macOS ffmpeg probes intermittently fail with 'process-tree completion kill failed: Operation not permitted' (~2.5% under concurrency) — Darwin EPERM race in asupersync kill_process_tree; e2e python_portal_native_outputs red
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (macOS 26, Apple M4 Pro, a certified platform)

**On macOS, about 2.5% of ffmpeg capability probes fail under concurrency with:**

```
ffmpeg: unavailable at "ffmpeg" (... cannot execute as an identity-bound private copy:
I/O plumbing to .../fmn-bound-ffmpeg failed: process-tree completion kill failed:
Operation not permitted (os error 1); use a relocatable/self-contained ffmpeg build)
```

### Reproduction (outside any sandbox, release `fmn` at 96b7b7c8, Homebrew ffmpeg 8.1.2)

- 40 serial `fmn doctor` runs: 40 OK.
- 80 runs, 10-way parallel (8 rounds × 10 concurrent): **2 report "ffmpeg: unavailable"**.
- The workspace `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` run on the same host failed `render_matrix.python_portal_native_outputs.v1` (`crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs:6562`) with the same error. A `MissingSound.mp4` render returned `render-capability-unavailable` (exit 4), so 10 assertions failed downstream. The red e2e is this race, not a portal regression.

The message is also misleading. It says to "use a relocatable/self-contained ffmpeg build" when the ffmpeg build is fine.

### Root cause

The chain runs from `fmn-platform/src/process.rs:2355` (`supervise_child` completion kill) through `kill_process_tree` (`:2196`) into asupersync `ExactImagePlatformChild::kill_process_tree` (pinned `c48399f`, `src/process.rs` ~934). On Darwin:
- `killpg(pg, SIGKILL)` returns `EPERM` when no group member can be signalled.
- The pinned fix then calls `try_wait()` on the leader and treats `Ok(Some(_))` as "group gone".
- **But there is a window where the leader is already unsignalable (exiting) and not yet reapable**, so `waitpid(WNOHANG)` returns 0. `try_wait` gives `Ok(None)`, and the code escalates to a hard `EPERM` error.

There is no bounded retry for that transient. The window widens under load: the host here ran at load average 20–90.

### Work

1. **Upstream** (UPSTREAM_LEDGER row; asupersync branch `fmn/darwin-exact-image-spawn`): on Darwin `EPERM` plus `try_wait() == Ok(None)`, retry `killpg` + `try_wait` with a short bounded backoff before returning `EPERM`, e.g. 1 ms, 2 ms, 4 ms … with a total deadline of about 100 ms. Only a leader still live at the deadline keeps `EPERM` a real error. Repin per R17.
2. **fmn-platform**: until the repin lands, an equivalent bounded retry in `kill_process_tree` for `ErrorKind::PermissionDenied` on macOS only. D3 holds: no unsafe; the retry is just control flow.
3. Make the doctor and capability message distinguish "probe plumbing failed transiently" from "ffmpeg is not relocatable".

### Acceptance and tests

- A stress test (`#[ignore]` locally, run in the owned-host gate): 500 concurrent probe spawns on macOS, **zero** plumbing failures.
- The e2e `render_matrix.python_portal_native_outputs.v1` passes 20/20 consecutive runs on a loaded macOS host.
- The unit test for the retry policy uses a fake platform child that returns EPERM n times and then exits.
- No behavior change on Linux (zombies are signalable there; the path is cfg(macos)).

title: W10: PrimeRace's remaining 2.5x is O(scene) Python-object work per frame (admission own-dict checks, has_updaters on animation copies); O(changes) needs observable instance-dict and updaters mutation
description:
## Measured (2026-09-30, ec956bf0 wheel, WildGoose)

PrimeRace runs 224.5 s against the Reference's 91.0 s on the same frame grid (fm-5wq.31 table), down from >900 s. On a ~19K-member scene, the profile's remaining per-frame Python-object work is:
- Scene._fmn_requires_public_scene_update: about 15 ms per frame. The loop is native since 0f859ea8, but it still checks every member's own __dict__ for hook names and reads every member's submobjects.
- has_updaters() on animation copies: about 1.3 ms of _path_family plus 4 ms of _any_updaters per call, once per animation per frame (Animation.update_mobjects -> mob.update -> the Reference's early-return check).
In a flat perf profile, PyObject_GenericGetAttr, PyDict_Contains and list iteration dominate the main thread.

## Why these stay O(scene)

The Reference answers both from cached state: Scene.mobjects is a plain list, and _has_updaters_in_family is invalidated by add_updater and friends. The portal answers from live truth, because neither change is observable today:
- an instance can gain a hook name (mob.update = f, or vars(mob)['update'] = f) with no signal;
- updaters is a plain list that authors mutate directly (mob.updaters.append(f)).

An exact O(changes) answer needs those signals. Candidates:
- a live updaters list (like _LiveSubmobjects) plus interception of the updaters assignment;
- an instance hook registry fed by the bridge's __setattr__.
Each leaves a documented hole for direct __dict__ writes. That is a Behavior-Note decision, and it belongs to the native dispatch protocol of fm-5wq.15.

## Acceptance

- After that protocol decision: admission and has_updaters cost O(changes) per frame, shown by a work counter that fails on ec956bf0. For example: members visited by the admission scan on an unchanged frame.
- PrimeRace same-work ratio within 2x.
