title: W2: QuadPath — the shared-anchor path model, formalized with exact fixtures first
description:
Implement Chisel's path model (§7.1, §1.2). VMobject paths are joined quadratic Béziers over a SHARED-ANCHOR layout: points = [a0, h0, a1, h1, a2, ...], length odd when nonempty, curve i = points[2i..2i+3], subpath break = a null curve whose anchor equals its handle. This invariant is API SURFACE — curve counts, partial reveals, alignment, and user code indexing points all depend on it — so it is implemented formally, with exact fixtures for empty / one-point / one-curve / closed / multi-subpath paths BEFORE any higher-level geometry lands (the fixture-first ordering is the W2 exit rule).

Also here: consider_points_equal tolerance and VectorizedPoint degeneracies preserved as API behavior; anchor modes (jagged / approx_smooth / true_smooth) and the smoothing solvers — banded solve for open paths, dense for closed (via fsci-linalg); arc primitives under ONE arc-density convention (the Reference has three inconsistent ones; ours is the unified rule, Behavior Note BN-09 — coordinate with the W7 geometry bead which consumes it); subdivision; per-vertex joint angles.

Design notes: object-space construction and the geometry APIs compute in f64 (§6.1); the QuadPath type is the shared vocabulary of Chisel, Marionette's point data, Scribe's glyph outlines, and Lumen's compiled paths — get the API right here and everything downstream composes.

Acceptance: invariant fixtures green (including adversarial: zero-length curves, coincident anchors, single-point subpaths); smoothing-solver tests against known closed forms; the arc-density rule documented with BN-09 drafted.
notes: Landed 2026-07-22: QuadPath in crates/fmn-geom (src/quadpath.rs) with bezier/cubic/smoothing/vec/scalar modules. Invariant fixtures (tests/invariant_fixtures.rs) + Reference structural parity (tests/reference_parity.rs) against fixtures generated by scripts/gen_geom_fixtures.py from a gitignored checkout of the pinned Reference at scripts/manim_ref (real VMobject driven headlessly; see script docstring for the uv env). BN-09 drafted at docs/behavior_notes/BN-09-arc-density.md (one rule: max(1, ceil(16|θ|/TAU))). Deliberate divergences: (1) joint angles for <3-point paths are 0.0, not the Reference's np.ones data-default artifact (D5, noted in reference_parity.rs); (2) true_smooth uses the Reference's own two-quad fallback until fm-6cf wires the error-bounded converter (note added to fm-6cf); (3) smoothing solves are temporary owned banded/dense GE pending fsci-linalg (follow-up fm-go7); (4) transcendentals funnel through src/scalar.rs pending fmn-dmath (follow-up fm-hbq). point_from_proportion/arc length deliberately NOT here (fm-xci owns the proportion layer).

title: W5: Zero steady-state per-frame allocation in the certified engine (PG-6)
description:
PG-6 requires zero steady-state heap allocations per frame, over bump arenas and pooled buffers (§10.8, §17.2). The certified CPU engine (fm-ig3) does not meet it yet, and the three places are known:

1. FrameJob::new builds a Vec<Draw> per frame, and each Draw owns a Vec<JoinWedge> and an Option<GradientField> (which owns two Vecs). For a text-heavy scene that is thousands of small allocations per frame.
2. render_into collects a Vec<(usize, &mut [u8])> of bands per frame.
3. Each worker allocates its Worker scratch (acc, cov, RowScratch) once per render_into call rather than once per pool.

None of these can change a bit — they are all storage, and the arithmetic is unchanged — so this is purely the §17 'eliminate work' rung and it is safe to do behind the existing goldens (crates/fmn-conformance/goldens/certified_engine.certified.lock will catch any accident).

Shape: a per-frame bump arena owned by the caller, threaded into FrameJob::new, plus a Worker pool keyed on tile width. Wants to land with or after fm-3df, which owns the ExecutionPlan that would size the pools.
close_reason: Per-frame bump arena + worker pool; zero steady-state heap allocations proven via engine counters; goldens untouched

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: LANDED (AllocWorker, Main-verified). ZERO steady-state per-frame heap allocation in the certified engine, with arithmetic untouched and every golden bit-lock intact. THE THREE SITES, per the bead: (1) Draw storage -> new crates/fmn-render/src/arena.rs FrameArena with typed bump pools (Pool<T> = one Vec truncated per frame, capacity retained — no unsafe, so typed pools instead of a raw byte arena); Draw now carries PoolRange indices (why the arena can be owned outright, no self-reference); geometry builders generic over a Sink<T> trait (Vec impl for retained paths, Pool impl for the counted path — one loop definition feeds both, so bit-lock cannot drift); PreparedStroke/GradientField are borrowed views. (2) bands Vec -> eliminated entirely: plane.chunks_mut(band_bytes).enumerate() IS the work queue (Mutex<Enumerate<ChunksMut>> threaded / direct serial) — bytes proven identical at every thread count. (3) Worker scratch -> WorkerPool in the arena: one typed sub-pool per monomorphized kernel (no type erasure), PooledWorker guard returning the slot on Drop, sizing converges to the render-team size on the warm-up frame. PG-6 SURFACE for fm-inr.3's producer: pub FrameJob::allocation_stats() / FrameArena::stats() -> AllocStats { heap_allocs_this_frame (exact — every pool Vec growth counted, no allocator shim), arena_buffer_bytes (constancy = buffer allocated once), pool_slots }; FrameJob::new_in/with_identity_in for the arena path (existing ~25 callers untouched). EVIDENCE: steady_state_frames_allocate_nothing on a glyph-heavy corpus (48 glyphs, join-wedge + gradient + transformed-segment pools all exercised, 4 threads): frames 2..=4 report heap_allocs_this_frame == 0, arena_buffer_bytes and pool_slots identical to warm-up, frame digest identical. Gates: fmn-render + fmn-conformance 28 suites green with ZERO golden re-blessing, clippy -D warnings 0, fmt, ubs Critical 0.

title: W7: The de-TeX'd natives, text-backed half — DecimalNumber, Matrix, BulletedList, Title, controls
description:
Split out of fm-y69 on 2026-07-25. fm-y69 landed the half of §12.3 that needs no typesetter (Brace/BraceLabel/LineBrace, SurroundingRectangle, BackgroundRectangle, Cross, Underline, Checkmark, Exmark, and the per-point stroke taper and detached positional layer they needed). THIS bead carries the half that routes through native text, whose acceptance criteria travel UNMODIFIED from fm-y69 per GOVERNANCE §5 clause 2.

BLOCKED ON fm-p5d (the Scribe bridge). Nothing here can start until TextLayout/Typeset become VMobjects.

DECIMALNUMBER / INTEGER — pure native text. Reference ctor (numbers.py:34): number=0, color=DEFAULT_MOBJECT_COLOR, stroke_width=0, fill_opacity=1.0, fill_border_width=0.5, num_decimal_places=2, min_total_width=0, include_sign=False, group_with_commas=True, digit_buff_per_font_unit=0.001, show_ellipsis=False, unit=None, include_background_rectangle=False, hide_zero_components_on_complex=True, edge_to_fix=LEFT, font_size=48, text_config={}. The GLYPH-RECYCLING seam is set_submobjects_from_number: when the digit count is unchanged it does sm.become(smt) in place rather than rebuilding, which is what makes a ticking counter not re-typeset every frame — W5IR's interning is the mechanism. Formatting edge cases that need a corpus: negative-zero suppression (num_string.startswith('-') and rounded_num == 0), the '-' to U+2013 EN DASH substitution, comma grouping, min_total_width zero-pad, the complex formatter, unit starting with '^' aligning UP, the ',' glyph shifted down by half its height, \\dots when show_ellipsis. Layout is arrange(RIGHT, buff=digit_buff, aligned_edge=DOWN) with digit_buff = digit_buff_per_font_unit * font_size. set_value restores edge_to_fix position and style. Integer is num_decimal_places=0 with get_value rounding to int.

MATRIX FAMILY — Matrix, DecimalMatrix, IntegerMatrix, TexMatrix, MobjectMatrix (matrix.py). Element grid via x_step=(max_width+h_buff)*RIGHT, y_step=(max_height+v_buff)*DOWN, elem.move_to(i*y_step + j*x_step, aligned_corner) — VMobject::moved_to_aligned already exists for this, landed by fm-y69. Brackets come from fmd-math's extensible-delimiter engine: typeset the Reference's own \\left[\\begin{array}{c}...\\end{array}\\right] with the row count, then set_height(rows.height + v_buff) and next_to(rows, LEFT/RIGHT, h_buff). ADR-0005's three-stage mechanism (natural glyph, uniform scale to delimiter_scale_ceiling=1.25, drawn path beyond) means the delimiters scale correctly BY CONSTRUCTION — crates/fmn-tex/tests/scribe2.rs already proves a pmatrix produces 2 drawn paths. Constants are public on fmd_math::MathConstants (canonical instance fmd_math::metrics::CM). Also get_column/get_row/get_columns/get_rows/set_column_colors/get_entries/get_brackets/get_ellipses, and swap_entries_for_ellipses(height_ratio=0.65, width_ratio=0.4).

BULLETEDLIST / TITLE (svg/special_tex.py). BulletedList(*items, buff=MED_LARGE_BUFF, aligned_edge=LEFT, numbered=False) + fade_all_but(index, opacity=0.25, scale_factor=0.7); the Reference uses \\begin{itemize}\\item and isolate=, ours composes on Scribe with our own bullet glyph and VMobject::arranged(DOWN, buff, LEFT). Title(*text_parts, font_size=72, include_underline=True, underline_width=FRAME_WIDTH-2, match_underline_width_to_text=False, underline_buff=SMALL_BUFF, underline_style=dict(stroke_width=2, stroke_color=GREY_C)) — the underline half already exists as fmn_library::matchers::underline.

INTERACTIVE CONTROLS (interactive.py): MotionMobject, Button, ControlMobject, EnableDisableButton, Checkbox, LinearNumberSlider, ColorSliders, Textbox, ControlPanel. Note ControlMobject IS a ValueTracker and fmn_mobject::dynamics already has the whole surface (add_value_tracker, tracker_value, set_tracker_value, increment_tracker_value, always_redraw, f_always). Event wiring lands with W9EVENTS; CONSTRUCT the compositions here.

Acceptance (carried from fm-y69, unmodified for these classes): Matrix layout fixtures (spacing/alignment vs Reference conventions) with delimiter-scaling tests; DecimalNumber formatting edge-case corpus + a glyph-recycling test proving an update does not re-typeset; structural fixtures for the remaining classes; BN-08 extended in place (docs/behavior_notes/BN-08-de-texed-natives.md already exists and says these land later).
close_reason: All four text-backed de-TeX'd class families landed on the Scribe bridge with the carried acceptance criteria met: Matrix layout fixtures + delimiter-scaling tests, DecimalNumber formatting corpus + glyph-recycling proof, structural fixtures for BulletedList/Title/controls, BN-08 extended in place

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: LANDED (GentleBeaver + 4 workers). FOUR NEW fmn-library MODULES, all on the fm-p5d Scribe bridge — no TeX anywhere: (1) numbers.rs: DecimalNumber/Integer, Reference ctor surface verbatim; formatting corpus ported case-for-case (negative-zero suppression, '-' to U+2013 en-dash with vertical reseat, comma grouping with the ',' glyph dropped half its height, min_total_width zero-padding WITH CPython's re-grouping overshoot verified against live Python for 15 cases, U+2026 ellipsis as one glyph child, unit '^' UP alignment). GLYPH RECYCLING: per-char cache (each char typeset once ever), typesets() counter as the witness — build(12.0)->4, set_value(21.0)->4 (no re-typeset), proven by test. Integer.value() rounds half-to-even (np.round); display truncates like the Reference. Complex formatter + TeX units honestly out (documented). (2) matrix.rs: Matrix/DecimalMatrix/IntegerMatrix/TexMatrix/MobjectMatrix. Grid via the Reference's x_step/y_step math + moved_to_aligned. BRACKETS: the Reference's own \left[\begin{array}{c}... source through fmd-math's delimiter engine (ADR-0005); pair located by Prim::Path identity in the drawn stage, Reference half-split fallback in glyph stages; rescaled_to_fit(rows.height + bracket_v_buff) + next_to. Defaults corrected to the Reference's actual values (v_buff 0.5, h_buff 0.5, bracket_h_buff 0.2, bracket_v_buff 0.25, corner DOWN). Delimiter-scaling tests rows 1..8, bracket height == rows.height + v_buff to 1e-9, glyph->drawn stage transition asserted. (3) special_tex.rs: BulletedList (native Text bullet U+2022 — bundled faces MAP it, checked; numbered '1.' labels; fade_all_but formula verbatim over the new family-recursive VMobject::map_style_deep) and Title (parts joined then re-grouped by source span via TextLayout::select so part i stays addressable; underline stroke 2 GREY_C at SMALL_BUFF, width FRAME_WIDTH-2 or text width). (4) controls.rs: the interactive.py constructions — ControlMobject + ScalarControl trait + add_scalar_control (Stage binding via always_redraw, the pattern dynamics.rs ratified), MotionMobject, Button, EnableDisableButton, Checkbox (drawn check/ex marks), LinearNumberSlider (clamping set_value, value_from_point pure half), ColorSliders (Reference checkerboard rule), Textbox, ControlPanel. Event hooks deferred to W9EVENTS, each NAMED in module docs. vmobject.rs gained map_style_deep (approved in-flight) + map_children. BN-08 extended in place (Status: landed both waves; Matrix bracket + DecimalNumber cache sections; migration notes for unit-as-text, typed matrix variants, Option accessors). Gates: cargo test -p fmn-library --lib 174/0 (67 new), fmt 0, clippy -D warnings 0 on workspace-minus-fmn-output (their mid-flight refactor: 26->13 test errors, E0609/E0061/E0046, no dependency on this bead's code; fmn-platform/tests/capabilities.rs ProcessOutcome adaptation I made mechanically, one scripted-runner logging-expectation failure left for FuchsiaPlateau as THEIR semantic call, mailed), ubs Critical 0 on the whole changed set (also fixed two pre-existing panic! criticals in vmobject.rs/matchers.rs tests). Unblocks fm-i1q (G2 gate), fm-jh7, fm-v4l, fm-3kr, fm-wy1.

title: W7: Bound de-TeX number and matrix dimensions
description: The recovered text-backed W7 surface still trusts public usize dimensions. DecimalNumber min_total_width repeatedly inserts zeroes until the requested width and can allocate pathologically; MobjectMatrix computes n_rows times n_cols unchecked in construction, slicing, mutation, and child-capacity paths, so overflow can panic or corrupt shape accounting. Add typed resource-limit and overflow errors, use checked arithmetic before every allocation or slice bound, keep ordinary Reference behavior unchanged, and add maximum, just-over-limit, and usize boundary tests.
close_reason: Implemented bounded native number and matrix dimensions with typed refusals.

title: W9: Make fmn-platform capability tests and atomic directory publish Windows-correct
description: Native windows-x86-64-msvc CI (run 31033744170, jobs 92400559533) fails 4 fmn-platform capability tests. Two are test bugs: scripted_runner_replays_and_logs and scripted_stream_preserves_chunk_order_and_enforces_both_input_bounds use the fixture program path /fake/ffmpeg, which is not absolute on Windows, so the scripted runner refuses with ProgramNotAbsolute before exercising anything; fixtures need per-OS absolute spellings (the host_bin pattern from the Darwin fix, or a drive-letter fake). Two are real Windows semantics defects in the std atomic publish capability: std_atomic_directory_concurrent_commit_is_no_clobber sees BOTH racers lose (assertion 'exactly one no-clobber commit must win' with false/false), and std_streaming_atomic_file_and_directory_publish_only_at_commit gets os error 5 Access is denied publishing the host generation — classic Windows rename-over/sharing-violation behavior the no-clobber commit path must handle (retry on ERROR_SHARING_VIOLATION, ensure handles closed before rename, map the winner/loser outcomes correctly). Acceptance: all four tests green on native windows-x86-64-msvc CI; no behavior change on Unix; UBS and repo gates green. Parent context: fm-x4pp acceptance requires the Windows functional leg.
close_reason: CI-proven: native windows-x86-64-msvc capability suite 21/21 including all four target tests (job 93290070263, run 31331370770, and three further green heads). Fix 937211b: sync_directory opens with GENERIC_WRITE + FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS (FlushFileBuffers refuses read-only handles); fake_ffmpeg() per-OS absolute fixture; targeted allow for windows-only clippy::zombie_processes. Unix unchanged; workspace windows-gnu clippy sweep clean.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Root causes identified and fixed (commit staged locally pending the in-flight CI run for the Darwin pin bump). (1) sync_directory on Windows opened the directory handle read-only; FlushFileBuffers refuses read-only handles with ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED — this alone explains both 'real' failures: streaming publish died syncing, and in the no-clobber race the create_dir winner died at the parent sync so both racers reported loss (false/false). Fix: GENERIC_WRITE + FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS. (2) /fake/ffmpeg is not Windows-absolute; fake_ffmpeg() helper now spells fixtures per-OS. Plus targeted allow for pre-existing windows-only clippy::zombie_processes on the deliberately-unreaped job-parent fixture. Unix unchanged (34/34); windows-gnu check + strict clippy clean. Awaiting native msvc CI for the functional verdict.

title: W9: Events + InteractiveScene — the dispatcher and the interaction surface
description:
Implement interactivity (§13.2, §1.4): the event dispatcher (EventDispatcher/EventListener/EventType — registration, propagation, listener ordering per the Reference) and InteractiveScene's behaviors: selection (click/drag-rect selection of mobjects, selection highlight rectangles), grab/move, resize, color-picking, clipboard copy/paste of mobjects, keyboard-map COMPATIBLE with the Reference's bindings (the muscle-memory surface: users' hands know these keys).

Consumers: the Studio (W9STUDIO) forwards browser/TUI input events into this dispatcher; the interactive control mobjects (W7DETEX's Button/Checkbox/sliders/ControlPanel) register listeners here; MotionMobject/Textbox behaviors.

Design care: events interleave with the frame loop at a DEFINED point (they run in the serial front-end, before capture — they are scene-state mutations and pipeline barriers when they must observe pixels per §13.4); event handling in a paused/presenter-hold state has defined semantics; the dispatcher is deterministic under replay (the journal records event streams with timestamps on the rational clock — replaying a session re-fires events identically, §13.4's contract).

Acceptance: dispatcher unit tests (registration/removal/ordering/propagation); InteractiveScene behavior tests against scripted event streams (select → drag → resize → color → paste, asserting scene-state outcomes); keyboard-map fixture vs the Reference's bindings; replay determinism test (recorded event stream re-applied ⇒ identical final state); frame-loop interleaving test (events never mutate mid-capture).
close_reason: Acceptance implemented; full local fmt, check, clippy, and cargo test gates exit 0; qualified UBS findings recorded in issue comment.

title: W8: SVG export (vmobject_to_svg) — gated on the W2 SVG document processor
description: The fm-65l tail: vmobject_to_svg — trivial by design since paths are native quads (emit path data + styles), with documented fidelity limits (gradients per our model, no filter effects). Split out because the acceptance criterion is a round-trip through our own SVG importer (export → import → structural equality within tolerance), and the W2 hardened SVG document processor has not landed. Implement in fmn-codec (or alongside the importer) once the W2 bead ships; wire the round-trip test then.
close_reason:
Landed at 3138689: SVG export alongside the importer in crates/fmn-geom/src/svg.rs — emit_path_data (M + one Q per shared-anchor curve; Z on self-closed subpaths, where the importer's close_path is idempotent so Z re-imports without a degenerate segment), emit_style_attributes (every resolved style field written explicitly in fixed order — the round-trip never depends on importer defaults), emit_svg / emit_svg_document, all re-exported at the fmn-geom root.

Documented fidelity ruling: resolved shapes live in post-viewBox/preserveAspectRatio user space, so emit_svg_document deliberately does NOT re-emit the viewBox record — a re-emitted viewBox would make re-import apply the mapping twice (caught by the viewbox_default_meet corpus case during development). The emitted geometry IS the final user space. Colors round-trip through 8-bit hex (the importer's own grammar); the round-trip test uses the corpus's 4-decimal dump for structural equality.

Acceptance wired: tests/svg.rs::every_golden_case_round_trips_through_the_emitter runs the WHOLE golden corpus parse->emit->parse and asserts dump equality plus byte-idempotence of a second emit; closure_state_survives_the_round_trip pins open-stays-open / closed-stays-closed (stroke-visible). Gates: fmt clean, clippy -p fmn-geom --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo test -p fmn-geom => 244 passed / 0 failed. A VMobject-level convenience wrapper (Style->SvgStyle mapping with the stroke-width conversion) is left for the W7/W8 integration surface that exposes export to users — this bead's round-trip contract is complete at the document level.

title: G0-8: Accelerator proof spike — stroke SDF + AA resolve as frankentorch Metal kernels into a Studio-preview frame
description:
Compile-tested spike proving the render IR maps to a GPU BEFORE W5 freezes it (§20.1 spike 8 → §10.7, §17.5; resolves OQ-10's opening; risk R21 context). Rev 4 moved this from W5-time to G0 deliberately: discovering IR/GPU mismatch late would be expensive, and discovering it after CPU-specific assumptions harden would be worse.

Scope: express the render IR's highest-ROI stage — stroke signed-distance evaluation + AA resolve (the dominant cost of typical 2D scenes, per-pixel independent) — as frankentorch kernels on Metal, running end-to-end into an actual Studio-preview frame on Apple silicon: IR upload through ft shared buffers (unified memory makes the handoff nearly free), kernel dispatch, composite, present. Simultaneously open the CUDA-via-ft feasibility question as an upstream-ledger item (§2.9) — the annex's second backend is spiked on the ledger before any production claim.

Hard constraints that survive regardless of outcome: the annex is standard-mode ONLY, never certified (D-18's permanent refusal of GPU in the certified path); excluded from core gates; measured under its own PG-A profiles; backend identity journaled into the input closure; frankentorch is the ONLY GPU gateway — no wgpu ever (a dependency of that size is a D1 audit catastrophe and duplicates ft).

Acceptance: a Metal-rendered preview frame demonstrably produced from the prototype IR; a written mapping report — which IR tables/stages translate cleanly, which need layout changes (feed those changes back into the §10.8 IR design NOW); the CUDA ledger item filed with its feasibility notes; go/defer recorded for G3's annex-preview requirement (G3 has a declared CPU fallback if the annex misses — OQ-12).
close_reason:
G0-8 delivered in full: a Metal-rendered Studio-preview frame produced from the prototype render IR on Apple silicon, the written IR->GPU mapping report, the CUDA ledger item with feasibility notes, and the go/defer record. Verdict: GO for the Accelerator Annex.

WHAT LANDED. spikes/g0-8-accelerator (non-member, ADR-0003 dev tier, own committed Cargo.lock, 36 tests green on linux-x86-64 AND macos-aarch64): the prototype compiled render IR (§10.8 subset — SegmentTable/PathTable/StyleTable/TileGrid/CSR per-tile command lists, plus the Metal-shaped FlatIr derivation), the CPU reference engine, the MSL kernel, the §16.3 equivalence measurement, and a preview scene built to exercise curvature, the Line primitive hint, joins, round caps, arc-length width tapers, translucent painter-order overlap and a sub-pixel hairline. Report: docs/g0/G0-8-accelerator-ratification.md. Renders: docs/g0/g0-8-renders/.

THE MEASUREMENT (Apple M4 Pro, 960x540, tile 16, 30 paths / 164 segments / 2040 tiles):
  CPU f32 vs CPU f64 (arithmetic floor): max_u8 152, 200/2073600 differing (0.0096%), ssim 0.999949
  Metal vs CPU f64, MathMode::Safe:      max_u8 152, 201/2073600 differing (0.0097%), ssim 0.999949
  Metal vs CPU f64, MathMode::Fast:      max_u8 184, 235/2073600 differing (0.0113%), ssim 0.999790
Read rows 1 and 2 together: under safe math the Metal engine's ENTIRE divergence from the reference is what f32 does to the algorithm — the GPU contributes one differing component in 2,073,600. That is a controlled experiment, not an inference: sdf::distance_to_quadratic_f32 is a literal f32 transcription run on the CPU, so the annex's numerical behaviour is testable in CI on a machine with no GPU.

THE FINDING THAT WAS NOT IN THIS REPO. frankentorch had no route to a GPU for a consumer's own kernel — only sgemm and the fused NN ops behind fixed entry points — so D-22's "ft is the only GPU gateway" and "the annex runs its own kernels" were flatly contradictory, with standing pressure on the D1 closure to admit a second, far larger GPU dependency. Closed upstream as ft-kernel-metal::compute (UPSTREAM_LEDGER row 8): compile caller-supplied MSL, unified-memory buffers, dispatch, readback, all unsafe contained in ft, no new dependency, stubbed off macOS. The spike kept #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. Landed as a local frankentorch commit; push + SUITE.lock pin bump + class=ffi rows are fm-xsz's §2.9 steps 3-5, so the spike consumes it BY PATH and says so in its Cargo.toml.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED, all of which W5 would otherwise have inherited:
  F7 Rust's signum(0.0)=1.0 vs MSL's sign(0.0f)=0.0f collapsed the stable-quadratic pairing to a double root at zero on the GPU alone. Both engines now write the predicate longhand; regression test added.
  F8 An absolute 1e-12 degeneracy threshold is a bug only the f64 engine cannot see: at screen scale a near-straight curve's leading cubic coefficient lands ~1e-8 in f32, so the shader entered the cubic branch and divided by noise. Thresholds are now relative to coefficient scale and sized per engine precision. Two robustness changes rode along.
  F9 Metal compiles fast-math BY DEFAULT. Measured: it doubles rms error and adds 17% more differing components for no measurable time saving. The upstream gateway now defaults to MathMode::Safe — a deliberate reversal of the platform default, because half the §16.3 budget was being spent on a compiler flag nobody had chosen.

F10, THE FINDING WITH THE LONGEST REACH, IS NOT ABOUT THE ANNEX. The 200 surviving components sit at two symmetric spots on one curve — a Lissajous's turning points, where the distance function is near-degenerate and the general quadratic solve is ill-conditioned. 0.0096% at ssim 0.99995 is comfortably inside any budget §16.3 will write for a standard-only annex. But fm-4wt's FAST CPU ENGINE is licensed to use mixed precision under §6.1, and this is the quantified warning: f32 in the stroke SDF costs visible error at curvature extrema on a mainstream curve at ordinary widths. The G0-5 spike's PyO3 graph pins syn 2; this spike's Metal graph pins syn 3 through foreign-types-macros, and neither can move — so one non-shipped spike's transitive constraint would have vetoed another's. ADR-0008 rules rows are keyed by (name, version), with both halves pinned by tests: an unlisted VERSION still fails, and two listed versions coexist. 16 new class=dev rows plus a path row for ft-kernel-metal.

OQ-10 resolved -> ADR-0007: CUDA-via-ft WAITS on upstream ft device work, on two named preconditions (the gateway's buffer API must generalize to device-resident handles with delta upload, since unified memory is an Apple luxury and §17.6 wants a resident scene; and D1 must rule on shipping precompiled PTX). Plan §23 trued up in the same commit per GOVERNANCE §3. OQ-12: recommendation recorded on fm-3g6 that G3 will not need its annex-preview fallback — the decision stays G3's. D-22 stands unamended; every constraint held (standard-only, never certified, PG-A only, backend identity journaled in AnnexReport, ft the only gateway, no wgpu).

FILED: fm-orn, the analytic-fill GPU mapping spike, which the report's §5 names as the one deferred item needing its own spike before W5 commits to a fill layout — fills are per-SCANLINE with an ordered area accumulation, not per-pixel independent, so nothing about the stroke result transfers for free. title: W10: graphing/graph_queries/vector_fields wheel protocol tests broken since 6915ef65 (relative import + stale native doubles)
description:
Observed 2026-09-24. Installed-wheel suite (`python -m unittest discover` in crates/fmn-python/tests,
CPython 3.13.1 + NumPy 2.5.2): 2026/2029 pass. Three tests fail to load:
test_graphing_protocol, test_graph_queries_protocol (imports the first) and test_vector_fields_protocol.
Error: `ImportError: attempted relative import with no known parent package`.

Cause 1, the loader. The tests load the source adapter standalone via
importlib.util.spec_from_file_location("graphing_under_test", ...). 6915ef65/db766ba9 added
package-relative imports to fmn_python/graphing.py (`from .invocation import InvocationGuard`), and
vector_fields.py has the same pattern. Verified fix: load it as a submodule, with
spec_from_file_location("fmn_python.graphing_under_test", ...), after ensuring `fmn_python` is importable
(the installed package, or insert the source python/ dir). fmn_python/__init__ and invocation.py import only
the stdlib, so no native extension is needed.

Cause 2, stale doubles, exposed once the loader is fixed. 67 of 81 tests then error, because the tests'
native geometry doubles no longer match the adapter. Example: graphing.py:176 `before = current.data.copy()`
fails with AttributeError on the fixture's VMobject double, which has no `.data`. The doubles must be brought
up to the adapter's current contract, in the same change as the loader fix, so the suite never regresses from
3 load errors to 67 test errors.

Acceptance: all three modules load and pass against the source adapter and against an installed wheel;
the full wheel suite reports 0 errors.
close_reason: Fixed in d256b2ba. The source adapters now load as fmn_python submodules, and the doubles gained data/get_family/_is_bound/pointlike_data_keys; guard assertions read InvocationGuard.busy and _STYLE_TARGETS. Evidence: test_graphing_protocol, test_graph_queries_protocol and test_vector_fields_protocol 81/81 on CPython 3.14 (source tree) and CPython 3.13 (portal package importable). The full installed-wheel suite (discover, CPython 3.13.1 + NumPy 2.5.2, portal built from a HEAD tree) ran 2107 tests OK, 97 skipped, 0 errors; before it was 2026/2029 with 3 load errors. Verified by the same agent that made the fix; no independent verifier.

title: W9: Public render API in the fmn facade (extract RenderSink from fmn-cli) so the README Rust example produces frames
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

Plan §15.1 makes the Rust API "a first-class, CPython-free front door". A native Rust user can author a scene today (the README example's symbols all exist and the README's rust block runs as a doctest via `crates/fmn/src/lib.rs:43`; `crates/fmn/examples/square_to_circle.rs` mirrors it), but cannot get pixels out through any public API:

- The README example ends in `run_scene(..., &mut NullSceneSink)` — it renders nothing.
- `crates/fmn/Cargo.toml` depends on fmn-core/config/platform/geom/mobject/anim/text/tex/library/scene only — not on `fmn-render` or `fmn-output`.
- The only pixel-producing `SceneSink` is `RenderSink`, private inside the ~9,600-line `crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs` (~3736, capture at ~4181).
- `export_timeline_bundle` (`crates/fmn-scene/src/timeline_bundle.rs` ~929) takes the lower-level `Timeline + Stage`, not a `SceneConstruct`; its only callers are the WASM demo and conformance.
- Python has `render_scene(Scene, "x.gif")` (docs/PROGRAMMATIC_RENDERING.md); Rust has no equivalent. A Rust user must depend on internal crates and re-implement ~400 lines of sink.

## Work

1. Extract the offline render sink (materialize -> Lumen -> frame conversion -> ordered emitter -> PNG/PNG-sequence/GIF/y4m/WAV/ffmpeg publication + manifest) out of `fmn-cli` into a reusable component in `fmn-output` (or a new module of the facade crate if the §19 DAG requires), with the CLI becoming a thin caller. No behavior change for the CLI (prove with existing CLI e2e + byte-identical certified outputs before/after).
2. Public facade API, e.g. `fmn::render(&mut scene, RenderOptions { format, resolution, fps, threads, output, determinism }) -> fmn::Result<RenderReport>`, re-exported in the prelude.
3. Update the README Rust example and `examples/square_to_circle.rs` to actually write frames; make the doctest assert the artifacts exist and are non-uniform.

## Acceptance

- The README Rust example, compiled as a doctest and as an example, writes a PNG sequence whose frames decode, differ across time, and contain upright text (asymmetric-glyph orientation assertion).
- `fmn` CLI outputs for all 25 builtins are byte-identical before/after the extraction under `--reproducible` at 1/4/16 threads.
- e2e scenario registered in `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs` (render-matrix class).
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.

title: W10: Point-less mobjects ignore positional operations (Reference: an empty VGroup shifted/moved/next_to reports the moved center)
description:
## Found by the Appendix-A class sweep (fm-5wq.26), 2026-09-27

In the pinned Reference, a point-less mobject keeps a position through positional operations. In the portal it stays at the origin. Measured in both engines:

| code | Reference `get_center()` | portal |
|---|---|---|
| `g = VGroup(); g.shift(2*RIGHT)` | (2, 0, 0) | (0, 0, 0) |
| `g.move_to(3*UP)` | (0, 3, 0) | (0, 0, 0) |
| `VGroup().next_to(Square(), DOWN)` | (0, −1.25, 0) | (0, 0, 0) |

The class sweep shows it inside `BarChart([1, 2, 3])`: an empty label group at path 0.4 has its bbox center at (−2.593, −5.75) in the Reference and at the origin in the portal.

Scene code commonly creates empty groups as placeholders, positions them, then positions other mobjects relative to them (`next_to(group)`, `group.get_center()`, `arrange` with empty members) or adds children later. In all of those, the portal places things differently.

## Work

Give point-less mobjects the Reference's positional state: the bounding box that `shift`/`scale`/`move_to`/`next_to`/`align_to`/`rotate` update, and that `get_bounding_box`/`get_center` report while there are no points. Find out how the Reference stores it at the pin (for example a bounding-box record kept when points are empty) and match its semantics when the first points arrive.

## Acceptance

- An installed-wheel regression reproducing the table above with the Reference's values. Planted negative: fails at 35c65d6e.
- The class sweep shows `BarChart#1` equal. The open-bead row citing this bead is removed.
- The corpus differential's geometry tier: scenes whose first difference is a point-less member's bbox fall to zero.

title: W10: Harden generated agent-brief temporary-file ownership against inode reuse
description:
The generated agent-brief publisher remembers only `(st_dev, st_ino)` for its owned temporary file. A failed replace can unlink that file, recreate a foreign file at the same path, receive an immediately reused inode, and trick cleanup into deleting the substitute. Bind cleanup to a post-write metadata fingerprint while retaining ordinary failed-replace cleanup.

Acceptance:
- Ownership includes device, inode, final size, mtime_ns, and ctime_ns.
- The fingerprint is refreshed through the still-open descriptor after write/flush/fsync.
- An ordinary replace failure removes the publisher-owned temporary.
- A substituted path is preserved and emits the stable identity-changed diagnostic.
- Deterministic inode-reuse and end-to-end substitution regressions pass with the complete agent control-plane suite.
close_reason: Temporary ownership is now bound to a post-write device/inode/size/mtime/ctime fingerprint. Ordinary failed replacements clean up their owned file, substituted paths survive with the stable identity-changed diagnostic, and the complete agent control-plane acceptance slice passed.

title: W9: Keep interactive clipboard handles valid across undo
description: InteractiveScene stores copied mobject templates as detached handles inside the live Stage, while its single undo record stores only a whole-Stage Snapshot. If a clipboard copy is created after the saved snapshot, Ctrl-Z restores the older arena and leaves InteractiveClipboard pointing at stale handles, so the next paste silently produces nothing and overwrites the undo point. Replacing a mobject clipboard or switching to host text also leaves the superseded detached family resident in the arena. Make clipboard replacement reclaim complete detached families, bind the clipboard identity to the undo state restored with its Stage snapshot, and preserve valid copy/paste behavior across undo without accumulating replaced templates. Acceptance: repeated copy invalidates and releases the superseded template family; text replacement releases mobject templates; undo restores a clipboard whose handles exist in the restored Stage; paste after undo creates the expected scene root; replay remains deterministic.

Reality-check evidence at source HEAD 03d7bde84a974a9373dccaf9a336cd93c1bbd99b: the closed fm-xsz acceptance requires Studio preview to use the Metal annex on supported Apple hardware with an explicit CPU fallback, and crates/fmn-studio/src/preview.rs already contains StudioPreviewRenderer/NativePreviewRenderer plus that fallback. The shipped composition root does not use it: crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs NativeStudioWorker::from_command maps ExecutionEngine::Metal or Cuda to the capability error "the selected annex engine has no production Studio renderer" (around lines 2714-2721), while derive_execution_plan rejects standard render.engine=metal as having no verified compiled backend (around lines 1556-1560). This makes the production claim and the closed implementation bead disagree.

Wire the existing fmn-studio StudioPreviewRenderer into the native Studio worker/composition root; do not create another renderer or relax certified-mode GPU refusal. Standard-mode Metal should use native presentation on supported Apple silicon, record the actual backend identity, and fall back to the existing fast-CPU stream on unavailability/failure exactly as the completed renderer specifies. Browser/terminal CPU-visible streams remain explicit.

Acceptance: (1) supported Metal builds no longer hit the generic production-Studio refusal; (2) non-Metal/Linux tests exercise the declared CPU fallback and preserve a useful reason; (3) certified+metal still fails before side effects; (4) the actual route/backend identity is journaled; (5) a real Studio E2E scenario covers the composition seam; (6) fm-xsz and G3 evidence can cite the shipped front door rather than a library-only proof.
acceptance_criteria: Production fmn studio composes through the existing StudioPreviewRenderer: native Metal on supported Apple, explicit fast-CPU fallback elsewhere, certified GPU refusal unchanged, route identity journaled, and a real Studio E2E scenario green.
close_reason: Native Apple Metal/no-readback, shipped Studio first-frame, truthful CPU fallback, backend identity, and certified refusal proofs are complete at exact current source.

title: W9: Validate inline PNG frames before preview publication
description: At exact HEAD ce221315aff89f362b601ff9b0861506914cf814, FrameStream::validate checks an inline PNG payload's digest, signature, and zero stride only. FrameHub::publish then clones those bytes, checks the host byte ceiling only after the clone, and publishes the worker-declared width and height without validating the PNG container or binding its IHDR dimensions. A corrupt or dimension-mismatched worker frame can therefore enter retained host history and the browser multipart stream under false metadata. Searches found no Beads owner or regression. Acceptance: enforce the host PNG-byte ceiling before clone or codec work; validate complete inline PNGs with the owned codec under the declared frame pixel count; require decoded width and height to equal FrameStream metadata; preserve the raw-RGBA conversion path and valid multipart bytes; reject corrupt, over-pixel, and equal-area dimension-mismatch PNGs without advancing publication sequence or altering history; admit exact byte/pixel boundaries; add focused regressions; run focused Studio gates, mandatory repository wrapper, git diff check, and UBS; land only host source and Studio tests while preserving shared WIP. Use no DSR, RCH, GitHub CLI, or GitHub Actions.

title: W9: Connect native Studio input to live InteractiveScene state and replay
description:
At source fbf66bf6, the native Studio genuinely renders, scrubs, inspects and restarts, but NativeStudioWorker::handle in crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs rejects every SupervisorRequest::Event with "the selected native preview artifact has no live command/event adapter". InspectorView advertises input_events=false. The real browser acceptance intentionally verifies this refusal. Plan sections 13.2 and 13.5 promise selection, grab, resize, color and clipboard behavior through Studio. The closed fm-eiw supplies the dispatcher/InteractiveScene mechanism; fm-ffj.71 supplies the browser controls. Neither proves a positive browser-to-native-scene input path. fm-ffj.70 separately owns host-Python worker composition and must not become a prerequisite for CPython-free native interaction.

Deliver one production native interactive scene registration/worker adapter over the existing event dispatcher, scene runtime, journal and immutable capture boundary. Advertise input only for adapters that implement it. Retain explicit refusal for immutable FMTL and other unsupported artifacts. Map stable worker-generation identities and object handles so stale browser events cannot affect restarted scenes. Drain/render barriers when input observes pixels; journal accepted input in deterministic order at the rational clock boundary. Keep all engine and CLI operation CPython-free and the existing loopback/token/Origin/Host/budget protections.

Acceptance: launch the actual shipped fmn Studio in a real browser, select a nested object, drag/move it, resize, recolor, copy/paste and undo using the documented keyboard map. Assert both decoded rendered pixels and inspected scene state change correctly. Pause and resume, scrub/replay the accepted input, restart from a checkpoint and prove identical final state. Inject a stale-generation event, a stale handle, malformed input, budget overflow and unauthorized request; require named bounded refusals and no mutation. Prove unsupported immutable artifacts still refuse and never advertise a false capability. Unit tests cover adapter routing and generation/boundary behavior; register a positive native interactive lifecycle E2E with deterministic logs and FMNA repros. Existing negative-only browser tests remain. Run the ordinary complete scripts/check.sh through strict RCH on unchanged committed source, scoped UBS and the real browser driver before closure. PG-4 timing needs separately qualified pinned-host measurements; this task supplies functionality, not a timing or G3 verdict.

Scope: W9/G3 implementation follow-up under fm-ffj; closed fm-eiw and fm-ffj.71 are existing mechanisms to reuse, not new frameworks to replace. No Python worker, CUDA, new runtime dependency, new renderer or weaker security policy. This is a remaining integration leaf, not reopening already-proven browser inspection functionality.

title: W10: The Gauntlet e2e harness — scripted end-to-end scenarios with detailed structured logging
description:
Build the END-TO-END test harness that every epic's beads register scenarios with — the program-wide answer to "how do we KNOW it all works together after implementation":

THE HARNESS: scripted e2e scenarios driven through the REAL surfaces (the fmn CLI, the Rust API, fmn-python, the Studio's HTTP surface, the batch runner) — never through test-only backdoors — each scenario a checked-in script/manifest declaring: the scene/inputs, the invocation (flags, config, determinism mode, engine), the ASSERTIONS (bit-locked hashes via the self-golden rig for certified paths; structural assertions — object counts, timings, envelopes — for standard paths; exit codes; emitted-file inventory; NDJSON schema validation for robot outputs), and the LOG EXPECTATIONS (see below). Scenario classes to seed: render-matrix (formats x quality x reproducible x engine, vs fake-ffmpeg and native sinks); determinism drills (same scene at {1,4,16} threads and twice-in-a-row ⇒ identical bytes, wired into PG-5); failure-path drills (ffmpeg absent ⇒ named capability error; unsupported TeX construct ⇒ precise error; corrupt cache ⇒ recovery; worker crash ⇒ supervisor restart); lifecycle drills (edit→rebuild→restore→replay; checkpoint_paste; scrub); Python-vs-Rust parity drills (the same scene through both front doors ⇒ identical structural results).

DETAILED LOGGING AS A TESTED CONTRACT (§17.1, §18): every e2e run captures the owned structured-tracing output (scene→play→frame→phase→tile spans, stage timings, counters, decision points: engine selected, ExecutionPlan derived, cache hits, purity classifications, barriers) into a per-run artifact; scenarios ASSERT ON LOGS where behavior is otherwise invisible (e.g. "the preflight typeset N strings before frame 0", "the wait() frames hit the tile cache", "the segment classified pure") — so a regression in the machinery, not just the pixels, fails the run; on ANY failure the harness auto-bundles the repro (scene + input closure + logs + journal tail per §18's repro-bundle machinery) so every red e2e run is a one-command deterministic replay.

DOCTRINE (binding, cross-referenced from every epic): each feature bead registers at least one e2e scenario when it lands user-visible behavior; unit tests live in-crate with the bead; the harness runs the fast tier per-commit and the full matrix nightly (CI budgets per R22).

Acceptance: the harness + scenario format + log-assertion machinery running in CI with the seed scenario classes above; the repro-bundle-on-failure path demonstrated; per-epic registration documented in AGENTS.md's testing section; a deliberately-injected regression drill per scenario class (break it → red with useful logs → repro bundle works).
close_reason: e2e harness + 31-spec seed catalog + registration doctrine landed; all gates green

title: W5/W10: Behavior Note + Appendix C entry for the Reference's x0.95/x1.06 fill round-trip (0.70% overshoot)
description:
G0-2 (fm-k77, finding L3 and the follow-ups section) measured a systematic defect in the Reference's fill compositing that we do NOT inherit, and it should be recorded so the difference is never mistaken for a colour bug in our renderer.

THE DEFECT: quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl:32 scales fill alpha by 0.95 before the signed-alpha winding blend (to bound the -a/(1-a) singularity at a=1), and shader_wrapper.py:489 un-scales the resolved texture by 1.06. The exact inverse of 0.95 is 1.0526315789...; 1.06 x 0.95 = 1.007, a 0.70% OVERSHOOT applied to rgb AND alpha of every fill in every frame the Reference has ever rendered.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE: our analytic fill has no winding-blend scaling at all, so there is nothing to un-scale. Any side-by-side of a filled shape will therefore show our fill ~0.7% darker/less opaque than the Reference's, uniformly. That is us being right, but a reviewer comparing pixels without knowing this will read it as a colour regression.

DELIVERABLE: an Appendix C row (Reference-defect register) and a line in BN-04, both citing shader_wrapper.py:489 and fill/frag.glsl:32. Evidence is in docs/g0/G0-2-look-study-ratification.md section 8.
close_reason:
DONE. Two Appendix C rows and a BN section, all evidence-backed.

C-12 — the 0.70% fill overshoot. quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl:32 scales fill alpha by 0.95 before the signed-alpha winding blend (bounding the -a/(1-a) singularity at a=1) and shader_wrapper.py:489 un-scales the resolved texture by 1.06. The exact inverse of 0.95 is 1.05263..., so the round trip is 1.06 x 0.95 = 1.007: a 0.70% overshoot applied to rgb AND alpha of every filled shape in every frame the Reference has ever rendered. Our analytic fill has no winding-blend scaling, so there is nothing to un-scale — meaning a side-by-side shows our fills uniformly ~0.7% darker and less opaque. Written up as a full section in BN-04 (the colour note, where a compositing difference belongs) with the trace, and cross-referenced from BN-06's fill note so a reviewer measuring a filled panel does not read a systematic 0.7% as a regression in our colour pipeline.

C-13 — the swapped joint constants, added while here because it is the same class of finding and it turned up in fm-oac's work an hour earlier. stroke/geom.glsl:110-122: BEVEL_JOINT (code 2) sets miter_factor=0, giving shift = -tan(θ/2), the POINTED corner; MITER_JOINT (code 3) sets miter_factor=1, giving +cot(θ/2), the blunt one. The names are swapped relative to the geometry the shader produces, corroborated by G0-2's captured apex widths (auto 4 px, bevel 6 px, miter 9 px — miter visibly blunter). There is also no miter_limit constant anywhere. Ruling recorded in the row: our names mean what they draw, with auto's measured de facto limit of sqrt(10) adopted as the real one (ADR-0012, BN-06-strokes.md).

Appendix C had eleven rulings; it now has thirteen. Both rows carry file:line citations and their ruling, matching the register's existing shape.

title: W8: fmn-cache — the content-addressed store
description:
Implement the persistent cache (§14.4): content-addressed on fmn-hash — atomic writes (write-temp + rename, never partial visibility), cross-process locks (two fmn invocations share a cache safely), per-entry checksums verified on read, versioned namespaces (a schema/version bump invalidates cleanly without clearing unrelated namespaces), corruption recovery (a bad entry is evicted and recomputed, never trusted, never fatal), traversal protection (keys never map to paths outside the cache root), defined eviction (LRU-class with pinning for in-use entries), size ceilings (config-visible).

Serves three consumers with one discipline: TYPESET RESULTS (fmd-math + text layout, keyed on string + preamble-pack hash + font hashes + engine version — W6TEX's contract; the dominant win, PG-7's <100µs cached path); FETCHED ASSETS (through the AssetFetcher capability — cached by content hash with the fetch policy recorded); THE REPLAY JOURNAL's storage (§13.4 — journal segments and checkpoint snapshots live under a cache namespace with pinning while a session is live).

Determinism interaction: a cache is an OPTIMIZATION, never an oracle — certified renders must produce identical output with a cold or warm cache (the key includes everything semantic, so a hit is definitionally equivalent; test it), and --clear-cache (the Reference flag, kept) must be safe at any moment.

Acceptance: atomicity tests (kill -9 mid-write leaves a consistent store); cross-process lock test (two writers, no corruption); corruption-injection tests (flipped bytes detected, evicted, recomputed); eviction/ceiling tests with pinning; cold-vs-warm equivalence test on a typeset-heavy scene; traversal fuzz on keys.
close_reason: The content-addressed store is real: crates/fmn-cache/{lib,key,entry,store}.rs over the fs/clock capabilities — no ambient I/O anywhere. Addresses are SHA-256 of canonical key material (KeyBuilder over fmn-hash serial: fixed field order, framed fields, canonicalized floats, domain separation, self-golden address lock) or of content itself (blobs self-certify). Entries ride the checksummed serial envelope recording kind+address, so flipped bytes, truncation, garbage, AND a valid envelope at the wrong path all classify corrupt → evicted, miss, never fatal (every-byte-flip test). Atomic writes via write-temp+rename; cross-process safety by construction for put/get (content-addressed idempotence) plus an advisory per-namespace maintenance lock with wall-clock staleness breaking (fresh→skip, stale/garbage→break; non-blocking, FakeClock-scripted). Versioned namespaces ns/<name>/v<N> with auto-purge of stale versions, unrelated namespaces untouched. LRU-class eviction on a logical access sequence (never wall time) with shared PinSets, config-visible ceilings, Manual policy for the journal ns; advisory index is merge-flushed and disk-truth-reconciled (lost/corrupt index degrades LRU, never correctness). Traversal protection: validated names + digest-hex-only paths, adversarial+LCG fuzz asserts the shape. Cold-vs-warm equivalence + read-only-cache tests pin the never-fatal contract; get_or_compute swallows cache trouble, surfaces only compute errors. clear() (--clear-cache) safe at any moment, format-stamped store with precise FormatUnsupported refusal. FileSystem capability grew create_new (atomic-content via hard-link)/remove_file/remove_dir_all; torture tests (2 store openings, 7 threads, real StdFs) caught+fixed a genuine pre-existing write_atomic temp-name collision (pid-only unique → pid+seq). 58 tests green (14 unit + 35 deterministic acceptance + 2 host torture ×5 stable + doctest + 6 platform), full gate green, ubs criticals all false-positive (test panics, advisory-token pattern matches). Scene-level cold/warm equivalence on a typeset-heavy scene lands with fm-7dw (consumer). Fuzz-harness follow-up filed as fm-tdp (rides fm-ntp infra).

title: W1: fsci-linalg solve certificate's two_prod uses mul_add (FMA) on fmn's solve path; property 2 forbids FMA. Upstream a Dekker/Veltkamp TwoProduct or argue the certificate out
description:
Found 2026-10-11 by the certified-arithmetic guard after its parser fix (fm-wi8l): signatures with array types had hidden functions from the reachability walk.

At the frankenscipy pin 85edd7a, every portfolio solve runs certify_accuracy (fsci-linalg lib.rs:3211), which calls residual_and_magnitude, which calls two_prod. two_prod computes the exact error of a*b as a.mul_add(b, -p) (lib.rs:2393). ADR-0010 property 2 (section 10.5d) keeps FMA off certified paths, and the guard counts this site with fm-bp82's twelve Cholesky-kernel sites, 13 mul_add in fsci-linalg lib.rs.

What it affects: only SolveResult.certificate (the accuracy section: componentwise backward error and forward bound). fmn-geom smoothing.rs reads x, and acceptance is decided before the certificate is built. IEEE fma is correctly rounded, so the value is platform-independent wherever mul_add is a true fused operation.

Options:
(a) Upstream, replace two_prod's FMA with Dekker's TwoProduct over a Veltkamp split (+, -, * only; exact barring overflow in the split, |a|,|b| < ~1e300). Certificate bits stay exact, and the site leaves with the next pin bump.
(b) Argue in certified_arithmetic.rs that certificate values never reach fmn output. The guard has no value-flow exemption today, so that needs one, with a witness.

Acceptance: the fsci-linalg lib.rs mul_add known-leak count returns to fm-bp82's 12, or to 0 with fm-bp82.

title: W5: Adaptive coverage anti-aliasing — classify tiles, supersample only complex edges, fuse the resolve
description:
Implement Rev 4's AA scheme (§10.4, D-21). Frames render at native output resolution; tiles are CLASSIFIED (via W5IR/W5BIN metadata) as empty, fully-covered, simple-edge, or complex-edge: interiors fill as vectorized spans; analytic coverage is evaluated only near edges; 2x/4x edge supersampling applies ONLY to complex-edge cells (thin overlapping strokes, dense self-intersections, high-frequency 3D silhouettes); and the resolve is FUSED into the coverage pass so the supersampled buffer never makes a second trip through memory. Full-frame SSAA spent most of its work on pixels that were empty or fully covered; the adaptive scheme spends it where the picture is — this matters most on bandwidth-limited parts (§17.6: Apple silicon's wall is bandwidth, not FLOPs).

Contract discipline: in `standard`, the classification thresholds are a QUALITY knob (§4) — but the escalation defaults are FIXED in G0-2's look study so default output reads as "the same feel, cleaner." In `certified`, the canonical analytic path runs everywhere and classification is a scheduling choice that CANNOT change bits (§10.5) — assert this by construction: the certified engine's per-pixel result must be independent of tile class. A forced-SSAA knob remains for A/B comparison and debugging.

Acceptance: certified-invariance test (frames bit-identical with classification on/off/forced across an adversarial corpus); standard-mode quality tests vs forced-4x SSAA within the versioned visual-equivalence budget (§16.3's engine-equivalence machinery); performance evidence (measured work reduction on the gallery scenes, recorded via §17.1 instrumentation); threshold calibration constants from G0-2 applied and documented.
notes: Implemented adaptive fused coverage AA. AaPolicy is canonical in fmn-core and re-exported by fmn-config and fmn-render without adding an upward crate edge. Standard engines honor adaptive, forced 2x, and forced 4x; certified normalizes all requests to the canonical analytic path while journaling the request and fixed thresholds. The classifier fuses general-fill boundary counting into the monotone row walk, preserves admitted primitive kernels, counts exact horizontal sheets, probes off-centre stroke edges while retaining probes for width ramps, applies the G0-2 full-width >= two-AA-band eligibility rule, and recomposites only complex cells in fixed painter order with no supersampled frame. Deterministic stats cover all four tile classes and 1/4-thread invariance. W5 corpus: 12,544 output cells; 29 at 2x; 34 at 4x; 13,204 sample units versus forced-4x 200,704; 93.42 percent reduction. Forced-4x error: max 0.219482421875, RMS 0.008526512734628627, inside V1 budgets 0.23 and 0.009. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the certified engine is landed and it deliberately does NOT classify.

§10.4 is explicit that 'certified runs the canonical analytic path everywhere — classification there is a scheduling choice that cannot change bits'. The engine does exactly that: every partial tile evaluates analytic coverage, and the only classification it honours is bin.rs's existing CLASS_INTERIOR, which is a correctness mechanism (exactly 1.0, the precondition for byte-exact occlusion pruning) rather than an AA policy.

So your adaptive scheme is additive and standard-mode, and the engine gives you two footholds:

1. FrameJob::fill_pass already picks one of three coverage sources in a documented order — classified interior, hinted kernel, general machinery. A complex-edge escalation is a fourth arm at the same site.
2. the_engine_matches_a_brute_force_reference is the test that will hold you honest: it renders the same frame with no binning, no interior class and no slab rejection and compares bytes. Anything you add that claims to be an optimization can be measured against it directly; anything that changes the picture has to be a declared standard-mode divergence with its own visual-equivalence budget (§16.3), not a quiet default.

Also worth knowing: the AA band's reach is now in the binner. bin::screen_aabb grows a stroked instance's AABB by half its widest width plus anti_alias_width (§10.3's per-draw width expansion, which was specified and never implemented — a stroke used to lose w/2 + aa pixels wherever its hull ended on a tile boundary). If your escalation widens the region a command can touch, it has to widen that expansion too.

comments.text:
ADDENDUM from fm-ig3's review (2026-07-27) — one number that bears on your escalation thresholds.

The cap/join corpus was drawing at 3.6 px and ALL FOUR joint settings rendered inside the ~1.5 px AA band — the golden was locking a picture no joint setting could move. That is the same regime your complex-edge classifier has to reason about: below roughly two AA bands of stroke width, the joint geometry is entirely inside the antialiasing and the distinctions §10.3 makes are sub-pixel.

Two consequences: (a) a corpus or gallery panel meant to show join behaviour needs width above that threshold or it shows nothing — the fixture now draws at 8.4 px; (b) if your escalation is keyed on edge complexity, thin overlapping strokes at that width are exactly where the analytic path is already delivering the right answer and supersampling would buy nothing. §10.4 names 'thin overlapping strokes' as an escalation trigger; the measurement suggests the trigger wants a width term, not just a count.

title: W5: The compiled render IR — retained tables, independent revisions, primitive hints, glyph instancing
description:
Implement Lumen's retained core (§10.8, D-20). Between Marionette's authoritative state and the execution engines sits a compiled, backend-neutral render IR: PathTable, SegmentTable, StyleTable, InstanceTable, ImageTable, and per-tile command lists — synchronized LAZILY from the RecordBuffer under §8.2's mirror rule, with backend-specific layouts derived from it (SoA/AoSoA sized to SIMD lanes on CPU; device arrays for the annex).

INDEPENDENT REVISIONS per renderable resource — topology, geometry, transform, style, visibility/order, image, camera-projection — and the distinctions pay directly: a color change does not regenerate curve coefficients; a translation does not recompute an object-space arc-length table; a camera move does not re-decode font outlines. Each COMPILED PATH retains: y-monotone quadratic splits (at vertical-tangent parameters), screen-independent coefficients, object- and screen-space bounds, the arc-length LUT (shared artifact with W2ARC), conservative stroke slabs, fill winding metadata, its primitive hint, previous tile coverage, and old + new dirty bounds.

PRIMITIVE HINTS route semantic shapes off the general quadratic solver: line/polyline → capsule-distance kernel; circle/arc → direct arc kernel; rectangle/rounded-rect → specialized coverage; dot → radial kernel; image → sampler kernel; nearly-linear quadratic → line fast path under an explicit screen-space error bound; glyph → cached path instance. Mutation through set_points or a writable live view invalidates the hint back to the general path — correctness never depends on a hint.

GLYPH/SHAPE INTERNING: an outline compiles once (content-addressed with the §11.3 span machinery and fmn-cache) and each occurrence is an INSTANCE (transform, color, clip, order) — for text-heavy mathematical scenes this deletes the bulk of geometry duplication and binning work; the same mechanism serves dots, arrow tips, repeated graph nodes, copied decorations.

G0-8's mapping report feeds this design (device-layout implications discovered there land here, not at W9-time).

Acceptance: revision-independence tests (each mutation class touches exactly its revision); lazy-sync tests (untouched resources never recompile); hint-invalidation tests; instancing dedup test (N copies of a glyph ⇒ 1 compiled path + N instances); IR golden snapshots for fixture scenes.
design:
INHERITED FROM G0-8b (fm-orn), docs/g0/G0-8b-analytic-fill-ratification.md — four layout verdicts, all cheap now and expensive to retrofit:

F11 THE FILL NEEDS ITS OWN GEOMETRY TABLE. Axis-monotone pieces (split at BOTH dy/dt=0 and dx/dt=0 — the plan named only one; §10.2 is trued up) are a DERIVED table keyed by the geometry revision, NOT a reshaped SegmentTable. Strokes read whole segments and their normalized arc-length spans (s0,s1); splitting invalidates those spans and gives the nearest-point search more work for the same answer. Bound: one segment yields at most 3 pieces, so a device allocator can size at 3*segments with no second pass. Device form: flat f32 at stride 6 (no arc-length span — §10.2 never asks where along the path a pixel is).

F12 THE STYLETABLE IS STAGE-SPECIFIC. Fills read rgba/rgba_end/gradient_axis (stride 12); strokes read rgba/width_start/width_end/aa_width (stride 8). Keep ONE interned host style table (dedup is semantics, §8.5 BatchKey bitwise) and derive a per-stage device row. Shared dedup index, unshared layout — a union row wastes a third of every entry or reintroduces the mixed-type access F1 forbids.

F13 THE COMMAND LIST NEEDS A FLAG WORD, AND OCCLUSION PRUNING DOES NOT WORK WITHOUT IT. Per-tile runs should carry (path_index, flags), not path_index — 4 bytes per command. §10.4's interior/edge class is a property of a (path, tile) PAIR, so flags are parallel to draws, not to tiles. The interior class must SHORT-CIRCUIT the accumulation and write exactly 1: an accumulated interior coverage is 1-epsilon, so an opaque cover lets the layer beneath show through by an ulp, and dropping the hidden command then changes the frame. Measured: 21.8% of commands interior, 16.5% pruned, frames byte-identical.

F14 THE TILE CARRY IS FREE AND CHANGES NO BINNING. Each row needs the winding deposited left of the tile, in closed form (one root solve per piece), so the fill iterates EVERY piece of a path, not only those meeting the tile. Slab-keyed binning is still sufficient: a path enclosing any pixel of a tile has hull bounds containing it. No shadow binning, no clip geometry.

Executable reference: spikes/g0-8-accelerator/src/analytic_fill.rs (the algorithm, generic over f32/f64) and shaders/analytic_fill.metal (both dispatch shapes).
close_reason:
All five acceptance criteria met, in crates/fmn-render (48 tests): revision-independence (each mutation class touches exactly its axes), lazy-sync (an unchanged renderable's points are never read — SyncStats counts the work NOT done), hint-invalidation (consumed from Marionette's revision comparison, all four write channels tested), instancing dedup (8 copies of an outline => 1 compiled path, 2 segments, 8 instances), and an IR golden snapshot bit-locked through fmn-hash's canonical envelope.

LANDED: revision.rs (the seven axes, Dependency), hint.rs (kernel routing + §10.8's nearly-linear fast path under a screen-space bound), table.rs (object-space segments, styles interned by bits matching BatchKey, shapes interned by content digest with position excluded, instances), plan.rs (the retained plan and its lazy sync), snapshot.rs (canonical encoding + the golden).

CARRIED FORWARD, each recorded on its owner: per-tile command lists -> fm-tg6; previous tile coverage + old/new dirty bounds -> fm-0l8; the backend-derived flat layouts -> the engines that derive them (F1 says one derivation per backend; fm-xsz carries the Metal one); ImageTable + the image axis producer -> fm-nve (blocked on an image mobject existing); the transform revision channel -> fm-7if.

TWO BUGS THE TESTS CAUGHT, both invisible: the joint type folded into the style key via f64::to_bits() as u32, which takes the low 32 bits — all zero for small integers — so all four joint types interned as one style; and the test that should have caught it used 2.0 + f32::EPSILON as a one-ulp value, which rounds straight back at 2.0.

title: W4: Composition & timeline algebra — AnimationGroup/Succession/LaggedStart + the declarative Timeline
description:
Implement animation composition (§9.4): AnimationGroup / Succession / LaggedStart / LaggedStartMap over (start, end) interval math — group run_time derivation, lag_ratio spreading across members, nested composition (groups of groups with independent rate_funcs), squish_rate_func and time_span flowing through the single normalized-alpha pipeline (W4CONTRACT owns the pipeline; this bead exercises its composition surface hard). Interval semantics are the Reference's: members map their (start,end) sub-intervals onto parent alpha; a member's rate_func applies inside its window.

THE DECLARATIVE TIMELINE: keyframes, labels, seek — compiling to the SAME primitives (an authored Timeline is sugar over composed animations on the rational clock, never a second engine). This is the substrate for Studio scrubbing (§13.5) and the WASM tier-2 serialized-timeline player (§10.7): a Timeline must serialize (fmn-hash canonical format) with enough fidelity that the player replays it without scene code. Seek semantics: seeking to time t reconstructs state deterministically — for pure segments via snapshot + interpolate-at-alpha; across stateful segments via the nearest checkpoint + replay (coordinate with §13.4's journal; the Timeline records segment boundaries).

Acceptance: interval-math fixtures vs the Reference (nested groups, lag interactions, unequal member run_times); normalized-alpha composition tests shared with W4CONTRACT; Timeline round-trip (author → serialize → load → replay ⇒ identical frame states); seek determinism tests (seek(t) ≡ play-through-to(t) for pure content).

title: W6: fmd-math layout — Appendix-G placement, synthesized CM math metrics, output paths
description:
Implement fmd-math's placement mathematics (§11.4): numerator/denominator shifts, rule thicknesses, sub/superscript placement (including the simultaneous-scripts kern rules), radical geometry (rule height, degree placement), big-operator limit placement, accent positioning with skew/italic-correction behavior — per the TeX Appendix-G parameter family — over a MATH-METRICS TABLE SYNTHESIZED AND HAND-CALIBRATED for the bundled faces (axis height, x-height, quad, sup/sub shift constants, radical parameters, fraction gaps) in the spirit of OpenType MATH. title: hoeffding_d example: unknown flags (e.g. --fsp 30) are taken as chapter names instead of rejected
description:
crates/fmn/examples/hoeffding_d/main.rs parse_args (line 119, `other => args.targets.push(other.to_owned())`) treats every unrecognized argument, including mistyped flags, as a chapter name.

Failure scenarios on the current code:
- `render all --fsp 30`: "--fsp" and "30" become targets; because "all" is present, every chapter renders at the default 60 fps and the typo is silently ignored.
- `render 01_hook --fsp 30`: fails late with the misleading "unknown chapter --fsp".
- `stats --verbose`: accepted silently.

Fix (mirrors the explainer skill template's main.rs, whose test `typos_are_errors_not_chapter_names` pins this): any argument starting with '-' that is not a known option is an error ("unknown option --fsp"); main prints the error plus a usage message listing commands and options and exits 2; -h/--help/help print the usage and exit 0. parse_args takes an argv iterator so unit tests can drive it, and the example is built with `test = true` so `cargo test` runs those tests.

Acceptance: a unit test proves `render --fsp 30` and `stats --verbose` error with "unknown option ...", and a full valid render invocation (every flag) still parses to the expected values; the test fails with the unknown-option arm removed.
close_reason: Landed in 3d45fdb4. parse_args takes an argv iterator; any '-'-prefixed argument that is not a known option is Err('unknown option X'); main prints it with a full usage text and exits 2; help/-h/--help print usage, exit 0. crates/fmn/Cargo.toml sets test = true on the example so cargo test runs its tests. Re-run at 3d45fdb4: cargo test -p fmn --example hoeffding_d (rch) 5 passed (typos_are_errors_not_chapter_names incl. 'render all --fsp 30', malformed_values_are_errors, every_valid_flag_still_parses, defaults_and_the_libx264_animation_tune, help_in_any_position). Planted negative (scratch copy, arm deleted): typos test FAILS, 'render --fsp 30' parsed Ok (left None vs Some("unknown option --fsp")). Binary: 'render all --fsp 30', 'render 01_hook --fsp 30', 'stats --verbose' exit 2 with 'unknown option ...' + usage; 'render 08_outro --format png --res 160x90 --fps 2 --silent --threads 4' rendered 45 frames, exit 0. clippy -p fmn --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; ubs 0 critical.

title: W1: Make atomic publication semantics and capability tests correct on Windows
description: Reality-check evidence at GitHub Actions run 31322553482 for exact HEAD a922a4a7815b1f915cbec6b6841466c405e2debf: the Windows exact-image capability suite fails std_atomic_directory_concurrent_commit_is_no_clobber and std_streaming_atomic_file_and_directory_publish_only_at_commit. The observed publication error is PermissionDenied on the target Windows path. Determine whether the defect is in the StdFileSystem publication implementation, test ownership/handle lifetime, or Windows rename/replace semantics; fix the root cause while preserving atomic visibility, no-clobber concurrent commit, private staging, bounded streaming, and failure cleanup. Do not convert the tests into platform skips or weaken the durable publication contract.
acceptance_criteria: Both atomic-directory tests pass on Windows x86-64 MSVC in the exact-image job and remain green on Linux x86-64, Linux aarch64 musl, and macOS aarch64. A deterministic regression proves pre-commit invisibility, exactly one successful no-clobber winner, no partial destination after failure, and explicit closure of every source/destination handle before rename. Errors retain typed path and OS-source diagnostics. Run the exact mandatory repository gate and attach cross-platform CI evidence at one commit.

title: W8: The ordered asynchronous emitter — sequence-numbered frames, preallocated rings, never a stall
description:
Implement Reel's orchestration core (§14.1, D-19): sequence-numbered frames from the pipeline (§17.4) and from frame-parallel pure segments (§9.5) publish IN FRAME-INDEX ORDER through a preallocated ring of frame slots — Lumen never stalls on a sink, and no sink ever observes an out-of-order or torn frame.

Mechanics: a bounded ring sized by the RAM-derived, config-visible in-flight budget (PG-6: each in-flight 4K RGBA frame ≈ 33MB — the budget is real memory); workers deposit completed frames by index; the emitter drains the contiguous prefix to sinks (file writers, the ffmpeg pipe, the Studio stream, the y4m/PNG-sequence writers); backpressure propagates to the pipeline when the ring fills (bounded, deadlock-free: the ring never blocks a frame that the drain is waiting on — slot reservation happens at frame dispatch); the hot path never allocates, resizes, or synchronously flushes a frame-sized buffer (§14.3's rule).

Ordering is a determinism obligation, not a UX nicety (§10.5 e): frame-index-ordered emission is one of the parallelism contract's six clauses — the frame-parallel equivalence tests (W4PURITY, PG-5) depend on this component being airtight. Multi-sink: a render may feed video + PNG sequence + preview simultaneously; each sink observes the same ordered stream; a slow sink applies backpressure rather than dropping (drops are an explicit per-sink policy, only for preview-class sinks).

Acceptance: out-of-order deposit tests (adversarial completion orders ⇒ in-order emission, always); backpressure test (slow sink throttles pipeline without deadlock); torn-frame impossibility test (a slot is never visible to sinks mid-write — API review + concurrency test under the thread sweep); multi-sink consistency test; ring-budget accounting test vs the configured in-flight limit.
close_reason: Bounded preallocated ordered emitter, multi-sink backpressure/drop policy, direct Lumen integration, concurrency acceptance suite, and full green workspace gate landed.

title: W8: PNG-sequence export is encoder-bound on one emitter thread — encode frames concurrently (same bytes) for a multi-x 1080p export speedup
description:
## Measured (calibration under ADR-0024, not a gate)

Release fmn at e877b5c8+ on the 64-thread dev box (load average 8-17). Every builtin (--write_all, 575 frames) at 1920x1080 and 60 fps; interleaved arms in one invocation, two reps, agreeing within about 3%:

| arm | --threads 1 | 4 | 16 | auto (32) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| certified png_sequence (CompressionLevel::Best), wall | 200 s | 113 s | 113 s | 112 s |
| the same, user CPU | 199 s | 200 s | 202 s | 203 s |
| standard png_sequence (Default), wall | 39 s | 32-35 s | 33 s | 32 s |
| raster-only y4m, layered_polygon (23 frames), wall | 0.6 s | 0.8-0.9 s | 0.6-0.9 s | 0.8 s |

So:
- PNG encoding dominates export: about 350 ms of CPU per certified 1080p frame (Best), and about 73 ms at Default. This is after 569aca9b's 4.6x matcher speedup.
- The sink encodes inside OrderedEmitter's write() (fmn-output/src/sinks.rs ~694-720), one frame at a time. Parallelism comes only from encode_rgba8_segmented_parallel's fixed DEFLATE segments (fmn-codec/src/png.rs ~1082), which load-balance poorly: about 1.8 cores busy, flat beyond 4 threads.
- Raster thread count barely matters for 2D content. Per-frame scoped spawning (fmn-render/src/engine.rs run_scoped_workers, plus the encoder's own thread::scope) makes 4-32 threads no faster, or slower, than 1 on y4m. That is fm-sq8.7 item 2.

## Work

Encode frames concurrently inside the PNG-sequence sink:
- write() already copies each frame into an owned scratch buffer. Hand it to a bounded encoder pool (std threads and channels, 'static jobs, forbid(unsafe) holds), within resident_bytes and frames-in-flight limits.
- Publish each frame's file as its encode completes. finish() joins, surfaces the first error in sequence order, then writes the completion marker.
- Bytes are identical by construction: the same encode function runs per frame.
- wasm32 (no threads) keeps the synchronous path.

## Acceptance

- Certified outputs byte-identical before/after. The e2e lock already pins all 25 CLI builtins' certified PNGs (b00c3a9f) and the scene/render-matrix locks; also cover --threads 1/4/16.
- Error ordering: a failing frame reports the same error and sequence as today, and no completion marker is written (planted negative).
- Interleaved A/B in one invocation recorded under docs/ratchet/ with ADR-0024 labels; calibration, not a gate claim.
- An e2e scenario logging encode concurrency and in-flight bytes.
close_reason:
Done.
- 0eec605f: frame-concurrent PngSink encoding on a bounded pool, the same canonical encode function per frame, commits in sequence order, frames in flight bounded by max_resident_bytes. ExecutionPlan::encoder_threads() (every planned CPU thread) sizes the PNG sink in the CLI, fmn::render and the portal.
- 175068b3: e2e render_matrix.png_sequence_frame_concurrency.v1 logs concurrency, the in-flight byte bound and the encoder lanes, and asserts 1-vs-4-worker byte identity.
- Byte identity: fmn-output tests (12 frames at 1/2/4/16, Default and Best); the 29-builtin CLI PNG e2e lock unchanged; A/B PNG-tree SHA-256 identical old vs new.
- Error ordering: frame_concurrent_png_sequence_failure_never_exposes_a_partial_generation. The serial test keeps its exact-timing assertion.
- Calibration (ADR-0024): docs/ratchet/png_sequence_encode_ab.md. All 25 builtins at 1080p60: certified 6.4x (165 -> 25.6 s median), standard 3.4x; y4m control unchanged; about 35% more user CPU.
- Gates through rch: 360 tests (output/runtime/cli/fmn), 50 e2e/golden tests, workspace clippy -D warnings, cargo check after the rebase, and fmt on the changed files.
