title: W5: The certified CPU engine — canonical raster arithmetic, the definition of the bits
description:
Implement the certified execution engine (§10.5, §6.1, §6.6, D-18; consumes G0-6's OQ-1 decision): the engine whose output IS the definition of correct bits for self-goldens, PG-5, and --reproducible.

Arithmetic: per G0-6's ruling — either floating-point with fmn-dmath transcendentals, fixed-order reductions, FMA off; or canonical fixed-point screen coordinates + integer coverage accumulation at defined precision with explicit rounding. Either way: NO fast-math, NO FMA on certified paths, reductions in fixed order and LANE-COUNT-INDEPENDENT (no horizontal sums whose association varies with vector width — the trap that silently breaks bit identity across SIMD build tiers); within the certified engine THE SCALAR PATH IS THE DEFINITION and every SIMD tier must match it bit-for-bit; degenerate/badly-conditioned cases route to the precision-exception path in every mode.

The parallelism contract, enforced here structurally (§10.5 a–f): frame bits are a pure function of (begin snapshot, alpha, frame-indexed RNG, input closure); write-disjoint tiles, fixed composite order; frame-index-ordered emission; engine/backend identity journaled into the input closure (§16.7).

Verification hooks: PG-5's thread-count sweep ({1,4,16} per commit, {32,96}+ weekly) runs THIS engine's output through the self-golden rig; the certified matrix cross-platform check (W1WCI's runners) compares frame hashes across linux-x86-64/linux-aarch64/macos-aarch64. The engine-equivalence suite (W10) holds every OTHER engine to this one's reference frames.

Acceptance: bit-identity at {1,4,16} threads on the primitive corpus; cross-platform bit-identity on the certified matrix for the G0-6 frame plus a growing corpus; scalar-vs-SIMD-tier bit-identity harness in place (tiers land in W5FAST but the harness is certified-side); the input-closure journaling path tested.
close_reason:
DONE. The certified CPU engine is landed, the certified matrix is measured on its own corpus, and ADR-0010's load-bearing property is now enforced rather than assumed.

WHAT LANDED
- crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs — FrameJob: a serial front-end deriving per-instance draw state once, and a parallel back-end that slices the frame into bands with chunks_mut so §10.5(b)'s write-disjointness is enforced by the borrow checker. A multi-threaded rasterizer under #![forbid(unsafe_code)] with no escape hatch anywhere. Raw frame is linear-light Rgba16F; canonical PNG is one table lookup away.
- EngineIdentity + journal() — §10.5(f) and C7/C10, canonically serialized. EngineKind::certifiable is where 'certified requires the certified CPU engine' stops being prose.
- tests/certified_arithmetic.rs — ADR-0010's two mechanically checkable properties as permanent gates, one-line exemption list, with a self-test because a scanner that finds nothing is indistinguishable from one that is broken.
- tests/certified_engine.rs — the raw-frame corpus under Scope::Certified, PG-5's {1,4,16} sweep, and the tier harness.
- ADR-0013 (accumulation order) and ADR-0014 (fmn-dmath at the DAG root), with the plan trued up in the same commits — including ADR-0010's own true-up, which its commit never made.

ACCEPTANCE, ITEM BY ITEM
1. Bit-identity at {1,4,16} threads on the corpus — DONE, per commit, and additionally measured natively on a 14-core M4 Pro.
2. Cross-platform bit-identity on the certified matrix — DONE AND MEASURED, not merely claimed by scope. All three legs pass one Scope::Certified lock: linux-x86-64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu-user, cross-compiled), macos-aarch64 (Darwin, native, M4 Pro). The corpus is stronger evidence than G0-6's single frame: gradient fills, a winding hole, all four joint settings including two miter-limit escapes, round caps at three widths, an arc-length taper, both hinted fill routes, an inner border, a backstroke, a sub-AA hairline. 631 further tests green on macOS.
3. Scalar-vs-tier harness in place — DONE. Tier::ALL has one entry today and the test says so plainly rather than implying coverage it lacks; fm-4wt's first tier becomes real coverage by adding a variant and dispatching on identity.tier.
4. Input-closure journaling path tested — DONE.

ADR-0010'S FOUR PROPERTIES: 1 and 2 are permanent CI gates; 3 is ADR-0013's ruling; 4 is structural (nothing weaker than + - * / sqrt).

THE TWO ITEMS HANDED HERE BY fm-oac AND fm-5oi: discharged. caps_and_joins.v1 and fills.v1 are rasterized, looked at, and bit-locked. The accumulation-order open question is ADR-0013.

THREE DEFECTS FOUND, ALL BY THE BRUTE-FORCE REFERENCE TEST OR THE GUARD
- bin::screen_aabb applied no per-draw width expansion, so every stroke was binned to its centreline hull and lost w/2 + aa pixels wherever its outline ended on a tile boundary. §10.3 specified the expansion; nothing implemented it, and nothing could notice until a rasterizer existed.
- The same function returned an un-normalized AABB, so a negative ScreenMap::scale — the natural spelling of a y-flip — binned the entire scene out of existence, silently.
- BN-04's 'decode to linear light at the render boundary' had no implementation. The record buffer holds sRGB, Style documents linear, and nothing between them decoded. Now done once per interned style row through fmn_frame::transfer::srgb_decode.

AND ONE FINDING ABOUT THE EVIDENCE ITSELF: the funnel guard found sixteen live libm call sites, two of them inside the very frame G0-6 hashed (rate::wiggle's sin and rate::exponential_decay's exp, which compute alpha and therefore move points, not last bits). G0-6's digests stand — but its argument was stronger than the code supported. Fifteen of the sixteen were unreachable from the funnel because fmn-core, fmn-mobject and fmn-library had no edge to fmn-dmath, and fmn-core could not have one without a cycle. That edge turned out to be vestigial (fmn-dmath uses nothing from fmn-core), so ADR-0014 inverts it.

ALSO: self_goldens.rs's two artifacts were measured identical on all three legs and graduated from per-platform locks to one certified lock, which is what that file said should happen once G0-6 landed. self_goldens.linux-x86_64.lock is superseded and no longer read — left in place, not removed.

FILED: fm-e9h (zero steady-state per-frame allocation, PG-6 — the Vec<Draw>, the band list, the per-worker scratch; all storage, none able to move a bit) and fm-qtd (canonical PNG panels from the corpus for Look Gallery review).

HANDOFFS POSTED: fm-4wt, fm-uql, fm-0gy, fm-3df, fm-gmr.

GATES: scripts/check.sh green — 1131 tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, crate-DAG (22 crates, all edges downward), ubs 0 critical.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
G0-6 (fm-zn9) resolved OQ-1 on 2026-07-25 — ADR-0010. This unblocks you, and it also hands you four acceptance criteria.

THE DECISION: floating-point suffices for the certified path. §10.5's canonical fixed-point raster boundary is RETIRED, NOT DEFERRED — it should not reappear in a W5 review as an unresolved option, and no precision or rounding constants enter the input closure.

THE EVIDENCE: one frame exercising gradient fills, a winding hole, strokes with joins and arc-length tapers, per-vertex atan2 joint angles that reach pixels, the Reference's true_dot glow with its pow falloff, rate functions driving the geometry, and alpha compositing — hashed byte-identically on linux-x86_64 (glibc, native), linux-aarch64 (musl, qemu-user) and macos-aarch64 (Darwin, M4 Pro). All 18 digests: the f64 frame, the f32 frame, and each of 16 fmn-dmath functions. The three legs vary ISA, libc and OS independently, so agreement is not one comparison repeated. Raw data docs/g0/g0-6-hashes/; methodology docs/g0/G0-6-determinism-ratification.md.

THE RESULT IS ONLY AS DURABLE AS FOUR PROPERTIES, WHICH ARE NOW YOUR ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
  1. fmn-dmath owns EVERY transcendental on the certified path. This is the load-bearing one — three platforms with three different libms agreed precisely because the libm is not in the loop.
  2. No FMA contraction (§10.5d). Verified in aarch64 object code; guarded in source by determinism::fma_guard.
  3. Fixed-order reductions (§10.5c). Trivially true today because the prototype is scalar; it stops being trivial the moment the SIMD tiers land (that risk is noted on fm-4wt).
  4. IEEE-754 basic operations only. Nothing weaker on the certified path.

THE CERTIFIED MATRIX IS FROZEN into docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5: linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64 certified; windows-x86-64 functional-CI only, its bit-certification still OQ-6. Adding a platform is an ADR, not a CI-config change.

ONE CAVEAT TO CARRY, NOT TO FORGET: the linux-aarch64 leg ran under qemu-user, because no aarch64 Linux hardware is reachable. QEMU's softfloat is IEEE-754 correct for the basic ops and nothing certified uses anything weaker, so it is valid evidence about the ARITHMETIC — but not about an aarch64 Linux MACHINE. fm-sol replaces it with real hardware if any becomes available.

SELF-GOLDEN ALREADY IN PLACE: the frame's f64 and f32 digests are bit-locked as single cross-platform constants in the spike's tests, so the property fails on whichever machine breaks it rather than waiting for someone to re-run the sweep. That is the Scope::Certified shape docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §6 now points at.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-5oi (2026-07-26) — the analytic fill is landed and green (crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs), so this bead's fill half is unblocked. Three things it hands you that bear on 'the definition of the bits':

1. The core is generic over a Real trait with f64 and f32 instantiations from ONE expression tree, so the certified/fast split is a type parameter rather than two transcriptions. The f32 instantiation is already exercised as 'the annex's arithmetic without the annex's hardware' (measured divergence < 1e-5 of coverage on a 15px-radius disc).
2. RowScratch::interior_row returns bit-exactly 1.0, written as a fill of the literal rather than a clamp of an accumulation. That is the precondition that makes occlusion pruning byte-identical (G0-8b F13) — do not replace it with a clamp.
3. Everything transcendental in the fill routes through fmn-dmath: the disc kernel's antiderivative uses fmn_dmath::atan2 (NOT asin — asin has infinite derivative at +/-1 and cost 1.4e-7 of area at r=6, and pixels sit a hair under r at every disc's extremes), and fmn_geom::distance uses the scalar funnel for cbrt/acos/cos. sqrt is used directly, since IEEE 754 requires it correctly rounded.

Open question this bead owns and the fill did not resolve: whether the certified path fixes the accumulation ORDER across pieces. fill_row accumulates pieces in table order and then prefix-sums the row, which is deterministic for a given plan — but the plan's piece order is a property of the sync, so PG-5's thread-count sweep will want that pinned explicitly rather than inherited.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ADDENDUM from fm-oac (2026-07-26) — strokes are landed too (crates/fmn-render/src/stroke.rs), so both §10.2 and §10.3 are now waiting on this bead. Three things bear on it:

1. TWO ACCEPTANCE ITEMS FROM fm-oac LAND HERE, not there. §10.3's acceptance asks for 'cap/join golden fixtures (every combination, including miter-limit escapes to bevel)'. The GEOMETRY of every combination is tested in stroke.rs — round cap circularity over twelve directions, the join arc with no notch and no gap, bevel trimming, miter extending, the miter-limit escape on a reversal — but a bit-locked GOLDEN is a rasterized frame, and there is no engine to rasterize one. The same is true of the fill. Wire both corpora into fmn-conformance's golden rig when the engine exists; that is this bead's, and fm-oac was closed saying so rather than sitting open on it.

2. THE STRUCTURE IS ANNEX-SHAPED ALREADY. stroke_coverage is per-pixel independent with no accumulator and no scan — the one-thread-per-pixel shape G0-8 proved on Metal — and the fill offers the same shape via coverage_at_cell alongside its scanline form. §10.3 asked for 'scalar-complete first; the structure must not preclude lanes', and nothing here does: the hot loop is a min over segments of one nearest-point solve.

3. THE ARITHMETIC IS ALREADY FUNNELLED. Everything transcendental goes through fmn-dmath: the fill's disc kernel via atan2, fmn_geom::distance via the scalar funnel for cbrt/acos/cos. sqrt is used directly (IEEE 754 requires it correctly rounded). What this bead still owns is the ORDER: the fill accumulates pieces in table order then prefix-sums the row, and the stroke takes a min over segments in table order. Both are deterministic for a given plan, but the plan's order is a property of the sync — PG-5's sweeps will want that pinned explicitly rather than inherited.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FRESH-EYES REVIEW (2026-07-27) — four defects found in the work closed under this bead, all fixed, plus two corpus weaknesses. Recorded here because the bead is closed and these are its consequences.

1. THE DRAW LIST WAS COMPACTED WHILE BINNING INDEXES BY INSTANCE. FrameJob skipped instances with no visible pass; Binning's command lists hold instance indices. From the first skipped instance onward, every command paired with the wrong shape and style — a scene whose first object is invisible drew its second object's geometry in its third object's colour and dropped the last. 1075 of 12544 pixels. I had written the comment explaining that the two indices diverge and then indexed by the wrong one.

2. compile_shape DETECTED SUBPATH BREAKS BY ZERO LENGTH. fmn-geom's convention (QuadPath::subpath_end_indices, and the Reference's) is a handle sitting on the previous anchor. The two coincide only when a subpath begins where the last ended, so an annulus with distinct radii and EVERY GLYPH COUNTER compiled as one subpath — §10.2's named failure, 'fill as one ring with a chord through it' — and the break survived as a drawn segment, so a stroked annulus grew a radial spoke. This one predates fm-ig3 (fm-gw7's compile_shape) and would have hit W6 hard the moment text landed.

3. THE FUNNEL GUARD WAS BLIND AFTER LINE 6 OF bezier.rs. It stopped at the first #[cfg(test)]; that file's line 6 is a #[cfg(test)] use, hiding 173 lines of production geometry while reporting clean. Now skips only the item the attribute introduces (47k lines read, floor raised 20k->40k), and its self-test covers this plus a // inside a string literal.

4. A HINTED FILL KERNEL WOULD HAVE FILLED A MULTI-SUBPATH SHAPE'S HOLE. Prophylactic — no constructor tags such a shape today — but §10.8 says correctness never depends on a hint.

Plus: encode_frame guessed 4 bytes/px for non-Rgba16F (a planar buffer would have hashed luma and dropped chroma); the journal wrote PixelFormat as a discriminant, so reordering fmn-frame's enum would have moved every manifest digest ever issued; render_into did not check the binning was built for its viewport.

TWO CORPUS WEAKNESSES, WHICH MATTER MORE THAN THEY LOOK:
- The cap/join grid drew at 3.6 px, where all four joint settings sit inside the AA band — the golden was locking a picture no joint could move. Widened to 8.4 px, and the test now proves the joints reach pixels and asserts ADR-0012 at frame level (Auto == NoJoint byte-for-byte; Bevel and Miter each differ).
- At 60 px/unit every Circle was inside HINT_BUDGET_PX, so §10.2's general machinery was exercised by the annuli alone. Added a self-intersecting pentagram: its centre has winding 2, so it fills under nonzero and would be a hole under even-odd — a discriminator for the rule, not just a workout for the evaluator.

ALSO CORRECTED: interning_order_does_not_move_a_pixel proved nothing. RenderPlan::sync interns in painter order, so on a FRESH plan the two orders cannot diverge — they diverge only on a RETAINED plan when an object is inserted behind ones already compiled, which is the normal path. Replaced with a retained-vs-fresh comparison that asserts the divergence as a precondition. ADR-0013's Context and Consequences are trued up.

All three certified legs re-verified against the final tree (14 certified tests each, one shared lock). Gates green: 1135 tests, fmt, clippy -D warnings, crate-DAG, ubs 0 real criticals.

The superseded self_goldens.linux-x86_64.lock was removed with the owner's written authorization.

title: W10: The performance rig — PG-1..PG-8 + PG-A on pinned profiles, with scaling annex
description:
Implement §17.2's gate machinery: dedicated PINNED bare-metal profiles (8-core x86-64 Linux; Apple-silicon macOS), multiple repetitions, median + robust dispersion, ALERT vs BLOCKING thresholds, versioned baselines.

THE GATES: PG-1 end-to-end (OpeningManimExample-class 1080p vs the Python Reference under the PINNED benchmark definition from W1PROF — ≤0.5x at G2, ≤0.35x at G4); PG-2 rasterizer (≥300 Mpx/s fill-equivalent, ≥120 Mpx/s stroke at 8 threads on canonical workloads with stated path/segment/overdraw parameters); PG-3 throughput (≥60fps 1080p preview median primitive scene; ≥30fps 4K export typical 2D); PG-4 latency (cold CLI → first frame <150ms; edit-to-frame <1s); PG-5 determinism (bit-identical frames {1,4,16} per commit — frame-parallel and pipelined schedules INCLUDED — {32,96}+ weekly, certified matrix under --reproducible); PG-6 memory (≤1.5GB peak on the 4K 3D gallery under the RAM-derived in-flight budget; zero leaks over 1h soak; ZERO steady-state per-frame heap allocations on the primitive corpus); PG-7 typesetting (<3ms cold / <100µs cached median formula; 10k-glyph layout <20ms); PG-8 binding tax by class (from W10TAX's budgets).

SCALING PROFILES (published, then ratcheted): parallel efficiency at {1,8,32,96} threads for raster-bound and frame-parallel workloads, per release, alert-first graduating to blocking after two releases of baseline. PG-A: annex engines on their own pinned profiles (Apple Max-class; RTX-4090-class), gating ANNEX changes only — the CPU engine stands alone so acceleration can never mask a core regression (R21).

Rig telemetry beyond fps (§17.2): bytes up/back per frame, reuse and tile-cache hit rates, dirty-tile percentage, allocations per frame, team utilization, cross-NUMA steals, GPU occupancy, encode queue depth; scene classes static/locally-dirty/full-screen/dense-stroke/text-heavy/high-overdraw/3D; latency probes + 10-minute thermal runs; outputs raw/PNG/software-video/hardware-video.

Acceptance: every gate has a bench binary, committed baseline, variance budget, and flamegraph-on-regression artifact; blocking wired per gate's schedule (G2/G4 thresholds staged); the scaling annex publishes per release; a demonstrated regression drill (inject slowdown → gate blocks).

comments.text: Activation and existing-coverage audit: governance had three active lanes (W9, W7, G1), so W10 became the fourth and remains within the cap. Existing mechanisms are real but fragmented: fmn-profile/1 already records the complete phase taxonomy and most §17.2 counters; PG-5 has a blocking {1,4,16} certified corpus; PG-A has explicit ignored native-Metal median probes; Studio records PG-4 edit-to-frame; frame-pool tests give only the structural layer of PG-6; render has libtest microbenches; W1 supplies only a calibration Reference denominator and explicitly is not a PG-1 result; PG-7 and PG-8 only have seed evidence, not permanent gates. Missing common machinery includes pinned-host/closure identity matching, raw valid/invalid sample retention, robust median/MAD evaluation, alert versus blocking schedules, versioned observed baselines, regression evidence requirements, and a truthful runner that refuses absent pinned-host evidence. First tranche will build that fail-closed common core and regression drill; it will not relabel shared-host calibration or synthetic tests as passing PG gates.

title: W10: Pin benchmark hosts and land a replayable baseline corpus
description: Define the dedicated 8-core x86-64 Linux and Apple-silicon macOS benchmark profiles required by plan §17.2, including exact hardware/topology, OS/kernel, pinned toolchain and SUITE.lock closure, power/thermal state, CPU isolation, storage, repetition counts, and invalid-run criteria. Capture attributable raw sample/evidence TSV for every applicable PERF_GATES.tsv BenchmarkKey on real bare metal, derive versioned baselines only through fmn-perf verify-baseline, and commit the profile manifests, raw evidence, and replay-verified baseline records. Virtualized or incomplete runs must remain Inconclusive. Acceptance includes deterministic replay, schema/resource-cap adversarial tests, and an explicit baseline-version update ritual.

title: W10: Rule on TOP/BOTTOM frame-marker constants vs direction-argument misuse (candidate C-16)
description:

title: W6: native TexText defaults to flush-left lines (Reference: \centering) and fmd-math keeps the space after \\
description:
## Context (fm-5wq.14, 543b999a)

fmd-math aligns `\\`-split text lines only inside its flushleft/center/flushright blocks; a top-level `\centering` is inert. 543b999a added fmn-tex `LineAlign` and `TexEngine::typeset_aligned`, which wraps a non-left body in the matching environment with span projection. The Python portal now passes the Reference default (`\centering`), so portal TexText centers its lines like the Reference.

Two gaps remain:

1. **The native Rust default is still Left.** `fmn_library::TexText::new` documents "the Reference's defaults", but its line alignment defaults to `LineAlign::Left`. The Reference default is `\centering`, so multi-line TexText built through the Rust API or `fmn` CLI scenes renders flush left. Changing the default touches self-goldens and vertical placement, because an AlignBlock is vcentered on the axis while a bare hlist sits on the first baseline. So it needs an adjudicated golden update, not a reflexive re-bless.
2. **Upstream fmd-math keeps the space after `\\`.** LaTeX's `\\` skips following spaces (its `*`/`[len]` lookahead). fmd-math lays a leading interword space on the next line, so `TexText(r"ab\\ cd")` centers line 2 about half a space off the LaTeX position (measured: first-line center offset 0.117 scene units at font_size 48, against 0.001 without the space). This belongs in the franken_markdown repo (UPSTREAM_LEDGER.md / SUITE.lock repin; see fm-fmd-repin-g2-truth-y3gr).

## Acceptance
- (1) The Rust TexText default matches the Reference's `\centering`, with golden deltas adjudicated in the commit and a Look Gallery note if the look changes.
- (2) An upstream fmd-math fix or ledger entry exists, with a franken_manim witness (`TexText(r"ab\\ cd")` centers line 2 within 1e-3) that lands with the repin.
close_reason: Both parts landed: Rust TexText centers by default (9839408b); fmd-math unskip pinned (96c4d660) with witness (self-verified)

title: W3: Family tree, positional API, bounding boxes, uniforms
description:
Implement the structural/positional surface (§8.4, §1.1): the full positional API — next_to, arrange, arrange_in_grid, to_edge, to_corner, align_to, shift, move_to, center, scale, stretch, set_width/height/depth, match_* — locked by structural fixtures against the Reference (loose f32 tolerances per §16.4, since we compute in f64); bounding boxes with dirty-flag propagation through the family tree (invalidate on point mutation via the RecordBuffer dirty channel, on submobject add/remove, on transform); the cached family flattening with correct invalidation.

Uniforms (§1.1, §8.4): the COMPLETE per-object uniform inventory as typed state — including the four clip-plane slots, stroke_behind, depth-test flag, is_fixed_in_frame (a float mix, per the kept camera model), per-kind AA widths, shading triple (reflectiveness, gloss, shadow) — because scene code reads and writes mobject.uniforms directly (API surface), and Lumen's StyleTable synchronizes from it.

Design care: positional operations are defined against bounding boxes in the Reference; ours must match its box conventions (about_point/about_edge semantics, buff application, stretch vs scale) exactly enough that fixture arrays coincide. Where the Reference's box is subtly wrong (stale caches), ours is correct — any user-visible divergence gets a Behavior Note.

title: W3: The render-order model — z_index, batching partitions, ordering-trace fixtures
description:
Implement the Reference's ACTUAL render-order semantics (§8.5, §1.5): top-level sort by z_index with STABLE scene order for ties; adjacent compatible-item batching; depth-test and fixed-in-frame partitions — kept as semantics, because what draws over what is meaning, not pixels. Lumen consumes this as its draw-order model (§10.1); painter's order for transparent content descends from it (§10.4, §10.8's exact-painter-order command runs).

Deliverable is a specification-with-tests, engine-side: given a scene graph (with shared submobjects, multiple parents, mixed z_index, stroke_behind, depth-tested 3D content, fixed-in-frame overlays), produce the deterministic draw sequence. ORDERING-TRACE FIXTURES pin the tricky cases: a submobject shared by two parents (drawn when? once or twice?), z_index on a child vs parent, stroke_behind interleaving (fill/stroke split ordering), add/remove/bring_to_front/bring_to_back effects on stable order, and the depth-test partition boundary (painter order within non-depth-tested; per-tile depth among depth-tested).

Generate the fixture expectations from the pinned Reference's batching code by INSPECTION (its semantics, not its pixel output), recording each ruling with a source citation — this is the kind of archaeology that must be done once, in one bead, not rediscovered per renderer bug.

Acceptance: the ordering-trace corpus green; property test (stable under no-op mutations; insertion order preserved among equal keys); the written ordering spec committed beside the fixtures (Lumen's W5 beads cite it as normative).
close_reason: Render-order model landed (§8.5). docs/RENDER_ORDER.md is the normative spec: 12 rulings, each cited into the pinned Reference (scene.py:300/327/338/360/371/389/394, mobject.py:435/1238/2056, shader_wrapper.py:117/277/354, utils/family_ops.py:23, utils/iterables.py:48). Implementation: fmn_mobject::order (BatchKey = ProgramKind + the uniform inventory, bitwise on floats; DrawPlan with per-item group/batch/root/passes; Stage::draw_plan is a pure function of scene state) plus the scene-list ops brought to the Reference's exact semantics (add = remove+append+stable-sort by (z_index,position); bring_to_front = add; bring_to_back = remove+prepend with NO sort, deliberately beating z_index until the next add; remove = recursive ungrouping; replace = splice-if-member; set_z_index writes the family and never re-sorts). z_index is per-object data threaded through the detached Mobject, the VMobject builder, copies, become, and snapshots — durable schema to minor 1.2 by append (§6.7). Two D5 divergences documented: a diamond child draws once (our family dedups; the Reference's get_family would draw it twice and double-composite alpha), and a child's z_index orders nothing (stated rather than rediscovered). Acceptance: 23-test ordering-trace corpus green (shared submobject one-per-root, diamond, child-vs-parent z_index, stroke_behind pass order, every shader-id uniform splitting a batch, the group-boundary batch rule, add/remove/front/back/replace traces, no-op-mutation stability, snapshot round-trip); self-goldens verified NOT drifted (the stage golden writes its own STAGE_SCHEMA document, not the persist form). 866 workspace tests, scripts/check.sh green.

title: G0-2: Renderer look study — calibrate the analytic renderer against captured Reference imagery
description:
Executed calibration study fixing Lumen's aesthetic parameters BEFORE W5 scales (§20.1 spike 2 → §10, §6.3). The product contract is "correct AND beautiful, judged as at-least-as-good" — this spike turns "the same feel, cleaner" from aspiration into a measured statement.

Scope: render the calibration set with the prototype analytic renderer — fills with per-vertex gradients, self-intersecting paths, every joint/cap combination, glow dots, 3D lighting spheres/surfaces, text samples — side-by-side against one-time captured Reference imagery (no certified Pango/llvmpipe capture environment is maintained; capture once, keep forever). Fix, by decision recorded in the plan: (a) the adaptive-AA defaults and tile-escalation thresholds (§10.4), (b) the AA profile and the ~1.5px weight, (c) the smooth "auto" join tuning and miter-limit default (§10.3), (d) gradient behavior — confirming the kept interpolate_color sqrt(lerp(c1^2,c2^2,a)) form and RMS average_color composite correctly in linear light (§6.3), (e) the finalize_color lighting match — (reflectiveness, gloss, shadow), light at (-10,10,10), dark_shift 0.2 (§1.5, Appendix B), (f) the cubic→quad converter tolerance default so curve fidelity visibly exceeds the Reference's (§7.2).

Why: the Reference's look constants are the aesthetic DNA of 3Blue1Brown and are KEPT deliberately (D-04); but they were tuned for a GPU pipeline full of workarounds (signed-alpha fills, x1.06 composite un-mangle, polyline ribbon strokes). Porting the constants onto honest mathematics shifts their visual effect; only side-by-side calibration can close that loop.

Acceptance: the calibration gallery checked in (small, public, permissively-licensed primitives); a parameters document with every chosen constant + rationale; risk R2's standing mitigation (Gallery review as gate input) stood up.
close_reason:
The G0-2 look study is executed and ratified: docs/g0/G0-2-look-study-ratification.md, with the rendered evidence in docs/g0/g0-2-renders/ and the measurements reproducible via scripts/g0_2_measure.py. Unblocks fm-5oi, fm-oac, fm-6cf, fm-3g6, fm-o3j.

METHOD — two independent lines of evidence, kept separate so they could disagree: the Reference's GLSL/Python read as source (every constant carries file:line), and measurements of the fm-o3i captures. Where they agreed the number is settled; where they disagreed, the disagreement WAS the finding.

DECISIONS FIXED (the bead's (a)-(f), plus glow):
(b) AA = smoothstep over a 1.5 px band. Measured: band 1.560 px, RMS 0.0031 — under one 8-bit level across the whole profile. 10-90 width 0.99 px.
(c) Round joins from the distance field; auto crossover smoothstep(-0.8,-0.9,cos t); effective miter limit 3.1623 half-widths, DERIVED (the Reference has no miter_limit constant).
(d) interpolate_color is EXACTLY sqrt(lerp(c1^2,c2^2,a)) — 0.000000 error — and average_color is exactly RMS. Composite in linear light; the kept form is a gamma-2 stand-in differing by at most 9.4/255, peaking at a~0.2 and exact at both endpoints. That table is BN-04's evidence.
(e) add_light kept verbatim; Surface shading (0.3,0.2,0.4); light (-10,10,10).
(f) cubic->quad tolerance 0.1 px, justified by measurement: the Reference's fixed 2-quad approximation deviates up to 7.71 px at 1080p — over 5x the entire AA band. 0.1 px is 77x tighter.
glow: (1-r/R)^2 exactly, confirmed twice (source glow_factor=2.0; measured exponent 1.986, competing models 10x worse).
(a) is the one decision measurement CANNOT fix: the Reference has no escalation concept, it supersamples every fill unconditionally. So the criterion and the default are fixed here (analytic coverage, no supersampling) and fm-gmr is named owner of record for the numeric threshold.

THREE FINDINGS THAT CHANGE WHAT GETS BUILT:
1. THE FILL AA IS 2.3 BITS. quadratic_bezier/fill/frag.glsl has no AA term at all — a hard discard plus a 2x supersampled f16 target, box-resolved. Predicted 5 coverage levels; measured on a bare fill edge (stroke_width=0, so nothing covers the boundary): 4 distinct intermediate levels at 0.2471/0.4981/0.7452/0.7567. Against the stroke's continuous smoothstep this is the concrete at-least-as-good claim for §10.2, and it is why (a) defaults to NO supersampling — we would be paying 4x to lose precision.
2. bevel AND miter ARE NAMED BACKWARDS. miter_factor=0 (BEVEL_JOINT, code 2) yields -tan(t/2), the pointed corner; miter_factor=1 (MITER_JOINT, code 3) yields +cot(t/2), the blunt one. Corroborated independently from the captures: at the zig-zag's turn cos t = 0.154 > -0.8 so auto must equal bevel, and the measured apex widths are auto 4 px, bevel 6 px, miter 9 px. Ports must key on the NUMERIC CODES; ours already does.
3. dark_shift IS NOT A LIGHTING PARAMETER. The bead (and plan §10.4, now trued up) listed 'dark_shift 0.2' alongside reflectiveness/gloss/shadow. At the pin its only occurrence is textured_surface/frag.glsl:16, a light/dark TEXTURE crossfade that finalize_color never sees. Struck, so the port does not manufacture a parameter that never existed.

THE MEASUREMENT I GOT WRONG FIRST, AND WHY IT MATTERS (L2). Per-scanline 10-90 ramps on the square gave 1.07 px on the vertical edge and 1.59 px on the horizontal one — an anisotropy the shader cannot produce, since pixels are square. The cause: an axis-aligned edge lands at ONE sub-pixel phase, so the 'ramp' measured was the phase, not the profile. A circular boundary sweeps every phase; binning ~7,800 near-boundary pixels by exact signed distance to a least-squares circle (residual 0.041 px) recovered the true profile. Two other first-pass numbers were also artefacts — the glow profile had run into the neighbouring dot, and the gradient sample had landed in the gap between the square and the circle, returning the background as the 'midpoint'. All three looked plausible. The rule that caught them: a measurement contradicting the source is a bug in the measurement until proven otherwise.

THE SIDE-BY-SIDE (4 of 6 panels; lighting_3d and text_sample need 3D and Scribe, filed as fm-gfn): self_intersections is at-least-as-good and shows why — the Reference's star core renders LIGHTER than its limbs because winding 2 composites the fill twice through the signed-alpha trick, while ours is one uniform colour. joints_and_caps is different-but-fine: four Reference corners collapse to one round join, with no notch at any vertex. glow is at-least-as-good. gradient_fills is OPEN and is fm-5oi's input, not a settled result — the Reference shows a hard diagonal fan seam (per-vertex interpolation across the triangle fan from base_point), ours is smooth, but ours is a defined stand-in and §10.2's real interior field is unbuilt.

PLAN TRUED UP: §10.4 and Appendix B corrected on dark_shift; §10.4 now records the per-vertex Gouraud lighting as a §12 question.
FILED: fm-fte (Appendix C + BN-04 entry for the x0.95/x1.06 round-trip, a 0.70% systematic overshoot we do not inherit — worth recording so our correct fills are not read as a colour regression), fm-gfn (the two remaining gallery panels).
GATES: scripts/check.sh all green (22 crates, DAG OK); spike fmt/clippy clean, 75 tests pass; ubs Critical 0 (the 55 scene.rs warnings are pre-existing whole-file inventory — my delta is 4 unwraps on hardcoded path builders, the file's own idiom); ruff clean.

title: W10: a play that animates the camera frame moves its other animated mobjects to the end of scene.mobjects (Reference: only missing ones are added)
description:
## Found by the corpus differential (fm-5wq.33), 2026-10-10

A `play` that animates the camera frame and other mobjects moves those
other mobjects to the end of `scene.mobjects`, even when they are already in
the scene. The Reference leaves them where they are. `scene.mobjects` is
draw order, so the moved mobject is painted over everything added after it.

Cause: `crates/fmn-python/python/manimlib/_animation_semantics.py`
`scene_play`, camera branch (around line 2010):

```python
for animation in animations:
    if drawable[id(animation)]:
        for root in g["_fmn_animated_mobjects"](animation):
            self.add(root)
```

`Scene.add` removes and re-appends. The Reference's `begin_animations`
(scene.py) adds only what is missing:
`if animation.mobject not in all_mobjects: self.add(animation.mobject)`.

Measured on portal wheel 6d4a4463, scene probe:
`self.add(a, t, b, c)`, then
`self.play(a.animate.shift(UP), self.frame.animate.shift(UP))`
gives roots `[t, b, c, a]` in the portal and `[a, t, b, c]` in the
Reference. Without the frame animation nothing moves. With
`t.animate.set_value(..)` and the frame, `t` moves to the end.

Corpus: `_2023/convolutions2/diagonal_slices.py` `DiagonalSlices` and two
siblings (the "ValueTracker class" cluster) end with the tracker last in the
portal and before the last two Tex in the Reference.

## Work

Add a root only when it is not already in the scene's family, updating the
family set as roots are added, as the Reference does. Keep the private slot
and the camera detached as they are.

## Acceptance

- A portal test: the probe above keeps `[a, t, b, c]`. It fails at
  6d4a4463 (planted negative).
- The corpus differential: DiagonalSlices and its siblings have no root-order
  difference.
close_reason:
Fixed in 2286f7fc. The camera branch of scene_play adds only animated roots missing from the scene's family, as the Reference's begin_animations does. Evidence:
- camera_animation_semantics camera_play_keeps_present_roots_in_draw_order fails on wheel 6d4a4463 (planted negative) and passes on a wheel built from the tree (14/14).
- Full portal gate survey on that wheel: 78/78 suites.
- Corpus differential (cdiff8_kpvx): DiagonalSlices and OscillatingGaussianSlice are structurally equal-with-exclusions. Blocks' first difference moved past the tracker order to a fm-c1up Rectangle class.

title: W5: The CUDA annex production backend — via frankentorch, per the §17.6 playbook (post-ledger-spike)
description:
Implement the annex's second engine (§17.5, §17.6, §10.7, D-22; gated on OQ-10's ledger-spike outcome from G0-8): CUDA via frankentorch — ft is the ONLY GPU gateway; no wgpu, no direct CUDA bindings.

The §17.6 NVIDIA playbook, implemented: keep the scene RESIDENT — path headers, quadratic segments, styles, instances, image descriptors, macrotile bins, and fine-tile command lists live on-device (24GB is ample for persistent scene state + several 4K surfaces); upload ONLY DELTAS (changed transforms, styles, geometry ranges, ordering metadata — W5IR's revision taxonomy is exactly the delta vocabulary). Batch by pipeline class (solid fills, strokes, gradients, images, 3D triangles) WITHIN painter-order command runs; one block or cooperative block group per tile; raster and composite in stable command order; DETERMINISTIC count/prefix/scatter binning — never one-kernel-per-mobject, never unordered atomic appends. A small pinned-memory ring + multiple non-default streams overlap delta upload, rasterization, NV12 readback, and host-side ffmpeg submission; shared memory stages command/segment chunks ONLY where it provably removes repeated global reads (occupancy costs are real). Don't over-engineer the bus: 4K@30 readback is ~1GB/s RGBA / ~0.4GB/s NV12 against ~25GB/s PCIe gen4 x16 — plain pinned readback is fine; zero-copy is an Apple luxury. NVENC rides the §14.3 boundary. Tensor/RT cores are the WRONG tools here (branchy geometric coverage, ordered compositing, memory movement) — ordinary CUDA execution, good binning, persistent layout.

Hard boundaries (identical to Metal, R21): standard-only, never certified; PG-A profiles (RTX-4090-class pinned machine) gate ANNEX changes only; backend identity journaled; engine-equivalence budget vs certified frames; annex work pauses when core PG-1..PG-3 regress.

Acceptance: the corpus rendering through CUDA within the engine-equivalence budget; delta-upload instrumentation (bytes/frame recorded, resident-state verified across frames); binning determinism test (same scene ⇒ same command lists across runs); PG-A rig numbers on the pinned CUDA profile; graceful absence (no CUDA ⇒ CPU/other engines, no error).

title: W1: The single RNG — PCG64DXSM with named substreams and keyed per-frame forks
description:
Implement fmn-core's one-RNG rule (§6.5, D-06). The Reference carries TWO seeded legacy streams (CPython random + NumPy legacy RandomState); with output parity dropped, both are irrelevant — FrankenManim standardizes on fnp-random's PCG64DXSM, already bit-exact against NumPy for explicit seeds.

Requirements: (a) a single seeded root stream exposed via fmn-core; OS entropy when unseeded; (b) NAMED SUBSTREAMS derived per subsystem (layout jitter, stream-line seeding, sampling, shuffle...) so features don't perturb each other's sequences — adding a new consumer must never shift an existing consumer's draws; (c) snapshot/restore of full stream state into SceneState and the replay journal; (d) KEYED PER-FRAME FORKS (Rev 4, load-bearing for §9.5): a frame's stream state derives from (substream id, frame index) — NEVER from sequential pulls consumed in scheduler completion order. This is the property that makes frame-parallel rendering replay-identical BY CONSTRUCTION, and the reason per-thread completion-order RNG is on §10.5's permanent refusal list (D-18); (e) render-affecting map iteration uses ordered maps only — audit helper + lint note.

Testing: substream independence tests (adding draws on stream A leaves stream B's sequence untouched); fork determinism tests (fork(sub, k) identical regardless of call order/thread); snapshot/restore round-trip; NumPy seed-parity vectors via fnp.

Draft Behavior Note BN-01: seeded scenes reproduce within FrankenManim, not across engines.

Acceptance: all above tests green; the fork API documented for Choreo (§9.5) and StreamLines (§12.4) consumers.

RngRoot -> named Substreams (canonical name encoding mirrored in the generator) -> keyed per-frame forks (pure function of (substream, frame); call-order/thread invariant by construction, D-18). Snapshot/restore round-trips full state. OrderedMap alias + doc as the ordered-iteration audit hook. BN-01 drafted. Subtlety pinned by vectors: NumPy seeds PCG64DXSM via the FULL 128-bit multiplier srandom, runtime steps use the DXSM cheap multiplier. Owned temporarily per SUITE.lock gap: migration to fnp-random filed as fm-ai1 (blocked on fm-g2c). title: W8/W6: the typeset cache refuses every root under $TMPDIR, /tmp or /var on macOS (OS-owned /var -> /private/var symlink) — persistent cache silently off; fmn-python persistent-cache test red on every Mac
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (macOS aarch64, HEAD 96b7b7c8)

On macOS, **the persistent typeset cache cannot open any root under the system temp dir, `/tmp` or `/var`.**

`reject_symlink_components` (`crates/fmn-cache/src/store.rs:1431`) walks every ancestor from `/` downward and refuses the root if **any** component is a symlink. On macOS:
- `/var` → `/private/var` is a symlink, so every `$TMPDIR` (`/var/folders/...`) path contains one;
- `/tmp` → `/private/tmp` is a symlink;
- `/etc` → `/private/etc` is a symlink.

These are OS-owned, root-owned, immutable symlinks. A user cannot create or redirect them, so they are not the attack the check exists to stop: an attacker-planted symlink redirecting cache writes or `--clear-cache` deletions.

### Evidence

`cargo test --workspace` on macOS failed `fmn-python --lib portal_typography::typesetting::tests::production_tex_constructors_use_the_persistent_cache` (`crates/fmn-python/src/portal_typesetting.rs:260`) with:

```
'typeset cache unavailable: refusing cache root /var/folders/.../fmn-typeset-cache-pkkdvrka
 [wrong_node_kind]: root contains a symlinked path component or reparse point'
```

The test builds its cache root under a `tempfile` directory, so the failure is **deterministic on every Mac**. Linux CI never sees it.

The default user cache root, `~/Library/Caches/franken-manim`, happens to avoid the problem. Any user who sets the cache dir under `/tmp` or `$TMPDIR` (common in CI, scripts and sandboxes) gets a silently non-persistent cache: `persistent: False`, every lookup a miss.

### Work

1. Keep the security property while admitting trusted system links. Options, roughly from best to weakest:
   - (a) Canonicalize only the prefix of ancestors that are **owned by root and not writable by the current user**: those links cannot be attacker-controlled. Still refuse any symlink in a user-writable ancestor or in the root itself.
   - (b) Canonicalize the configured root once, at configuration time, and record the canonical path in provenance. Refuse if the canonical path differs from the configured one only through user-owned links.
   - (c) A fixed allowlist of known OS link roots (`/var`, `/tmp`, `/etc` on Darwin). This is the weakest option and must be documented as such.
2. Apply the same policy wherever `reject_symlink_components` guards a root: `Store::open` and `CacheClearAuthorization::authorize`. The `clear` path must stay at least as strict.
3. Make the portal and `fmn doctor` report *why* a cache is non-persistent, not just `persistent: False`.

### Acceptance and tests

- Extend `crates/fmn-cache/tests/torture.rs`:
  - a user-planted symlink in the root or in any user-writable ancestor is still refused, for both open and clear (existing cases);
  - a root under `std::env::temp_dir()` on macOS opens persistently (new, `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]`);
  - a root reached through a root-owned system link opens, and provenance records the canonical path.
- `production_tex_constructors_use_the_persistent_cache` passes on macOS.
- No change to the refusal reason codes for genuinely refused roots.
close_reason: Duplicate of fm-macos-var-symlink-gate-aqr1 (filed 46 minutes earlier with the same root cause and a fuller test table); the security nuance from this bead was added there as a comment.

title: W1: HardwareTopology introspection on macOS (a certified platform) — doctor reports 'fallback'; render teams ignore Apple P/E core classes
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (Apple M4 Pro, macOS 26)

`HardwareTopology::current()` (`crates/fmn-platform/src/topology.rs:349-363`) introspects **Linux only**. Every other non-wasm OS gets `HardwareTopology::fallback(logical)`, a flat topology with no core classes. On an M4 Pro (10 performance + 4 efficiency cores, one cluster per core class), `fmn doctor` prints:

```
topology: fallback (macos topology introspection is not implemented)
cores: 14 logical / 14 physical
plan: standard fast-cpu, 3 frame slots, 1 render teams / 14 render threads
```

### Why it matters

- **macos-aarch64 is a certified platform** (Revision 4 matrix, ADR-0010/0019).
- **Apple silicon is the declared first production home of the Accelerator Annex** (§10.7).
- **D-24 says scheduling derives from introspected HardwareTopology** through the ExecutionPlan, and §17.4's topology-aware render teams are a headline leapfrog ("saturate a 96-core workstation or an Apple Max part on one scene").

A flat 14-thread team ignores the P/E split. Tiles scheduled onto E-cores straggle, and a frame's latency is set by its slowest tile. fm-x68 (closed) delivered the trait and the Linux detector. fm-0do covers only a recorded aarch64 *fixture*. Nothing covers live macOS introspection.

### Work

1. Implement `detect_macos`:
   - Read `sysctlbyname("hw.nperflevels")`, `hw.perflevel{N}.{physicalcpu,logicalcpu,l2cachesize,cpusperl2}`, `hw.physicalcpu` and `hw.logicalcpu`. Reading these needs the `sysctl` FFI from a governed crate, or a `std`-only route if one exists. Respect D3: **no project-authored unsafe**. If the only route is libc FFI, it must come from an allowlisted, already-audited dependency, or ride the UPSTREAM_LEDGER into a suite crate.
   - Map perf levels to core classes and caches.
2. Teach the ExecutionPlan to prefer P-cores for render teams and leave E-cores to the emitter/encoder. That is `standard` only; certified bits are unaffected by construction (§10.5a).
3. Record a real topology snapshot fixture from this machine (closes the fixture half of fm-0do for macOS).

### Acceptance and tests

- Unit test: the parser over a recorded sysctl snapshot (fixture) yields 10P + 4E with the right L2 sharing.
- `fmn doctor` shows a non-fallback topology on macOS.
- PG-5: certified outputs stay bit-identical at {1,4,14} threads before and after.
- A calibration-mode throughput A/B (flat vs topology-aware plan), same invocation, published as a loss or a win.

title: W1: A live macOS sysctl reader from a governed crate, so HardwareTopology::current() and fmn doctor use detect_macos instead of the flat fallback
description:
## Found while working fm-macos-hardware-topology-l29x (2026-10-09)

90e2f256 landed `HardwareTopology::detect_macos` over a new `SysctlSource` capability, plus a
verbatim `sysctl` recording of an Apple M4 Pro
(`crates/fmn-platform/fixtures/sysctl_macos-aarch64_m4pro.txt`). The parser derives 10P + 4E and
the 5/5/4 L2 clusters. What is missing is a **live** `SysctlSource`, so `HardwareTopology::current()`
and `fmn doctor` still report `topology: fallback` on macOS.

### Why this cannot be done inside fmn-platform

- A live read is `sysctlbyname(3)`, which is FFI. D3 puts `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` on fmn-platform.
- D2 rules out the `sysctl(8)` subprocess: ffmpeg is the only subprocess.
- No governed dependency exposes a safe reader. Checked against `SUITE_ALLOWLIST.tsv` and the
  registry sources:
  - `libc` 0.2.189 (an ffi row) only offers `unsafe extern` calls.
  - `nix` 0.31.3 and `rustix` 1.1.4 have no `sysctlbyname`.
  - `sysinfo` 0.39.6 is a dev-only row and has no performance-level API.
  - `core-foundation` and `objc` reach fmn only through the ft Metal gateway.

### Routes (an owner decision; hence `agent:claim:manual`)

1. **Suite crate (asupersync).** Add a safe Darwin `sysctlbyname` read (integer and string OIDs)
   on asupersync `main`.
   - asupersync's AGENTS.md forbids branches, and fmn's pin `c48399f2` is an off-`main` commit
     (UPSTREAM_LEDGER row 11) whose forward-port to `main` is still owed.
   - So consuming the primitive means repinning asupersync to a `main` commit under the R17
     ritual, including a closure review of the drift.
2. **An ADR amending D3.** It would admit one narrowly audited Darwin `sysctl` boundary.

### Acceptance

- A `SysctlSource` implementation from a governed crate. The UPSTREAM_LEDGER row, `SUITE.lock`
  pin and allowlist all land in the same tranche.
- On macOS, `HardwareTopology::current()` and the CLI's `detect_topology` call `detect_macos`.
  `fmn doctor` names the sysctl source and, on the recorded M4 Pro, reports 14 logical CPUs as
  10 P + 4 E.
- A planted negative: an unreadable or inconsistent MIB still falls back, with the reason named.
- The `cargo test` gate is green.

title: W1/W10: macOS leg of the cargo test gate is red — /var -> /private/var symlink: persistent typeset cache refuses $TMPDIR roots (product bug) and 3 portal acceptance tests compare canonical vs caller paths
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check: the macOS leg of the `cargo test` hard gate is red

`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` at HEAD `96b7b7c8` on macOS 26 / aarch64 (a **certified** platform, pinned nightly-2026-08-31): **3,874 passed, 6 failed, 11 ignored**, exit 101. Four of the six failures have **one root cause**: on macOS, `$TMPDIR` is `/var/folders/...`, and **`/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`**. The owned-host gate runs on Linux, where `/tmp` is not a symlink, so this never shows up there.

All four reproduce deterministically: run serially, in isolation, with `-p fmn-python --lib -- <names> --test-threads 1`.

| Test | What breaks |
|---|---|
| `portal_typography::typesetting::tests::production_tex_constructors_use_the_persistent_cache` (`crates/fmn-python/src/portal_typesetting.rs:260`) | **Product bug.** The hardened cache-root check refuses the root: `typeset cache unavailable: refusing cache root /var/folders/.../fmn-typeset-cache-xz48062w [wrong_node_kind]: root contains a symlinked path component or reparse point`, so the cache reports `persistent: False`. Any macOS cache root under `$TMPDIR`, or under any OS-owned symlinked ancestor, silently degrades to memory-only typesetting. |
| `portal_texture::obj::tests::production_obj_material_acceptance` (`tests/obj_materials.py`, `test_constructor_identity_signature_material_parts_and_shared_normalization`) | `'/var/folders/.../materials/maps/tiles.png' not found in ('/private/var/folders/.../model.obj', ...)`. The input-closure identity reports canonical paths; the test compares the caller's spelling. |
| `portal_audio::tests::portal_compressed_audio_acceptance` (`tests/audio_inputs.py:101`) | `assert result.audio_inputs[0]["path"] == str(native_asset)`: canonical vs caller path. |
| `tests::production_bridge_acceptance_suite` (`tests/bridge.py:15006`, `verify_portal_console_scene`) | `assert pathlib.Path(rendered["destination"]) == destination`: canonical vs caller path. |

### Work

1. **Cache root policy.** Keep the security property (no symlink traversal *below* the root, no attacker-controlled redirection), but evaluate it against the **canonicalized** root:
   - Resolve the root once with `std::fs::canonicalize` (realpath), and walk from there with `openat`-style no-follow semantics for every component the engine creates or reads below it.
   - Symlinked ancestors that the OS owns (`/var` → `/private/var`, `/tmp` → `/private/tmp`, a symlinked `$HOME`) are not a traversal risk the cache can defend against anyway. Record the canonical root in the provenance manifest.
   - Check `fmn-cache` and `fmn-platform/src/fs.rs` for the same `wrong_node_kind` rule on other roots (video_dir, asset roots).
2. **Path reporting.** Decide, in one place, whether receipts and reports carry canonical paths (the right answer for input-closure hashing) or the caller's spelling. Then make the three tests compare `Path.resolve()` on both sides, or `os.path.samefile`. The tests must not paper over the product behavior; they should assert the decided contract.
3. Add `macos-aarch64` to the owned-host gate's run list, so a certified platform cannot be red unobserved. fm-0qvo (land gate) and fm-5wq.7 (owned-host inputs) are related.

### Acceptance

- The four tests pass on macOS and stay green on Linux.
- New unit test: a cache root behind a symlinked ancestor (`tempdir` → symlink → root) opens persistently, and a symlink *below* the root is still refused with `wrong_node_kind`.
- `cargo test --workspace` on macOS is green apart from the separately tracked Darwin EPERM race (fm-darwin-killpg-eperm-race-7aae) and the Studio shutdown flake.

title: W5: Opt-in Metal route for fmn::render on Apple silicon — MetalRenderer::render_nv12 exists but NativeFramePipeline refuses non-CPU plans
description:
## Problem

`fmn-render/src/metal.rs` already has a complete Metal renderer: `MetalRenderer::render_nv12` and `render_p010` rasterize on the GPU and convert on-device. Only the compact Y′CbCr planes cross to the host, and the RGBA16F surface stays device-resident. But `NativeFramePipeline::new` refuses every non-CPU plan ("native frame pipeline requires a CPU execution plan"). So `fmn::render` on Apple silicon never uses the GPU. The annex is only reachable from Studio preview and the conformance harnesses.

## Work

1. **Decide the identity contract.** Metal renders are the annex identity, not certified bytes. Record that through fm-sq8.6 (OQ-12, Metal opt-in only). This bead depends on that decision.
2. **Add an opt-in Metal route to `fmn::render`.** For example, `RenderOptions` or config `render.engine = "metal"`, valid only for non-reproducible renders. It feeds `OwnedVectorFrame` plans to `MetalRenderer::render_nv12` and writes straight into the output reservation.
   - Keep the CPU route as the fallback whenever `MetalRenderer::is_available()` is false, or a frame needs a feature the annex lacks. The existing `PreviewFallback` classification shows how.
3. **Benchmark** the Hoeffding explainer at 4K60 on an M-series Mac against the CPU route, now with fused conversion and recycled rasters. Report fps and the backend journal digest.
4. **Document** in README "Performance" that `--reproducible` stays CPU-certified.

title: W8: Rebuild advisory cache index from disk truth and bound counters
description: At commit 1c849de, the checksum-valid FMNC/2 advisory index is treated as trusted bookkeeping. crates/fmn-cache/src/store.rs:1765-1768 increments persisted next_seq with unchecked addition, so u64::MAX panics in debug and wraps in release. Lines 1911 onward and 1949 onward reuse persisted IndexEntry.size for already-known digests rather than refreshing every on-disk object, so cross-process or recreated-object drift can misreport usage and enforce the wrong ceiling; total, sum, and evicted_bytes aggregation are also unchecked. This violates the stated disk-is-truth and never-fatal index contract. Normalize or deterministically rebase logical sequences on load and merge, refresh actual object sizes during usage and maintenance, and define overflow-safe accounting. Acceptance: an externally authored but schema-valid maximum sequence never panics or wraps; stale recorded sizes cannot under-report or over-report usage or evade the ceiling; aggregation cannot overflow; rewritten ordering stays deterministic; add VirtualFs plus separate-opening regression coverage. FILED, NOT FIXED.

title: W6: G2 criterion 7 (HTML) owner ruling — does fmd's MathML from the fmd-math parser satisfy 'via the same crates', or must fmd HTML math go through fmd-math Layout?
description:
## Why

fm-djcw landed fmd PDF inline math through fmd-math Layout (franken_markdown f059cac, UPSTREAM_LEDGER row 21). PDF inline and display math now both use the shared layout; the G2 evidence packet (docs/gates/G2-native-word-evidence.md, "Cross-repo payoff (criterion 7)") records PDF as green.

HTML is unchanged. fmd emits MathML (`<math display="inline|block">`) generated from the fmd-math parse tree, and the browser lays it out. It shares the parser (one grammar, one named-error doctrine) but not the layout. The packet counts this as NOT green and does not reinterpret criterion 7 ("fmd renders `$…$` in HTML/PDF via the same crates").

## The decision (human; agent:claim:manual)

Pick one and record it in the packet (and as an ADR if it amends the criterion):

1. Parser-only MathML satisfies criterion 7 for HTML. Rationale to weigh: reflowable, selectable, zoomable, accessible math; the browser owns text layout in HTML anyway.
2. HTML must use fmd-math Layout too, e.g. inline SVG outlines with MathML kept as the accessible alternative. This becomes upstream franken_markdown work with its own UPSTREAM_LEDGER row and repin.

## Acceptance

- The packet's criterion-7 row states the ruling and its owner.
- Under option 2, a follow-up implementation bead exists and blocks fm-i1q.

title: W6: The public coverage ratchet — occurrence-weighted fmd-math coverage as a headline metric
description:
Implement the coverage ratchet (§11.5, §18; R1's public mitigation). With no LaTeX fallback, coverage DISCIPLINE replaces fallback discipline — and it must be public, precise, and monotone.

Mechanics: against G0-4's frozen corpus (the ratchet's denominator), compute per-construct and aggregate coverage — OCCURRENCE-WEIGHTED (what fraction of real-world formula mass typesets) and UNIQUE-STRING (what fraction of distinct formulas), with PARSE-vs-LAYOUT success split out (a string that parses but mislays counts as layout-fail, not success). Wire as: (a) a CI job producing the numbers per commit; (b) a RATCHET RULE — coverage may never decrease (a regression is a build break; deliberate tier changes require updating a committed baseline with a written note); (c) the public dashboard artifact (§18: a first-class DX artifact — badge + per-construct table + trend, generated into the repo/docs), naming which T2 constructs are pending with their tracked issue links, honoring the licensing rule from G0-4 (publish numbers and construct names, never the 3b1b-authored strings).

Also here: the per-construct named-error audit — every construct in the harvest that is NOT tier-1 must produce its precise unsupported error with tier + tracking link (test the error text against the harvest inventory, so no construct ever fails silently).

Acceptance: ratchet CI green with committed baseline; a deliberate-regression negative test (removing a construct fails CI); dashboard artifact generated and rendered; error-audit test over the full harvest construct list; G2's coverage checkpoint criteria (R1: coverage misses gate → public amendment with construct-sprint plan) documented as the escalation path.
close_reason: The ratchet is live: docs/ratchet/{baseline.tsv,trend.tsv,dashboard.md} + fmn-conformance::ratchet + tests/coverage_ratchet.rs. Headline numbers (frozen G0-4 denominator, 9269 strings / 17711 occurrences): PARSE 99.577% occurrence-weighted / 99.266% unique; PARSE+LAYOUT 98.916% / 98.188%, per-construct pending tables with tracked links (fm-j5t / fm-kg9 / the upstream fonts bead), trend by pin rev, escalation path (R1 public-amendment rule) and §15.3 licensing documented on the dashboard. CI teeth via pin-coupling: coverage is a pure function of (frozen corpus, fmd-math pin), so the always-on test requires baseline.tsv to name the current SUITE.lock franken_markdown rev — a pin bump without a ratchet re-run fails CI even without the private corpus; corpus-bearing runs recompute all four counts, fail on any decrease (deliberate-regression negative test at the comparator: unit-tested), and bless with RATCHET_UPDATE=1 regenerating all three artifacts atomically. The per-construct named-error audit runs always-on: all 29 T2 command/env constructs from the harvest table produce their precise tier-tagged error naming fm-j5t (probed in both modes); char: rows are layout-plane. Full gate green (one fm-rvm flake retry).

title: W6: ADR — missing font-family policy (18 corpus scenes the Reference renders; 42 name Consolas)
description:
## Found by the 2026-09-27 reality check (corpus vs Reference)

18 corpus scenes render in the pinned Reference but are refused by the portal because they request a font family that FrankenManim does not bundle, for example `CrankEmail` (Roboto). Across the whole sweep, 42 `capability_refusal` scenes name an unbundled family, mostly Consolas: the Reference's default `Text` face, via manimpango, is Consolas. The Reference renders these on a Linux host without Consolas because Pango/fontconfig substitutes a fallback face. The portal refuses by name ("font family 'Roboto' is not available; bundled families: Computer Modern, CM Typewriter, IBM Plex Sans (load a TTF by path)").

Plan §11.1: "User TTFs load by path; family-name platform scanning is a convenience tier; … There is no default that depends on the host machine." Nothing implements or decides the convenience tier, and no ADR records the refusal as the chosen policy.

## Work (owner decision; label manual)

An ADR choosing among these options:
- (a) keep refusing, documenting it as a Behavior Note with migration guidance;
- (b) a named, logged fallback to a bundled face (monospace families to CM Typewriter, sans to IBM Plex Sans, serif to Computer Modern), in standard mode only. Certified mode refuses. The fallback is recorded in provenance and warned about once per family;
- (c) family-name platform lookup: scan the standard font directories for an sfnt whose name table matches, parse it with fmd-font and record the path and hash in provenance. Standard mode only; certified requires bundled or declared fonts.
- (d) (b) plus (c): lookup first, then the named fallback.
Then implement the choice.

## Acceptance

- ADR accepted, with plan §11.1 and the Behavior Notes trued up.
- If (b), (c) or (d): the 18 Reference-renderable scenes render in the portal on the dev host, and certified runs still refuse unbundled families with the named error.
- Tests: a requested unbundled family produces the chosen behavior, and the warning or provenance record is present.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Refinement round 4: the same ADR should answer the one CJK scene of the 43. There the requested family is bundled, but no bundled face covers the glyph, and the per-character fallback (3981d93c, GH #2) runs out of faces. Option (c) platform lookup would also resolve glyph-coverage misses by name-table and cmap scan. Option (b) cannot, because no bundled face has CJK coverage. The ADR states which misses each option covers: family misses (18 scenes) and glyph-coverage misses (1 scene). Tests for the chosen behavior: a missing family and a missing glyph each produce the chosen outcome (substitution with a provenance record and a one-time warning, or the named refusal). Log fields: requested family, codepoint (for glyph misses), resolved face path and sha256 or the refusal name, and the mode (standard or certified).

title: W4: Validate decoded timeline schedule invariants and aggregate frame range
description: At exact HEAD fb8408af02dcfd36b2d2191b47e47a00eda53e5d, TimelinePlan::from_bytes verifies container framing but constructs the decoded schedule without checking its semantic invariants. Canonical bytes can therefore carry fps=0, non-finite or inconsistent run_time values, negative frame counts, discontinuous/overlapping base_frame values, overflowing base_frame+n_frames ranges, or labels whose segment/frame do not match the schedule. PlannedSegment::end_frame and downstream total/locate consumers then perform unchecked signed addition, so malformed durable input can yield incorrect lookup and can panic in checked builds. Timeline::compile also accumulates per-segment frame counts and first-frame label positions with unchecked addition, so multiple individually valid long segments can overflow the aggregate schedule. This is independent of fm-ujtl, which covers only lossy wire count encoding. Acceptance: define and enforce one canonical TimelinePlan invariant validator at decode and compile boundaries; require nonzero fps, finite canonical run times consistent with n_frames, nonnegative counts, contiguous nonoverflowing base ranges, and exact label segment/frame semantics including end labels; make end/total/locate arithmetic nonpanicking; add focused malformed-container and aggregate-overflow regressions; preserve valid canonical bytes; run focused fmn-anim gates, mandatory scripts/check.sh, exact UBS, and clean committed-tree verification. Keep open without claiming because W4 is not an active governance lane.

Current TimelinePlan::from_bytes validates every named invariant — fps through RationalFrameClock::new (zero refused), per-segment base_frame continuity against the advancing clock, n_frames re-derived and compared, overflow via checked clock advance, label segment/frame/order checks, strict reader finish — verified in code (also the closure basis of fm-o3j.2, same defect).

title: W7: Axes/NumberPlane cannot be repositioned in the native API — c2p and every derived helper stay in the unmoved frame (manim's axes.to_edge(...) then c2p idiom does not transfer)
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (writing a real explainer in the native Rust API)

In manim, `axes.to_edge(LEFT)` (or `.shift`, `.scale`, `.move_to`) moves the whole coordinate system, and `axes.c2p(...)` keeps answering in scene coordinates because it reads the live mobject. In the native Rust front door:
- `Axes` is a value built centred at the origin.
- `NumberLine` has `shifted()` (`crates/fmn-library/src/coords.rs:737`), which carries the n2p state.
- **`Axes` has no shift, move or scale at all** (`impl Axes` at `coords.rs:1164`).

Once you `stage.add(axes.vmob().clone())` and move the handle, `axes.c2p` still answers in the unmoved frame. Graphs from `get_graph`, Riemann rectangles, v-lines and labels are likewise built in the unmoved frame.

### Evidence

Every chapter of the external Hoeffding's D explainer had to:
- avoid `Axes`, or carry a manual `Vec3` offset through every `c2p` call and `.shifted(off)` every derived mobject;
- or roll its own data-window type.

The surveyed authoring notes for the native facade list this as a top gotcha ("Axes cannot be moved after build").

This is a real API-compatibility gap under D-01. Scene code that relies on `axes.to_edge(...)` followed by `c2p` does not transfer. It is the most common layout idiom in 3b1b scenes.

### Work

1. Add `Axes::{shifted, scaled_about, moved_to, to_edge, next_to}`, and the same for `NumberPlane`/`ComplexPlane`/`ThreeDAxes`.
   - Each carries both axes' n2p state and the vmob together, mirroring `NumberLine::shifted`.
   - Every helper (`c2p`/`p2c`/`get_graph`/`get_riemann_rectangles`/`get_v_line_to_graph`/labels) then answers in the moved frame.
2. Better still, investigate a live binding: an `Axes` added to a stage records its `Mob`, and `stage.c2p(axes_mob, coords)` reads the mobject's current transform. That would match the Reference's semantics after arbitrary animation (`axes.animate.shift(...)`, then `c2p` inside an `always_redraw`).
3. Add a structural fixture against the Reference: `Axes(...).to_edge(LEFT); c2p((1, 2))` agrees within the existing loose f32 tolerance.

### Acceptance and tests

- Unit and property tests: for random affine moves, `c2p` composed with `p2c` is the identity; c2p after a shift equals c2p before the shift plus the offset; every derived helper stays in agreement (extend `shifted_origins_keep_both_axes_in_agreement`).
- e2e (render-matrix class): a scene that shifts axes, then plots, renders with the graph on the moved axes, checked by a semantic placement oracle (fm-5wq.46 style).

title: W7: Native gaps for the Rust front door — 7 Appendix-A classes and 5 animations exist only as portal Python (OldTex family, bubbles, VMobjectFromSVGPath, FlashyFadeIn, ApplyMethod, TransformMatchingTex/Strings)
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check

**The Rust front door is missing a small set of Appendix-A classes that exist only as Python in the portal**, and the native `.animate` builder covers a fixed command set. Plan §15.1 and §16.2 say the two front doors share one engine and one API schema. Today a Rust user cannot construct these at all.

### Evidence (v0.5.0, `8b6fdbf0`)

**Library classes (7 of 157 Appendix-A mobject-plane classes) with no native implementation.** They exist only in `crates/fmn-python/python/manimlib_bootstrap.py`:
- SpeechBubble (`:10164`)
- ThoughtBubble (`:10199`); both are geometry-only in the Reference
- VMobjectFromSVGPath (`:8132`)
- SingleStringTex (`:10745`)
- OldTex (`:10897`)
- OldTexText (`:11028`)
- TexTextFromPresetString (`:9757`)

(The plan's "161 classes" is really 157 when Appendix A is counted; fix that number in §12/§20 while here.)

**Animation classes (5 of 80) with no native Rust implementation:** Fade (the base class), FlashyFadeIn, ApplyMethod, TransformMatchingStrings, TransformMatchingTex. The Parity Ledger (`docs/api/ledger.tsv`) wrongly attributes FlashyFadeIn and the two matchers to Rust source files. fm-5wq.12 covers ledger witness honesty; cross-link it.

**Native `.animate`** (`crates/fmn-mobject/src/animate.rs`) supports a fixed set of about 17 commands. `animate.rs:2-3` claims one builder serves both front doors, but the portal has its own Python builder.

**Native span-map consumers:** only building blocks exist (`Typeset::occurrences`, `Tex::t2c`, `fmn-anim/src/transform_matching.rs:197 transform_matching_keys`). There is no native `TransformMatchingTex` or `isolate` API, while the portal's matching-block logic is Python.

### What to do
1. Port the 7 classes natively in fmn-library, using the existing Brace/Tex/SVG machinery. ADR-0020 still applies: drawings with Reference art take user files.
2. Implement the 5 animations natively in fmn-anim over the existing mechanisms. TransformMatchingTex/Strings consume the native span map (D-09).
3. Extend native `.animate` to the full chainable surface the schema lists, or document the subset in the Parity Ledger as `tiered`, and fix the false doc comment.
4. Where the portal currently uses Python for these, switch it to the native implementations, removing Python logic (consistent with fm-5wq.15's direction).

### Acceptance
- Native constructors exist, with structural fixtures against the Reference (points, family shape, bbox) via `crates/fmn-conformance/python/structural_facts.py` class-sweep rows.
- Native animation tests: lifecycle (begin/interpolate/finish) plus endpoints. TransformMatchingTex maps matching spans by provenance, tested on `a^2+b^2=c^2 → c^2=a^2+b^2`.
- The ledger implementation column is accurate for every touched row.
- **e2e scenario** (parity class) using the native TransformMatchingTex from Rust through `fmn::render`.
- **Gates:** cargo test and portal gate suites green.

title: native_video test: incompatible_video_profiles_fail_before_any_process fails on hosts without ffmpeg (capability refusal precedes the profile refusal)
description:
crates/fmn/tests/native_video.rs `incompatible_video_profiles_fail_before_any_process` silently depends on an ffmpeg binary on PATH.

It sets `odd.ffmpeg = host_capability()`, which is `None` when `StdFfmpegLocator::from_host_path()` finds no ffmpeg. The render then refuses with the missing-capability error before it reaches the odd-dimension check, and the assertion fails:

    expected "even width and height" in refusal, got "video output requires RenderOptions::ffmpeg (or render() with the `ffmpeg` feature); native PNG-sequence, GIF and Y4M outputs need no external tool"

Observed 2026-10-09 in `cargo test -p fmn --no-fail-fast` offloaded by rch to worker ts1 (3 passed, 1 failed in that target; every other fmn target green). The same test passes on macOS with /opt/homebrew/bin/ffmpeg (4/4).

Either the profile refusals (odd 4:2:0 dimensions, translucent MP4) should be checked before the capability, as the test's name says ("before any process"), or the test should skip with a logged reason when no host ffmpeg exists, as its MP4/MOV encode sibling does. Decide which contract is intended; do not weaken the assertion.

title: W3: Copy semantics — manim's rules, to the letter
description:
Implement Mobject.copy() to the Reference's exact contract (§8.3) — user code depends on these rules, so they are API semantics, not pixel trivia: recursive copy of submobjects and ndarray attributes; updater CALLABLES kept by reference (not cloned); family-internal attribute references REMAPPED (if self.arrow is also self.submobjects[2], the copy's attribute points at the copy's submobject, not the original's); selected links cleared (parents; scene backrefs) per the Reference's rules.

Also here: the interaction with the arena (copying allocates fresh handles; generation bookkeeping), with the RecordBuffer (deep field copy; live views on the ORIGINAL unaffected; the copy starts with no views), and with target/saved-state machinery (generate_target, save_state / Restore use copies — get the reference topology right or Restore breaks).

The binding tier (fmn-python, W10) layers Python-level copy.copy / copy.deepcopy / pickle onto this engine contract — design the engine-side hooks now (a stable copy-map from old handle → new handle that the Python layer can walk for __dict__ remapping).

Acceptance: fixture tests generated from the Reference's copy behavior on representative object graphs (shared submobjects, attribute aliases, updaters, nested groups); remap-correctness property test (no copy ever references an original's family member); Restore round-trip test; documented rules for which attribute categories copy deep / by-reference / cleared.

title: W1: Neutralize the 59 code-mutating, main-pushing CI workflows and land-or-retire the 69 committed patch files
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

A large share of production code reaches `main` through hosted CI jobs that write source files and push, bypassing the local mandatory gates and AGENTS.md's "No Script-Based Changes" rule:

- `.github/workflows/` holds 96 workflow files; 59 grant `permissions: contents: write` and 59 contain a `git push` step (`grep -l 'contents: write'` / `grep -l 'git push'`), typically pushing `HEAD:main` (often `HEAD:main HEAD:master`) as `github-actions[bot]`.
- Example: `implement-rng-reservations.yml` (624 lines) embeds whole Rust source files as heredocs (`cat > crates/fmn-core/src/rng_reservation.rs <<'RS'`, line ~52), commits them, then `git push --atomic origin HEAD:main HEAD:master` (line 624). It installs `nightly-2026-07-05`, not the pinned `nightly-2026-08-31`.
- `activate-animation-semantics.yml` / `native-method-transforms.yml` run `scripts/activate_*.py`, which rewrite core crates (e.g. `crates/fmn-mobject/src/animate.rs`, `crates/fmn-anim/src/animation.rs`) by anchor string replacement, run a few crate-scoped tests, then push.
- `scripts/patches/` holds 69 committed patch files (~14.8k inserted lines); `scripts/apply_animation_composition_patch.py` embeds a base64 gzip patch.
- 48 commits since 2026-09-10 were pushed by `github-actions[bot]`.
- Several of these workflows can still fire: e.g. `activate-animation-semantics` triggers on pushes touching `Cargo.lock`; `native-subset-reveals` on edits to `subset_reveal.py`; `workflow_run` chains trigger others on upstream completion.
- Some patches were never landed at all: `git apply --check scripts/patches/native-frame-overlap.patch` still applies cleanly, i.e. the "bounded frame overlap" feature announced in `70eff4c1` is not in the tree; `crates/fmn-runtime/src/stream.rs` and `crates/fmn-python/src/portal_pipeline.rs` exist but are not declared as modules (orphans).
- Root cause stated in `scripts/enable_camera_readback.py:2-4`: agent tooling writes whole files, and `lib.rs`/`bridge.py`/the 836 KB bootstrap are too large, so agents route edits through scripts and CI.

## Work (label agent:claim:manual — deletions and policy changes need the owner)

1. Inventory every workflow into three classes: (A) read-only verification (keep), (B) code-mutating / pushing (neutralize), (C) archived-inert stubs. Publish the table in this bead.
2. For class B: immediately disable automatic triggers (remove `push`/`workflow_run` triggers, drop `contents: write`) in one reviewed commit so nothing can push to main again; then present the owner with an explicit deletion list. Per AGENTS.md RULE 1, do NOT delete any workflow, patch file, or script without the owner's written approval in-session.
3. For every patch in `scripts/patches/` and every `scripts/activate_*`/`apply_*`/`enable_*` script: determine landed / not-landed (by `git apply --check` and grep guards). Not-landed ones get either a normal reviewed implementation bead or an explicit "abandoned" note.
4. Add a policy test to `scripts/check.sh`: fail if any workflow grants `contents: write` or runs `git push` (allowlist only an owner-approved release workflow, if one is ever added).
5. Decide orphan modules (`fmn-runtime/src/stream.rs`, `fmn-python/src/portal_pipeline.rs`, `crates/fmn-python/python/animation_semantics.py` which nothing loads): wire in under a real bead or remove with owner approval.

## Acceptance

- No workflow on `main` can push to any branch or write repository contents (policy test green; negative control: a fixture workflow with `contents: write` makes the test fail).
- Classified inventory and landed/not-landed patch table recorded in this bead.
- Owner decision recorded for deletions; nothing deleted without it.
