title: W5: Refresh retained geometry and style under writable live views
description:
Root cause found during fm-ys2 fresh-eyes review. RenderPlan::sync reuses retained geometry/style solely from revision dependencies before checking live-view state, and marks Instance::volatile only for whole-buffer writable views. Direct writes through a zero-copy Python/NumPy view need not call RecordView::write and therefore need not bump revisions. A held field-scoped writable point/style view is not included in volatile at all. The result can be stale compiled geometry/style and even cache hits from stale pixels, violating plan §8.2: while a writable live view exists, the affected object or field is conservatively invalidated every frame.

Acceptance:
1. Whole-buffer writable views force fresh point and style observation every sync even when revisions do not move.
2. Field-scoped point views invalidate geometry/hints and poison affected tile keys; field-scoped style views rebuild style and poison affected tiles; unrelated field views do not needlessly recompile geometry.
3. Regression tests model mutation with no Stage/RecordView revision callback, matching a zero-copy external writer, and prove rendered output changes immediately rather than only after view drop.
4. Hint demotion remains fail-closed under every writable point-view lifetime.
5. scripts/check.sh and UBS gates pass.
notes: Implemented exact field-scoped writable-view invalidation across retained geometry/style, mirrors, bbox, primitive hints, copy/snapshot, binning, fill-kernel selection, plan identity, and tile-cache poisoning. Added a foreign-write bridge/conformance hook and regression proving frame bytes change while the field revision remains fixed. Evidence 2026-07-28: rch exec -- cargo test -p fmn-mobject -p fmn-render exited 0; rch exec -- scripts/check.sh exited 0 with fmt, all-target check, clippy -D warnings, all tests/doctests, and crate-DAG green. UBS 5.3.7 scanned all 13 changed Rust files; nonzero only for 10 audited false positives: 4 deliberate fixture-test panics, 3 ordinary render/cache comparisons misclassified as secret comparisons, and 3 srgb_decode calls misclassified as JWT decoding; no unsafe or actionable finding. Authoritative pre-stage Agent Mail conflict check: 13 paths clear, 0 conflicts.

title: W5: Route portal 2D frames through the retained vector engine (today every portal frame takes the camera route: per-frame plan clone, no tile cache, no adaptive AA, one team)
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check

**fmn-python, the front door most manim users will use, bypasses Lumen's retained 2D engine entirely.** Every portal frame, including pure-2D scenes, renders through the camera route:
- `crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs:718-731` calls `self.renderer.render_with_camera(&stage, &self.camera)`, which reaches `ThreeDJob`.

On that route:
- the whole `RenderPlan` is cloned per frame (`prepare_with_camera`: `plan: self.plan.clone()`);
- `ThreeDJob` is rebuilt every frame;
- 2D fill is per-pixel, O(pixels × pieces) (`fmn-render/src/fill.rs:1409-1501`);
- there is no tile cache, no occlusion pruning and no adaptive edge supersampling (the default camera has `samples=0`);
- it runs on the certified engine only, and uses one render team's thread count (`fmn-python/src/lib.rs` ~480-488).

The CLI's 2D route (`VectorFrameCompiler` → `OwnedVectorFrame::render_cached` through `NativeFramePipeline`, `crates/fmn/src/rendering/pipeline.rs:312-400`, `vector_frame.rs:111-128`) has all of these.

**The reason in the code comment is stale.** The comment says bypassing the camera route "reflects the delivered image vertically and violates D-23". That vflip was a bug in the 2D route itself (fm-sq8.9), fixed on 2026-09-24 (`b28c9dcb`, `fd6bea1d`). The 2D route now renders upright: the v0.5.0 `fmn` builtins were checked on 2026-10-04.

### Why it matters
- PG-1 (≤0.5× Reference wall-clock) and PG-3 (60 fps preview) are measured on exactly this path. The same-host corpus ratio is median 0.96× and work-matched 1.40× (`docs/ratchet/speed_ratio.md`). Most of the per-frame cost is Python orchestration, but the raster side is also leaving its retained-engine wins unused.
- §10.8's retained compositor and §10.4's adaptive AA are design pillars. The portal should not silently use a weaker engine.

### What to do
1. Route portal frames that contain no camera-only content (no Surface, DotCloud, Image, depth test or non-default CameraFrame orientation) through the same retained 2D path the CLI uses. Use the frame-in-flight pipeline with all render teams, and keep the camera route for 3D content. Coordinate with fm-sq8.5 item 6 (all render teams for portal and Studio).
2. Define the switch semantics:
   - under `--reproducible`, both routes must already produce certified bits for the same content (the engine-equivalence suite decides);

3. Pin with the semantic orientation oracle (separate bead) and the engine-equivalence suite (`crates/fmn-conformance/tests/engine_equivalence.rs`): add portal-route cases.
4. Measure the effect with a same-invocation interleaved A/B over the slow corpus scenes (fm-5wq.31 list). This is calibration labelled under ADR-0024, not a gate claim.

title: W5: Make IR snapshots cover full hint and subpath semantics

title: W5: Wire pure-segment frame parallelism and the FramePipeline into the production render path (FramePacket is Rc today)
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The plan calls pure-segment frame parallelism "the single biggest CPU lever" (§9.5) and designs a pipelined frame loop with render teams (§17.4, D-19). The mechanisms exist and are tested — but not in the product:

- `FramePacket` holds `state: Rc<Snapshot>` (`crates/fmn-anim/src/frame.rs:28`), so packets cannot cross threads; frame-parallel reconstruction is impossible as typed.
- The CLI renders each frame synchronously inside the capture callback (`crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs` ~4187). Purity is classified and journaled, and pure-frame reconstruction is used for Studio scrubbing (`crates/fmn-studio/src/scrub.rs` ~70), never for parallel rendering.
- `FramePipeline` (`crates/fmn-runtime/src/pipeline.rs`) is invoked only by `crates/fmn-conformance/src/perf_pg5.rs` (~759, ~906) and conformance tests — PG-5 certifies a "production mechanism" the shipping CLI never runs.
- The CLI uses only `render_teams.first()` (~3787, ~5590): on a 96-core plan that is 32 of 96 render threads (`crates/fmn-runtime/src/plan.rs` ~997-1001), while `fmn doctor` reports `render_threads` as the SUM over teams (~1827-1832) — overstating what a render uses.
- `crates/fmn-runtime/src/stream.rs` is an orphan (no `mod stream`), and `scripts/patches/native-frame-overlap.patch` still `git apply --check`s cleanly: the "bounded frame overlap" feature announced by `70eff4c1` never landed.

## Work

1. Make the packet thread-shareable (`Arc<Snapshot>` or an owned immutable snapshot) without changing its semantics; prove with the existing FramePacket tests.
2. In the production render path (CLI and the facade render API): render pure segments frame-parallel across render teams from the begin-state snapshot + alpha + keyed per-frame RNG fork; stateful segments use the bounded pipeline (front-end serial, raster/convert/emit overlapped), with ordered emission by frame index.
3. Use every render team in the ExecutionPlan; make `doctor` report exactly what a render will use.
4. Resolve the orphan `stream.rs` and the unlanded frame-overlap patch (wire in via this bead or retire with owner approval).
5. Point PG-5 at the production path: the {1,4,16} (per commit) and {32,96} (weekly) determinism checks must exercise the CLI/facade path, not a conformance-only pipeline.

## Acceptance

- Certified outputs for the full builtin + corpus scenes are byte-identical before/after and across {1,4,16} threads (and {32,96} on the weekly lane); frames emit strictly in index order under randomized completion delays (fault-injection test).
- Calibration measurement (dev EPYC, one socket) shows wall-clock scaling for a pure-segment-heavy scene at 1/8/16/32 threads; numbers recorded, not gated.
- A purity-misclassification negative control (a scene with a dt-updater) is demoted to stateful and still correct.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Register at least one e2e scenario as data in crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs (fm-fjq doctrine) exercising the user-visible behavior end-to-end, with deterministic structured NDJSON logs and an auto-bundled FMNA repro on failure; run it in the fast tier (or FMN_E2E_FULL=1 if heavy).
- [ ] Unit tests: FramePacket Send/Sync compile-time assertions; ordered-emitter tests under randomized completion order; purity classifier tests for every effect class listed in plan §9.5.

Today only compiled FMTL bundles reconstruct frames in parallel (capture_compiled, a second replay law limited to straight-path/uniform-rate segments). comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text:
Calibration-mode evidence from the 2026-10-06 reality check. These numbers are not a qualified observation: the host is a shared M4 Pro with 14 cores (10P + 4E) at load average 20–90.

A real long-form native render: the Hoeffding's D explainer, 8 chapters, 16,021 frames at 1920×1080, 60 fps, through `fmn::render` to MP4.
- Wall time: **249.5 s** in total (64 fps on average; 38–138 fps per chapter).
- CPU: **454 s user** for the render process and its ffmpeg child together, i.e. **about 1.8 cores busy on average out of 14**. The render process alone sat around 138% CPU while ffmpeg (libx264) used about 126%.
- Peak RSS 0.90 GB; peak footprint 0.41 GB.
- `fmn doctor`: "plan: standard fast-cpu, 3 frame slots, 1 render teams / 14 render threads".

So the shipping native path is roughly 7× under-utilizing this machine on ordinary 2D explainer content. That is the lever this bead describes: pure segments, rendered frame-parallel. Almost every `play()` in this video is a pure segment (Transforms, fades, tracker tweens). The exceptions are the `always_redraw` updaters that recompute statistics from live dot positions; those demote their segments to stateful.

See also fm-macos-hardware-topology-l29x: macOS gets a flat fallback topology, so even a parallel plan would ignore the P/E split here.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
2026-10-07 code map (read-only, FuchsiaHorizon). Several premises are stale; corrected scope follows.

Already true at HEAD:
- Live scenes already overlap the front end with raster through NativeFramePipeline + FrameStream, and every render team gets frames round-robin (crates/fmn/src/rendering/pipeline.rs:99-113, fmn-runtime/src/pipeline.rs:993-1000).
- Item 4 is done. mod stream exists (fmn-runtime/src/lib.rs:19) and is used by NativeFramePipeline. Both pieces of native-frame-overlap.patch are in the tree (fmn-render/src/retained.rs:291,334); the patch no longer applies. docs/IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS.md:299 still says 'orphan'.

The real serial cost is the main thread, every frame: interpolate, updaters, FramePacket::freeze (full snapshot), materialize_stage (a second copy), Arc::make_mut(RenderPlan) (a deep clone whenever a frame is in flight), and sync (geometry and SHA-256 identity).

Snapshot blocker: everything in Snapshot is Send+Sync except updaters (Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut>>, stage.rs:125-174). A projection without updaters lets FramePacket switch Rc -> Arc.

Proposed order:
(1) Freeze an updater-free Send snapshot; move VectorFrameCompiler and camera prepare into NativeFrameStages::prepare (one in-order thread, so bits are identical by construction); make RenderPlan tables Arc-chunked so make_mut stops deep-cloning.
(2) Measure PipelineStats.scene vs .raster on the corpus.
(3) Only then pure fan-out: Animation::freeze_pure for the allowlisted types, plus a PureSegmentJob sink hook. Do not reuse the FMTL replay law; it needs an end snapshot and a serial proof, and does not cover ShowPartial, Rotate or arc paths.

Cheap suspect worth testing now: RenderOptions::new defaults frames_in_flight to 2 (rendering.rs:281). That overrides the offline plan's 3-6 and cuts render teams to 2 (plan.rs:522).

comments.author: jemanuel
comments.text: Field evidence 2026-10-07 (Hoeffding explainer, 4K60 on trj, --threads 16, h264_nvenc), with fm-4k-fused-yuv-recycled-raster-4r7h applied. 600 frames of 07_shuffle render in 13.3 s per process (~45 fps); all 8 chapters (31,130 frames) run concurrently in 162 s wall. Before that bead, the profile showed the frame-coord thread as the single hot thread per process, with conversion and page zeroing as the top serial costs; those two are gone. The next per-process ceiling is serial scene capture on the owner thread. In the 540p profile, SHA-256 compress on the scene thread is 2.75% (perf/trj_hook540_hotspots.txt in the explainer). This bead's frame parallelism is now the main remaining CPU lever for one long scene.

title: W5: Decide G3's annex requirement (OQ-12, Metal opt-in only) and record the Studio security verdict
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

G3 (fm-o4q) requires "the annex serving Studio preview on supported Apple-silicon hardware (W5's Metal backend), with a declared fallback: if the annex misses, G3 passes on CPU preview meeting PG-3 and the annex requirement moves to G5 with a public note" (plan §20.3; OQ-12 owned by G3). No bead owns this decision, and the current state is:

- Metal is real but feature-gated (`metal`) and opt-in (`render.engine=metal`); it is never selected automatically, contrary to §13.5 ("on supported hardware the Studio renders through the annex engine by default").
- The published v0.4.0 macOS binary was built WITHOUT the Metal annex (it contains the "built without the Metal annex" error string), despite the release being titled "native Studio/Metal".
- The live interactive Studio worker refuses any non-CPU engine.
- PG-A has no target row (`-` in PERF_GATES.tsv); PG-A probes are `#[ignore]`d pending an Apple profile that the qualification rules currently make impossible.
- G3 also needs a Studio security sign-off (the security model is implemented: loopback-only, token, Host/Origin checks, body caps, expiry — verified by probing v0.4.0: 200 with token, 403 without, 403 bad Host, 403 bad Origin), for which no owner bead exists.

## Work (label agent:claim:manual — gate-level decision)

1. Decide OQ-12: exercise the annex path on mac-mini-max (feature build, Studio preview, CPU fallback on device loss) and either declare "annex serves preview" with evidence, or invoke the declared fallback with the public note moving the annex requirement to G5. Record as an ADR or a G3 packet section, and resolve OQ-12 in plan §23 in the same commit.
2. Decide whether release macOS artifacts ship with the `metal` feature; fix the v0.4.0 release-title claim in the next release notes.
3. Define the Studio security review (scope, reviewer, threat list: token leakage, DNS rebinding, CSRF from other local origins, oversized/forged frames, path traversal through asset routes) and record its verdict.

## Acceptance

- OQ-12 resolved in the plan; G3 packet carries the annex verdict and the security-review verdict with evidence links.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.

title: W5: Honest per-frame allocation measurement and retained caching on the real CLI path (PG-6 harness is tautological)
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

Rev-4's retained render plan (§10.8, D-20) promises that unchanged geometry is not recompiled, a `wait()` frame reduces to clock advance plus tile reuse, and PG-6's "zero steady-state heap allocations per frame" holds on the primitive corpus. In the shipping CLI path:

- Scene sync and the pixel tile cache persist across frames, but curve pre-processing (`MonoTable::build`, `crates/fmn-render/src/fill.rs` ~581-640) and binning (`Binning::build`, `bin.rs` ~600, one buffer per macrotile) are rebuilt for every shape every frame (`retained.rs` ~225-233).
- Per-frame allocations on the CLI path include `Stage::snapshot` (`crates/fmn-mobject/src/stage.rs` ~1811), `materialize` (~372), and OS threads started and joined inside every render (`crates/fmn-render/src/engine.rs` ~149-190).
- The PG-6 "zero allocations" check (`crates/fmn-conformance/src/perf_pg6.rs` ~364-409, `arena.rs` ~426) re-renders the SAME prepared frame into the same arena and counts only arena-pool growth — no global allocator counter; scene update, plan sync and binning are excluded. It cannot fail for the reasons above.
- The 3D path (`three_d.rs`) rebuilds its whole scene every frame (the approach §10.8 says was abandoned) and has no retained compositor or hierarchical depth summary.

## Work

1. Honest measurement first: a counting global allocator (test/bench builds only; `forbid(unsafe_code)`-compatible via `std::alloc::System` wrapper in a test crate) on the real CLI/facade path for the 25 builtins; report allocations/frame by stage.
2. Revision-keyed caching of monotone splits and bins for unchanged geometry/transform (per §10.8's per-resource revisions); persistent render-team thread pool instead of per-frame spawn; bump arenas for per-frame scratch.
3. Retained caches for the 3D path where revisions allow.
4. Replace the tautological PG-6 harness with the real-path counter; keep the old one only if it measures something distinct, renamed accordingly.

## Acceptance

title: W5: Bring Scribe (text and math) into the WASM graph within the size budget
description:

title: W5: 2D ScreenMap maps world +Y downward — every native 2D render (CLI, WASM, Studio, certified goldens) is vertically mirrored
description:
## Defect (found 2026-09-24 while adjudicating the 67b1c438 golden re-pin)

Every 2D render that goes through `fmn_render::ScreenMap` is vertically mirrored. `ScreenMap::place` (`crates/fmn-render/src/bin.rs` ~103-109) maps object space to pixels as `origin + world * scale` on BOTH axes, but object space is manim's +Y-up plane and every `FrameBuffer` is top-row-first (D-23: no vflip anywhere). The same formula is inlined in fill.rs, stroke.rs, fill/color_field.rs, engine.rs (hull_slab), metal.rs, and `fill::instance_translation`.

Evidence:
- HEAD `fmn --format png @builtin tex_span.v1` renders "Hello" upside down (standalone native CLI).
- Certified scene goldens: `matchers_marks.v1` shows "match me" upside down, its Underline above the text and the Checkmark as a caret — locked bit-for-bit in `crates/fmn-conformance/goldens/scene_goldens.certified.lock`.
- The Python portal hit the same bug and fixed it ONLY for itself (fd6bea1d, fm-5wq.4.20: "Portal coordinates follow manim's +Y-up camera plane, while every FrameBuffer is already in top-row-first output orientation. The camera route owns that projection (including the Y inversion) ... Bypassing it ... reflects the delivered image vertically"). The native CLI, WASM tier 1, native Studio and the certified golden harness still use the 2D ScreenMap path.
- Studio's browser mapping (`crates/fmn-studio/src/studio.js` ~233 overlay projection, ~501 pointer picking) encodes the same y-down convention.
- The primitive corpus (circles, polygons, arcs) is nearly symmetric, which is why G1's Look Gallery did not catch it.

## Fix

- One definition of the object->pixel map on `ScreenMap` (forward point, translation delta, inverse) with y inverted; every inline duplicate in fmn-render routed through it; `studio.js` overlay + picking inverted consistently.
- `RENDERER_VERSION` 6 -> 7: identical inputs now produce different certified bits, so journals, caches and FMTL bundles must not mix orientations. Regenerate `demo/wasm/bundle.fmtl`.

## Acceptance

- Mechanical adjudication of every changed certified 2D golden: the new frame is the vertical mirror of the old frame (origin is at the frame centre, so pixel centres map to mirrored world rows), within last-bit float tolerance, recorded per scene. Camera-route goldens (3D gallery) must not change.
- A permanent orientation test: an asymmetric shape above the origin lands in the upper half of the frame (native retained path AND camera path agree), with glyph orientation checked on real text.
- `fmn --format png @builtin tex_span.v1` renders upright text (visual check recorded).
- Full `cargo test` for fmn-render, fmn-conformance, fmn-cli, fmn-wasm, fmn-studio green; every re-blessed lock adjudicated in the commit message.

ScreenMap.y_up + one mapping definition; front doors oriented; y_up journaled + cache key; RENDERER_VERSION 7; studio.js inverted; new orientation tests (bin mapping laws, retained 2D + camera route agree). Adjudication: 54/54 scene-golden frames are exact vertical mirrors of pre-fix frames (max diff 0); raw golden sizes unchanged; gallery_3d unchanged. Suites: fmn-conformance all green after re-bless (was 421 pass/8 expected fails); rest of workspace 2905 passed 0 failed; clippy -D warnings and fmt clean. Fresh-pass verification from git archive of b28c9dcb: fmn @builtin tex_span.v1 renders upright; certified circle_shift identical at 1 vs 16 threads; engine identity certified-cpu:scalar:7. Not verified: macOS/aarch64 certified matrix (fm-5wq.16), Metal feature build (compiled with --all-features on linux only).

title: W9: fmn-studio worker_frame_publication test flakes on macOS — shutdown() returns ENOTCONN (os error 57) after the peer's FIN; unwrap panics under load
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (macOS, workspace `cargo test` under load)

`fmn-studio` `host::tests::worker_frame_publication_uses_the_supervisor_protocol_budget` failed once in the full workspace run on macOS:

```
panicked at crates/fmn-studio/src/host.rs:3565:51:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: Os { code: 57, kind: NotConnected, message: "Socket is not connected" }
```

It passed 2/2 when re-run in isolation, so it is timing-dependent.

Line 3565 is `server.shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Both).unwrap()`, immediately after `client.shutdown(Both)`. On Darwin, `shutdown(2)` on a socket whose peer has already completed its shutdown returns `ENOTCONN`; Linux returns success. Under load the client's FIN is processed first and the unwrap panics.

### Work

- In this test and any sibling Studio tests (grep `shutdown(std::net::Shutdown::Both).unwrap()` in `crates/fmn-studio` and `crates/fmn-cli`), treat `ErrorKind::NotConnected` from `shutdown` as success. Do the same in production socket-teardown paths, if any unwrap or propagate it: a peer that already hung up is not an error at teardown.

### Acceptance

- The test passes 200/200 under `--test-threads 16` on macOS with a background CPU load.
- No production teardown path surfaces `NotConnected` as a user-visible error.

# W9: Populate the native Studio worker's Inspect SpanRegistry from Scribe span maps

## Background (reality check 2026-08-29)
The Studio inspector's span-map machinery is built and tested in `fmn-studio`:
`inspect.rs::SpanRegistry::bind_native`, `SourceSpanSnapshot`/`SpanKind`,
`source_span_registration_is_atomic_across_late_map_errors`, budget-bounded JSON. But the SHIPPED

span maps") is only partially real — hover-a-glyph-see-its-source, W6SPAN's in-Studio payoff, is

2. Keep InspectorLimits budgets (byte/depth bounds) — span tables for large formulas must truncate

3. Wire the debug-overlay path consistently (overlays already follow visible family order).

# W8: Expose native SVG export through a Reel sink and the CLI (`--format svg`)

## Background (reality check 2026-08-29, post fm-ek1)
fm-ek1 closed 2026-08-24 having landed the export *machinery* in `crates/fmn-geom/src/svg.rs`

re-exported at the fmn-geom root, with importer round-trip proofs and the documented fidelity
ruling (shapes are in post-viewBox user space; viewBox deliberately not re-emitted).

But plan §14.2 lists "SVG export (`vmobject_to_svg`)" under **Reel's native codecs**, and today no
output crate exposes it: `OutputFormat` has no Svg variant, no sink exists in fmn-output, and the
only reachable exporter is the Python-portal Reference shim (`manimlib_bootstrap.py:7190`). The

title: W10: Reject invalid absolute-tolerance budgets

Add a precise invalid-tolerance verdict, require a finite non-negative tolerance before comparing operands, and cover scalar plus inherited slice/point behavior without changing valid finite comparisons. title: W6: Tex lays out in TeX text style; the Reference's Tex is display style (align*) — formulas render ~2.3x too small with wrong limit placement
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check (side-by-side against the pinned Reference)

**Every `Tex` is laid out in TeX *text* style. The Reference's `Tex` is *display* style.** Big operators, fractions and integrals therefore come out at roughly half the Reference's size and with the wrong limit placement. This affects the README hero formula and most of the 3b1b corpus.

### Why the Reference is display style
- The Reference's `Tex` wraps its source in `\begin{align*} … \end{align*}` (`tex_environment = "align*"`, Reference `manimlib/mobject/svg/tex_mobject.py`).
- `align*` is display math. `\sum`/`\prod` limits stack above and below, `\frac` uses display-size numerators and denominators, and `\int` is the large display glyph.
- The portal records this (`crates/fmn-python/python/manimlib_bootstrap.py:8657`, `tex_environment = "align*"`), but nothing reads it for layout.

### Where we go wrong
- `crates/fmn-library/src/tex.rs:166-181`: `Tex::new` defaults to `mode: Mode::Math(MathStyle::Text)`. Its doc comment says this is "the Reference's defaults: text-style mathematics". That statement is false.
- `Tex::display()` (`tex.rs:184-188`) exists, but neither the portal nor the native default uses it.

### Measured evidence (v0.5.0 wheel vs Reference `6199a00d`, same host, 2026-10-04)

`Tex(r"\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2}")`:

| Engine | Height | Width |
|---|---|---|
| Portal | 0.5877 | 1.4125 |
| Reference | 1.3309 | 1.3679 |

The heights differ by **2.26×**. Final frames of the README `SquareToCircle` and of a `Matrix`/`cases`/`\sum` scene show the same thing:
- Reference: a large integral with limits at the bottom and top corners, display fractions, and `\sum` limits stacked.
- Portal: a small integral, script-size fractions, and `\sum` limits as sub/superscripts.

Repro:
```python
import sys; sys.argv = sys.argv[:1]
from manimlib import *
eq = Tex(r"\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^2}")
print(eq.get_height(), eq.get_width())   # Reference 1.331 / 1.368; portal 0.588 / 1.413
```
Run it with the portal venv, and with the Reference as `PYTHONPATH=scripts/manim_ref xvfb-run -a refenv/bin/python probe.py`.

### Why nothing caught it
- The corpus structural differential (`crates/fmn-conformance/fixtures/structural_facts/exclusions.json`) blankets whole Text/Tex subtrees, so Tex geometry is never compared.
- The Look Gallery has one math panel.
- The ratchet's "layout" column only means `typeset()` returned Ok, and oracle-checked layout is 0% (`docs/ratchet/dashboard.md`).
- G0-2 measured fmd-math as 6.4% narrower than LaTeX, attributed it to "tighter inter-atom spacing", and never established the cause.

### What to do
1. Make the Reference semantics the default:
   - `Tex` lays out each line in display style with `align*` behaviour: `&` alignment points and `\\` line breaks, as the Reference does.
   - `TexText` stays text mode. Its `$…$` islands are text style and `$$…$$` is display, per ADR-0006.
   - Fix the false doc comment.
2. Check every caller that relied on the text-style default and decide each one explicitly:
   - de-TeX'd natives such as DecimalNumber, which should stay text style;
   - Matrix entries (`MobjectMatrix`/`TexMatrix` entries are `Tex` in the Reference, so display);
   - axis labels;
   - the `tex_span.v1` builtin;
   - the portal's `Tex`/`SingleStringTex`/`OldTex`.
3. Re-bless the affected self-goldens with provenance: name the commit, show old vs new frames side by side, and state that the bits changed because the layout style changed. No silent re-bless.
4. Add a Reference-derived oracle:
   - For about 200 corpus formulas, ranked by occurrence and covering `\sum`, `\int`, `\frac`, `\prod`, `\lim`, `\binom` and matrices, capture the Reference's `Tex(...).get_width()` and `get_height()` once into a checked-in TSV.
   - Assert that fmd-math's box is within ±8% in each dimension.
   - The capture uses LaTeX once, offline, the same way Reference imagery is captured. No LaTeX enters CI or any runtime path.
   - This coordinates with fm-tex-layout-oracle-bkbc and should feed it.
5. Check whether the G0-2 "6.4% narrower" finding is fully explained by this. If not, record the remaining cause in the TeX oracle bead.

### Acceptance
- **Unit tests** (fmn-library and fmd-math consumers):
  - `\sum_{a}^{b}` in `Tex` puts its limits above and below the operator (limit box centres lie on the operator's vertical axis);
  - `\frac{1}{2}` numerator height is at least 0.9× the text-size digit height;
  - `\int` uses the display-size glyph;
  - `TexText("$\frac12$")` stays text style.
- **Portal installed-wheel test:** the Reference-derived size TSV is within tolerance for all rows, with a per-row diff logged on failure.
- **e2e scenario** (parity class) in `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/e2e_scenarios.rs`: renders the README SquareToCircle formula and asserts the display-style bbox envelope.
- **Logging:** each oracle row prints formula, expected (w, h), actual (w, h) and relative error.
- **Gates:** cargo fmt/clippy/test green; portal gate suites (`scripts/check_portal_runtime.sh`) green; G2 packet criterion 1 updated with the new evidence.

title: W6: Corpus-wide TeX layout-correctness oracle and a real math Look Gallery (today: one math panel)
description:
## Why this exists (reality check 2026-09-23)

The plan's quality bar for fmd-math is "side-by-side indistinguishable at a glance from LaTeX output on the corpus, judged in the Look Gallery; spacing rules verified against the published parameters" (§11.4). Evidence today:

- Correctness: 21 placement tests check positions against published TeX math parameters (`fmd-math/tests/placement_params.rs`); the spacing table is checked against TeXbook p.170. Nothing compares whole-formula box dimensions or glyph positions against real TeX across the corpus. The 17 layout goldens are the engine's own output, locked (self-goldens), so they detect change, not wrongness.
- Beauty: the Look Gallery has exactly ONE math panel (Euler's identity, `look_gallery.tsv`), ratified by an AI delegate who preferred the LaTeX Reference render; strokes were visibly lighter than the Reference.
- The coverage ratchet's 99.8% "parse+layout" counts formulas for which `typeset()` returned `Ok`.

## Work

1. One-time capture (like the Look Gallery's Reference-imagery capture — never a runtime or CI dependency, consistent with D-03's "no LaTeX on any path"): for a stratified sample of >=500 corpus formulas (by construct class and occurrence rank), record TeX's box width/height/depth and per-glyph positions from real TeX on the dev box (the Reference environment there already has LaTeX), committed as licensing-safe numeric fixtures (no corpus text in the public repo if restricted).
2. An oracle test comparing fmd-math layouts to those fixtures with documented tolerances (e.g. in em units), reporting per-construct-class error distributions; failures above tolerance are filed by construct.
3. Extend the Look Gallery with >=24 math panels spanning fractions, radicals, big operators with limits, matrices/cases, extensible delimiters at several sizes, accents, text islands and multi-line align; human review verdicts recorded (at-least-as-good / different-but-fine with Behavior Note / regression).
4. Add a "passed layout oracle" column to the ratchet dashboard.

## Acceptance

- Fixtures + oracle test committed; per-class error table published; >=24 math Look Gallery panels with recorded verdicts; ratchet dashboard shows oracle-pass rate separately from typeset-Ok rate.
acceptance_criteria: - [ ] Every new check emits bounded, deterministic structured logs (NDJSON: inputs, digests, decision, refusal reason) so a red run is diagnosable from logs alone; record the exact commands run and their exit codes in the close reason.

title: W6: fmd-math formulas are 2-18% narrower than LaTeX at equal font_size — relation glyphs (≥ ≤ ≠) fall back to a heavy non-CM face, no italic correction (f( abuts), tight relation spacing
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check (side-by-side against the pinned Reference)

**fmd-math formulas are systematically 2-18% narrower than the Reference's LaTeX output at the same `font_size`.** Some relation glyphs also come from a visibly different, heavier face than Computer Modern. This is independent of the display-style bug (fm-tex-display-style-nclg): none of the cases below uses a display-sensitive construct.

The quality bar for §11.4 is "side-by-side indistinguishable at a glance from LaTeX". G0-2 recorded fmd-math as 6.4% narrower than LaTeX on one formula and attributed it, without proof, to "tighter inter-atom spacing". It was accepted as "different-but-fine" by an AI delegate who preferred the LaTeX render.

### Measured: `Tex(s).get_width()`, v0.5.0 portal vs Reference `6199a00d`, same host, 2026-10-04

| source | portal w | Reference w | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| `x \geq 0` | 0.9681 | 1.1373 | **0.851** |
| `a = b` | 1.0636 | 1.0891 | 0.977 |
| `f(x)` | 0.7123 | 0.8733 | **0.816** |
| `x + y` | 1.0407 | 1.0978 | 0.948 |
| `a \leq b \neq c` | 1.7389 | 1.9546 | **0.890** |
| `x \quad y` | 0.9330 | 0.9895 | 0.943 |
| `e^{i\pi} + 1 = 0` | 2.1714 | 2.3180 | 0.937 |
| `\alpha\beta\gamma` | 0.7126 | 0.8588 | **0.830** |
| `\sin x + \cos y` | 2.4535 | 2.5079 | 0.978 |
| `x^2 + y^2 = r^2` | 2.4418 | 2.6068 | 0.937 |

Heights agree to within about 1-3%, except the relation rows: `a \leq b \neq c` is 0.355 tall against 0.454, because the `\neq` slash is shorter.

### Visible defects (rendered `Tex(r"x \geq 0 \quad f(x) \quad \leq \neq", font_size=120)` in both engines)
1. **Relation glyphs `\geq`, `\leq`, `\neq` come from a heavy, short fallback face, not CM's cmsy shapes.** CM draws a thin, wide ≥ with a separate bar and a long \neq slash; ours are stubby and bold. The likely cause is that CM Unicode lacks the codepoints, so the mapping falls through to the curated Noto Sans Math subset. Verify in `fmd-math`'s symbol table and the fmd-font fallback chain. Every inequality in the corpus is affected.
2. **No italic correction after `f` before `(`.** Our `f` abuts the parenthesis; the Reference leaves TeX's italic-correction gap. In TeX an Ord italic glyph followed by a non-script atom gets its italic correction added (TeXbook Appendix G rule 17 and the math italic handling). The same likely explains `\alpha\beta\gamma` at 0.83×.
3. **Relation and binary spacing look tight.** The gap around ≥ is visibly smaller than TeX's thickmuskip (5mu plus 5mu; 18mu = 1em, so a natural 5/18 em each side). Check the spacing table values and the mu→em conversion at text/display styles.
4. **Even `x \quad y` is 5.7% narrower.** `\quad` is exactly 1 em of the current font. Either our em, i.e. the `font_size_for_unit_height` scaling, differs from the Reference's, or glyph advances do. Establish which, because it scales everything.

### What to do
1. **Root-cause each of 1-4** with fmd-math layout traces: box widths, kerns, italic corrections and glue per atom. Compare against TeX's own numbers for the same string; a one-time offline LaTeX `\showbox`/`\wd` capture gives exact TeX widths.
2. **Glyph coverage:** make CM-family glyphs the source for the standard relation set (≤ ≥ ≠ ≡ ≈ ∼ ⊂ ⊃ ∈ …):
   - use the bundled CM Unicode face where it has them;
   - otherwise use the cmsy-equivalent outlines bundled under OFL (Latin Modern Math is OFL/GUST, and its D1/allowlist status needs checking before use);
   - otherwise draw them as paths, as ADR-0005 does for delimiters.
   Noto Sans Math stays the last-resort fallback, and every fallback use is logged and counted in the ratchet.
3. Implement italic correction per Appendix G, and fix spacing values if they are wrong.
4. **Add the width oracle:** the table above plus about 200 occurrence-ranked corpus strings, with Reference-derived widths captured once offline into a checked-in TSV. Tolerance ±3% for plain strings, ±6% for strings with fallback glyphs, and zero fallback glyphs in the standard relation set. Coordinate with fm-tex-layout-oracle-bkbc, which owns the corpus-wide oracle; this bead owns these specific defects.
5. Re-bless affected goldens per protocol (before/after side-by-side).

### Acceptance
- **fmd-math unit tests:**
  - `f(x)` includes italic correction (width within 2% of TeX's box);
  - `\geq`/`\leq`/`\neq` glyphs come from the CM-family source (glyph source asserted);
  - `\quad` equals 1 em of the current size;
  - thickmuskip/medmuskip/thinmuskip spacing equals TeX's values at text style.
- **Portal installed-wheel oracle test:** every row of the width TSV is within tolerance. Failures log source, expected, actual and the per-atom trace.
- **e2e scenario** (parity class): a formula strip rendered and its width asserted.
- **Ratchet:** a new column "glyph fallback occurrences" (target 0 for the standard relation set).
- **Gates:** cargo test (fmn and franken_markdown at the pinned rev, via UPSTREAM_LEDGER), portal gate suites.

So every relation and many operators render in Noto Sans Math's heavier sans design, not cmsy. Fix options, all cross-repo (franken_markdown + SUITE.lock + allowlist): (a) bundle CM-design math symbol outlines under a D1-acceptable license (Latin Modern Math is GUST/OFL-style: check D1 and the font licence bundle); (b) drawn-path relation glyphs in CM proportions, as ADR-0005 does for delimiters; (c) a curated cmsy-equivalent subset. The italic-correction and spacing findings in the description are separate and still open.

comments.text:
Root-cause measurement, 2026-10-05: per-glyph ink boxes at font_size 48. Portal wheel git:173f447a vs the pinned Reference (refenv, private config dir), via scratch glyph_trace.py.

1. **Upright glyphs match; italic letters do not.**
   - '1' 0.1599 vs 0.1607 (0.995); '11' 0.995; '=' 0.3208 vs 0.3238.
   - Math-italic 'x' is 0.2252 vs 0.2425 (0.929) and 'y' 0.935, heights within 0.5%.
   - fmd-math sets math letters in FACE_ITALIC (CM Unicode *text* italic, cmunti). TeX sets them in cmmi10, a different design: cmmi10 f advances 0.49 em against cmti's 0.31 em. This is the main source of the 2-18% narrowness; alpha/beta/gamma at 0.83 is the same cause (see fm-5wq.60, where alpha reads as a Latin a and theta as vartheta).
2. **Rule 17 italic correction is missing.**
   - fmd-math synthesizes delta as max(0, ink xmax - advance) (faces.rs:148) but uses it only for superscript placement (layout.rs:949).
   - TeX Appendix G rule 17 also appends delta as a kern after a math-font character when no subscript follows. In f(x) the portal '(' starts at 0.2082, inside f's ink (0.2311); the Reference's starts at 0.3132.
3. **Scripts.** The superscript in x^2 is 0.1355 vs 0.1507 wide (0.90): a 0.7x-scaled cmr10 against TeX's optically sized cmr7.
4. **Relations.** x >= 0: the ≥ ink is 0.228 vs 0.2975 wide and shorter (Noto Sans Math fallback, already diagnosed). Spacing around = at the ink level: portal gaps 0.150/0.219, Reference 0.177/0.186. The asymmetry is consistent with italic-face side bearings, not the thickmuskip value.

Consequence: items 1, 3 and 4 need a CM *math* face (cmmi, cmsy, cmex and script sizes), i.e. a new bundled font asset. That is a licensing and closure decision (D-08, §11.1) and goes to an ADR. Item 2 (rule 17) is face-independent and can land in fmd-math now.

title: W5: Two-level binning, per-tile command lists, painter-order-safe occlusion pruning
description:
Implement Lumen's spatial organization (§10.8): object bounds → ~128x128 MACROTILES → engine-sized fine tiles → stable per-tile command runs, with sizes tuned per platform by the ExecutionPlan (§17.4) — tuning changes speed, never semantics. Command lists keep STABLE draw indices derived from W3ORDER's deterministic draw sequence; transparent runs stay in EXACT painter order; (annex note for later: deterministic count/prefix/scatter or stable key sort, never unordered atomic appends — the CPU binning must be expressible that way too, so keep the algorithm order-stable by construction).

OCCLUSION PRUNING, painter-order-safe: a conservative back-to-front opaque-coverage mask per tile lets provably-hidden commands be skipped ONLY when the result is provably unchanged (full opaque cover by later-drawn content in the same tile, no blending interactions); depth-tested 3D adds a hierarchical per-tile depth summary. The rule is absolute: pruning is an optimization with a proof obligation per skip — when in doubt, draw.

Determinism obligations (§10.5): tiles are write-disjoint by construction (one owner per tile per pass); composite order is fixed; binning output is identical at any thread count (parallel binning must produce the same command lists as serial — stable partitioning, no completion-order dependence).

Acceptance: binning golden tests (fixture scenes ⇒ identical tile command lists at {1,4,16} threads); painter-order preservation tests through binning; occlusion-pruning equivalence tests (pruned vs unpruned frames bit-identical on an adversarial corpus: translucent stacks, opaque covers, depth-tested mixes); macrotile/fine-tile size-sweep test proving size choices don't change output bits.
notes: FROM fm-gw7: the per-tile command list is this bead's to build. What exists upstream of it: fmn_render::plan::RenderPlan produces the painter-ordered instance list (ShapeTable::instances(), each carrying shape/style/offset/order), which is the input a binner consumes. The CSR shape (u32 offsets + u32 draws, built by a deterministic host-side count -> prefix -> scatter) was proven end-to-end on Metal in G0-8 and is structurally what §10.8 mandates — see the earlier note on this bead for F13's flag word.
close_reason:
Landed in crates/fmn-render/src/bin.rs (64 tests in the crate). Two-level binning (object bounds -> macrotiles -> fine tiles), CSR command lists with F13's per-command class word, and painter-order-safe occlusion pruning.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Binning golden / thread-count invariance: build_partitioned(n) makes §10.5's obligation testable WITHOUT threads — a partition is a slice of the painter-ordered instance list, counts sum in partition order, and each instance scatters to a slot derived from that sum. Byte-identical offsets/draws/flags at n in {1,2,3,4,5,7,16,64}, including counts that do not divide the work evenly. Pruning is checked under the same sweep.
- Painter order through binning: every tile run ascends in instance index, which IS painter order because the instance list is.
- Occlusion-pruning equivalence: stated the way it can be checked before an engine exists — for every pixel, the VISIBLE SUFFIX (everything from the last opaque full-cover onward) is identical pruned vs unpruned. Adversarial corpus: translucent covers (prune nothing), concave covers (never claim to cover), covers that miss a tile, and the covering command itself never dropped.
- Size sweep: tile size is a scheduling choice. The invariant is NOT identical per-pixel lists — binning is conservative, so a coarser tile legitimately lists more — it is that every tiling delivers every RELEVANT command in painter order, agreeing with an unbinned ground truth. Checked at 5 tilings over a pixel grid.

FOUND AND FIXED A REAL BUG IN fm-gw7's TABLES: shape_digest excluded position (which is what makes interning find anything) but compile_shape stored ABSOLUTE points, so two copies of one outline shared geometry sitting at the first copy's position — the second binned on top of the first, and an opaque cover pruned a draw nowhere near it. Compiled outlines are now shape-local, hints are localized with them (Hint::translated), and ScreenMap::place REQUIRES the instance offset so the mistake is not expressible. The IR golden moved and was adjudicated in the same commit, which is the golden doing its job.

DEFERRED, with reasons: frame-level pruned-vs-unpruned bit-identity needs a rasterizer — the visible-suffix property above is the strongest available now, and G0-8b already proved frame bit-identity for this mechanism against the spike's own fill. Depth-tested 3D's hierarchical per-tile depth summary waits on depth existing (fm-2u6/G3). Tile sizes come from §17.4's ExecutionPlan, which is fm-3df; Tiling carries defaults and takes them as parameters, which is the shape it needs either way.

title: W5: Tile-key hashing is ~12% of a 4K frame — TileKey::build mixes every command byte-wise (FNV-1a, 8 dependent multiplies per u64) plus SipHash on tile indices
description:
## Evidence

Profiled on trj (Threadripper PRO 5995WX) with the Hoeffding explainer: 07_shuffle at 3840x2160 and 60 fps, `--threads 16`, h264_nvenc. This was after fm-4k-fused-yuv-recycled-raster-4r7h and fm-skip-restore-recycled-tiles-xikh, at 600 frames in 9.97 s. `perf record -F 499 -g` ran for 6 s and collected 42,566 samples:

| Rank | Symbol | Share |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `FrameJob::render_band` (real rasterization) | 11.2% |
| 2 | **`revision::Mixer::write_u64`** | **8.1%** |
| 3 | `convert_band` (NV12, now parallel) | 6.0% |
| — | `RandomState::hash_one::<&usize>` | 2.4% |
| — | `PixelTileCache::retain_rasterized_tiles` | 2.6% |
| — | `cache::TileKey::build` | 1.4% |
| — | `fmn_hash::sha256::Sha256::compress` (scene thread) | 1.7% |

Building tile keys (`Mixer` + `hash_one` + `TileKey::build`) therefore takes about 12% of a 4K frame. That is more than the NV12 conversion, and second only to real rasterization.

## Cause

`TileKey::build` (`fmn-render/src/cache.rs` ~136–153) feeds every command of every tile through `Mixer::write_u64`. That function is byte-wise FNV-1a: 8 dependent multiplies per `u64` (`revision.rs` ~333). Per tile and per frame it mixes the shape, style, flags, every coefficient's bits, and every revision. A `HashMap<usize, _>` with SipHash `RandomState` adds `hash_one::<&usize>` on top.

## Work

1. **Separate hasher.** Give tile keys their own process-local hasher. Don't change `mix`/`Mixer`, which may feed journaled revision digests; check every caller first.
   - Use a word-at-a-time mixer with full avalanche: a wyhash/rapidhash-style 64x64→128 fold, or two independent 64-bit lanes giving a 128-bit key.
   - A collision silently reuses wrong pixels, so the key must stay at least as strong as today's 64-bit FNV-1a. Prefer 128 bits, and document the bound.
2. **Tile-index map.** Replace SipHash `RandomState` on `usize` tile indices with direct indexing or an identity/FxHash map. The keys are dense tile indices.
3. **Incremental keys (optional).** A tile whose command list is unchanged since the last frame (same plan revision ranges) could skip rehashing entirely.
4. **Prove identical output.** Bytes and hit/miss behavior must not change. Run the existing `retained_pixels_*` tests and the resumed-surface test. If a colliding-under-FNV input can be constructed, add a test showing the new key separates it.
5. **Re-measure** the same scenario. Expect up to about 10% at 4K.

title: W6: Wire the fmn-cache typeset cache and pre-play Tex preflight into fmn, fmn::render and fmn-python (built and tested, unused); G2 criterion 5 is overclaimed
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-04 reality check

**The typeset cache and the pre-play typesetting preflight are built and tested, but no shipped entry point uses either.** G2's evidence packet nevertheless counts "typeset caching" as live (criterion 5). That is an overclaim.

### Evidence (v0.5.0, `8b6fdbf0`)

**Cache:**
- `fmn_tex::TexEngine::with_cache(&fmn_cache::Store)` (`crates/fmn-tex/src/engine.rs:159`) is called only from tests and the PG-7 harness (`crates/fmn-conformance/src/perf_pg7.rs:526`).
- The portal (`crates/fmn-python/src/lib.rs` ~10453, `portal_typography.rs:57`) and the `fmn` facade (`crates/fmn/src/lib.rs:290`) build engines with only a bounded in-memory cache.
- The only production `fmn_cache::Store::open` is on an in-memory `VirtualFs` used for Studio replay (`crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs` ~7451).
- `fmn doctor` reports `cache: ~/.cache/franken-manim (exists false, direct entries 0)` after real renders, which corroborates this.

**Preflight:**
- `TexEngine::preflight` (`engine.rs:345`) parallelises typesetting across a worker pool. The only non-test callers are PG-7 and the scene runtime's hook point.
- That hook point (`crates/fmn-scene/src/runtime.rs:1835`) defaults to `NoPreflight` (`runtime.rs:457, 735`), and no front door installs a real hook.
- `Tex` is also typeset eagerly inside `build()`, so even an installed hook would find nothing left to do. Plan §11.5 wants static Tex/Text strings typeset in parallel before the first `play()` so PG-4's <150 ms cold start holds "by design".

### What to do
1. **Persistent cache in the shipped paths.**
   - `fmn`, `fmn::render` and `fmn-python` open the content-addressed store at the conventional cache dir (`docs/dist/cache_config_conventions.md`), honour `--clear-cache` and the config's cache settings, and pass it to `TexEngine::with_cache`.
   - Key on (string, pack, font hashes, engine version) as §14.4 specifies.
   - `--reproducible` must stay correct: a cache hit has to be bit-identical to a miss. Test this.
2. **Preflight.**
   - Make Tex/Text construction lazy enough that the runtime can collect static strings before the first `play()` and typeset them across the worker pool (`TexEngine::preflight`).
   - Alternatively, run construct-time typesetting on the pool and join before the first frame.
   - Install the hook in the CLI, facade and portal runtimes.
3. **Correct the G2 packet** (`docs/gates/G2-native-word-evidence.md`): criterion 5 is NOT GREEN until (1) lands.

### Acceptance
- **Test:** rendering the same Tex-heavy scene twice in fresh processes, the second run reports cache hits (counter in provenance or log) and identical frame bits. Under `--reproducible` the hit and miss bits are identical.
- **Test:** with preflight enabled, all static Tex strings of a 20-formula scene are typeset before frame 0. The hook log shows N strings preflighted on more than one worker, and no typesetting happens inside `play()`.
- `--clear-cache` empties the store; a corrupted entry is detected and recovered (fmn-cache already has these primitives; prove them end to end).
- **e2e scenarios** (lifecycle class): cache-warm second run; preflight-before-first-play.
- **Logging:** cache hits, misses and bytes per run; preflight count and wall time.
- **Gates:** cargo test, portal gate suites, PG-7 harness run through the same entry point.

title: W6: a checksum-valid typeset entry with a foreign or undecodable payload is rejected on every run and never replaced (put loses to the incumbent with KeyConflict)
description:
## Found by the fresh-eyes review of the typeset cache wiring (fm-typeset-cache-preflight-wiring-1sn0)

`TexEngine::typeset` (`crates/fmn-tex/src/engine.rs`) treats a checksum-valid envelope
whose payload does not decode to a `Typeset`, or decodes to another source, as a rejection:
it recomputes and does not trust it. That is correct. But the bad entry is never removed.
The recompute's `Namespace::put` then loses create-if-absent publication to the incumbent,
verifies it, finds a different payload and returns `KeyConflict`. So the key stays poisoned:
every later run rejects it again and lays the formula out again, forever.

The envelope-corrupt path does not have this problem: `Namespace::get_at` evicts a corrupt
envelope, so the next run republishes and heals.

### When it happens

Any change to the `Typeset` codec's decode rules (a new canonicality check, say) that
lands without a `TYPESET_FORMAT_VERSION` bump inside one fmn-tex version. Old entries then
decode-fail on every read. Also any producer that publishes a different payload under a
typeset key.

### Visibility today

Since the review's store-error counting, each such request shows in the render record as
`rejected` +1 and `store_errors` +1 on every run (the failed republish), so it is no longer
silent. Test: `crates/fmn-tex/tests/memory_cache.rs`
`corrupt_or_wrong_source_disk_documents_recompute_and_warm_memory` (2 rejected, 2 store
errors, 0 bytes written).

### Suggested fix

Give fmn-cache a keyed-entry eviction that removes an entry only if it still holds the
verified bytes the caller rejected (compare-and-remove by payload digest, through the owned
root's managed-path checks). fmn-tex calls it on a payload rejection, then republishes. Test:
plant a foreign payload, run twice, and the second run is a verified hit.

title: W6: fmn-text — shaping, markup, and layout over fmd-font (Scribe I)
description:
Implement the text plane (§11.2): native shaping — cmap→gids, kerning via kern + focused GPOS, bundled-face ligature sets OFF by default (matching the familiar manim look; opt-in flag) — greedy line breaking with manim's width semantics (Knuth–Plass as an option, never the silent default), and the manim markup tag set: <span>, <b>, <i>, <u>, <s>, <sub>, <sup>, <tt>, <big>, <small> with color attributes, plus the t2c/t2f/t2g/t2s/t2w maps, justification/indent/alignment/line-spacing at full constructor granularity.

Font policy (D-08): the bundled default face renders identically on every machine; user TTFs by path; the family-name scan is a convenience tier that never silently substitutes (a missing font is a named capability-style error, not a fallback surprise). Default text face decision: the Reference defaults to Consolas via Pango — ours is the bundled default face, Behavior-Noted (BN-05 covers native-typesetting metric differences).

Markup parsing is untrusted-adjacent: bounded nesting/size, precise diagnostics, fuzz target (§16.5).

description:
Found in the regenerated Look Gallery (readme.braced_matrix, readme.piecewise_cases at release 6d4a4463): the portal's matrix brackets and the cases brace are visibly heavier than the pinned Reference's.

Cause: ADR-0005 draws delimiters past the 1.25x ceiling, with stroke weights calibrated against the authored CM Unicode glyph. The cmunrm '[' has a 0.067 em stem, and drawn.rs uses 0.065 em + 0.004 h. TeX switches to cmex's size variants at \big (1.2 em) and beyond. Those are drawn with a thin rule; in the side-by-side the Reference's stems are about a third as thick. So TeX's own look has a seam (cmr's small delimiters are heavy, cmex's big ones thin), which ADR-0005 deliberately smooths away.

Options:
(a) ADR-0028's cmex faces supply the real variants (and their 1.2/1.8/2.4/3.0 em size chain, which also fixes \left/\right sizes).
(b) Re-calibrate the drawn constructions to cmex's weights. That amends ADR-0005's 'calibrated against the authored glyph' rule and needs an ADR.

Acceptance: the bracket and brace stem weight of a two-row matrix and of cases within 15% of the Reference's in the Look Gallery side-by-side, with an owner verdict.

title: W2/W10: Path booleans return flatten-first point structures (Exclusion 45 vs 279 points, other start point) with no Behavior Note
description:
## Found by the Appendix-A class sweep (fm-5wq.26), 2026-09-27

The path booleans `Union`, `Difference`, `Intersection` and `Exclusion` return different point structures from the pinned Reference. The Reference computes them with `pathops` on its curves and keeps quadratic segments. Chisel's booleans are flatten-first (plan §7), so the portal returns many line segments:

| construction | Reference points | portal points |
|---|---|---|
| `Exclusion(Square(), Circle())` | 45 | 279 |
| `Intersection(Square(), Square().shift(RIGHT))` | 35 | 257 |
| `Union(Square(), Circle())`, `SpeechBubble()` | 71 | 183 |
| `Difference(Square(), Circle(radius=0.5))` | 45 | 43 |

Starting points and orientation also differ; for example, the Reference's Union starts at (1, 1) and the portal's at (−1, −1). Also, `Difference(Circle(), Square(0.5))` takes the subject's red stroke in the portal, where the Reference's result keeps the default style.

No Behavior Note documents any of this. Scene code sees it through:
- `get_num_points()`;
- `point_from_proportion` and `get_start`/`get_end`;
- `Transform` alignment between a boolean result and another path, where more points means different morph correspondences;
- `ShowCreation`, which draws from a different starting point.

## Work (decide, then implement)

- Either return the Reference's structure: recover quadratic segments from the flattened result (Chisel's error-bounded fitting), with the Reference's start point and orientation convention;
- or write a Behavior Note stating the flatten-first output, with migration guidance (for example `get_start`, `ShowCreation` direction), and keep the style fix either way. The result's style should match the Reference's default, not the subject's.

## Acceptance

- The class sweep shows the four booleans equal, or equal only through a BN row that cites the new note. The open-bead row citing this bead is removed.
- A test for each operation: point count, start point and orientation, per the chosen rule. Planted negative at 35c65d6e.

title: W5: Wire the retained compositor to real pixels — pooled frame buffers, bump arenas, reuse-equivalence goldens
description:
fm-0l8 landed the retained compositor's KEY and its dirty-tile machinery in crates/fmn-render/src/cache.rs: §10.8's four-part key (command list, resource revisions, camera revision, output transform), poisoning for §8.2's writable live views, per-frame counters for §17.2, and an adversarial key-completeness suite (every mutation class invalidates: style, transform-both-old-and-new-bounds, order, camera, output transform, live view).

TileCache is GENERIC over its payload because there is no rasterizer in the tree. What remains is everything that needs pixels:

1. REUSE-EQUIVALENCE GOLDENS: cached vs cold frames bit-identical across an animation corpus with waits, static layers and moving objects. The key-completeness suite is the strongest form available without an engine; this is the form the bead asked for.
2. POOLED FRAME BUFFERS + BUMP ARENAS: 'per-frame allocation in bump arenas over pooled frame buffers — the zero-alloc steady state PG-6 measures (allocation count is a sharper regression tripwire than wall-clock)'. fmn_frame::FramePool already exists and is the thing to pool.
3. THE wait()-FRAME FAST PATH, MEASURED: the counters are wired (CacheStats::hit_rate, dirty_fraction) and a wait() frame already reports 100% hits — what is missing is measuring the RASTER WORK avoided, which needs raster work to exist.
4. STATIC LAYER RUNS CACHED AS UNITS: §10.8 asks for runs above/below animated content cached as a unit rather than per tile. Deferred deliberately: it is a coarser key over the same mechanism, and choosing its granularity without a rasterizer's cost model would be guessing.

BLOCKED ON: the first engine (fm-ig3, the certified CPU engine).

DO NOT re-derive the key. TileKey::build reads the binning and the plan precisely so a new input cannot be forgotten at one call site and remembered at another; TileCache::store takes the key plan_tile returned so a payload cannot be stored under a state it was not rendered from.
close_reason: Verified landed at HEAD 9c1e086+. The dormant 2026-08-10 claim (YellowPrairie) committed the full pixel wiring code-first in 18ddd68: engine-side retained pixel rendering over fmn_frame::FrameBuffer, bump-arena draw derivation with per-frame arena reset, and PixelTileCache binding the generic TileCache<T> to real tile bytes. Batch-verify this session at that HEAD: cargo test -p fmn-render green — 328 tests incl. retained_pixels_bypass_unchanged_raster_work_and_match_cold_rendering (item 1 reuse-equivalence golden + item 3 raster-work-avoided measurement) and the zero-steady-state-allocation assertion across frames 2..=N+1 (item 2 pooled buffers/bump arenas); cargo fmt --check clean; clippy -p fmn-render --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; ubs exit 0. Item 4 (static-layer unit runs) remains deliberately deferred per the in-bead rationale — coarser key over the same mechanism, granularity needs a rasterizer cost model; tracked for the post-engine optimization pass rather than silently dropped.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FROM fm-ig3 (2026-07-26) — the rasterizer TileCache<T> was waiting for exists now.

cache.rs said it plainly: 'the engines own pixels (§10.1), and there is no rasterizer in the tree yet; parameterizing means the cache mechanism is complete and tested now, and the payload type arrives with the engine that produces it'. The engine renders into a fmn_frame::FrameBuffer of PixelFormat::Rgba16F (linear light, straight alpha, output orientation), so T is a tile's slice of that.

Four things that bear on wiring it:

1. THE TILE FUNCTION IS ALREADY PURE. FrameJob::render_into slices the frame into bands with chunks_mut and hands them to a shared queue; a band's bytes are a function of (band index, plan, config) and nothing else. A cache that substitutes stored bytes for a tile is substituting for a pure function, which is what makes reuse byte-identical rather than nearly so.

2. OCCLUSION PRUNING IS ALREADY PROVEN BYTE-EXACT AGAINST THE ENGINE — occlusion_pruning_is_byte_exact renders the same scene with and without prune_occluded and compares bytes. That is G0-8b's F13 discharged with pixels rather than argued from interior_row's literal 1.0.

3. TileKey'S EXCLUSION OF THE INSTANCE INDEX AGREES WITH ADR-0013, and now on purpose. The key omits the instance index because 'an object inserted earlier shifts every later index without changing what this tile draws'; ADR-0013 rules that the engine's accumulation order is painter order and outline order, never an interned table's order. Same reasoning, two places, now cross-referenced.

4. WATCH THE STRIDE. engine::frame_digest hashes payload rows only, never the whole allocation, because a pooled buffer carries the previous frame's stride padding — hashing it would make a golden a function of pool history. A cached-and-restored tile payload must respect the same boundary; the_frame_digest_ignores_stride_padding is the shape of the test you want.

Also filed: fm-e9h (zero steady-state per-frame allocation, PG-6), which overlaps your bump-arena work and should probably land with it.

title: W4/W10: Write/DrawBorderThenFill leaves a point-less root at the outline's style (fill opacity 0); the Reference keeps its style (AnalyzeStepAlongDiagonalLine)
description:
Found 2026-10-11 while splitting fm-78b6's scene row. _2023/convolutions2/diagonal_slices.py AnalyzeStepAlongDiagonalLine has rects = VGroup(...Rectangles); rects.set_fill(TEAL, 0.5); then self.play(Write(rects)). At teardown the root's fill_opacity is 0 in the portal and 0.5 in the Reference. The members are right in both.

Minimal repro, both engines (portal wheel11, Reference 6199a00d):
  rects = VGroup(Square(), Square().shift(RIGHT)); rects.set_fill(TEAL, 0.5); rects.set_stroke(WHITE, 1)
  self.play(Write(rects))   -> root fill_opacity: Reference 0.5, portal 0.0; rects[0]: 0.5 in both
  self.play(FadeIn(rects))  -> portal root stays 0.0

Mechanism (fmn-anim/src/creation.rs DrawBorderThenFill):
- after_begin runs match_style_from(mobject, outline), the Reference's creation.py:105. Under C-31 the portal applies it to the point-less root, so the root takes the outline's style (fill opacity 0). In the Reference it is dropped there.
- interpolate_submobject's second half calls interpolate_fields(submob, outline, start). A point-less root has an empty RecordBuffer, so interpolation never reaches its phantom _data_defaults row, and the root stays at the outline's style.

Fix: when a family member's buffer is empty, interpolate its defaults row (record.rs defaults_row / restore_defaults_row) from the outline to the start, as for real records. At alpha 1 the root's style is then the start's. Do it once, where interpolate_fields serves every Transform, so point-less roots follow the C-29 model (their style is real) in every animation. Check that self-goldens do not move: point-less roots draw nothing.

Acceptance: the repro reads 0.5 after Write in the portal, and AnalyzeStepAlongDiagonalLine leaves fm-78b6-style-defaults-sweep's subject list.

title: W3: Bound snapshot decode allocation amplification before capacity growth

title: W8/W9: no front door can set video quality — fmn::render and the CLI hard-code crf None (x264 CRF 23, preset medium, no tune; 1080p60 explainer came out at 451 kb/s and reads blurry)
description:
## Found by the 2026-10-06 reality check (a real explainer, viewed by the owner: "it looks blurry")

**Every MP4/MOV franken_manim produces is encoded at x264's defaults, and no front door can change that.**
- The negotiated `VideoJob` has a `crf: Option<u8>` field, and `encode_argv` honours it (`crates/fmn-output/src/negotiate.rs:198, 302`).
- But `fmn::render` hard-codes `crf: None` (`crates/fmn/src/rendering.rs:1175`), and so does the CLI (`crates/fmn-cli/src/lib.rs:5340`).
- No preset or tune is passed anywhere.

So every render gets libx264 CRF 23, preset medium, no tune. The AAC mux stage passes no bitrate, so audio gets ffmpeg's AAC default.

### Evidence

The 4:27 Hoeffding's D explainer at 1920×1080, 60 fps came out at **451 kb/s** in total. That is fine for flat dark backgrounds, but thin strokes and small coloured text soften visibly in motion, and the owner's first verdict was that it "looks blurry".

The only way to get delivery quality today is to wrap the host process runner. That means injecting an `FfmpegCapability` whose `ProcessRunner` rewrites the encode argv, adding `-crf 16 -preset slow -tune animation` after `-c:v libx264` and `-b:a 256k` after `-c:a aac`. This works: the x264 SEI in the output confirms `crf=16.0 subme=8 psy_rd=0.40`. But it is argv surgery that no user should have to write, and it bypasses the negotiation layer that should own encoder policy.

### Work

1. `RenderOptions::video_quality` (or `EncodeSettings { crf, preset, tune, audio_bitrate }`), validated by `VideoJob::resolved_encoder`:
   - CRF only for x264/x265 (already enforced);
   - preset and tune drawn from the encoder's known set;
   - hardware encoders take a bitrate or quality instead.
2. CLI: keep the Reference's flag surface where it exists (`--vcodec`, `--pix_fmt`) and add `--crf`/`--preset`, recorded in BN-15. Wire the config file's `file_writer` section.
3. Choose a better default for manim-style content, e.g. CRF 18, tune animation. Measure it, don't assume it.
4. Record the encode settings in the provenance manifest. They are part of the ffmpeg invocation identity, and ffmpeg products stay outside certification.
5. The audio mux gets an explicit AAC bitrate.

### Acceptance and tests

- Unit tests: `encode_argv` contains exactly the requested `-crf/-preset/-tune` in output-option position, and invalid combinations are named refusals.
- Fake-ffmpeg CI: the argv the boundary spawns matches the request.
- e2e (render-matrix class): a short MP4 at the requested CRF/preset, with the setting verified from the stream's x264 SEI (`x264 - core ... crf=..`) and logged.
- No silent behaviour change for callers who request nothing, unless the default changes deliberately with a BN entry.

title: W10: The one API schema — classes, methods, defaults, flags, config keys; codegen for both front doors
description:
Implement the single source of API truth (§16.2, D-05 adjacency): ONE machine-readable schema describing classes, methods, parameters, defaults, CLI flags, and config keys — from which are GENERATED: Rust config structs + builders (the kwargs displacement: Default structs + builder methods, §15.1), fmn-python signatures (argument names/defaults/keyword-ness matching the pinned manimlib surface), Parity Ledger rows (W10LEDGER consumes), CLI flag tables (W9CLI consumes), and docs. DRIFT BETWEEN FRONT DOORS IS A BUILD ERROR — the schema check runs in CI; a Rust builder or Python signature that disagrees with the schema fails the build.

Bootstrapping: extract the initial schema from the pinned Reference (signatures, defaults, keyword arguments) via the W1GAUNT extraction tooling; then the schema is AUTHORED (our canonical names per C-9's typo rulings — tickness_multiplier et al. get canonical names in the schema with exact-name aliases in fmn-python), reviewed, and versioned. Include the wildcard-export inventory (§1.6: from manimlib import * has no authoritative __all__ — the Ledger enumerates SYMBOLS, and the schema is where that enumeration lives).

Also here: fmn-config's struct migration to codegen (W1CONF hand-wrote; this bead swaps in generated types), and the CLI exit-code/flag-interaction table (W9CLI's normative source).

Acceptance: schema file + generators in CI; drift negative tests (mutate a generated signature → build fails); import-surface conformance harness comparing the schema's export list against the actual pinned wildcard namespace; C-9 alias tests; docs generation smoke test.
close_reason:
The one API schema landed (§16.2). Two committed layers — API_SCHEMA.tsv, extracted from the pinned Reference by scripts/gen_api_schema.py (2276 symbols, 4441 params, 34 flags, 149 config keys), and API_OVERLAY.tsv, authored (C-9 canonical names, §16.1 tiers, optional config keys, Rust bindings) — merged by fmn_conformance::schema, which is the only thing generators ever see.

Extraction is a static ast walk, not an import: the Reference cannot be imported here (colour/moderngl/pyglet/a GL context) and importing it would make the schema a function of the local environment. CPython's wildcard rules are modelled faithfully, including skipping the TYPE_CHECKING guard bodies that never execute at runtime. The walk lands on 257 classes — exactly Appendix A's independently verified census, now asserted as a test, so a Reference pin bump that moves the census says so.

Acceptance, item by item. Schema file + generators run under cargo test and therefore CI. Drift negative tests present: a mutated accessor AND a mutated config path, both generated in memory so they neither race the bless run nor depend on the artifact existing. Import-surface harness compares the enumerated export closure against the extractor's own count and asserts both that the numpy leak IS present and that TYPE_CHECKING-only names are NOT. C-9 alias tests assert every misspelled symbol has a canonical name, that the Reference spelling survives as the fmn-python alias, and that each ruling stays within two edits so an API redesign cannot ride in disguised as a typo fix. Docs generation is smoke-tested by the same byte-for-byte gate as everything else. fmn-config's migration to codegen is done: 99 hand-written lines replaced by generated.rs, with all 35 pre-existing config tests passing unchanged as the behaviour-preserving evidence.

Findings recorded in the commit: C-9's real extent is 26 symbols and 2 params, not the 3 the plan names (the listner misspelling is systematic across the whole event surface); the wildcard surface leaks 73 third-party/stdlib names; class-level attributes are public surface and 105 are now carried. Two modelling gaps found by the coverage check were fixed in the schema rather than papered over in the test — map-valued parent keys that are bound as a whole, and optional keys that by definition have no default line to extract.

NOT DONE, deliberately, and noted on fm-c53 with a how-to: the CLI exit-code and flag-interaction tables. §13.6 wants them pinned in the schema and the schema is now where they go, but neither is extractable (the Reference signals by exception, not exit code) and authoring them is a W9 design decision rather than a transcription. Inventing them here would have been fabricating a contract under cover of codegen.

2265 of 2276 symbols read unreviewed — the honest number for a surface nobody has adjudicated, and the one fm-iz4's Ledger ratchets down; docs/api/ledger.tsv is the substrate it consumes.

Gates: scripts/check.sh green (fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, test, crate-DAG); 915 tests passing, up from 889; no new crate, no new DAG edge, no new dependency. ubs reports 19 criticals, all one class — panic! inside test code, the same fixture-test idiom geometry_parity.rs and self_goldens.rs already use — adjudicated false positives.

title: W1: fsci-linalg solve policy reads libm log10 (condition signal) — platform-dependent FailClosed at exact thresholds; make it deterministic upstream
description:
## Found by the governed-closure sweep (fm-certified-libm-leak-3aja), 2026-09-27

`fsci_linalg::solve` is on a certified path: fmn-geom `smoothing.rs` calls it for smoothing solves. At the pin `5b1441b`, `solve` reaches `solve_policy_decision`, which builds its policy signals from `condition_signal_from_rcond(rcond) = (-rcond.log10()).clamp(0.0, 16.0)` (`fsci-linalg/src/lib.rs:1479-1484`). `f64::log10` is the platform libm.

Impact: the solution values do not depend on the signal. The policy controller's action does: `FailClosed` returns `LinalgError::PolicyRejected`, and `FullValidate` adds a backward-error check that can reject. If `rcond` sits on a policy threshold, the last-bit difference between libms could make a solve error on one platform and succeed on another. That is narrow, but it is a platform dependence of certified output, and ADR-0010 property 1 does not admit it.

The certified-arithmetic guard carries this call as a known leak owned by this bead. Its entry fails once the call is gone.

## Work (upstream, frankenscipy)

Make the policy signal deterministic:
- compare `rcond` against the thresholds directly, since log10 is monotone;
- or compute the signal with IEEE-only arithmetic (exponent extraction plus a fixed polynomial), keeping the controller's behavior on the scipy-parity tests.
Land it on frankenscipy main (and master), then take it with the fm-9esi pin bump. Remove the known-leak entry in `crates/fmn-conformance/tests/certified_arithmetic.rs`.

## Acceptance

- The guard reports no reachable fsci-linalg call.
- A test with an `rcond` exactly on a policy threshold gives the same decision under a planted libm-style perturbation (±1 ulp in the signal) as without it.
close_reason: Upstream: frankenscipy d00db63ac (main+master, frankenscipy-8xgmd). fsci-runtime gains deterministic_exp (FDLIBM e_exp) and deterministic_log10 (musl log10), built from +, -, *, / and bit moves only. All four decision sites on the solve path use them: condition_signal_from_rcond, the policy softmax, and the portfolio's condition_posterior and rcond_decade. The softmax exp means the posterior that picks FailClosed/FullValidate no longer reads libm either, which a deterministic log10 alone would not cover. Tests, upstream on rch: golden bits; every normal decade 1e-307..1e308 exact; within 2 ulps of glibc over 100k points; solve_policy_signal_is_exact_at_decades (signal == k at rcond 1e-k, k=0..16); fsci-runtime and fsci-linalg suites green (758 linalg); clippy clean. Acceptance 2 as literally written (a ±1 ulp signal perturbation at a threshold keeps the decision) holds for no continuous signal. What the tests pin instead is that the signal and posterior bits are platform-independent, so there is no libm perturbation left to plant. Local: d98dd701. The guard now sweeps fsci-runtime, which nothing had read, and a parser fix makes functions with array signatures visible. The guard reports the three fsci-runtime calls as known leaks owned here, plus the existing fsci-linalg log10. All four leave with fm-9esi's pin bump (>= d00db63ac), whose acceptance already requires no fsci known leaks; the guard fails each stale count. guard 12/12, clippy clean.

title: W8: The negotiated ffmpeg boundary v2 — FFMPEG_PROTOCOL.md, sandbox, hardware encoders, fake-ffmpeg CI
description:
Implement the ONE external-tool boundary (§14.3, §3 D2, D-23). FFMPEG_PROTOCOL.md v2 replaces any fixed pipe with NEGOTIATION: fmn-frame renders in output orientation (no vflip, ever) and applies transfer natively (no obligatory eq); the sink negotiates pixel format (RGBA8/BGRA8 for alpha/compat, NV12 for ordinary 8-bit video, P010 for 10-bit/HDR, canonical RGBA for certified raw/PNG), orientation, transfer, primaries, range, row stride, and encoder. The arithmetic is the argument: 4K RGBA8 is 33.2MB/frame vs NV12's 12.4MB — 2.67x less pipe payload at 60fps.

THE SECURITY PROTOCOL (D2, complete): argv-only invocation (no shell), per-job private temp dirs, timeouts + process-tree cancellation (via fmn-platform's process capability), output-size limits, environment allowlist + locale pinning, atomic result publication, executable path AND content hash into provenance. ffmpeg is OPTIONAL: absence yields a capability error NAMING the native alternative — never silent substitution.

HARDWARE ENCODERS enter here and only here (§14.3): hevc_videotoolbox/ProRes on macOS, h264_nvenc/hevc_nvenc/AV1 on NVIDIA — a documented standard-mode knob (ffmpeg products are excluded from certification by construction, so hardware encode changes nothing about the determinism story); fmn doctor reports what the installed ffmpeg offers; selection explicit or auto; encoder identity in provenance.

Protocol retentions: GIF mode, the two-stage audio mux (video first; then -c:v copy -c:a aac -map ...), --subdivide outputs, insert files, --prerun counting. ALL testable against a FAKE-FFMPEG in CI (a scripted binary asserting argv/stdin contract and emitting canned outputs) — the protocol is CI-verified without real encoders.

Acceptance: fake-ffmpeg contract suite (every negotiation dimension, both mux stages, failure modes: timeout, oversized output, nonzero exit); sandbox tests (env allowlist, tree-kill on cancel); capability-error tests with ffmpeg absent; provenance fingerprint test; real-ffmpeg smoke test behind an env flag.
