title: W4: The RationalFrameClock — manim's exact sample points, drift-free
description:
Implement the clock (§9.2, D-07, BN-02): an i64 frame index over fps, computing time as exact rationals — emitting the SAME nominal sample sequence as the Reference's arange(0, run_time, 1/fps) + 1/fps semantics: no emitted alpha-zero progression frame (begin() interpolates at zero separately, outside the emission sequence); upward duration rounding (a run_time that is not a whole number of frames still covers its end); the final sample may exceed run_time (alpha clamps per the Reference's rule); finish() applies final_alpha_value. Scene code experiences manim's timing model without manim's float drift — hour-long renders accumulate zero error (Behavior Note BN-02).

Why rational: the Reference advances a float accumulator; at 30fps an hour of frames drifts visibly, and two runs disagree with themselves under different chunkings. Our clock is (frame_index, fps) — time derives, never accumulates. Every subsystem that needs "now" (updaters' dt, wait_until predicates, presenter holds, A/V sync in Reel) reads this clock; dt is exactly 1/fps as a rational, converted to f64 at the consumer boundary.

PERMANENT REFUSAL (D-18, §10.5): adaptive or variable frame sampling is refused forever — the sample points are semantics, and every scheduler freedom in §17 is defined relative to them. Encode this in the type: there is no API to emit off-grid samples.

Acceptance: sample-sequence fixtures vs the Reference formula across awkward run_times (0.1, 1/3, 2.9999, exact multiples); drift test (10^6 frames: exact equality with closed-form time); wait/wait_until/skip interaction tests; the no-off-grid-API property documented and asserted.

BN-02 drafted at docs/behavior_notes/BN-02-rational-clock.md.

title: W1: fmn-platform — capability traits (fs/process/clock/AssetFetcher) + HardwareTopology introspection
description:
Implement fmn-platform (§6, §17.4). Two halves:

(1) Capability traits: filesystem, process spawning (the ffmpeg boundary's substrate — argv-only, env allowlist, timeouts, process-tree cancellation live HERE as the one sanctioned subprocess mechanism), monotonic + wall clocks, and the host-provided AssetFetcher trait — the ONLY place network exists; no TLS in core (D2). Every capability is a trait object the engine receives, never an ambient global: this is what makes the deterministic lab, WASM tiers, and the Studio's isolated worker possible. Provide std implementations + test doubles (virtual fs, fake clock, scripted AssetFetcher).

(2) HardwareTopology introspection (Rev 4, §17.4): physical/logical cores, performance classes (P/E), cache groups and NUMA nodes/CCDs, SIMD tier detection (portable/v3/v4/NEON), annex device presence, available memory, encoder capabilities — processor-group-aware on Windows (systems above 64 logical processors span groups and explicit scheduling code must know it). This feeds fmn-runtime's ExecutionPlan derivation (W5 bead): engine, frames in flight, render-team count/threads, tile dimensions, SIMD tier, scratch sizes, output pixel format.

Platform notes to honor from §17.6: no core pinning on Apple silicon (no clean no-unsafe API; output is thread-count-independent so placement cannot affect bits anyway); QoS class mapping is a consumer concern but the topology must expose what it needs.

Acceptance: trait suite + test doubles; topology snapshots from at least linux-x86-64 and one aarch64 committed as fixtures; Windows processor-group handling unit-tested against synthetic topologies; doc comments making the capability doctrine explicit for every later crate.
close_reason: fmn-platform landed: capability traits + std impls + test doubles (fs: FileSystem/StdFs/VirtualFs with manifest loading; clock: Clock/StdClock/FakeClock; fetch: AssetFetcher/NoNetwork named-capability-error/ScriptedFetcher; process: the D2 mechanism — argv-only, env-clear+allowlist, timeout kill, output-cap kill via shared overflow flag, absolute-program-path contract, ScriptedRunner) and HardwareTopology introspection reading sysfs THROUGH the fs capability (SMT/packages, capacity+freq P/E derivation, L2/L3 cache domains, NUMA, Windows processor-group model with 64-cap invariant + synthetic tests, SIMD tier via std::arch, meminfo). Real linux-x86_64 snapshot committed (128L/64C/8xCCD); synthetic x86 SMT+CCD and aarch64 big.LITTLE sysfs fixtures; real aarch64 snapshot = fm-<new> (hardware). Capability doctrine documented at crate root. Also fixed pre-existing check_crate_dag failure (G0 spike crates now exempt, with a no-production-dep-on-spike check). Notes: process-tree cancellation is direct-child kill (no libc under forbid(unsafe); ffmpeg doesn't daemonize — revisit documented); UBS's one remaining critical is the scanner's Command::new heuristic on the capability's program parameter — mechanism-vs-policy by design, absolute-path contract enforced, fixed-tool allowlist lands at the W8 boundary.

title: W4: The six-step frame order + the FramePacket freeze
description:
Implement the frame loop's load-bearing order EXACTLY (§9.3, §1.4, D-19): (1) animation update_mobjects(dt) → (2) animation interpolate(alpha) → (3) time advances → (4) SCENE updaters run, observing post-interpolation state → (5) capture → (6) emit. always_redraw-style scenes semantically depend on step 4 seeing step 2's output; this order is a contract, not an implementation choice.

The UPDATE-ORDER CORPUS locks it: dt-updaters on animated mobjects; target-with-updater; suspend both ways (animation suspending target updaters; explicit suspend_updating); wait and wait_until; skip mode; final samples; unequal run_times in one play(); time_span re-windowing. Each corpus scene asserts observable state at specific frames — these are semantic regression tests, not pixel tests.

THE FRAMEPACKET (Rev 4's boundary at step 5, reordering nothing): capture freezes an immutable FramePacket — frame index and alpha, camera state, RNG substream states (via §6.5's keyed forks), and revisioned references into Lumen's compiled render state — after which the frame no longer depends on mutable scene state. Everything before the freeze is the serial front-end; everything after (IR sync, binning, raster, color conversion, emission) consumes ONLY the packet. This is what makes the §17.4 pipeline and §9.5 frame-parallelism legal. Design the packet as genuinely immutable (no interior mutability, revision handles not live pointers) and cheap (CoW snapshot references, not deep copies).

Acceptance: the update-order corpus green; FramePacket immutability enforced by construction (API review + a test that mutating scene state after capture cannot affect a held packet); packet-cost measurement (O(touched-state), suitable for 3-6 in flight per §17.4).
close_reason: Six-step frame order + FramePacket freeze landed (§9.3, D-19): play_segment/wait_segment in fmn-anim drive the load-bearing order exactly — per-animation update_mobjects(dt) interleaved with interpolate(t/run_time, raw-unclamped so the §9.4 pipeline clips unequal run_times), time advance (clock + Stage::update fixed to advance its float mirror BEFORE updaters, matching increment_time-then-update_mobjects), scene updaters over post-interpolation state, capture, emit. Skip = one big-dt step, no capture/emit; BN-10 corrects the Reference's skip-mode double-dt (finish pass is dt=0 in both modes, so skipped and played segments end in identical updater state — corpus-locked). Reference begin_animations (roots unrooted animated mobjects) and finish_animations (remover cleanup + dt=0 pass) kept. FramePacket: immutable by construction — frame index, segment frame, clamped alpha, exact RationalTime, Rc'd CoW snapshot (O(touched) verified via storage_id sharing), and DERIVED rng: keyed per-frame forks are pure fns of (seed, substream, frame_index) so the packet carries two words and rng_fork() reproduces any substream exactly (D-18 property). Camera state + IR revisions join at fm-gw7/fm-5xm (documented subset). 16-scene update-order corpus green: post-interpolation observation (always_redraw property), time-before-updaters, suspend matrix, copy ticking, skip-parity, unequal run_times, final-sample clamp, time_span re-window, wait/wait_until/skipped-wait, membership edges, packet isolation/cost/rng. 339 workspace tests; all gates green (ubs: 0 critical).

title: W2: True arc length under the original names — adaptive quadrature + inverse-arclength LUTs
description:
Implement the proportion/length layer correctly (§7.3, BN-03). The Reference's layer is chord-distance heuristics — three mutually inconsistent approximations, with quick_point_from_proportion assuming equal curve lengths. We keep the NAMES and fix the MATH (D-05).

Scope: (a) get_arc_length returns actual arc length via adaptive Gauss–Legendre quadrature (fsci quad) with a stated tolerance; (b) point_from_proportion and MoveAlongPath consume a per-revision inverse-arclength LUT — built lazily per path revision (coordinate with §10.8's compiled-path caches: the LUT is one of the retained per-path artifacts, invalidated by geometry revision only, NOT by transform/style changes), giving constant-speed motion, as every user always assumed it worked; (c) quick_point_from_proportion REMAINS as the documented fast approximation — heuristics survive beside true math as labeled options, never silent substitutes; (d) downstream consumers get length-true placement: dashes, arrow tips, and tracers place by true length (W7 consumes this).

Behavior Note BN-03: paths animate at slightly different (correct) pacing than the Python engine; document with a migration example (a MoveAlongPath whose apparent speed changes).

Acceptance: arc-length oracle tests against closed forms (circles, parabolic arcs, lines); LUT inverse-error property tests (point_from_proportion(L(t)/total) ≈ t within tolerance); LUT-revision invalidation tests (transform does NOT rebuild; geometry edit does); constant-speed metamorphic test (equal proportion steps ⇒ equal arc steps).
close_reason: Proportion/length layer landed in fmn-geom/src/arclength.rs. Design upgrade over the plan sketch: quadratic Bezier arc length has a CLOSED FORM (|B'| is the norm of a linear function), so no quadrature and no fsci dependency — exact to rounding, deterministic (ln via fmn-dmath), with exact branches for lines, points, and interior cusps. get_arc_length = true length; point_from_proportion = constant-speed via ArcLengthTable (Newton on exact partial lengths + bisection safeguard, fixed 24 iterations, convergence break); quick_point_from_proportion kept verbatim as the labeled heuristic; CachedArcLength implements the §10.8 geometry-revision-only keying (transform/style never rebuild — tested). Oracles: 20k-interval Simpson agreement 1e-9, analytic parabola sqrt(2)+asinh(1) at 1e-12, cusp exactly 1, line exact; inverse round-trip; constant-speed metamorphic on an uneven path incl. demonstration that the quick heuristic diverges. BN-03 drafted with the MoveAlongPath migration example. All gates green (58 suites), ubs 0 critical.

title: W5: The Metal annex engine — Studio preview production backend (via frankentorch)
description:
Implement the Accelerator Annex's first production engine (§10.7, §17.5, D-22; building directly on G0-8's proven kernels): Metal via frankentorch — the ONLY GPU gateway (no wgpu, ever: D1 audit catastrophe + duplicates ft) — serving Studio preview on Apple silicon, where unified memory makes the handoff nearly free and preview frames carry no bit promise.

Offload set, ranked by ROI (§10.7): stroke SDF + AA resolve (dominant 2D cost, per-pixel independent — G0-8's stage); SSAA resolve + transfer functions; DotCloud/glow splats (overdraw-heavy, additive); 3D surface tessellation with the kept lighting; large fill coverage. Platform playbook (§17.6): ft shared buffers for upload; tile-shader/threadgroup techniques keeping tile-local coverage and compositing on-chip (Apple TBDR rewards exactly this); memoryless attachments for pass-local results; threadgroup sizes from pipeline introspection, never CUDA habit; direct presentation for preview; GPU-side NV12/P010 conversion before any export readback (§14.3).

Hard boundaries (R21): standard-mode ONLY, never certified (D-18 refusal); annex binning uses deterministic count/prefix/scatter or stable key sort, never unordered atomic appends; excluded from core gates — PG-A profiles gate ANNEX changes only, so acceleration can never mask a core regression (annex work PAUSES whenever core PG-1..PG-3 regress); backend identity journaled into the input closure; held to the engine-equivalence visual budget vs certified frames.

Acceptance: Studio preview renders through the annex by default on supported hardware with the declared CPU fallback intact (G3's required-with-fallback rule, OQ-12); engine-equivalence suite green for the annex on the corpus; PG-A rig measuring fps, bytes up/back per frame, occupancy on the pinned Apple profile; fallback-path test (annex unavailable ⇒ CPU preview, no error).
notes:
G0-8b (fm-orn) verdict: FILLS ARE IN SCOPE for the Metal preview backend, not deferred to CPU-only. The fill kernels land at the f32 arithmetic floor (max delta-8bit = 1, vs the stroke stage's 152), use the same one-thread-per-pixel dispatch model as the stroke kernel, and add no new upstream requirement on frankentorch. Use FillShape::PerPixel and MathMode::Safe.

ALSO OWNED HERE (G0-8b finding F17): at preview resolution the boundary is the cost, not the kernel. An EMPTY scene on the same grid costs ~1.1 ms of the 1.3-2.2 ms frame — allocate an 8.3 MB device buffer, clear it, read it back. Two levers, both outside the kernel: (1) hold ONE surface for the engine's lifetime instead of buffer_zeroed per dispatch (the spike reallocates deliberately, because a spike should not cache); (2) §17.6's GPU-side NV12/P010 conversion before any export readback. For Studio preview, present rather than round-trip. A PG-A per-frame number is meaningless without the empty-scene floor beside it.
close_reason: Metal annex acceptance satisfied with current Studio default/fallback, equivalence, PG-A, native presentation, and governed closure evidence.

title: W5: Harden the frankentorch Metal gateway completion and size contract

title: W10: authored-override checks with no memo cost 60% of Mobject.rotate (93 of 151 us); cache per-class verdicts under a type-watcher epoch
description:
## Measured (2026-09-29, main 51c6740f wheel, same process, unprofiled)

point_editing.rotate calls movement._changed(self, rotation_mapping) with no memo on every call. The check
re-derives static lookups over the whole MRO each time:

| object | rotate | the check alone |
|---|---:|---:|
| Square | 150.9 us | 92.6 us (61%) |
| Dot | 172.4 us | 96.0 us (56%) |
| VGroup of 10 | 254.5 us | 65.2 us (26%) |

In corpus Confetti (colliding_blocks_v2/supplements.py), 82K rotate calls made this 44% of a 45 s profile.
cProfile inflates call-heavy Python about 4x, so the unprofiled share is lower, but still large.

Other per-call sites with no memo:
- decimal_authoring.set_submobjects_from_number (every DecimalNumber.set_value);
- vector_field_lifecycle;
- per-play admission in playback, rotation, indication and movement (once per play).

## Why a per-scan memo does not apply

These checks run inside authored code, between arbitrary Python statements. A class or its MRO can be
monkeypatched between two calls, and the fm-qead / updater tests pin that late patches are honored.

## Candidate design (decide before building)

- Cache (class, protocols) -> verdict. Invalidate on any modification of a class in the class's MRO or
  its metaclass MRO, using CPython type watchers (PyType_AddWatcher / PyType_Watch, 3.12+).
  - The watcher callback bumps a native epoch.
  - _changed with no memo reuses a verdict only at the same epoch.
  - It still checks the instance __dict__ for hook names on every call, which is cheap.
- pyo3-ffi 0.29.2 skips PyType_AddWatcher, so this needs a hand-declared extern in fmn-python, the
  only non-forbid crate. Up to 8 type watchers exist per interpreter.
- Key the cache by the protocols object held strongly, not by id(protocols): finalize() rebinds the
  dicts, and ids can be reused.
- Alternative without native code: none found. CPython exposes no type version tag to Python.

## Acceptance

- Same-process: the rotate check drops to about the cost of the instance-dict test.
- Scene A/B, same invocation, identical final frames (Confetti, a DecimalNumber-updater scene).
- Differential test against the uncached _changed across these cases:
  - class patched after caching;
  - __bases__ reassigned;
  - metaclass attribute set;
  - instance hook added/removed.
- Planted negative: a cache without invalidation must fail.
close_reason: Landed eba4020b: per-class verdicts under the ratified version-tag read; acceptance re-verified on the committed code (same-process 68-91 -> 1.2 us, Confetti 1.7x with identical PNG, differential and planted-negative witnesses, all gates)

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Wider payoff (WildGoose, 2026-09-29). The same type-watcher epoch would also make per-class caching exact in the per-frame public update walk. PrimeRace on d1b36519 spends 19 s self time of a 150 s profile in updater_dispatch._static_is: an MRO walk per member per frame, 4.16M member visits.

That walk runs authored code (updaters, overrides) between members, so class answers cannot be memoized today without type-mutation detection. With the epoch they could be reused across members and frames, re-checking only each instance's own __dict__. The same applies to the per-frame requires_public_update scan: 43c1c807 made it per-class within one scan, and an epoch would let it skip unchanged frames.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Scope extension (WildGoose, 2026-09-30). After 7fdc43b3 the remaining O(scene)-per-frame Python costs are:
(1) has_updaters(), a live get_family walk. It runs on every Animation.update_mobjects copy each frame; the Reference caches _has_updaters_in_family.
(2) The requires_public_update scan.
Both need exact change signals:
- class mutation: this bead's type watcher;
- updater-list edits: updaters is a plain list authors mutate directly, so a live list subclass like _LiveSubmobjects, plus interception of the updaters attribute assignment;
- family edits: _LiveSubmobjects._replace_projection already sees them.
With those, has_updaters can keep per-node path-wise updater counts propagated along parents, and the scan can skip unchanged frames.
Risk: a missed mutation path silently skips updaters. Validate counts against the live walk in the test suite, including copy, deepcopy, pickle, become and restore.

comments.author: WildGoose
comments.text: Claimed after graph, reservation, and HEAD checks (HEAD 9d05524c): per-class _changed verdicts cached under a CPython type-watcher epoch; differential tests against the uncached path

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Landed eba4020b (WildGoose). Design change from the candidate: no CPython type watcher and no new unsafe item. Verdicts are keyed on the existing ratified tp_version_tag read (ADR-0015 Amendment 1, now also exposed as _type_version_tags) of the class and its metaclass. Any mutation of either MRO changes or zeroes a tag, and a zero tag never caches. The cache hangs off each _protocols table, which the installer closures own. A first version kept it in fmn_python.movement's module globals, which pinned the embedded worker's temporary module across teardown: 70 of 101 embedded tests failed, and the fix is in the landed commit.

Exactness limits in the landed code:
- only classes whose MRO is all metaclass type are cached (__class__ assignment on a base with a heap metaclass changes no tag);
- objects whose own __dict__ holds a hook name, or is not an exact dict, are decided alone;
- a class passed as the object is never cached.

Acceptance, re-run on the committed code (wheel61 vs wheel59 = main 7fdc43b3, same host, alternating):
- Same process, the rotate check: 76/68 -> 1.2/1.1 us (Square), 91/81 -> 1.2/1.3 (Dot), 60/59 -> 1.2/1.1 (VGroup of 10). Rotate itself: 130/128 -> 45/42 us.
- Confetti, same invocation: {35.64, 39.57} s -> {21.74, 23.97} s, identical final PNG.
- ScaleIndicator (DecimalNumber-updater scene), same invocation: {174.12, 160.26} s -> {154.92, 151.54} s, identical PNG. An earlier pair on the uncommitted wheel60 overlapped ({162.8, 173.3} vs {166.7, 168.9}), so the effect there is small and noisy.
- Differential test (point_editing test_override_checks_follow_class_edits_between_calls): cached equals uncached across a class patched after caching (rotate then routes to the authored apply_points_function), a subclass patch and delete, __bases__ reassigned both ways, an instance hook added and removed, and a metaclass attribute set. It also asserts that the cache fills.
- Planted negative: a reader returning constant tags fails that test.

Gates: check_portal_runtime.sh PASS; 166/166 portal suites; embedded fmn-python lib 101/101; fmt and clippy clean. ubs findings match the baseline, apart from deliberate exact-type checks and test introspection.

Self-verified. No independent verifier ran; every acceptance item was re-executed on the committed code.

title: W7: The de-TeX'd natives — Brace, Matrix delimiters, Checkmark/Exmark, DecimalNumber
description:
Implement §11.6/§12.3's de-TeXing — the Reference routes several NON-math classes through LaTeX because LaTeX was there; we make them native and better, removing the deepest early typesetting dependency from the library's critical path:

BRACE becomes a PARAMETRIC PATH GENERATOR — correct at any width (the Reference renders \underbrace{\qquad} and stretches it, distorting the curl at extreme widths; ours is a proper parametric family), with BraceLabel/BraceText composing with Scribe text; LineBrace orientation semantics preserved. MATRIX delimiters use fmd-math's extensible-delimiter engine DIRECTLY (W6MATHEXT) — Matrix/DecimalMatrix/IntegerMatrix/TexMatrix/MobjectMatrix lay out their element grids natively (row/col spacing, alignment per the Reference's conventions) with delimiters that scale correctly by construction. CHECKMARK/EXMARK draw from bundled glyphs (no pifont). DECIMALNUMBER/INTEGER are PURE NATIVE TEXT — one face, GLYPH-RECYCLING updates (a ticking counter re-uses glyph instances, W5IR's interning — no per-frame typesetting), correct formatting edge cases (negative zero, rounding mode, trailing zeros, unit suffixes, edge_to_fix semantics for ChangingDecimal).

Also here (§12.3): SurroundingRectangle/BackgroundRectangle/Cross/Underline; BulletedList/Title on Scribe; the interactive.py control mobjects (Button, Checkbox, sliders, ControlPanel...) as compositions bound to Proscenium events (event wiring lands with W9EVENTS; construct them here).

Behavior Note BN-08: de-TeX'd classes render from native constructions; metrics differ from the LaTeX-derived originals; scaling behavior is better-defined.

Acceptance: Brace parametric tests across widths (smooth, symmetric, correct curl); Matrix layout fixtures (spacing/alignment vs Reference conventions) with delimiter-scaling tests; DecimalNumber formatting edge-case corpus + glyph-recycling test (update does not re-typeset); structural fixtures for the remaining classes; BN-08 drafted.
close_reason:
The de-TeX'd natives landed for the half that needs no typesetter; the text-backed half is SPLIT OUT, not dropped — fm-ebl carries its acceptance criteria unmodified, blocked on fm-p5d (the Scribe bridge). Every dependent of fm-y69 that needed the text classes (fm-3kr, fm-jh7, fm-v4l, fm-wy1, fm-i1q) has been re-pointed at fm-ebl, so nothing is unblocked by this close that should not be. GOVERNANCE §5 clause 2: a postponed item moves to a later bead publicly, with its criteria travelling intact.

LANDED HERE: Brace / BraceLabel / LineBrace as a parametric path family; SurroundingRectangle, BackgroundRectangle, Cross, Underline; Checkmark and Exmark as drawn marks. Plus two pieces of substrate the tier needed and the crate lacked — per-point stroke tapers (VMobject::with_stroke_profile, carrying set_stroke(width=[0,6,0]) by linear resize onto the point run) and the detached positional layer (bbox_point, moved_to_aligned, next_to, next_to_point, aligned_to, arranged) mirroring Stage's critical-point semantics exactly.

THE BRACE IS CORRECT AT ANY WIDTH, BY CONSTRUCTION. The Reference renders one \underbrace{\qquad} and resizes it: widening is a special case over six hard-coded submobject indices of that render, narrowing has no special case and squashes the curl via set_width(stretch=True). Ours generates the shape, with three clamps proved rather than tuned — cap+waist ≤ 0.40w < 0.50w (hooks cannot reach the centre point), thickness ≤ 0.10w < cap (inner hooks cannot cross), height > 1.2·thickness (the point cannot punch through its runs). The property test walks widths 0.001 to 200 checking all three. The thickness clamp was not in the first draft: the test caught a real inversion at width 0.01, where a brace narrower than its own stroke turned inside out — precisely the regime where the Reference distorts, so it would have been easy to ship and easy to excuse. The tip is closed-form where the Reference scans the rendered glyph with np.argmin.

CHECKMARK/EXMARK DIVERGE FROM THE BEAD TEXT, ON EVIDENCE. The bead said "draw from bundled glyphs (no pifont)". The faces were checked, not assumed: U+2713 ✓ is mapped by IBM Plex Sans and Noto Sans Math (not Computer Modern); U+2717 ✗ is mapped by NO bundled face, nor are U+2714/2718/2715. A glyph exists for the check and none exists for the cross. U+00D7 is present but is a thin multiplication sign, the wrong weight for \ding{55}; bundling a dingbat face for two glyphs expands the closure. Both are therefore drawn, in one shared unit box — drawing only the cross would leave a matched pair mismatched, since the Reference's two dingbats come from one font and read as siblings. This is ADR-0005's precedent (drawn path as mainline when the authored glyph is absent) applied to marks. Recorded in BN-08 with the cmap table.

BN-08 drafted at docs/behavior_notes/BN-08-de-texed-natives.md, per §16.8's assignment of that number to the de-TeX'd classes. A numbering collision was found and FLAGGED RATHER THAN SILENTLY FIXED: a file already holds BN-08 for the animation contract, and BN-07 is duplicated across two files. Renumbering a published, user-facing note is a documentation act with its own review, and RULE 1 forbids deleting files, so fm-nn8 carries the reconciliation.

title: W9: The replay journal + effect model — record everything, replay cheaply, invalidate conservatively
description:
Implement replay (§13.4, R16): the journal records COMMANDS AND EFFECTS — play/wait/add/remove operations, RNG substream states at barriers, camera/audio state, content hashes of every file/font/asset read, callback version hashes, ffmpeg invocations — with OPAQUE BARRIERS for non-replayable operations and CONSERVATIVE invalidation (when in doubt, a barrier).

Three consumers, one record: (1) the supervisor's edit-replay (W9SUPER: restore checkpoint, replay journal from the last valid barrier — entries whose recorded hashes still match replay from cache; a changed callback hash invalidates from that point); (2) the PURITY CLASSIFIER's evidence (§9.5: the effect model IS the classifier's vocabulary — segments whose recorded effects are pure are frame-parallel eligible; classifications are journaled per segment, R20); (3) the PIPELINE's synchronization vocabulary (§17.4: any operation that must observe rendered pixels is a pipeline barrier that drains in-flight frames; ordinary manim scene code never hits one — assert this on the corpus).

Soundness doctrine (R16): replay-cache unsoundness is the failure mode — the design answer is conservative invalidation everywhere: unrecognized effects are opaque; divergent operation classes become barriers BY DEFAULT; a replay that would diverge (hash mismatch mid-replay) falls back to full re-execution, correctly, silently, and records why.

Also here: the one-command REPRO BUNDLE (§18) — scene + input closure packaged so every bug report is a deterministic replay — and the journal's appearance in provenance sidecars.

Acceptance: record/replay equivalence tests (replayed session ⇒ bit-identical final state + frames on pure content); invalidation tests (edited callback → replay stops at the right barrier); opaque-barrier tests (an unrecognized effect forces re-execution, never wrong reuse); purity-evidence round-trip with W4PURITY; pipeline-barrier drain test; a repro-bundle end-to-end test (bundle → fresh machine sim → identical render).
close_reason: Replay journal + effect model + repro bundle landed in fmn-scene (FMNA/3+4). Command/effect/asset/subprocess/checkpoint records; plan_replay with conservative invalidation naming its reason; ReplayAudit divergence fallback; EffectClass embedding W4 purity evidence (R20); PixelObserving pipeline-barrier vocabulary with corpus assertion; Custom→Opaque coercion; §18 repro bundle with closure verification. 10 acceptance tests incl. bit-identical fresh-stage replay and bundle end-to-end. 538 workspace tests green.

title: W6: fmd-font — factor the Font module out of fmd + build the glyf outline decoder (cross-repo)
description:

Factor fmd's text::Font sfnt machinery (cmap formats 4/12, glyf/loca, composite glyphs, hmtx, kern + focused GPOS, subsetting) into a new fmd-font workspace crate, and EXTEND it with the piece FrankenManim needs and fmd never did: the GLYF OUTLINE DECODER — simple and composite glyphs decoded to quadratic contours (TrueType outlines are already quadratic — zero-loss into our QuadPath model) with phantom-point-correct metrics (left/right side bearings, advance interaction with hmtx, composite offset/anchor semantics).

Bundled faces (§11.1): Computer Modern roman/bold/italic/bold-italic (the default face — the 3b1b typographic identity), CM Typewriter (code), IBM Plex Sans, Noto Sans Math (symbol coverage) — all OFL, all shipped in-crate; a bare install renders every built-in scene identically everywhere; NOTHING depends on host fonts (D-08). Honestly tiered out with revisit triggers (§16.6): CFF/CFF2, variable fonts, color glyphs, GSUB ligature machinery beyond the bundled-face sets, mark positioning, bidi/complex shaping.

Security (§16.5, R14): fonts are untrusted input — bounded table sizes, offset validation, composite-recursion limits, fuzz target from day one (malicious font tables are a DoS surface even in safe Rust).

Governance (R8): fmd-font rides UPSTREAM_LEDGER.md + SUITE.lock like any foundation crate; FrankenManim CI builds both repos from the lock. G0-3 (the fmd-math spike) needs CM outlines decoded — this bead's decoder is its prerequisite.

title: W9: The Studio — preview server, inspector, scrubbing, TUI, security model
description:
Implement the Studio (§13.5, D-14, leapfrog #6): localhost with an EXPLICIT security model — loopback-only binding, per-request capability token, Host/Origin validation, size limits, no filesystem serving beyond embedded UI assets, event-rate limits, session expiry. Untrusted content renders only in the isolated worker (W9SUPER).

Streams: baseline is MULTIPART PNG (we own PNG — no dependency, works everywhere); MJPEG as the ffmpeg-accelerated option; browser-local WASM rendering is the endgame (G5). On supported Apple silicon the preview renders through the METAL ANNEX by default (W5METAL — speed welcome, bit promises irrelevant for preview) with the CPU fallback declared (OQ-12/G3's rule).

Surfaces: TIMELINE SCRUBBING over W4TIMELINE + checkpoints (seek anywhere; pure segments reconstruct instantly, stateful segments snap to checkpoints); THE INSPECTOR — family tree, live record fields (the RecordBuffer's typed views), uniforms, TYPESET SPAN MAPS (W6SPAN's in-Studio payoff: hover a glyph, see its source span); DEBUG OVERLAYS — tiles, control cages, bounds, winding, depth (§18); a kitty/sixel TUI in the fp-frankentui lineage for SSH sessions (leapfrog #5's terminal leg).

Embedded UI: assets compiled into the binary (no runtime file serving, no CDN — the one-binary story extends to the Studio).

Acceptance: security tests (non-loopback refused; missing/stale token refused; oversized/flooding events limited; no path escapes); stream conformance (multipart PNG consumable by stock browsers); scrub correctness tests (seek(t) state matches play-through, via W4TIMELINE's machinery); inspector data-accuracy tests against engine state; TUI smoke test over a pty; annex-preview fallback test.
notes: Timeline substrate for scrubbing landed with fm-hfe: Timeline::seek restores the nearest checkpoint, replays whole segments, and lands via reconstruct_pure_frame for pure segments (O(1)) or by stepping frames for stateful ones. title: G0-6: Determinism spike — one nontrivial frame hashed across four platforms; fix the certified arithmetic
description:
Executed decision spike resolving OQ-1: floating-point + fmn-dmath vs fixed-point raster arithmetic for certification (§20.1 spike 6 → §6.6, §10.5; risk R11, High).

Scope: render ONE nontrivial frame — it must exercise transcendental-dense paths (arcs, per-vertex atan2 joints, rate functions, glow falloff), gradient fills, strokes with joins, and alpha compositing — through the prototype renderer on linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64, and windows-x86-64, and compare raw-buffer hashes. Two sub-questions: (a) with f32/f64 floating screen-space arithmetic + fmn-dmath transcendentals + fixed-order reductions + FMA off, are the four platforms bit-identical? If yes, floating suffices for certified; if no, adopt the canonical fixed-point raster boundary (fixed-point screen coordinates + integer coverage accumulation at defined precision, explicit rounding) that §10.5 sketches. (b) Decide the certified matrix: linux-x86-64/linux-aarch64/macos-aarch64 certified from day one; windows-x86-64 functional-CI from W1 with bit-certification a SEPARATE declared decision (OQ-6, §16.7).

Prerequisite: an fmn-dmath prototype for the exercised functions (sin/cos/atan2/exp/tanh/sqrt at minimum) with documented accuracy — this spike is also fmn-dmath's first accuracy/portability shakedown.

Why now: everything in §10.5's parallelism contract, §6.1's tiered numeric doctrine, and the §17.3 SIMD lane rules is written against whichever arithmetic wins. Changing the answer after W5 exists would invalidate every self-golden.

Acceptance: hashes + methodology committed; OQ-1 resolved with the decision recorded in §23; the certified-matrix definition frozen into the input-closure spec (§16.7); if fixed-point wins, the precision/rounding constants specified.
close_reason:
OQ-1 RESOLVED: floating-point suffices. §10.5's canonical fixed-point raster boundary is RETIRED, NOT DEFERRED. ADR-0010; plan §23 trued up in the same commit; certified matrix frozen into docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5; note at docs/g0/G0-6-determinism-ratification.md; raw data at docs/g0/g0-6-hashes/.

THE MEASUREMENT. One frame — gradient fills under the nonzero winding rule, a filled ring whose hole depends on winding DIRECTION, strokes with joins and arc-length tapers, per-vertex atan2 joint angles that reach pixels, the Reference's true_dot glow with its pow falloff (and its hard-dot branch), five rate functions driving the geometry, alpha compositing throughout — hashed through fmn-hash's canonical container, alongside per-function digests of all 16 fmn-dmath entry points.

  linux-x86_64   glibc   x86-64    native      cca55de642d54f2e...
  linux-aarch64  musl    aarch64   qemu-user   cca55de642d54f2e...
  macos-aarch64  Darwin  aarch64   native      cca55de642d54f2e...

ALL EIGHTEEN DIGESTS IDENTICAL ON ALL THREE. frame.f64 = 3ff2cac55c33a8b2..., frame.f32 = 9e94bf5e95765eca...

The legs vary things INDEPENDENTLY rather than repeating one comparison: x86-64-glibc vs aarch64-Darwin crosses both the ISA and the OS boundary at once; aarch64-musl shares an ISA with one and an OS family with the other. So the ISA, the libc and the OS are each shown not to be in the loop — which is the actual claim, and it is exactly why running one leg on musl was a stronger test than running it on glibc would have been.

NO-FMA EVIDENCE, AND A METHOD FAILURE WORTH RECORDING. llvm-objdump on the aarch64 build: 1652 scalar FP instructions, ZERO fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub/fmla/fmls, on a target where FMA is baseline. The scalar-op count is reported because it is what makes the zero mean anything — my first pass used plain objdump, which on this host cannot disassemble aarch64 at all: it emitted 3 lines and reported zero of every instruction, including the ones certainly present. A zero from a tool that found nothing is not evidence. determinism::fma_guard now refuses hand-written mul_add across the certified source roots, since rustc's no-contraction is a default rather than a setting.

WHAT I BUILT TO GET THERE. The prototype renderer (spikes/g0-8-accelerator, shared with G0-8) grew the two stages the frame needed and did not have: a nonzero-winding fill (exact in x, 4x supersampled in y, closed-form roots per sub-scanline, total-ordered crossing sort) with a defined gradient field, and the Reference's true_dot glow profile in full including pow(1-r, glow_factor). Plus per-vertex joint angles by atan2, reaching pixels through a miter-gain stand-in — because a joint angle that never reaches a pixel cannot be tested by a frame hash. All three are labelled IN THE SOURCE as defined stand-ins, not as §10.2's analytic-area fill (fm-5oi's) or §10.3's join model (fm-oac's): the question OQ-1 asks is whether two platforms compute the same bits from the same algorithm, and a spike claiming to be W5's renderer would have answered a question nobody asked.

G0-8's PUBLISHED NUMBERS ARE UNAFFECTED, deliberately. The Metal device layout (FlatIr) is byte-for-byte unchanged, the annex refuses non-Stroke IR and nonzero miter_gain BY NAME (checked before the device is opened, so the contract is testable without a GPU), and the stroke render loop was restructured to a row accumulator with the arithmetic preserved exactly — verified by re-running the G0-8 comparison and getting the identical max_abs/mean_abs/rms/max_u8/differing/ssim line. Refusing rather than skipping is also what D-18 requires: the frame that defines the certified bits must never reach a GPU.

THE FRAME IS NOW A CROSS-PLATFORM SELF-GOLDEN. Both digests are bit-locked as SINGLE constants in the spike's tests — not three per-platform ones — so the property fails on whichever machine breaks it instead of waiting for someone to re-run the sweep. That is the Scope::Certified shape docs/INPUT_CLOSURE.md §6 now points at.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, stated so nobody reads more into it: (a) that f32 is safe for the fast CPU engine — f32 hashed identically everywhere, so it is PORTABLE, but G0-8 measured that it changes the PICTURE at curvature extrema; portable and correct are different questions, and fm-4wt now carries that comment; (b) that the SIMD tiers preserve any of this — they are the standing risk, since PG-5's per-commit sweep tests thread counts, not lane counts; (c) that linux-aarch64 HARDWARE behaves like linux-aarch64 emulation.

THE CAVEAT, RECORDED IN THREE PLACES RATHER THAN BURIED: the aarch64 Linux leg runs under qemu-user, because no aarch64 Linux hardware is reachable by this program. QEMU's softfloat is IEEE-754 correct for the basic operations and nothing certified uses anything weaker, so the leg is valid evidence about the ARITHMETIC — not about a machine. fm-sol replaces it with real hardware if any becomes available. Getting the leg at all required registering an arm64 binfmt handler on the dev box (owner-authorized), then cross-compiling to aarch64-unknown-linux-musl with rust-lld and running the static binary under qemu — compiling natively under emulation would have cost ~30x for an identical binary.

CERTIFIED MATRIX (sub-question b): linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64 certified from day one; windows-x86-64 functional-CI only, bit-certification remaining OQ-6's separate declared decision. Frozen into INPUT_CLOSURE.md §5, with the note that adding a platform is an ADR and not a CI-config change — the list IS the promise --reproducible makes.

DOWNSTREAM: fm-ig3 (certified CPU engine) is unblocked and now carries ADR-0010's four binding properties as acceptance criteria; fm-4wt carries the f32 finding and the SIMD lane-rule risk; fm-yp0 (G4b) enforces the frozen matrix; fm-sol owns the real-hardware replacement.

GATES: scripts/check.sh green; 937 workspace tests + 53 spike tests, 0 failing; spike fmt/clippy clean; the aarch64 record re-verified byte-identical after the final lint fixes. UBS: 1 critical, a panic! inside #[cfg(test)] code — the same false-positive class this repo has adjudicated before.

title: W10: The binding-tax program — batched crossings, GIL discipline, the opt-in acceleration ladder
description:
Implement §15.2's Rev-4 performance program for the Python boundary — arbitrary Python callbacks are the ONE serial, GIL-sensitive component no scheduler can dissolve, so the tax is engineered down and made visible:

MECHANISMS: method-resolution and callback handles CACHED (resolve once per (type, method), invalidate on class mutation); native→Python crossings BATCHED wherever semantics allow (updater groups crossing once per frame, not once per field); the GIL RELEASED across all native compilation, rasterization, conversion, and output waits (the interpreter and rasterizer overlap instead of alternating — §17.4's pipeline overlaps rendering with subsequent Python frame construction); dirty propagation batched once per callback group rather than per field write.

THE ACCELERATION LADDER (opt-in, never silent): above the always-correct Python updater sit explicit substitutions with identical semantics for their declared class — batched Python updater (fewer crossings) → array updater (one vectorized RecordBuffer operation) → native updater (Rust/engine-executable). Each is an EXPLICIT opt-in with documented semantics; silent substitution is prohibited (D-05's spirit: labeled, never silent).

title: W11: npm/WASM packaging — the browser artifacts
description:
Package the WASM tiers (§20.2 W11, §10.7): the tier-1 frame renderer (W5WASM) as an npm package — ESM module + typed JS surface via wasm-bindgen, single-threaded default with the threads variant behind cross-origin-isolation documentation; the tier-2 serialized-timeline player as it lands at G5 (consuming W4TIMELINE's format; the browser Studio endgame's substrate).

title: W10: A Line or GlowDot costs ~300 us to construct in the portal; DirectMGFInterpretation builds 120 per frame (3.4x the Reference, same work)
description:
## Measured (2026-09-30, ec956bf0 wheel, cProfile 200 s budget, WildGoose)

DirectMGFInterpretation (_2023/clt_proof/main.py) is 436.4 s against the Reference's 128.8 s on the same frame grid (fm-5wq.31 table). Its get_sample_group updater builds 60 Lines and 60 GlowDots every frame. That accounts for 152 of 200 profiled seconds: 201K objects, ~300 us each.

Contributors (cProfile, so Python overhead is inflated ~2-4x):
- Mobject.data: 2.64M reads, ~13 per object. Each builds a fresh record view through the native _data_array (5 us self). Callers: _style_data 878K, points 610K, resize_points 627K, set_points 204K, the point-cloud init 201K.
- svg_ingress's set_rgba_array_by_color wrapper (by_color): 653K calls, 32 s cumulative. Every set_fill, set_stroke and set_color walks the family through copying.family_preorder, even on a leaf: 1.79M family_preorder calls, 19 s.
- GlowDot point-cloud init (point_cloud_lifecycle.cloud): 59 s for 201K, including ten point_cloud_materials.setitem calls per dot (15.7 s) and _initialize_point_cloud (14 s native).
- Line/VMobject init (<string>:3438): 63 s cumulative; init_colors 36 s.

## Candidate levers (each must stay exact)

- A record view per object that stays valid until the buffer generation changes. The constraint: a live view pins its generation under the section 8.2 view protocol, so a cached view must not block reallocation or copy-on-write.
- by_color on a leaf (one member) without a family walk.
- Point-cloud material writes batched per dot.

## Acceptance

- Deterministic work counters that fail on the pre-fix build. Examples: record views built per Line construction; family walks per set_stroke on a leaf.
- DirectMGFInterpretation same-work ratio within 2x of the Reference, or a comment stating why not.
- Frames byte-identical; all portal suites green.

title: W8: Make cache traversal no-follow across reads, writes, eviction, and purge
description: A valid owned cache root can still be subverted by symlinked ns/name/version/objects/shard components. StdFs::list_dir follows directory symlinks; scan plus eviction can enumerate and delete a victim outside the cache, while get/put and stale-version purge can read, overwrite, or remove through replaced ancestors. Extend the filesystem capability with node-kind/no-follow primitives (and exact-leaf directory creation where needed), make every cache traversal fail closed without following symlinks or reparse points, and add real-host sentinel tests for shard, namespace ancestor, get-corruption cleanup, put, and stale-version paths. Document the remaining handle-relative TOCTOU boundary if safe std cannot close it.
